IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r4.speaker: الآخر
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r4.claim: An unnamed interpreter says each woman is made equivalent to a male, so the two together stand for one man and one reminds the other.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p5/r4.anchor: وقال الآخر في قوله: {أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} (4) أن تجعل كل واحدة منهما ذكرا؛ يريد: أنهما يقومان مقام رجل

BURHAN:v1p253#2/r14.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r14.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p253#2/r14.claim: The verse on deferred debts contains thirty-three instances of the letter mīm.

BURHAN:v1p251/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.claim: The debt verse is longest at 128 words and 540 letters; al-Duha then al-Fajr are shortest. He rejects مدهامتان and ثم نظر as shorter candidates based on their letter or word counts.
BURHAN:v1p251/r8.anchor: وأطول آية فيه آية الدين مائة وثمانية وعشرون كلمة وخمسمائة وأربعون حرفا

ITQAN:v4p431/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p431/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p431/r12.claim: The debt verse is the Qur'an's only āya containing twenty-three kāf letters.
ITQAN:v4p431/r12.anchor: ولا آية فيها ثلاثة وعشرون كافا إلا آية الدين

DAMGHANI:v1p396/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p396/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p396/r7.claim: Kabīr can mean much or numerous, paired with ṣaghīr for little; examples concern recording debts and spending.
DAMGHANI:v1p396/r7.anchor: ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله

DAMGHANI:v1p293/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r2.claim: Ḍalāl can mean forgetting; one of the two women may forget.
DAMGHANI:v1p293/r2.anchor: السابع الضلال النسيان قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r3.claim: A Qur'anic use of ضل is forgetting, as in the case of one witness needing the other to remind her.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p408/r3.anchor: الثامن : النسيان . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ﴿ أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى ﴾

MAJAZ:v1p82/r9.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p82/r9.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p82/r9.claim: Lā yabkhas means not to diminish; the proverb describes her as foolish but unjust.
MAJAZ:v1p82/r9.anchor: «لا يبخس منه شيئا» (282) : لا ينقص، قال: لا تبخسنى حقى (؟) ، قال فى مثل: «تحسبها حمقاء وهى باخسة» أي ظالمة.

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r1.claim: The stated due date should use days, months, years, or another precise measure; harvest, threshing, or a pilgrim’s arrival are too uncertain.
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r1.anchor: بالأيام أو الأشهر أو السنة وغيرها مما يفيد العلم ويرفع الجهالة لا بالحصاد والدياس

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r2.claim: Writing the debt and its due date is safer and prevents disputes; the majority consider the command a recommendation.
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r2.anchor: الدين بأجله لأنه أوثق وأدفع للنزاع والجمهور على استحبابه

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r3.claim: The scribe should mediate between both parties and record what each says, in equal terms without favor, addition, or omission; they should choose a learned, religious jurist whose document is legally reliable.
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r3.anchor: وقوله بينكم للإيذان بأن الكاتب ينبغي أن يتوسط بين المتداينين ويكتب كلامهما

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r4.claim: A scribe should not refuse to write the debt in the manner God taught for documenting agreements; the command reinforces the preceding prohibition.

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r5.claim: The debtor should dictate because he is the party answerable and must acknowledge the obligation.
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r5.anchor: الإملال هو الإملاء وهو إلقاء المعنى على الكاتب للكتابة

BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r6.claim: The debtor is especially warned to fear God and not reduce the dictated amount, since self-protection gives him an incentive to understate what he owes.
BURSEVI:v1p359#2/r6.anchor: لما فيه من الدواعي إلى المنهى عنه فإن الإنسان مجبول على دفع الضرر عن نفسه وتخفيف ما في ذمته

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r1.claim: A person unable to dictate may also be hindered by ignorance or another impediment; a guardian then takes over.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r1.anchor: أو جهل أو غير ذلك من العوارض

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r2.claim: The person’s guardian, administrator, proxy, or translator dictates fairly, without increasing or reducing the amount.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r2.anchor: أي : الذي يلي أمره ويقوم مقامه من قيم أو وكيل

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r3.claim: Two male witnesses are sought to carry testimony about the transaction; they are called witnesses in anticipation of giving testimony later.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r3.anchor: أي : اطلبوهما ليتحملا الشهادة على ما جرى بينكما

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r4.claim: ‘From your men’ means free adult Muslims of your community; in transactions between unbelievers or where the debtor is an unbeliever, unbelievers may be witnesses according to the author’s school.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r4.anchor: من أهل دينكم يعني من الأحرار البالغين المسلمين إذ الكلام في معاملاتهم

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r5.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness financial matters by consensus; women do not testify in fixed punishments or retaliation, where men are required.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r5.anchor: وشهادة النساء مع الرجال في الأموال جائزة بالإجماع دون الحدود والقصاص فلا بد فيهما من الرجال

BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r6.claim: The requirement that witnesses be approved applies to both the man and the women; women are included by grammatical predominance, and the phrase points to trust and known integrity.
BURSEVI:v1p359#3/r6.anchor: كائنون مرضيين عندكم وتخصيصهم بالوصف المذكور مع تحقق اعتباره في كل شهيد

BURSEVI:v1p360/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r1.claim: One woman may forget and the other remind her; reminder is the real purpose, while possible error is named as its cause, as in preparing a weapon to repel a possible enemy.
BURSEVI:v1p360/r1.anchor: وهذا تعليل لاعتبار العدد في النساء والعلة في الحقيقة هي التذكير ولكن الضلال لما كان سببا له

BURSEVI:v1p360/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r2.claim: Witnesses should not refuse when summoned to give or bear testimony.
BURSEVI:v1p360/r2.anchor: ثم حث الشهداء على إقامة الشهادة بقوله :

BURSEVI:v1p360/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r3.claim: Do not tire of documenting a debt, large or small, whether summarized or detailed, through its agreed due date.

BURSEVI:v1p360/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r4.claim: Documenting it to the due date is fairest before God, strengthens testimony, and best prevents doubt about the debt, amount, term, or witnesses.
BURSEVI:v1p360/r4.anchor: أي : أعدل {عند الله} أي : في حكمه تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p360/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r5.claim: Immediate exchange with both parties present may be left unwritten because hand-to-hand trade is less prone to dispute and forgetting.
BURSEVI:v1p360/r5.anchor: لكن وقت كون تداينكم أو تجارتكم تجارة حاضرة

BURSEVI:v1p360/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360/r6.claim: Witness sales either in this particular transaction or generally as a precaution; the majority take the verse’s commands as recommendations.
BURSEVI:v1p360/r6.anchor: أي : هذا التبايع أو مطلقا لأنه أحوط

BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r1.claim: If active, the prohibition bars a scribe from refusing or altering the document and a witness from withholding testimony; if passive, it bars others from harming them while occupied or withholding their fee.
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r1.anchor: كاتب} عن الكتابة المقصودة {ولا شهيد} أي : ولا يمتنع الشاهد

BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r2.claim: Violating the ban on harm is disobedience; believers should fear God in all His commands and prohibitions, and He teaches rulings that serve their interests and knows their conduct.
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r2.anchor: في مخالفة أوامره ونواهيه التي من جملتها نهيه عن المضارة

BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r3.claim: The verse’s detailed protection of people’s rights shows that safeguarding property is necessary; those who pursue truth are saved, while others stray.
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r3.anchor: يعلم بذلك أن مراعاة حقوق الخلق واجبة والاحتياط على الأموال التي بها أمور الدين والدنيا لازم

BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r4.claim: God teaches transaction rules out of mercy to prevent injustice, quarrels, resentment, and worldly distress; this shows that religious obligations also bring purification and blessing.
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r4.anchor: والله تعالى من كمال رحمته على عباده علمهم كيفية معاملاتهم فيما بينهم لئلا يجري من بعضهم

BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r5.claim: The first of three lessons concerns God’s relation to servants: His care in worldly dealings prevents loss and dispute and indicates that religious duties likewise express mercy and bring His blessings.
BURSEVI:v1p360#2/r5.anchor: فيشير بهذه المعاني إلى ثلاثة أحوال

BURSEVI:v1p361/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361/r1.claim: The second lesson concerns servants’ relation to God: carefulness over fleeting worldly transactions should teach even greater care over enduring afterlife matters, for every atom of good and evil is rewarded or punished.
BURSEVI:v1p361/r1.anchor: وثانيها حال العباد مع الله ليعلموا برعاية هذه الدقائق للأمور الدنيوية الفانية أن للأمور الأخروية الباقية

BURSEVI:v1p361/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361/r2.claim: God’s covenant with believers is a purchase of their lives and property for Paradise, witnessed by the angels; the written contract records a jewel from Paradise deposited as the Black Stone.
BURSEVI:v1p361/r2.anchor: فإن الله تعالى اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم بأن لهم الجنة وعلى هذا عاهدهم وأشهد الملائكة

BURSEVI:v1p361/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361/r3.claim: The third lesson concerns people’s dealings with one another: imitate God’s gentleness, keep His limits in agreement and disagreement, love, accompany, guide, and advise one another for His sake.
BURSEVI:v1p361/r3.anchor: حال العباد فيما بينهم فليعتبر كل واحد منهم من ملاطفات الحق معهم

BURSEVI:v1p361/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361/r4.claim: In all three conditions, remain mindful of God, who teaches through explicit statements and indications.

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r1.claim: God knows hidden thoughts and secrets and rewards people according to the sincerity and purity of their intentions; blessed is the person who purifies his character and seeks the unseen.
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r1.anchor: يعلم مضمون ضمائركم ومكنون سرائركم فيجازيكم على حسن معاملتكم بقدر خلوصكم وصفاء نياتكم

BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r2.claim: A Persian poem compares the unseen to a decorated palace and desire to a cloud of dust: abandoning desire removes the screen and enables sight of the desired reality.
BURSEVI:v1p361#2/r2.anchor: حقائق سراييست آراسته هوا وهوس كرد برخاسته نه بيني كه جايى كه برخاست كرد

AKHFASH:v1p205/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r1.claim: فرجل وامرأتان means the witnesses to be summoned are one man and two women.

AKHFASH:v1p205/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r2.claim: تسأم is from the verb سئمت, with the listed verbal nouns سآمة, سأمة, سآما, and سأما.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r2.anchor: وقال {ولا تسأموا} لانها من "سئمت" "تسأم" "سآمة" و"سأمة" و"سآما" و"سأما".

AKHFASH:v1p205/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r3.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r3.claim: يأب is jussive because it is a prohibition; at pause it is pronounced without a final yāʾ.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r3.anchor: [وقال] {ولا يأب الشهدآء} جزم لانه نهي واذا وقفت قلت "يأب" فتقف بغير ياء.

AKHFASH:v1p205/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r4.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r4.claim: تكون in إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة can mean 'occur'; alternatively it can take an accusative predicate with an implied subject, تلك.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r4.anchor: وقال {إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة} أي تقع تجارة حاضرة. وقد يكون فيها النصب على ضمير الاسم "إلا أن تكون تلك تجارة.

AKHFASH:v1p205/r5.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r5.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r5.claim: ولا يضار can be parsed as a prohibition or as an indicative statement; compare لا تضار والدة بولدها, though that form was not read in the indicative.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r5.anchor: وقال {ولا يضآر كاتب ولا شهيد} على النهي والرفع على الخبر. وهو مثل {لا تضآر والدة بولدها} إلا إنه لم يقرأ {لا تضار} رفعا.

AKHFASH:v1p205/r6.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r6.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r6.claim: بدين reinforces تداينتم, since mutual lending already conveys debt, like سجَدَ الملائكة كلهم أجمعون.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r6.anchor: وقوله {إذا تداينتم بدين} فقوله {بدين} تأكيد نحو قوله {فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون} لأنك تقول "تداينا" فيدل على قولك "بدين"

AKHFASH:v1p205/r7.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r7.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p205/r7.claim: A rajaz line using داينت illustrates reciprocal dealing: داينتُها وداينتني yields تداينا.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r7.anchor: داينت أروى والديون تقضى * [فمطلت بعضا وأدت بعضا]

AKHFASH:v1p205/r8.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p205/r8.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p205/r8.claim: In أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا, الشاهد is understood; إلى أجله refers to the deadline through which the testimony is valid.
AKHFASH:v1p205/r8.anchor: وقال {82ء] {أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله} فأضمر "الشاهد". وقال {إلى أجله} الى الاجل الذي تجوز فيه شهادته والله أعلم.

FARRA:v1p185/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p185/r1.claim: In إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها, تديرونها may be accusative or nominative; an indefinite noun can take a verbal predicate in either position.

FARRA:v1p185/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p185/r2.claim: A definite noun cannot be replaced by its verb as predicate in the same way, because a definite noun is specified while an indefinite one is open-ended.
FARRA:v1p185/r2.anchor: ولم يصلح ذلك في المعرفة لأن المعرفة موقتة معلومة

FARRA:v1p185/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r3.speaker: المفضل الضبي
FARRA:v1p185/r3.claim: Al-Mufaḍḍal al-Ḍabbī recited poetry with الحميم الحميم, where the second repeats and intensifies the first; without it, the first would be nominative.
FARRA:v1p185/r3.anchor: أفاطم إني هالك فتبيني ... ولا تجزعي

FARRA:v1p185/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p185/r4.claim: In وإن كان ذو عسرة, nominative ذو is possible; ʿAbd Allāh and Ubayy instead read accusative ذا, implying an omitted subject of كان.
FARRA:v1p185/r4.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله وأبي «وإن كان ذا عسرة» فهما جائزان

FARRA:v1p185/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p185/r5.claim: The accusative with كان requires an understood, indefinite subject; the cited poetry supplies such a subject and illustrates the construction.
FARRA:v1p185/r5.anchor: لأن بنية (كان) على أن يكون لها مرفوع ومنصوب

FARRA:v1p185/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p185/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p185/r6.claim: When the noun is overt, as in فإن كن نساء, the predicate can still be nominative or accusative, as in the cited trade construction.

FARRA:v1p187/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p187/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p187/r3.claim: ولا يضار الكاتب والشاهد means do not summon either while occupied.
FARRA:v1p187/r3.anchor: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد أي لا يدع كاتب وهو مشغول

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r1.claim: وليّه means the guardian of the party whose right is owed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r1.anchor: فليملل وليه بالعدل} أي] : ولي الحق

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r2.claim: أن تضل means that one woman forgets the testimony and the other reminds her; Moses' phrase uses ضالّ for forgetful.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r2.anchor: أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} أي: تنسى إحداهما الشهادة

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r3.claim: ولا تسأموا means do not grow tired.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r4.claim: The written record should include the debt whether it is small or large.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r4.anchor: أن تكتبوه صغيرا} من الدين كان {أو كبيرا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r5.claim: أقسط means more just; the record strengthens testimony because it reminds witnesses of all they witnessed.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r5.anchor: وأقوم للشهادة} لأن الكتاب يذكر الشهود جميع ما شهدوا عليه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r6.claim: أدنى ألا ترتابوا means less likely to doubt.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r6.anchor: وأدنى ألا ترتابوا} أي: أن لا تشكوا

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r7.claim: A present trade means goods the parties buy and sell among themselves.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r7.anchor: تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم} أي: تتبايعونها بينكم

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r8.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r8.claim: The writer must not be made to record what was not dictated, nor the witness to testify without being summoned; another view says they may refuse a summons.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r8.anchor: ولا يضار كاتب} فيكتب ما لم يملل عليه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r9.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p99#2/r9.claim: Mujāhid and al-Kalbī explain لا يضار as not bothering a writer by distracting him from his trade or work.

MAJAZ:v1p83/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p83/r1.claim: أن تضل إحداهما means that one of the two forgets.
MAJAZ:v1p83/r1.anchor: «أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى» (282) أي تنسى

MAJAZ:v1p83/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r2.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p83/r2.claim: A witness who has already testified must not refuse a summons; before witnessing, the person may choose not to testify.
MAJAZ:v1p83/r2.anchor: قال فيمن شهد: لا يأب إذا دعي، وله قبل أن يشهد

MAJAZ:v1p83/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p83/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p83/r4.claim: فسوق means sin in this context.

NAHHAS:v1p343/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p343/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p343/r2.claim: The author says his earlier al-Maʿānī book already treats the grammar of this verse in full.
NAHHAS:v1p343/r2.anchor: قد ذكرنا كل ما فيه في كتابنا الأول المعاني

NAHHAS:v1p343/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p343/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p343/r3.claim: The lām is present in وليكتب for the absent third person and omitted in فاكتبوه for the addressees; omitting it in second-person commands is common and preferable.
NAHHAS:v1p343/r3.anchor: أثبت اللام في الثاني وحذفها من الأول لأن الثاني غائب والأول للمخاطبين

NAHHAS:v1p343/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p343/r4.speaker: محمد بن يزيد
NAHHAS:v1p343/r4.claim: Ibn Yazid says a third-person command must retain its lām.
NAHHAS:v1p343/r4.anchor: فأما الغائب فزعم محمد بن يزيد أنه لا بد من اللام في الفعل إذا أمرته

NAHHAS:v1p343/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p343/r5.speaker: سيبويه والكوفيون
NAHHAS:v1p343/r5.claim: Sibawayh and the Kufans allow omission of the lām in a third-person command and cite a verse addressed to Muhammad.
NAHHAS:v1p343/r5.anchor: وأجاز سيبويه والكوفيون حذفها وأنشدوا ( محمد تفد نفسك كل نفس

NAHHAS:v1p343/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p343/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p343/r6.claim: The Hijazis and Banu Asad say يملي; Tamim says أمليت. The Qurʾan uses both language forms.
NAHHAS:v1p343/r6.anchor: هذه لغة أهل الحجاز وبني أسد وتميم يقولون أمليت وجاء القرآن باللغتين جميعا

NAHHAS:v1p346/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r1.claim: The anonymous verse سئمت تكاليف الحياة is cited as usage evidence for the verb سئمت.

NAHHAS:v1p346/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r2.claim: صغيرا أو كبيرا is circumstantial, referring to whether the debt is small or large.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r2.anchor: صغيرا أو كبيرا ) على الحال أعطيته دينه صغر أو كبر

NAHHAS:v1p346/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r3.claim: ذلكم أقسط is a subject-predicate clause; وأقوم is coordinated, and أدنى أن لا is accusative with an understood من.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r3.anchor: ذلكم أقسط عند الله ) ابتداء وخبر ( وأقوم للشهادة ) عطف عليه وكذا ( وأدنى أن لا

NAHHAS:v1p346/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r4.speaker: الأخفش
NAHHAS:v1p346/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash construes تجارة as the subject of تكون; others take تديرونها as its predicate.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r4.anchor: إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة ) أن في موضع نصب استثناء ليس من الأول قال الأخفش أي إلا أن تقع تجارة

NAHHAS:v1p346/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r5.claim: Asim reads the exception as meaning the debt is a cash trade.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم ( إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة ) أي إلا أن تكون المداينة تجارة حاضرة

NAHHAS:v1p346/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r6.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p346/r6.claim: Some say recording deferred debts and witnessing sales are recommendations, by analogy with commands that grant permission after a prohibition.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r6.anchor: فزعم قوم أنه على الندب والتأديب وكذا قالوا في قوله إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه هذا قول الفراء

NAHHAS:v1p346/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r7.claim: Al-Nahhas calls that analogy wrong: hunting after ihram and dispersing after prayer are permissions after restriction, unlike debt documentation.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r7.anchor: هذا قول خطأ عند جميع أهل اللغة وأهل النظر ولا يشبه هذا قوله تعالى وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا

NAHHAS:v1p346/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r8.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r8.claim: Some say a later verse licensed leaving documentation; others say trust permits omission, while another view says writing deferred debt is obligatory to protect rights.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r8.anchor: فزعم قوم أن هذا مما رخص في تركه بغير آية وعلى هذا فسروا أو ننسها

NAHHAS:v1p346/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r9.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
NAHHAS:v1p346/r9.claim: Ibn Umar says witnessing is obligatory for every sale, large or small, citing the command to witness sales.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r9.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر المشاهدة واجبة في كل ما يباع قليل أو كثير

NAHHAS:v1p346/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r10.speaker: أبو إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p346/r10.claim: Abu Ishaq prefers taking ولا يضار as a prohibition on the writer or witness causing harm, since the next clause calls such conduct sinful.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r10.anchor: قال أبو جعفر ورأيت أبا إسحاق يميل إلى هذا قال لأن بعده وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم

NAHHAS:v1p346/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r11.speaker: المفضل
NAHHAS:v1p346/r11.claim: Al-Mufaddal reports al-Aʿmash reading ولا يضار with kasra on rāʾ; kasra or fatḥa resolves the meeting of two sukūns, with fatḥa lighter.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r11.anchor: قال المفضل وقرأ الأعمش ( ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد ) قال أبو جعفر كسر الراء لالتقاء الساكنين

NAHHAS:v1p346/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r12.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق
NAHHAS:v1p346/r12.claim: Umar, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Abi Ishaq read ولا يضارر with kasra on the first rāʾ.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r12.anchor: وقرأ عمر بن الخطاب وابن عباس وابن أبي إسحاق ( ولا يضارر ) بكسر الراء الأولى

NAHHAS:v1p346/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
NAHHAS:v1p346/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿud reads ولا يضارر with fatḥa on the first rāʾ; both readings explain the text and do not replace the codex reading.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r13.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود ( ولا يضارر ) بفتح الراء الأولى وهاتان القراءتان على التفسير

NAHHAS:v1p346/r14.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p346/r14.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p346/r14.claim: فسوق بكم refers either to this act itself or specifically to causing harm.
NAHHAS:v1p346/r14.anchor: وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم ) أي فإن هذا الفعل ويجوز أن يكون التقدير فإن الضرار فسوق بكم

NAHHAS:v1p348/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p348/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p348/r1.claim: An anonymous verse says that a fool rushes toward what he is forbidden, apparently continuing the preceding discussion of harm and wrongdoing.

IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r1.claim: The debt with a specified term includes an advance sale (salam) of wheat measured in a known quantity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس ، في قول الله : يايها الذين امنوا اذا تداينتم بدين إلى اجل مسمى فاكتبوه قال : السلم 2 في الحنطة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas testifies that a guaranteed advance sale for a fixed term is lawful and authorized by God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة ، عن أبي حسان الاعرج عن ابن عباس ، قال : اشهد ان السلف المضمون إلى اجل مسمى ، ان الله احله واذن فيه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r3.claim: A specified term means a known term.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد ، عن ابن عباس إلى اجل مسمى قال : إلى اجل معلوم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r4.claim: A report from the Prophet says Adam denied gifting David forty years of his thousand-year lifespan; God produced the written record, witnessed by angels, proving the gift.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ، في قول الله : اذا تداينتم بدين إلى اجل مسمى فاكتبوه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r5.claim: Writing and witnessing debts prevents denial and forgetfulness; one who fails to witness has disobeyed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p554#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله اذا تداينتم بدين إلى اجل مسمى فاكتبوه فامر بالشهادة عند المداينة ، لكيلا يدخل في ذلك جحود ولا نسيان

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r1.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r1.claim: All sales deferred for a short or long term must be written and witnessed until their due date.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r1.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : يايها الذين امنوا اذا تداينتم بدين إلى اجل مسمى فاكتبوه ما كان من بيع إلى اجل صغير أو كبير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r2.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r2.claim: The command to write was obligatory.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r2.anchor: عن الربيع ، قوله : فاكتبوه فكان هذا واجبا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq says the writing command was abrogated by the later clause allowing the entrusted debtor to discharge the trust.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r3.anchor: عن محمد بن اسحاق قوله : فاكتبوه وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل انها منسوخة ، نسختها فان امن بعضكم بعضا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r4.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r4.claim: The scribe is commanded to write fairly between the parties.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r4.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل امر الكاتب ان يكتب بينهما بالعدل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r5.claim: Among you means the buyer and seller.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : وليكتب بينكم بين البائع والمشتري

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r6.claim: Fairness requires that the scribe neither add to what is claimed nor reduce the claimant’s due.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : كاتب بالعدل يعني يعدل بينهما في كتابه لا يزيد على المطلوب ، ولا ينقص من حق الطالب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r7.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r7.anchor: عن السدي ، في قوله : بالعدل يقول : بالحق

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r8.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r8.claim: A scribe should not refuse to write as God taught him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : ولا ياب كاتب يقول : لا ينبغي للكاتب ان يابى ، ان يكتب كما علمه الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r9.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r9.claim: Writing is obligatory for the scribe; al-Rabiʿ agrees, while ʿAta and al-Shaʿbi say the scribe should not refuse.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p555/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : ولا ياب كاتب قال : واجب على الكاتب ان يكتب ، وروى عن الربيع بن انس ، مثل ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r1.claim: If a scribe has an urgent need and another is available, he may go and seek the other scribe, since scribes were few then.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قوله : ولا ياب كاتب ان يكتب كما علمه الله قال : الكاتب اذا كانت له حاجة ووجد غيره

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r2.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r2.claim: The scribe’s duty to write applies when he is free.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r2.anchor: عن السدي ، في قول الله : ولا ياب كاتب ان يكتب قال : ان كان فارغا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r3.speaker: سعيد بن حبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r3.claim: The phrase about God teaching the scribe refers to writing that He taught him.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن حبير ، في قول الله : ولا ياب كاتب ان يكتب كما علمه الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r4.claim: Writing as God taught means writing as He commanded.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ولا ياب كاتب ان يكتب كما علمه الله كما امره الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r5.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r5.claim: The instruction to write was obligatory.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r5.anchor: عن الربيع ، قوله : فيكتب فكان هذا واجبا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r6.claim: The debtor must dictate to the scribe the amount of the debt he owes.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير وليملل الذي عليه الحق يعني المطلوب . يقول ليمل ما عليه من الحق ، على الكاتب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r7.speaker: الشافعي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi interprets the debtor’s duty as acknowledging the debt, rather than literally dictating it.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r7.anchor: عن الشافعي ، في قوله : و ليملل الذي عليه الحق انما معناه ان يقر ، قط ، بالحق

IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r8.claim: The debtor, witness, and scribe must fear God and neither conceal any right nor add falsehood to the record or testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p557/r8.anchor: عن قتادة وليتق الله ربه يتقى الله شاهد في شهادته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r1.claim: Do not reduce any part of the claimant’s due.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : و لايبخس منه شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r2.claim: Not diminishing the debt means neither wronging the debtor nor reducing what he owes; Qatada and al-Rabiʿ agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r2.anchor: سالت الحسن عن قوله : و لايبخس منه شيئا قال : لا يظلم منه شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r3.claim: The person who owes the debt is the debtor being discussed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله : فان كان الذي عليه الحق يعني المطلوب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r4.claim: A foolish debtor is ignorant about dictating the debt; Ibn ʿAbbas and Saʿid ibn Jubayr report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد فان كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها قال : اما السفيه فالجاهل بلاملاء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r5.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r5.claim: A foolish debtor is a minor.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r5.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : فان كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها اما السفيه : فهو الصغير

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r6.speaker: مجاهد والسدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r6.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi interpret a weak debtor as foolish.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r6.anchor: و روى عن مجاهد و السدى ، انه الاحمق

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r7.speaker: الشافعي
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r7.claim: Al-Shafiʿi defines a weak debtor as one who merits legal interdiction.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r7.anchor: و قال الشافعي : الذي يستحق ان يحجر .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r8.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a weak debtor may be incapable, mute, or mentally impaired.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : أو ضعيفا يعني : عاجزا أو اخرسا ، أو رجلا به حمق .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r9.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r9.claim: Unable to dictate means unable to do so competently; al-Dahhak reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r9.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : أو لا يستطيع يعني : لا يحسن . وروى عن الضحاك نحو ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r10.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r10.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r10.claim: To dictate means to state what is owed.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p558/r10.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله : ان يمل هو قال : ان يمل ما عليه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r1.claim: The guardian of an incapable debtor must dictate the right owed with fairness; al-Dahhak agrees.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فليملل ولى الحق حقه بالعدل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r2.claim: The guardian is the guardian of an orphan.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r2.anchor: عن الحسن فليملل وليه بالعدل قال : ولى اليتيم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r3.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r3.claim: The guardian may mean the claimant.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قوله : فليملل وليه بالعدل : ولي طالبه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r4.claim: The guardian is the claimant, who must not add anything to the debt.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فليملل وليه بالعدل يعني : الطالب ولا يزيد شيئا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r5.claim: Witnessing is required to protect one’s rights; al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas agrees.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : واستشهدوا يعني : على حقكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r6.claim: For a cash sale, take witnesses without writing; for a deferred sale, write and take witnesses.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد ة في هذه الاية واستشهدوا قال : اذا باع بالنقد اشهد و لم يكتب واذا باع بالسيئة ، كتب و اشهد .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r7.claim: The two male witnesses must be free men, not slaves.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r7.anchor: عن ليث ، عن مجاهد و استشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم قال : شاهدين حرين و ليس العبدين

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r8.claim: The male witnesses must be free Muslims.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : شهيدين من رجالكم يعني مسلمين احرار

IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r9.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r9.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r9.claim: The witnesses must be men of probity.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p559/r9.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم قال : امر الله تعالى ان تشهدوا ذوى عدل من رجالكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r1.claim: The provision allowing one man and two women as witnesses applies to debts.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r1.anchor: عن الربيع بن انس فان لم يكونا رجلين فرجل و امراتان و ذلك في الدين .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r2.speaker: يزيد بن عبد الرحمن بن أبي مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r2.claim: In legal claims, four women cannot replace two men; women’s testimony requires a man alongside them, and one man and one woman do not suffice.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r2.anchor: عن أبيه يزيد بن عبد الرحمن بن ابى مالك : و لا يجوز شهادة اربع نسوة مكان رجلين ، في الحقوق ،

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r3.claim: Children are not acceptable witnesses because they are not among those whose testimony is approved.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r3.anchor: عن ابن أبي ملكية ، قال : سالت ابن عباس عن شهادة الصبيان ، فقال ابن عباس : قال الله : ممن ترضون من الشهداء وليسوا ممن نرضى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r4.claim: Acceptable witnesses are those not known to have a defect.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم ، في قوله : ممن ترضون من الشهداء قال ممن لا يعلم عليه خويه

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r5.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r5.claim: God commands the use of just men and women as witnesses.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r5.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : ممن ترضون من الشهداء يامر باشهاده العدل من الرجال والنساء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r6.claim: If one of the two women forgets, the other reminds her; Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Rabiʿ, al-Suddi, Muqatil, and al-Dahhak report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r6.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : ان تضل احدهما قال : ان تضل ان تنسى ، فتذكر احداهما الاخرى

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r7.claim: The woman’s error means that she forgets her testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ان تضل احداهما يقول ان تنسى احدى المراتين الشهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r8.claim: One of the women reminding the other means she makes her remember.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p561/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فتذكر احداهما الاخرى يعني : تذكرها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r1.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r1.claim: The other woman reminds her companion of the testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r1.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان فتذكر احداهما الاخرى قال : فتذكرها صاحبتها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r2.claim: The reminding woman is the one who retained her testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قوله الله : فتذكر احداهما الاخرى يعني : تذكرها التي حفظت شهادتها

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r3.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r3.claim: A person who has testified should attend when later summoned to give that testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r3.anchor: عن أبيه ، في قول الله : ولا ياب الشهداء اذا مادعوا قال : اذا شهد ، ثم دعي إلى شهادته

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r4.claim: A summoned witness must come if the testimony is in his possession.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : ولا ياب الشهداء اذا ما دعوا قال : اذا كان عندهم شهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r5.speaker: عامر
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r5.claim: A person who has already witnessed must attend when summoned, but one not yet a witness may choose whether to testify; Mujahid, Saʿid, Rabiʿa, and Zayd ibn Aslam report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r5.anchor: عن جابر عن عامر في قوله : و لا ياب الشهداء اذا ما دعوا قال : اذا شهد ، فدعى فلا ياب ، واذا لم يشهد ، فهو بالخيار

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r6.claim: Mujahid says responding to a summons to testify is obligatory, while al-Shaʿbi says it is optional until one has testified.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r6.anchor: عن جابر عن مجاهد ، في قول الله : ولا ياب الشهداء اذا ما دعوا قال : هي واجبة . قال : وسمعت الشعبي يقول : هي بالخيار

IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r7.speaker: الربيع
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r7.claim: The verse was revealed after people declined to help someone who went around seeking witnesses; Qatada reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p562/r7.anchor: عن الربيع ، في قوله : ولا ياب الشهداء اذا ما دعوا قال : كان الرجل يطوف في القوم الكثير ، يدعوهم ليشهدهم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r1.claim: A needed Muslim may not refuse a summons either to give testimony about another witness or to provide testimony already in his possession; al-Hasan says the verse covers both situations.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قوله : ولا ياب الشهداء اذا ما دعوا يعني من احتيج اليه من المسلمين ، فشهد على شهادة أو كانت عنده شهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r2.claim: Do not grow tired of writing the debt.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ولا تسئموا يقول : لا تملوا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r3.claim: Debts of any size, small or large, are equally to be witnessed and written.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r3.anchor: عن مقاتل ، في قول الله : ولا تسئموا ان تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى اجله جمعت الصغير والكبير في الدين سواء

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r4.claim: Record small and large debts through their due dates because writing better preserves the due date and amount.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ان تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى اجله يعني يعني : ان تكتبوا قليل الحق وكثيره

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r5.claim: The demonstrative “that” refers to the written document.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : ذلكم يعني : الكتاب

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r6.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r6.claim: The prescribed documentation is more just before God; Saʿid ibn Jubayr and Sufyan agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r6.anchor: عن السدي في قوله : ذلكم اقسط عند الله يقول : اعدل عند الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r7.claim: The prescribed procedure is obedience to God.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r7.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : ذلكم اقسط عند الله يقوله : ذلكم طاعة الله

IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r8.claim: More upright for testimony means more accurate for testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p563/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : واقوم يعني : واصوب للشهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r1.speaker: سفيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r1.claim: More upright for testimony means more firmly established testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r1.anchor: عن سفيان ، في قوله : واقوم للشهادة قال : اثبت للشهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r2.claim: More likely to prevent doubt means more fitting to do so.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : وادنى الا ترتابوا يقول : واجدر

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r3.claim: Documentation prevents doubt about the right, due date, and testimony; al-Suddi and Sufyan specify avoiding doubt in testimony, while Muqatil links the clause to what is recorded.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : الا ترتابوا الا تشكوا في الحق والاجل والشهادة ، اذا كان مكتوبا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r4.claim: The phrase also means that documentation is more likely to prevent forgetting.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك ، في قوله : وادنى الا ترتابوا يقول اجدر الا تنسوا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r5.claim: An immediate transaction means an exchange conducted hand to hand.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : الا ان تكون تجارة حاضرة يعني : يدا بيد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r6.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r6.claim: An immediate transaction means one carried out locally, in the same town.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r6.anchor: عن السدى ، قوله : الا ان تكون تجارة حاضرة يقول : معكم بالبلد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r7.claim: A transaction circulated between the parties has no deferred term; Muqatil ibn Hayyan reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : تديرونها بينكم قال : ليس فيها اجل

IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r8.speaker: السدى
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r8.claim: The exemption from writing refers to transactions between people present in the same town.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p565/r8.anchor: عن السدى يعني قوله : فليس عليكم جناح الا تكتبوها يعني : الذين معكم بالبلد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r1.claim: No blame means no hardship or difficulty.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : فليس عليكم جناح يعني : حرج

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r2.claim: The exception from writing applies to immediate trade.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : الا تكتبوها يعني : التجارة الحاضرة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r3.claim: Witness all sales to protect one’s rights, whether payment is deferred or immediate; Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, ʿAta, and al-Dahhak agree.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : واشهدوا اذا تبايعتم يعني : اشهدوا على حقكم ، اذا كان فيه اجل ، أو لم يكن

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r4.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r4.claim: Al-Hasan says the command to witness sales was abrogated by the clause allowing trusted dealings; al-Shaʿbi reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r4.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله : واشهدوا اذا تبايعتم قال : نسختها فان امن بعضكم بعضا

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r5.claim: Do not pressure two people called to write or witness by demanding their help when they are occupied; many early authorities report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في هذه الاية ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد قال : ياتي الرجل الرجلين فيدعوهما إلى الكتاب والشهادة

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r6.claim: Harming a witness includes concealing or distorting testimony.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r6.anchor: قال : قال الحسن : ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد فيكتم الشهادة ، أو يحرف ، أو نحو هذا .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r7.speaker: عطاء
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r7.claim: A scribe or witness should deliver what is entrusted to them.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن عطاء في قوله : ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد قال : ان يؤديا ما قبلهما .

IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r8.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r8.speaker: أبيه
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r8.claim: The judge was to prevent people from abusing or insulting scribes and witnesses, in light of this command.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p566/r8.anchor: عن عثمان بن عطاء ، عن أبيه ، قال : وكان السلطان القاضي لا يترك رجلا يشتم رجل ولا يشتم شهيدا ،

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r1.claim: Do not harm the scribe by making him write what was not dictated, or the witness by making him testify to what was not requested; Zayd ibn Aslam agrees.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r1.anchor: عن قتادة ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد قال : لا يضار كاتب ، فيكتب مالم يمل عليه ، ولا شهيد ، فيشهد بما لم يستشهد

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r2.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r2.claim: Failing to follow God’s instructions in the debt verse is sin and disobedience; al-Dahhak reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r2.anchor: عن مقاتل بن حيان ، في قول الله : وان تفعلوا يقول : وان لم تفعلوا الذي امركم الله في آية الدين ، فانه اثم ومعصية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r3.claim: Harming the scribe or witness, or doing what was forbidden, is transgression; Ibn ʿAbbas reports similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : وان تفعلوا يعني : ان تضاروا الكاتب أو الشاهد ، أو ما نهيتم عنه فانه فسوق بكم

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r4.claim: Transgression means disobedience; Mujahid, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, ʿAta ibn Dinar, and al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : فانه فسوق بكم يعني بالفسوق : المعصية

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r5.claim: They are warned to fear God and not disobey Him in these matters.
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ثم خوفهم فقال : واتقوا الله ولا تعصوه فيهما

IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v2p567/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير ، في قول الله : والله بكل شيء عليم يعني : من اعمالكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r1.claim: Adding bi-dayn may be emphatic, or it may provide the noun resumed by write it; al-Zamakhshari says it also makes clear the distinction between deferred and immediate debts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r1.anchor: كما يقولون رأيته بعيني ولمسته بيدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r2.speaker: الطيبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r2.claim: Al-Tibi, quoting al-Raʾid, notes that tadāyun could figuratively mean making a promise, as in Ruʾba's line about a debt owed and partly delayed, so bi-dayn removes that ambiguity.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r3.claim: In Arabic, dayn is deferred consideration; specifying a fixed term prevents disputes and inserts the rule of deferred payment within the rule requiring documentation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r3.anchor: والدين في كلام العرب العوض المؤخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r4.claim: An ajl is a bounded period assigned to an activity not requiring immediate completion; ajl is a noun, taʾjīl its verbal noun, and the term also means delay, as at 2:234–235.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r4.anchor: والأجل مدة من الزمان محدودة النهاية مجعولة ظرفا لعمل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r5.claim: Musammā literally means named or distinguished; here it metaphorically means a determinate endpoint known to people, like the juristic phrase al-mahr al-musammā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p98/r5.anchor: والمسمى حقيقته المميز باسم يميزه عما يشابهه في جنسه أو نوعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r1.claim: The wording covers every debt, including loans and sales. Ibn ʿAbbas reports revelation about forward sale of produce, but the specific occasion does not restrict the verse's general scope.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أنها نزلت في السلم يعني بيع الثمار ونحوها من المثليات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r2.claim: The majority, including Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafiʿi, and Ahmad, treat writing as recommended; the trust exception in 2:283 completes that recommendation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r2.anchor: وهو قول الجمهور ومالكك وأبي حنيفة والشافعي وأحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj, al-Shaʿbi, ʿAta, al-Nakhaʿi, a report from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, Dawud, and al-Tabari hold that writing is obligatory; those requiring witnesses may also require writing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r3.anchor: قاله ابن جريج والشعبي وعطاء والنخعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r4.claim: He prefers obligation because commands normally bind and the verse reinforces this one; 2:283 is a specific permission when contracting parties trust each other, not a general repeal.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r4.anchor: والأرجح أن الأمر للوجوب فإنه الأصل في الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r5.claim: Documentation protects rights, prevents disputes, organizes communal dealings, and reveals invalid contracts; requiring it also lets a creditor ask for a written record without appearing distrustful.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p99/r5.anchor: والقصد من الأمر بالكتابة التوثق للحقوق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says documentation is recommended, not obligatory, because a person may freely relinquish the right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r1.anchor: الصحيح عدم الوجوب لأن للمرء أن يهب هذا الحق ويتركه بإجماع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s inference is unsound: securing evidence is a different situation from voluntarily giving away a right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r2.anchor: ولكنه مردود بأن مقام التوثق غير مقام التبرع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r3.claim: The law alerts right-holders against careless neglect and later regret, preserves trust between parties, eases a debtor’s resentment at documentation, and prevents disputes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r3.anchor: ومقصد الشريعة تنبيه أصحاب الحقوق حتى لا يتساهلوا ثم يندموا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r4.claim: Writing may be done by both contracting parties, or by one who gives the document to the other, when both can write; one party’s illiteracy undermines trust in the other’s handwriting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r4.anchor: حالة كتابة المتداينين بخطيهما أو خط أحدهما ويسلمه للآخر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r5.claim: If either party cannot write, a third party writes their agreement, two witnesses attest it, and the document goes to the creditor; this was the common Arab situation because literacy was scarce and localized.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r6.claim: At revelation, illiteracy was widespread among Arabs; writing was found in a few places and among only a small number in Mecca and Medina.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p100/r6.anchor: وإنما كانت الكتابة في الأنبار والحيرة وبعض جهات اليمن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r1.claim: The imperative to have a writer between the parties addresses the contracting parties, since most were unable to write; its surface direction to the writer is rhetorical emphasis on their arranging documentation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r1.anchor: أمر للمتداينين بأن يوسطوا كاتبا يكتب بينهم لأن غالب حالهم جهل الكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r2.claim: The request’s grammatical complement is the phrase between you, not the writer; the writer’s own commands are the prohibition on refusing and the following imperative to write.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r2.anchor: متعلق فعل الطلب هو ظرف بينكم وليس هذا أمرا للكاتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r3.claim: Here al-ʿadl means the right or truth, not the moral probity required of a witness, because the preposition bi rules out that sense.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r3.anchor: ليس العدل هنا بمعنى العدالة التي يوصف بها الشاهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r4.claim: Exegetes restrict the initial command to writing by a third-party scribe because that was usual and the next clause explains how to do it; the parties’ own writing is understood implicitly.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r4.anchor: على أن يكتبه كاتب غير المتداينين لأنه الغالب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r5.claim: The verse supports the majority’s acceptance of written handwriting as evidence, since commissioning a scribe only helps if his handwriting can later be read.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101/r5.anchor: ولذلك كانت الآية حجة عند جمهور العلماء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r1.claim: The ban on a scribe refusing a request is a separate rule directed to the scribe, not a repetition of the command directed to the contracting parties.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r1.anchor: نهي لمن تطلب منه الكتابة بين المتداينين عن الامتناع منها إذا دعي إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r2.speaker: الربيع
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ, Mujāhid, ʿAṭāʾ, and al-Ṭabarī hold that the ban is prohibitive, making acceptance an individual duty; the author endorses this as the sound view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r2.anchor: وهو قول الربيع ومجاهد وعطاء والطبري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan makes the duty individual only when there is one scribe locally; if there are others, it is communal, and all are blameworthy if they collude in refusing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول الحسن ، ومعناه أنه موكول إلى ديانتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r4.claim: The author considers it plausible that literate people in the debtor’s locality owe a communal duty, made individual for whichever person the creditor selects to secure the debt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r4.anchor: إنه واجب على الكفاية على من يعرف الكتابة من أهل مكان المتداينين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says a scribe is obliged to respond only when he is free.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنما يجب على الكاتب في حال فراغه ، قاله السدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk, with a report from ʿAṭāʾ, regards the scribe’s duty as abrogated by the ban on harming a scribe or witness; the author objects that writing is not ordinarily harm except in rare cases such as great distance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r6.anchor: وهو قول الضحاك ، وروي عن عطاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r7.speaker: الشعبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd say the rule was abrogated by the later permission to rely on mutual trust; the author says he will refute this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r7.anchor: وعن الشعبي وابن جريج وابن زيد أنه منسوخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r8.claim: Whether a fee may be charged for writing depends on whether the service is obligatory: obligatory writing permits no fee, while a nonobligatory service may be paid.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا الخلاف يختلف في جواز الأجر على الكتابة بين المتداينين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r9.claim: The documentation rule extends to all transactions for which parties seek written records and witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p101#2/r9.anchor: ويلحق بالتداين جميع المعاملات التي يطلب فيها التوثق بالكتابة والإشهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r1.claim: On the first reading, as God taught him means writing in exact correspondence with divine instruction, not approximately; kāf is an adverbial cognate or describes an omitted verbal noun, and mā is relative.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r1.anchor: أي كتابة تشابه الذي علمه الله أن يكتبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r2.claim: God’s instruction is truth rooted in human nature: a scribe must record honestly without injustice or evasion, since people depart from truth through desire and alteration.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r2.anchor: أنه يكتب ما يعتقده ولا يجحف أو يوارب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r3.claim: The author connects the duty of truthful writing with the Prophet’s instruction to consult one’s own conscience even when people give contrary advice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r3.anchor: وهذا يشير إليه قوله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r4.claim: Alternatively, kāf conveys reciprocal recompense: the literate person repays God’s gift of literacy by using it to preserve others’ rights and avoiding deceit or omission.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r4.anchor: أي أن يكتب كتابة تكافىء تعليم الله إياه الكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r5.claim: In that alternative, kāf functions as an adverbial cognate or adjective of an understood object, mā is a verbal noun, and the phrase may attach to an yaktub.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r5.anchor: والكاف على هذا إما نائبة عن المفعول المطلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows the phrase to attach instead to fal-yaktub; the author calls this a possible interpretive construction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p102/r6.anchor: وجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) تعليقه بقوله فليكتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r1.claim: Fal-yaktub follows from the refusal prohibition, restates fa-uktubūhu, and reinforces both the command and the ban; it is repeated to link naturally to the command that the debtor dictate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r1.anchor: وهو تصريح بمقتضى النهي وتكرير للأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r2.claim: Amalla is the Hijazi and Banū Asad form, while amlā is Tamīmī; the Qur’an uses both forms, and amalla is original with lām changed to yāʾ for ease.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r2.anchor: أمل وأملى لغتان : فالأولى لغة أهل الحجاز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r3.claim: The verb means conveying speech for someone to write, narrate, or memorize; restricting it to writing arose from focusing too narrowly on this verse, while al-Furqān confirms narration and memorization too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r3.anchor: ليكتب عنه أو ليروى أو ليحفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r4.claim: Al-ḥaqq here is the established due owed to the creditor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r4.anchor: والحق هنا ما حق أي ثبت للدائن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r5.claim: Witnesses must not insert conditions in a deed that the party did not dictate, unless the creditor delegated the details or showed the terms before contracting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r5.anchor: وفي هذا الأمر عبرة للشهود فإن منهم من يكتبون في شروط الحبس ونحوه ما لم يملله عليهم المشهود عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr takes both pronouns about fearing God and not reducing the amount to refer to the debtor, who must acknowledge the whole debt rather than shortchange the creditor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r6.anchor: قاله سعيد بن جبير ، وهو على هذا أمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r7.claim: The author rejects the debtor as antecedent: the creditor is present and could object to omission, so the two pronouns more plausibly refer to the scribe, who might overlook dictated details.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p103/r7.anchor: وعندي أن هذا بعيد إذ لا فائدة بهذه الوصاية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.claim: Safīh means cognitively impaired, ḍaʿīf means a minor, and one unable to dictate is incapacitated, such as someone simultaneously mute, blind, and deaf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r1.anchor: والذي لا يستطيع أن يمل هو العاجز كمن به بكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.claim: The explicit pronoun in the phrase about inability prepares for the guardian’s command, showing disability does not remove the requirement to document what the person borrows.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r2.anchor: لئلا يتوهم الناس أن عجزه يسقط عنه واجب الإشهاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.claim: In pre-Islamic and early Islamic practice a guardian could be a senior relative, father, trustee, or tribal notable; the Prophet told Hawāzin’s delegation to bring their ʿurafāʾ to present their case.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r3.anchor: وكان الأولياء قبل الإسلام وفي صدره كبراء القرابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.claim: In the Hawāzin delegation report, the Prophet directs them to bring their tribal representatives to him, illustrating the early role of ʿurafāʾ in tribal affairs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r4.anchor: قال لهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ( ليرفع إلي عرفاؤكم أمركم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.claim: The guardian’s declaration in the ward’s interest is valid when its basis is apparent; later jurists set it aside as a precaution against collusion that wastes vulnerable people’s property.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p104#2/r5.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن إقرار الوصي والمقدم في حق المولى عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r1.claim: The command to witness is additional to writing: writing preserves the contract’s wording and conditions against forgetfulness; jurists call it remembrance of the right and also a contract.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r1.anchor: وهو غيره وليس بيانا له إذ لو كان بيانا لما اقترن بالواو

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r2.speaker: الحارث بن حلزة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r2.claim: Al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza’s verse illustrates the written record as something preserved on parchment against later whims and injustice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r2.anchor: قال الحارث بن حلزة : حذر الجور والتطاخي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.claim: The next verse gives pledge as the alternative when a writer cannot be found, without making unwritten testimony an intermediate option; thus a writer may also be one of the witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r3.anchor: فلم يجعل بين فقدان الكاتب وبين الرهن درجة وهي الشهادة بلا كتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r4.claim: The verse names one scribe and two witnesses because people who are both literate and qualified to witness are uncommon.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105/r4.anchor: وإنما جعل القرآن كاتبا وشاهدين لندرة الجمع بين معرفة الكتابة وأهلية الشهادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r1.claim: Istashhidū can mean simply have witnesses, with the s and t adding emphasis, or request two witnesses, making the creditor responsible for seeking testimony.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r2.claim: The creditor’s request is within a person’s capacity; the following ban on refusing then addresses the person asked to witness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r2.anchor: تكليفا لمن يطلب منه صاحب الحق أن يشهد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r3.claim: Shahāda literally means presence and observation; here it means attending to observe a debt, while elsewhere it means testimony offered to establish a disputed claim, as in the four-witness rule.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r3.anchor: والشهادة حقيقتها الحضور والمشاهدة ، والمراد بها هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r4.speaker: جمهور السلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r4.claim: The majority of early authorities interpret the command to obtain two witnesses as obligatory.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r4.anchor: قيل للوجوب ، وهو قول جمهور السلف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r5.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r5.claim: The later majority of jurists, including Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad, regard witnessing as recommended; the discussion continues at the command to witness sales.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p105#2/r5.anchor: قيل للندب ، وهو قول جمهور الفقهاء المتأخرين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r1.claim: Men among you means adult Muslim men: the address is to believers, minors lack judgment to assess the circumstances and suspicions, and the wording of rijāl itself excludes women and boys.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r1.anchor: أي من رجال المسلمين ، فحصل به شرطان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r2.claim: The author argues non-Muslims are excluded because religious difference prevents familiarity with one another’s integrity and duties; earlier religious communities did not clearly guarantee equal rights to outsiders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r2.anchor: فكيف نعتد بشهادة هؤلاء الذين يرون المسلمين مارقين عن دين الحق مناوئين لهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r3.claim: The Qur’an alludes to non-Muslims’ asserted exemption from obligations toward the unlettered, as a reason not to rely on their testimony for Muslims.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r4.claim: In the Khaybar killing report, the Prophet asked the Ansar for proof, then proposed that the Jews swear fifty oaths; the Ansar feared they would kill them and swear, so he paid the blood-money from charity funds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r4.anchor: فانطلقوا إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فشكوا إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r5.claim: The author takes the report as confirming the Ansar’s claim that the Jews would not hesitate to kill them all and swear falsely.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p106/r5.anchor: فقد أقر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قول الأنصار في اليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r1.claim: Two witnesses are the stipulated number for financial transactions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r1.anchor: والعدد هو اثنان في المعاملات المالية كما هنا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r2.claim: The condition means that if two men are not present at the transaction, one man and two women may testify; the answer clause is elliptical, understood from the command to obtain witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r2.anchor: لم يحضر المعاملة رجلان بل حضر رجل واحد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r3.claim: The incomplete kāna avoids implying that women count only when two men are impossible, contrary to the majority; it also brings women into public affairs after their exclusion in pre-Islamic practice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r3.anchor: لئلا يتوهم منه أن شهادة المرأتين لا تقبل إلا عند تعذر الرجلين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r4.claim: The two women provide a safeguard against confusion or forgetting, which the author describes as more common among women by ordinary disposition; ḍalāl here means forgetfulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p108/r4.anchor: وهذه حيطة أخرى من تحريف الشهادة وهي خشية الاشتباه والنسيان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r1.claim: The majority read an tadhilla with fatḥa, supplying a causal lām; the cause explains the pairing of women, and they read fa-tudhakkira in the subjunctive as coordinated with an tadhilla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r1.anchor: قرأه الجمهور بفتح همزة أن على أنه محذوف منه لام التعليل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads in tadhilla with kasra as a conditional, and raises tadhakkiru as the predicate of an omitted subject after fa; the author compares this syntax with Qur’an 5:95.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r2.anchor: على اعتبار إن شرطية وتضل فعل الشرط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r3.claim: Although the wording appears to make forgetting the cause, the practical aim is preventing loss of the testimony; remembering is the consequence that completes the causal explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r3.anchor: بل العلة هي ما يترتب على الضلال من إضاعة المشهود به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains the wording as stressing reminder so strongly that the sentence names its enabling cause, comparing prepared timber to brace a leaning wall and weapons to repel an enemy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r4.anchor: ووجهه صاحب ( الكشاف ) بأن فيه دلالة على الاهتمام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r5.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r5.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib proposes that Arabic places the cause of a cause first and joins the actual cause with fa, a rule he presents as characteristic of the language.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p109/r5.anchor: أن من شأن لغة العرب إذا ذكروا علة وكان للعلة علة قدموا ذكر علة العلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r1.claim: The author prefers a compound-cause account: the wording concisely expresses both avoiding loss when one woman forgets and gaining the benefit of the second woman’s reminder, better than al-Zamakhsharī’s account.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r1.anchor: وهذا أحسن مما ذكره صاحب ( الكشاف )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r2.claim: Repeating one of them instead of a pronoun lets either woman be subject or object without changing the meaning; an implicit pronoun would still have an unambiguous antecedent despite its different grammatical role.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r2.anchor: فلو أضمر للإحدى ضمير المفعول لكان المعاد واضحا سواء كان قوله إحداهما المظهر فاعلا أو مفعولا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r3.speaker: التفتازاني
