IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r3.claim: Al-Taftāzānī notes that the repetition is not an ordinary replacement of a pronoun because the woman who reminds is not the forgetful one, and asks for the rhetorical reason.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r3.anchor: ومما ينبغي أن يتعرض له وجه تكرير لفظ إحداهما

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r4.speaker: العصام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r4.claim: Al-ʿIṣām explains that the cause clause was fronted, preventing a pronoun and preventing the use of al-ukhrā before its counterpart had been named.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p110/r4.anchor: فلما قدم إن ضلت وأبرز في معرض العلة لم يصح الإضمار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r1.speaker: الخفاجي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r1.claim: Al-Khafājī says the repetition conveys generality: either woman may forget or remind, so neither is merely a secondary reminder rather than a witness in her own right.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r1.anchor: النكتة الإبهام لأن كل واحدة من المرأتين يجوز عليها ما يجوز على صاحبتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r2.speaker: شهاب الدين الغزنوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r2.claim: Al-Ghaznawī answers al-Khafājī’s question in verse: because the statement could refer to either woman, a pronoun would wrongly identify one particular woman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r2.anchor: تضل إحداهما فالقول محتمل كليهما فهي للإظهار مفتقره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r3.speaker: أبو القاسم المغربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r3.claim: Abū al-Qāsim al-Maghribī reads the first one as one of the two testimonies and takes ḍalāl as loss through forgetting, then assigns the second one to a woman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r3.anchor: إذ جعل إحداهما الأول مرادا به إحدى الشهادتين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r4.claim: The author rejects al-Maghribī’s interpretation as unsupported and contrived because it shifts the referents of the repeated expressions and scatters the pronouns.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r4.anchor: وهو تكلف وتشتيت للضمائر لا دليل عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r5.claim: The author says repetition makes each clause stand alone like a maxim: forgetting explains why one woman is insufficient, and the second woman can keep the first woman’s testimony from failing altogether.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p111/r5.anchor: قصد استقلال الجملة بمدلولها كيلا تحتاج إلى كلام آخر فيه معاد الضمير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r1.claim: The ban on refusing witnesses follows the command to the parties to seek them and ensures that the person asked will agree to attend.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r1.anchor: لما أمر المتعاقدين باستشهاد شاهدين نهى من يطلب إشهاده عن أن يأبى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r2.claim: The parties are commanded because they may neglect to secure witnesses, while witnesses are forbidden because they may refuse; each rule addresses the likely lapse and implies its opposite.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r2.anchor: فإن المتعاقدين يظن بهما إهمال الإشهاد فأمرا به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r3.claim: Those invited are called witnesses in anticipation: their invitation itself signals that they are already committed to accept the witnessing role.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r3.anchor: وتسمية المدعوين شهداء باعتبار الأول القريبب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r4.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ ibn Sulaymān, and a report from Ibn ʿAbbās understand the omitted object as being called to bear witness at the transaction; refusing to bear it is forbidden all the more.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r4.anchor: أي إذا ما دعوا إلى الشهادة أي التحمل ، وهذا قول قتادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r5.speaker: الحسن
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan, with a report from Ibn ʿAbbās, understands the invitation to include both bearing witness and later giving testimony.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r5.anchor: والأداء معا ؛ قاله الحسن ، وابن عباس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r6.claim: Mujāhid limits the invitation to giving testimony; the author notes his rationale that invitees are not truly witnesses until they have borne witness, but considers it weakened by the next verse’s ban on concealing testimony.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد : إذا ما دعوا إلى الأداء خاصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r7.claim: The author takes the omitted object broadly: people may be called both to witness the transaction and to give testimony when proof is later needed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r7.anchor: لإفادة شمول ما يدعون لأجله في التعاقد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r8.speaker: ابن الحاجب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r8.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib says bearing witness is a communal duty when needed, while giving testimony from a distance of two barīd is an individual duty and cannot be replaced by an oath.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r8.anchor: والتحمل حيث يفتقر إليه فرض كفاية والأداء من نحو البريدين إن كانا اثنين فرض عين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r9.claim: The author applies the earlier disagreement about scribes: accepting the request to bear witness becomes individual when designated, and giving testimony is individually obligatory if it causes no bodily or financial harm; Abū Ḥanīfa makes performance communal unless uniquely required, subject to court integrity, proximity, admissibility, and a claimant’s request.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r9.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة الأداء فرض كفاية إلا إذا تعين عليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r10.claim: The author objects to making testimony depend on each witness’s own varying judgments about these conditions, calling that a door to excessive legal qualification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p112/r10.anchor: وفي هذه التعليقات رد بالشهادة إلى مختلف اجتهادات الشهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r1.claim: The small and large debts represent trivial and substantial amounts; since small transactions are more frequent, parties are told not to tire of recording them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r1.anchor: تعميم في أكوان أو أحوال الديون المأمور بكتابتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r2.claim: The address primarily concerns contracting parties and by implication includes the scribe, who must write when they request it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r2.anchor: والخطاب للمتداينين أصالة ، ويستتبع ذلك خطاب الكاتب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r3.claim: The prohibition concerns the result of weariness—leaving the debt unwritten—because involuntary boredom itself cannot be prohibited.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r3.anchor: لأن السآمة تحصل للنفس من غير اختيار

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r4.claim: Another interpretation takes sāmah as a figurative expression for laziness and laxity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r4.anchor: وقيل السآمة هنا كناية عن الكسل والتهاون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r5.claim: Ṣaghīran aw kabīran is parsed either as a circumstantial accusative describing the debt or as a phrase with kāna and its subject omitted.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r5.anchor: وانتصب صغيرا أو كبيرا على الحال من الضمير المنصوب بتكتبوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r6.claim: Small precedes large, unlike the expected order, to emphasize complete coverage, since small debts are more frequent and might be neglected, while mentioning only small debts could imply large ones need no writing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114/r7.claim: Ilā ajalihi is circumstantial: the record must specify the debt up to the agreed term.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r1.claim: Writing is more just because it better preserves the right, supports giving testimony, and reduces doubt; these three reasons make evidence clear and free of suspicion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r1.anchor: أقوم للشهادة ، أي أعون على إقامتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r2.claim: The demonstrative points to the preceding documentation rules collectively, and the verse supports grounding one legal ruling in several reasons.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r2.anchor: واسم الإشارة عائد إلى جميع ما تقدم باعتبار أنه مذكور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r3.claim: Aqsatu derives from the quadriliteral aqsaṭa, meaning to act justly, not from qaṣaṭa, meaning to act unjustly; aqwamu derives from aqāma al-shahāda.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r3.anchor: من أقسط بمعنى عدل ، وهو رباعي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r4.claim: Al-Sībawayh permits comparative forms from hamzated quadriliteral verbs, whether the hamza makes a verb transitive or not; al-Zamakhsharī alternatively analyzes aqsatu as a nisba form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r4.anchor: جار على قول سيبويه بجواز صوغ التفضيل والتعجب من الرباعي المهموز

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives aqsatu from qāsiṭ, meaning possessing a share of justice; the author finds the pattern and derivation from a noun problematic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r5.anchor: وجوز صاحب ( الكشاف ) أن يكون أقسط مشتقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r6.claim: The author answers that a nisba from a verbal noun resembles a derivative because the verbal noun is the origin of derivation, and suggests aqwamu may also come from qawuma and yield the adjective qawīm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p114#2/r6.anchor: والجواب عندي أن النسب هنا لما كان إلى المصدر شابه المشتق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r1.claim: The immediate-trade exception qualifies the general range of transactions; it may be a disconnected exception because an immediate cash sale is not a debt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r1.anchor: لأن التجارة الحاضرة ليست من الدين في شيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r2.claim: Ḥāḍirah means immediate, without delay; ḥāḍir, ʿājil, and nājiz are synonyms, as are debt, term, and deferred payment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r2.anchor: والحاضرة الناجزة ، التي لا تأخير فيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r3.claim: Tudīrūnahā baynakum explains the immediate trade and likely indicates why writing is dispensable: the parties’ exchange itself makes the transaction evident.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r3.anchor: ولعل فائدة ذكره الإيماء إلى تعليل الرخصة في ترك الكتابة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats tudīrūnahā as an explanation of trade, like the poet’s explanation of two needs by asking how they can meet; it may also be a second descriptive phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r4.anchor: جعل صاحب ( الكشاف ) كيف يلتقيان بيانا لحاجة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r5.claim: The connected-exception reading takes immediate trade to mean a debt due soon and exempts that debt from writing, but the author considers this remote.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p115/r5.anchor: والمراد بالتجارة الحاضرة المؤجلة إلى أجل قريب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r1.claim: The explicit statement that there is no blame restates the exception and signals a concession; writing nevertheless remains preferable.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r1.anchor: من الإشارة إلى أن هذا الحكم رخصة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r2.claim: Most readers vocalize tijāratun as nominative with kāna complete; ʿĀṣim reads it accusative with kāna incomplete and an understood noun repeated as predicate.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور تجارة بالرفع : على أن تكون تامة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r3.speaker: سيبويه
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r3.claim: Al-Sībawayh cites ʿAmr ibn Shās’s verse with an implied repeated subject and predicate as a parallel for the incomplete-kāna reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r3.anchor: كما في قول عمرو بن شاس أنشده سيبويه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r4.claim: The written form allā is contracted from an lā.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r5.claim: Witnesses are also required for a sale without debt when it is not ordinary immediate commerce, completing the categories of debt, credit sales, immediate trade, and immediate noncommercial sales.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r5.anchor: تشريع للإشهاد عند البيع ولو بغير دين إذا كان البيع غير تجارة حاضرة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r6.claim: Reading the command as only referring to immediate trade and retaining witnesses without writing is very unlikely, since writing was instituted to support witnessing and documentation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116/r6.anchor: لأن الكتابة ما شرعت إلا لأجل الإشهاد والتوثق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r1.claim: Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, Abū Saʿīd, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn Jurayj, al-Nakhaʿī, Jābir ibn Zayd, Dāwūd, and al-Ṭabarī take witnessing at sales as obligatory.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.claim: The Prophet had a sale witnessed and wrote a document for al-ʿAdāʾ ibn Khālid describing the purchased slave as free of defects and prohibited liabilities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r2.anchor: وقد أشهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على بيع عبد باعه للعداء بن خالد بن هوذة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī, followed by Mālik, Abū Ḥanīfa, al-Shāfiʿī, and Aḥmad, regard witnessing as recommended; they cite the Prophet’s sales without witnesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r3.anchor: وهو قول مالك ، وأبي حنيفة ، والشافعي ، وأحمد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p116#2/r4.claim: The author answers the argument from unwitnessed sales by limiting those cases to contexts of mutual trust and refers to the following trust provision; he also rejects Ibn ʿAṭiyya’s earlier rationale.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r1.claim: The verb yaḍārr can be active or passive, allowing the ban to cover either scribes and witnesses harming the parties or the parties harming them; the wording deliberately carries both compatible rules.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r1.anchor: لأن يضار يحتمل البناء للمعلوم وللمجهول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r2.claim: Harm includes parties burdening a scribe or witness with hardship, loss, or exposure to punishment, and witnesses causing a party to lose a right or suffer the burden of answering.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r2.anchor: إدخال الضر بأن يوقع المتعاقدان الشاهدين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r3.claim: The verse grounds procedural protections: avoid distant travel and destabilizing questioning after long delays; public funds should cover witnesses’ travel, lodging, and resulting family losses to support justice.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p117/r3.anchor: أنه ينبغي لولاة الأمور جعل جانب من مال بيت المال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r1.claim: The omitted object of do refers to causing the prohibited harm; fusūq means grave sin, as in the denunciation of the term after faith.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r2.claim: The command to fear God presents piety as the basis of good conduct and abstention from wrongdoing; the teaching clause recalls Islam’s gift of knowledge of law and the order of life, and its present tense suggests its continuance.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r2.anchor: أمر بالتقوى لأنها ملاك الخير ، وبها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r3.claim: Some take the conjunction in wayuʿallimukumu Allāh causally, as meaning that God teaches because of piety; the author rejects treating this as a special grammatical meaning of wāw.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r3.anchor: إن الواو فيه للتعليل أي ليعلمكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r4.claim: Repeating the divine name across three clauses gives each independent force, so hearing one without another still conveys its point; it also creates awe.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r4.anchor: لقصد التنويه بكل جملة منها حتى تكون مستقلة الدلالة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r5.claim: A poem in al-Ḥamāsa repeats al-luʾm in three lines to censure a tribe and its descendants, illustrating deliberate repetition; al-Jurjānī says taste can discern rhetorical effects that resist explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v3p118/r5.anchor: قول الحماسي : اللؤم أكرم من وبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt-documentation verse was revealed specifically concerning forward sales (salam); Ibn ʿAṭiyya says such sales in Medina occasioned it, but the rule covers all debts by consensus.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه نزلت هذه الآية في السلم خاصة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r2.claim: Adding “with a debt” disambiguates tadaayantum, since Arabic can use it for mutual repayment; an expressly specified term rules out an unknown maturity date.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r2.anchor: ووصفه الأجل بمسمى دليل على أن المجهلة لا تجوز

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r3.speaker: الربيع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says documentation was initially made obligatory by the command, then lightened by the trust exception in 2:283.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r4.speaker: الشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r4.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, Ibn Jurayj, and Ibn Zayd report the view that “if one of you trusts another” abrogates the documentation command; a report attributes the position to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r5.speaker: جمهور العلماء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r5.claim: Most scholars treat writing as recommended protection of property and removal of doubt; it does not harm a pious debtor and protects the creditor against an unreliable one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r5.anchor: الأمر بالكتب ندب إلى حفظ الأموال وإزالة الريب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r6.claim: The sound view is that witnessing makes a transaction prudent while mutual trust leaves room; no abrogation follows, because documentation is recommended as a precaution for rights people may waive, and 2:283 instructs debtors to repay when trusted.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r7.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī treats documentation as obligatory and argues that commands remain obligatory until evidence shows otherwise.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p378/r7.anchor: ذهب إلى أن الأمر بالكتب فرض واجب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r1.speaker: عطاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and others say “let a scribe write” makes writing obligatory on the scribe; al-Shaʿbī and ʿAṭāʾ also specify that this applies when he is the only available scribe, while al-Suddī says it applies when he is free.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r2.claim: “With justice” modifies the act of writing, not the noun “scribe”; a child, slave, or disfavored person can draft a sound document, though officials should use upright, trusted, knowledgeable document writers.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r3.speaker: مالك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r3.claim: Mālik says only someone knowledgeable about documents, personally upright and trusted, should write them, citing the command to write justly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r3.anchor: لا يكتب الوثائق من الناس إلا عارف بها عدل في نفسه مأمون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r4.claim: The verb abā yaʾbā is irregular: among verbs with a fatḥa in the imperfect, this pattern normally occurs only when a guttural letter is involved; al-Zajjāj says the hamza resembles one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r4.anchor: قال الزجاج والقول في أبى أن الألف فيه أشبهت الهمزة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r5.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r5.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk, as transmitted by al-Mahdawī, say the prohibition on a scribe refusing was abrogated by the command not to cause harm in 2:282.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r5.anchor: أن قوله ولا يأب منسوخ بقوله لا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r6.claim: As Allah taught him can attach to “write” as the manner of writing, to “not refuse” as a reason to repay God's gift, or begin a new sentence that attaches to “let him write.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r6.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون كما متعلقة بما في قوله ولا يأب من المعنى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p379/r7.claim: No particular scribe must write if another is available, and he may decline unless hired; if none is available, an exhortatory duty falls on the present person. Documentation in general is recommended, like doing good in 22:77, and helps someone in need.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.claim: Because documentation can be burdensome, God removes blame for leaving immediate cash transactions unwritten; such dealings are usually small purchases rather than property. Al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk define them as immediate hand-to-hand exchange.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r1.anchor: هذا فيما كان يدا بيد تأخذ وتعطي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.claim: An is accusative as a disconnected exception. “You turn it over between yourselves” implies possession transfers; land, houses, and much livestock cannot be handed over cleanly in the same way, so debt-like documentation suits them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r2.anchor: تديرونها بينكم يقتضي التقابض والبينونة بالمقبوض

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.speaker: عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r3.claim: ʿĀṣim reads tijāratan in the accusative; the other readers read it in the nominative, though Abū ʿAlī is unsure about Ibn ʿĀmir.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.claim: With nominative, kāna means “occur” and needs no predicate; with accusative, its event sense is absent and an omitted subject or predicate is supplied, such as “unless the transaction is a trade.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p383#2/r4.anchor: فحجة من رفع تجارة إن كان بمعنى حدث ووقع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r1.speaker: أبو علي والمبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r1.claim: Abū ʿAlī and al-Mubarrad transmit a poetic line with “if it were an awful day” using accusative yawm; al-Ṭabarī's variant has nominative, as does Sībawayh's version.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r1.anchor: وأنشده سيبويه بالرفع إذا كان يوم ذو كواكب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r2.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī interprets “witness when you transact” as applying to transactions both small and large.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r3.speaker: الحسن والشعبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Shaʿbī, and others say witnessing a transaction is recommended; Ibn ʿAmr and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say it is obligatory, followed by Ibn ʿUmar's practice and ʿAṭāʾ, with al-Ṭabarī preferring obligation.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds obligation untenable: witnessing tiny sales is burdensome, while larger dealings may rely on social trust or customary practice. He prefers recommendation unless an excuse prevents it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r4.anchor: والوجوب في ذلك قلق أما في الدقائق فصعب شاق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r5.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r5.claim: Some say witnessing is abrogated by the trust exception in 2:283; al-Mahdawī records this view and Makkī attributes it to Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r5.anchor: وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم منسوخ بقوله فإن أمن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r6.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r6.claim: They say “do not harm a scribe or witness” prohibits a writer from adding to or subtracting from what was dictated and a witness from altering testimony; Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ also understand it to prohibit their refusal.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r6.anchor: ولا يضار الكاتب بأن يكتب ما لم يمل عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك والسدي وطاوس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r7.claim: They say a claimant harms a scribe or witness by demanding work when that person is busy or excused, then shaming him for refusing; the word's reciprocal sense encompasses these readings and the preceding ones.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p384/r7.anchor: بأن يؤذيه طالب الكتبة أو الشهادة فيقول اكتب لي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r1.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود ومجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r1.claim: They read the verb with the letters separated and the first rāʾ fatḥa, meaning a claimant may initiate harm to the scribe or witness; al-Ṭabarī reports and explains this reading accordingly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r1.anchor: كانوا يقرؤون «ولا يضارر» بالفك وفتح الراء الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r2.claim: Al-Dānī reports both kasra and fatḥa for the first rāʾ from ʿUmar, Ibn ʿAbbās, Ibn Abī Isḥāq, and Mujāhid; separating the consonants is Ḥijāzī usage, while assimilation is Tamīmī.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r2.anchor: وفك الفعل هي لغة أهل الحجاز والإدغام لغة تميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع وعمرو بن عبيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r3.claim: They read the geminated rāʾ with sukūn in the jussive; Abū al-Fatḥ calls it questionable but explains it as treating connected speech like a pause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع وعمرو بن عبيد «ولا يضار» بجزم الراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r4.speaker: عكرمة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r4.claim: ʿIkrima reads the first rāʾ with kasra and makes “scribe” and “witness” accusative, so that the rights-holder is forbidden to begin harming them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r4.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة «ولا يضارر» بكسر الراء الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r5.speaker: ابن محيصن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r5.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin reads the geminated verb with rafʿ; after Ibn Mujāhid questions it, Abū al-Fatḥ explains it as a negative statement meaning the scribe ought not to be harmed, supported by poetry. Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds it close to the earlier analysis.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r6.claim: If harm means falsification by a writer or witness, fisq is the legal commission of grave sins and invalidating rights; if it means mistreatment or refusal, fisq means departing from what is right, though disobeying God's command approaches the legal sense too.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r6.anchor: فالفسوق على عرفه في الشرع وهو مواقعة الكبائر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r7.claim: Bikum implies “a state of fisq upon you”; the close of the verse admonishes and recounts God's favor, and another interpretation promises that piety teaches a person what is good.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p385/r7.anchor: وقيل إن معنى الآية الوعد بأن من اتقى علم الخير وألهمه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj says dāyantu means transacting with someone by taking a loan from him or lending to him; a cited line about Arwa illustrates settling debts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r1.anchor: يقال داينت الرجل إذا عاملته فأخذت منه بدين وأعطيته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r2.claim: The command concerns a debt due at a specified term and requires writing and witnesses to protect property and people from injustice; documented proof restrains a debtor’s temptation to deny it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r2.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى بكتابة الدين وبالإشهاد حفظا منه للأموال وللناس من الظلم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, an advance-purchase transaction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r3.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في السلم خاصة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari distinguishes tadāyantum for dealing, selling, or lending from dayn for recompense; the latter is pronounced with kasra, as in 51:12, and a cited poem illustrates recompense.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r4.anchor: تداينتم يقع على معنيين أحدهما المشاراة والمبايعة والإقراض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r5.claim: Al-ʿadl means what is right; Qatada says to omit no rightful due and add nothing false.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p336/r5.anchor: فأما العدل فهو الحق قال قتادة لا تدعن حقا ولا تزيدن باطلا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r1.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says a scribe must not refuse to write as God taught him the skill of writing; al-Shaʿbi calls writing a communal duty like jihad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r1.anchor: كما علمه الله الكتابة قاله سعيد بن جبير وقال الشعبي الكتابة فرض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r2.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj instead understands “as God taught him” to mean writing according to God’s command and truth.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r2.anchor: كما أمره الله به الحق قاله الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says the person owing the debt must dictate what he owes the claimant to the scribe and must not reduce any part of it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r3.anchor: يعني المطلوب يقول ليمل ما عليه من حق الطالب على الكاتب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r4.claim: Amalla and amlā are two forms for dictating; the former is associated with the claimant repeating the statement at length.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r4.anchor: يقال أمللت أمل وأمليت أملي لغتان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r5.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr define the “foolish” debtor as ignorant about property and unable to dictate.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r5.anchor: الجاهل بالأموال والجاهل بالإملاء قاله مجاهد وابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the foolish debtor is a child or a woman.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r7.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r7.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi identify the foolish debtor as a minor.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r8.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says foolish here means someone who squanders money.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r8.anchor: أنه المبذر قاله القاضي أبو يعلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn Jubayr explain “weak” as incapacitated, mute, or mentally unsound.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r9.anchor: أنه العاجر والأخرس ومن به حمق قاله ابن عباس وابن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r10.claim: Mujahid and al-Suddi say “weak” means a fool.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r11.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r11.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla gives “minor” as a third meaning of weak.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337/r11.anchor: أنه الصغير قاله القاضي أبو يعلى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the debtor cannot dictate because he is slow or tongue-tied; Ibn Jubayr says he cannot properly dictate what he owes, while Qadi Abu Yaʿla says he is insane.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r1.anchor: لا يستطيع لعيه وقال ابن جبير لا يحسن أن يمل ما عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and Ibn Qutayba say the guardian is the creditor’s guardian, meaning the holder of the right.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r2.anchor: أنها تعود إلى الحق فتقديره فليملل ولي الحق هذا قول ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r3.claim: Al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd say the pronoun refers to the debtor, so his guardian dictates.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r3.anchor: أنها تعود إلى الذي عليه الحق وهذا قول الضحاك وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the debtor’s guardian: accepting the claimant’s dictation would leave no reason for writing and witnesses, and would simply accept the claimant’s word; Qadi Abu Yaʿla agrees.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r4.anchor: واختاره الزجاج وعاب قول الأولين فقال كيف يقبل قول المدعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r6.claim: Mujahid says “your men” means free men.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj and Qadi Abu Yaʿla take “your men” to mean Muslims, supported by the verse’s opening address to believers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p337#2/r7.anchor: والثاني أهل الإسلام وهذا اختيار الزجاج والقاضي أبي يعلى ويدل عليه أنه خاطب المؤمنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r1.claim: “If the two are not men” means if the two witnesses are not both men, not if two men cannot be found.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r1.anchor: أراد فان لم يكن الشهيدان رجلين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says witnesses “whom you approve” are people of merit and religious integrity.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the construction means appoint two women so that one may remind the other, or for that purpose.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r3.anchor: معناه استشهدوا امرأتين لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى ومن أجل أن تذكر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r4.claim: Hamza reads in tadhilla with kasra; here dalāl means forgetfulness, according to Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, Muqatil, and others.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة إن تضل بكسر الألف والضلال هاهنا النسيان قاله ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read fatudhakkira with a light kaf and accusative ra; Hamza reads it with a doubled kaf and nominative ra; the rest use doubled kaf and accusative ra.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r5.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير و أبو عمرو بالتخفيف مع نصب الراء وقرأ حمزة بالرفع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r6.claim: The majority take the light and doubled readings alike: the second woman recalls the matter after the first forgets.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r6.anchor: أنها بمعنى المشددة أيضا وهذا قول الجمهور قال الضحاك والربيع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r7.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r7.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna and al-Asmaʿi’s report from Abu ʿAmr take the light reading to make two women’s testimony equivalent to one man’s; Qadi Abu Yaʿla prefers this.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r7.anchor: أنها بمعنى تجعل شهادتهما بمنزلة شهادة ذكر وهذا مذهب سفيان بن عيينة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r8.speaker: أبو علي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r8.claim: Abu ʿAli rejects Ibn ʿUyayna’s view: no number of women’s testimony suffices without a man, and forgetfulness should be answered by a reminder.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p338/r8.anchor: ليس مذهب ابن عيينة بالقوي لأنهن لو بلغن ما بلغن لم تجز شاهدتهن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r1.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r1.claim: Qatada says the verse followed an incident where a man called around a large tented gathering for witnesses and no one came.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r1.anchor: كان الرجل يطوف في الحواء العظيم فيه القوم فيدعوهم إلى الشهادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, ʿAtiyya, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ say witnesses are called to bear testimony and have it recorded.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r2.anchor: إلى تحمل الشهادة و إثباتها في الكتاب قاله ابن عباس وعطية وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Tawus, Mujahid, and others say the call is to perform testimony before judges after first bearing it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r3.anchor: إلى إقامتها وأدائها عند الحكام بعد أن تقدمت شهادتهم بها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r4.claim: A third view, reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan and preferred by al-Zajjaj, includes both bearing and performing testimony.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r4.anchor: والثالث إلى تحملها و إلى أدائها روي عن ابن عباس والحسن واختاره الزجاج

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو يعلى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r5.claim: Qadi Abu Yaʿla says a witness must attend to perform testimony only if no one else can testify; both bearing and performing it are communal duties like jihad.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339/r5.anchor: إنما يلزم الشاهد أن لا يأبى إذا دعي لإقامة الشهادة إذا لم يوجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r1.claim: Do not grow weary of recording small or large debts customarily deferred, through their due date; the document is more just, strengthens testimony by reminding witnesses, and more nearly removes doubt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r1.anchor: أي لا تملوا وتضجروا أن تكتبوا القليل والكثير الذي قد جرت العادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r2.claim: The exception is an immediate exchange in which each party must deliver what it contracted for at once; ʿAsim reads tijāratan in the accusative, treating the funds as the commerce, and writing is waived to avoid burden in ordinary purchases.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r2.anchor: وهي البيوع التي يستحق كل واحد منهما على صاحبه تسليم ما عقد عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r3.claim: Witnessing is recommended for transactions where it is customary.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r3.anchor: الإشهاد مندوب إليه فيما جرت العادة بالإشهاد عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r4.claim: The majority treat writing debts and witnessing sales or debts as recommended, so the command remains operative without abrogation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r4.anchor: فذهب الجمهور إلى أنه أمر ندب واستحباب فعلى هذا هو محكم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r5.claim: A group including Ibn ʿUmar, Abu Musa, Mujahid, Ibn Sirin, and others regard writing and witnessing as obligatory.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r5.anchor: روي عن ابن عمر وابي موسى و مجاهد وابن سيرين وعطاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r6.claim: Among those who require it, most say the ruling remains, while others say it was abrogated by the trust verse at 2:283.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p339#2/r6.anchor: فذهب أكثرهم إلى أنه محكم غير منسوخ وذهبت طائفة إلى أنه منسوخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads yuḍār with a light ra and sukun.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r1.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر بتخفيف الراء من يضار وسكونها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, al-Suddi, al-Rabiʿ, al-Farra, and Muqatil say a scribe or witness must not be burdened with a summons while busy; al-Rabiʿ describes a requester insisting despite an available alternative.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r2.anchor: أن معناه لا يضار بأن يدعي وهو مشغول هذا قول ابن عباس و مجاهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r3.claim: Al-Hasan, Tawus, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd say the scribe must not alter what was dictated, nor the witness testify to something he was not asked to witness; Ibn Qutayba and al-Zajjaj prefer this reading.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r3.anchor: أن معناه النهي للكاتب أن يضار من يكتب له بأن يكتب غير ما يمل عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj argues that falsifying a document or testimony is the sort of harm called transgression in the next clause; merely summoning a busy person would not make one sinful.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r4.anchor: واختاره ابن قتيبة و الزجاج واحتج الزجاج على صحته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r5.speaker: عطاء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r5.claim: A third view from ʿAta and others says the harm is the scribe refusing to write or the witness refusing to testify.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p340/r5.anchor: أن معنى المضارة امتناع الكاتب أن يكتب والشهادة أن يشهد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p341/r1.claim: “If you do so” refers to committing this harm.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r1.claim: This is the longest verse in the Qur'an; Ibn Shihab says he was told it was the latest Qur'anic verse revealed at the Throne.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report says Adam first denied an agreement: God showed him his descendants, including David, gave David forty years from Adam's thousand-year lifespan, and documented and witnessed the gift; Adam later denied it until shown the record. A version says David lived one hundred and Adam completed one thousand. Ibn Kathir calls the report very strange and notes weakness in Ali ibn Zayd's narrations, though al-Hakim gives variants through Abu Hurayra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r2.anchor: إن أول من جحد آدم، عليه السلام، أن الله لما خلق آدم، مسح ظهره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r3.claim: Writing deferred transactions is guidance that better preserves the amount and due date and keeps the testimony accurate, as the verse's stated rationale explains.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p721#2/r3.anchor: أن يكتبوها، ليكون ذلك أحفظ لمقدارها وميقاتها، وأضبط للشاهد فيها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r1.claim: Through Mujahid, Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed concerning salam, an advance payment due at a known term.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r1.anchor: أنزلت في السلم إلى أجل معلوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas swears that deferred forward sale for a specified term is permitted by God and reads this verse as evidence; al-Bukhari transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r2.anchor: أشهد أن السلف المضمون إلى أجل مسمى أن الله أحله وأذن فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r3.claim: When people in Medina paid in advance for fruit deliveries two or three years ahead, the Prophet instructed that advance sales specify a known measure, weight, and term; the report is in both Ṣaḥīḥ collections.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p722/r3.anchor: من أسلف فليسلف في كيل معلوم، ووزن معلوم، إلى أجل معلوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r1.claim: Writing is ordered for documentation and preservation, not because religion itself requires writing: Qur'an and Sunna are made easy to memorize. Specific transactions should be written as guidance, not obligation, according to one view, reconciling the instruction with the report that the community neither writes nor calculates.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r1.anchor: فأمروا أمر إرشاد لا أمر إيجاب، كما ذهب إليه بعضهم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r2.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r2.claim: He says a borrower should write down a debt and a buyer should have witnesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r2.anchor: قال ابن جريج: من ادان فليكتب، ومن ابتاع فليشهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r3.claim: He recounts Abu Sulayman al-Mar'ashi's warning: a seller who grants credit without writing or witnesses and is later cheated has wronged himself by disobeying God, so his plea is not answered.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r3.anchor: رجل باع بيعا إلى أجل فلم يشهد ولم يكتب، فلما حل ماله جحده صاحبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد والشعبي والربيع بن أنس والحسن وابن جريج وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r4.claim: They hold that writing transactions was initially obligatory, then abrogated by the option to trust one another and discharge the entrusted obligation in 2:283.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r4.anchor: كان ذلك واجبا ثم نسخ بقوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r5.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r5.claim: A Prophetic story tells of an Israelite borrower who could find no ship to repay a thousand dinars, placed the money and a note in a sealed log, and entrusted it to the sea after invoking God as witness and guarantor; the lender found it, and the borrower later came with repayment too.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723/r5.anchor: فأخذ خشبة فنقرها فأدخل فيها ألف دينار وصحيفة معها إلى صاحبها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir calls the preceding loan story's chain sound and says al-Bukhari narrated it in seven sound routes, sometimes through 'Abd Allah ibn Salih from al-Layth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r1.anchor: وهذا إسناد صحيح (4) وقد رواه البخاري في سبعة مواضع من طرق صحيحة (5)

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r2.claim: A writer must record fairly and justly, without bias or adding to or reducing the agreed terms.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r2.anchor: ولا يكتب إلا ما اتفقوا عليه من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r3.claim: Someone who knows how to write should not refuse a request; writing for those unable to do so is charity, as supported by reports about helping a worker and concealing knowledge.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r3.anchor: فكما علمه الله ما لم يكن يعلم، فليتصدق على غيره ممن لا يحسن الكتابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r4.claim: They hold that it is obligatory for a capable writer to write.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p723#2/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وعطاء: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r1.claim: The debtor dictates the debt and must fear God, withholding none of it; if the debtor is wasteful and legally restricted, young, insane, or unable to dictate through speech difficulty or ignorance, the guardian dictates fairly.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r1.anchor: أي: وليملل المدين على الكاتب ما في ذمته من الدين، وليتق الله في ذلك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r2.claim: Witnesses accompany writing for additional assurance. In financial matters, one man and two women may testify; Ibn Kathir connects this arrangement to a hadith describing women's testimony as half a man's and explaining their lesser reason and religious practice.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724/r2.anchor: وهذا إنما يكون في الأموال وما يقصد به المال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r1.claim: The condition that witnesses be approved implies their probity; al-Shafi'i uses it to specify other unqualified Qur'anic witness commands, and some use it to reject unknown-status witnesses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r1.anchor: فيه دلالة على اشتراط العدالة في الشهود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r2.claim: If one woman forgets, the other reminds her; another reading intensifies the verb. Ibn Kathir rejects the claim that having two women together makes them equivalent to a man and prefers the reminder interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r2.anchor: أي: يحصل لها ذكرى بما وقع به الإشهاد، ولهذا قرأ آخرون: "فتذكر" بالتشديد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r3.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r3.claim: They interpret 'when called' as a summons to undertake testimony, which witnesses must accept; this makes taking testimony a communal obligation.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r4.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r4.claim: The majority interprets the summons as one to give testimony already borne; a witness must answer when personally required, otherwise the duty is communal.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r4.anchor: المراد بقوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} للأداء، لحقيقة قوله: {الشهداء}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مجلز
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r5.claim: If invited to take testimony, one may choose; after having witnessed, one must respond when called to testify.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r5.anchor: إذا دعيت لتشهد فأنت بالخيار، وإذا شهدت فدعيت (4) فأجب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r6.speaker: زيد بن خالد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r6.claim: A Prophetic report calls the best witnesses those who bring their testimony before being asked for it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r6.anchor: ألا أخبركم بخير الشهداء؟ الذي يأتي بشهادته قبل أن يسألها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r7.claim: Other reports condemn witnesses who testify before being asked, whose oaths and testimony precede each other, or who testify without a request; these are false witnesses.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن البصري
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p724#2/r8.claim: They say the prohibition covers both taking testimony and giving it.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r1.claim: Do not grow weary of recording a debt, large or small, through its due date; writing deferred claims is more just before God, strengthens testimony by helping witnesses remember, and reduces doubt in disputes.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r1.anchor: أي: هذا الذي أمرناكم به من الكتابة للحق إذا كان مؤجلا هو {أقسط عند الله}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r2.claim: An immediate cash trade may go unwritten because no harm results from omitting a record.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r2.anchor: أي: إذا كان البيع بالحاضر يدا بيد، فلا بأس بعدم الكتابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r3.claim: He says buyers should witness their rights whether or not a term is involved; similar views are reported from Jabir ibn Zayd, Mujahid, Ata, and al-Dahhak.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r3.anchor: أشهدوا على حقكم إذا كان فيه أجل أو لم يكن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r4.speaker: الشعبي والحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r4.claim: They say the command to witness sales was abrogated by the option to trust one another and return the entrusted property in 2:283.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r4.anchor: هذا الأمر منسوخ بقوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r5.claim: The majority treats witnessing sales as guidance and recommendation, not obligation; the report of the Prophet's disputed horse purchase and Khuzaima's extraordinary testimony supports this.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p725/r5.anchor: وهذا الأمر محمول عند الجمهور على الإرشاد والندب، لا على الوجوب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r1.claim: Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i transmit the horse-purchase story through other routes from al-Zuhri, supporting the report about Khuzaima's testimony.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r1.anchor: وهكذا رواه أبو داود من حديث شعيب، والنسائي من رواية محمد بن الوليد الزبيري

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r2.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r2.claim: A report says prayers are not answered for three: a man who keeps a badly behaved wife without divorcing her, a guardian who gives an orphan's wealth before maturity, and a lender who lends without witnesses. Al-Hakim calls its chain sound by the two Ṣaḥīḥ collections' criteria, but notes Shu'ba's companions stop it at Abu Musa and agree on a different report through that chain.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r2.anchor: ثلاثة يدعون الله فلا يستجاب لهم: رجل له امرأة سيئة الخلق فلم يطلقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir says witnessing remains the prudent safeguard.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r1.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r1.claim: They understand the prohibition as forbidding a writer from recording anything contrary to what was dictated or a witness from falsely testifying or concealing testimony.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r1.anchor: فيكتب هذا خلاف ما يملى، ويشهد هذا بخلاف ما سمع أو يكتمها بالكلية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r2.claim: Another interpretation forbids burdening or harming the writer and witness: a person summons them, and they explain that they are occupied, but he insists that they were commanded to answer; Ibn Abbas says the caller may not harm them. Similar views are attributed to many early authorities.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p726#2/r2.anchor: قال: يأتي الرجل فيدعوهما إلى الكتاب والشهادة، فيقولان: إنا على حاجة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r1.claim: Disobeying these directions and doing what was forbidden is an abiding sin from which people cannot escape.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r1.anchor: أي: إن خالفتم ما أمرتم به، وفعلتم ما نهيتم عنه، فإنه فسق كائن بكم، أي: لازم لكم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r2.claim: Fearing God means keeping watch, following His commands, and leaving His prohibitions; the promise that God teaches those who fear Him is compared with the discernment of 8:29 and light from 57:28.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r2.anchor: أي: خافوه وراقبوه، واتبعوا أمره واتركوا زجره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r3.claim: God knows the realities, interests, and consequences of all things; nothing is hidden from His knowledge, which encompasses all beings.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p727/r3.anchor: أي: هو عالم بحقائق الأمور ومصالحها وعواقبها، فلا يخفى عليه شيء من الأشياء

SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r1.claim: إلى أجل attaches to تداينتم; attaching it to an omitted adjective of دين is possible but weak because it fronts an interpreted adjective before an explicit one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { إلى أجل }: متعلق بتداينتم، ويجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r2.claim: تداين is reciprocal form of الدين, like تبايع from البيع; داينت means dealing in debt whether giving or taking, as in Ruʾbah's verse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r2.anchor: و " تداين " تفاعل من الدين كتبايع من البيع، يقال: داينت الرجل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r3.claim: دنت الرجل means selling to him on credit, while أدنته means borrowing from him; the two patterns differentiate the directions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r3.anchor: ويقال: دنت الرجل: إذا بعته بدين، وأدنته أنا: أخذت منه بدين

SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r4.claim: The pronoun in فاكتبوه returns to دين; that noun is repeated to provide an antecedent, disambiguate reciprocal تداينوا, or indicate every amount of debt.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282/r4.anchor: الضمير يعود على " بدين " وإنما ذكر قوله " بدين " ليعيد عليه هذا الضمير

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r1.claim: إلى أجل is emphatic because debt is necessarily deferred; مسمى's alif comes from yāʾ, itself from waw in the root.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: { إلى أجل } على سبيل التأكيد، إذ لا يكون الدين إلا مؤجلا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r2.claim: بالعدل can attach to فليكتب, as an adverbial meaning justly or as a cause; Abu al-Baqa gives both readings.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r2.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " بالعدل " متعلق بقوله: فليكتب، أي: ليكتب بالحق

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches بالعدل to كاتب as its adjective, meaning a trustworthy writer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " متعلق بكاتب صفة له، أي: كاتب مأمون على ما يكتب

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya attaches the bā to وليكتب, not كاتب, since a child or slave may write a document even if not personally just.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " والباء متعلقة بقوله: " وليكتب " ، وليست متعلقة بقوله " كاتب "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r5.claim: A third analysis makes باء extra, yielding كاتب العدل, the just writer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#2/r5.anchor: الثالث: أن تكون الباء زائدة، تقديره: فليكتب بينكم كاتب العدل.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r1.claim: أن يكتب is the direct object of لا يأب. كما علمه الله may modify that writing or attach to the later فليكتب; the Sheikh finds the latter strained by word order and فاء.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r1.anchor: قوله: { أن يكتب } مفعول به أي: لا يأب الكتابة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r2.claim: If كما علمه الله attaches to أن يكتب, refusal of the specified writing is forbidden and that writing is commanded; if to فليكتب, refusal in general is forbidden, then qualified writing commanded.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r2.anchor: قلت: إن علقته بأن يكتب فقد نهى عن الامتناع من الكتابة المقيدة، ثم قيل له

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r3.claim: كما may attach to لا يأب causally: since God favored him with literacy, he should not refuse but write generously; the Sheikh calls this unlikely.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطية: " ويحتمل أن يكون " كما " متعلقا بما في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r4.claim: Even if كما attaches to فليكتب, its كاف can still be causal: he should write because God taught him.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r4.anchor: وعلى القول بكونها متعلقة بقوله: " فليكتب " يجوز أن تكون للتعليل أيضا، أي: فلأجل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r5.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r5.claim: The general reading has a silent lām in فليكتب, treating the separate word like a connected word; al-Hasan reads its original kasra.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#3/r5.anchor: وقرأ العامة: " فليكتب " بتسكين اللام كقولهم:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r1.claim: وليملل is the command of أمل يمِل; with the second radical jussive, Hijazis use dissimilation and Tamimis assimilation, including in pause; وليمل is an anomalous assimilated reading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r1.anchor: فلما سكن الثاني جزما جرى فيه لغتان: الفك وهو لغة الحجاز، والإدغام وهو لغة تميم

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r2.claim: أمل and أملى both mean dictating; some call them dialects, others derive the yāʾ as a replacement for a doubled consonant, with repetition underlying both forms.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r2.anchor: ويقال: أمل يمل إملالا، وأملى يملي إملاء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r3.claim: الحق may be a subject with عليه as a fronted predicate, or a subject governed by the preceding preposition; the relative debtor is the subject of يملل and its two objects are understood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r3.anchor: و " الحق " يجوز أن يكون مبتدأ، و " عليه " خبر مقدم، ويجوز أن يكون فاعلا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r4.claim: The implied meaning is that the debtor dictates the written amount due to the writer; أمللت عليه takes على with one of its objects.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#4/r4.anchor: أي: وليملل الديان الكتاب ما عليه من الحق، فحذف المفعولين للعلم بهما

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r1.claim: منه attaches to يبخس, with من marking origin and the pronoun referring to the debt; alternatively it is an omitted adjective of an indefinite, fronted as a circumstantial.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r1.anchor: يجوز في " منه " أن يكون متعلقا بيبخس، و " من " لابتداء الغاية

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r2.claim: شيئا may be a direct object or cognate accusative; بخس means decrease, originally of a damaged eye, metaphorically applied to a right, with بخص as a variant.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r2.anchor: والبخس: النقص، يقال منه: بخس زيد عمرا حقه يبخسه بخسا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r3.claim: هو confirms the implicit subject of يمل to remove figurative attribution and specify that the debtor cannot dictate personally.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r3.anchor: وفائدة التوكيد به رفع المجاز الذي كان يحتمله إسناد الفعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r4.claim: The Sheikh calls the silent-hāʾ reading in هو more anomalous than ثم هو يوم القيامة; the author rejects that judgment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r4.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهذا أشذ من قراءة من قرأ:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r5.claim: The silent-hāʾ form is not anomalous: it is mutawatir from Nafi through Qalun and from al-Kisa'i.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r5.anchor: فإنها قراءة متواترة قرأ بها نافع بن أبي نعيم

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r6.claim: The pronoun in وليه refers to the debtor when he has one of the three stated limitations; بالعدل repeats the earlier construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#5/r6.anchor: والهاء في " وليه " للذي عليه الحق إذا كان متصفا بإحدى الصفات الثلاث

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r1.claim: استشهدوا may retain the request sense of استفعل, or استفعل may mean أفعل, as in استعجل/أعجل and استيقن/أيقن.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r1.anchor: يجوز أن تكون السين على بابها من الطلب أي: اطلبوا شهيدين، ويجوز أن يكون استفعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r2.claim: The intensive form شهيدين suggests choosing witnesses who testify repeatedly.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r2.anchor: وفي قوله: " شهيدين " تنبيه على أنه ينبغي أن يكون الشاهد ممن تتكرر

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r3.claim: من رجالكم may attach to استشهدوا with من marking source, or be an adjective of شهيدين with partitive من.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r3.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق باستشهدوا، وتكون " من " لابتداء الغاية

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r4.claim: If كان is incomplete, its dual subject refers to the two witnesses: if the creditor fails or chooses not to secure two men, the alternative applies.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r4.anchor: فإن كانت ناقصة فالألف اسمها، وهي عائدة على الشهيدين أي: فإن لم يكن الشاهدان رجلين

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r5.claim: If كان is complete, رجلين is an emphatic circumstantial: the alternative is used only when two male witnesses cannot be found.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#6/r5.anchor: وإن كانت تامة فيكون " رجلين " نصبا على الحال المؤكدة كقوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r1.claim: فرجل وامرأتان may be a subject with an omitted predicate such as sufficient for testimony, a predicate of an omitted subject الشاهد, or a nominative with an omitted verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يرتفع ما بعد الفاء على الابتداء والخبر محذوف تقديره: فرجل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supplies فليشهد رجل, meaning let a man and two women testify; this avoids deleting a construct noun and is the best analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r2.anchor: وقيل: تقديره الفعل: فليشهد رجل، وهو أحسن

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r3.claim: Other analyses make the phrase a subject of complete or incomplete كان, or passive فليستشهد رجل; complete كان is preferable because it requires fewer deletions.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل بالتامة وهو أولى، لأن فيه حذف فعل فقط بقي فاعله

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa notes that an accusative reading would imply فاستشهدوا.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r4.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " ولو كان قد قرىء بالنصب لكان التقدير: فاستشهدوا "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r5.claim: A reading gives وامرأتان with a silent hamza; one account treats the hamza as replaced by alif and then rehamzat, though that is not its regular softening.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r5.anchor: وقرىء: " وامرأتان " بسكون الهمزة التي هي لام الكلمة، وفيها تخريجان

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa explains the silent hamza as first softened between hamza and alif, then treated as alif and rehamzat, as in عألم and خأتم.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r6.anchor: وقال أبو البقاء في تقرير هذا الوجه، ونحا إلى القياس فقال: " ووجهه أنه خفف الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r7.claim: A second account silences hamza because successive vowels burden it; a poet's أنا after waw is offered as a parallel.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#7/r7.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون قد استثقل توالي الحركات، والهمزة حرف يشبه حرف العلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r1.speaker: ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r1.claim: Ibn Jinni rules out silencing hamza because fatḥa is light; the author says this generalization ignores other poetic, prose, and reading evidence for such easing.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r1.anchor: قد نص ابن جني على أن هذا الوجه لا يجوز فقال: " ولا يجوز أن يكون سكن الهمزة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r2.claim: ممن ترضون may be a nominative adjective of رجل وامرأتان; the Sheikh rejects this because it would exclude the two male witnesses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r2.anchor: أنه في محل رفع نعتا لرجل وامرأتين/. والثاني: أنه في محل نصب

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r3.claim: It may instead be an accusative adjective of شهيدين; Abu al-Baqa rejects this because intervening words separate adjective and noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه في محل نصب لأنه نعت لشهيدين. واستضعف الشيخ الوجه الأول

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r4.claim: It may be apposition to من رجالكم with the preposition repeated; the Sheikh objects that apposition would still restrict the phrase to the men.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r4.anchor: الوجه الثالث: أنه بدل من قوله " من رجالكم " بتكرير العامل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r5.claim: The Sheikh attaches ممن ترضون directly to استشهدوا so the qualification applies to every witness; its late position signals this scope.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#8/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " ويكون قيدا في الجميع، ولذلك جاء متأخرا بعد الجميع "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r1.claim: من الشهداء may be a circumstantial of the omitted relative pronoun in ممن ترضون, or apposition to its من with a repeated preposition.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من العائد المحذوف

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r2.claim: Hamza reads إن تضل as a conditional particle; others read أن تضل as an accusative verbal noun, with a causal lām understood.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r2.anchor: قوله: { أن تضل } قرأ حمزة بكسر " إن " على أنها شرطية

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r3.speaker: حمزة
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r3.claim: Hamza reads فتذكر with doubled kāf and nominative rāʾ as the conditional answer, understood as فهي تذكر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r3.anchor: وذلك أن حمزة رحمه الله يقرأ: " فتذكر " بتشديد الكاف ورفع الراء

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya makes the conditional and answer a nominative adjective of the two women; the Sheikh objects to the awkward order and possible intervening phrase.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r5.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r5.claim: Al-Wahidi had already proposed the conditional clause as an adjective of the two women, citing a relative clause followed by a condition and response.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r5.anchor: فإنه قال: " وموضع الشرط وجوابه رفع بكونهما وصفا للمذكورين وهما " امرأتان "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r6.claim: The apparent reading treats the conditional as an independent statement answering why two women are assigned in place of one man.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r6.anchor: والظاهر أن هذه الجملة الشرطية مستأنفة للإخبار بهذا الحكم

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r7.claim: With أن, the verb is subjunctive and the lām of purpose is omitted: لأن تضل or إرادة أن تضل; its fatha differs from the junction fatha in Hamza's jussive reading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#9/r7.anchor: وأن وما في حيزها في محل نصب أو جر بعد حذف حرف الجر

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r1.speaker: الواحدي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r1.claim: The causal phrase may govern an inferred verb of testifying, but the author says the estimated predicate or verb already makes that unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r1.anchor: وفي متعلق هذا الجار ثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: أنه فعل مضمر دل عليه الكلام السابق

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r2.claim: Two economical estimates are رجل وامرأتان يشهدون لأن تضل or فليشهد رجل; each supplies the needed predicate or verb.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r2.anchor: وكذلك الخبر المقدر لقولك: " فرجل وامرأتان " إذ تقدير الأول: فليشهد رجل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r3.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r3.claim: Sibawayh explains that error causes reminder, so cause and result are treated as interchangeable; the purpose is that one woman remind the other, as in preparing a prop for a leaning wall.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r3.anchor: وقد أجاب سيبويه وغيره عن ذلك بأن الضلال لما كان سببا للإذكار، والإذكار مسببا عنه

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r4.speaker: الجرجاني
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r4.claim: Al-Jurjani estimates مخافة أن تضل and cites Amr's verse; the author says this works alone, but فتذكر makes it mistakenly mean fearing that she reminds.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r4.anchor: وقد ذهب الجرجاني في هذه الآية إل أن التقدير: مخافة أن تضل، وأنشد قول عمرو:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far reports that al-Abbas estimated كراهة أن تضل; Abu Ja'far calls it mistaken because it makes the desired reminder something disliked.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#10/r5.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: " سمعت علي بن سليمان يحكي عن أبي العباس أن التقدير كراهة أن تضل "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r1.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ estimates كي تذكر إحدى الأخرى إن ضلت, with the result fronted and أن opened; his analogy is delighting in giving a petitioner when asked.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r1.anchor: وذهب الفراء إلى أغرب من هذا كله فزعم أن تقدير الآية الكريمة: " كي تذكر أحداهما الأخرى إن ضلت "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r2.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says he cannot see why a conditional should change أن to فتح when moved before its clause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: " لست أدري لم صار الجزاء [إذا تقدم] وهو في مكانه وغير مكانه وجب أن يفتح أن "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r3.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r3.claim: Al-Farisi calls al-Farraʾ's claim unsupported and contrary to analogy: changing a particle's vowel or moving it does not change its grammatical work.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r3.anchor: وقال الفارسي: " ما ذكره الفراء دعوى لا دلالة عليها والقياس يفسدها

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r4.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r4.claim: They lighten the kāf and read فتذكر with accusative rāʾ from أذكرته, meaning to make someone recall after forgetting; ضلال means forgetting, supported by 26:20 and al-Farazdaq.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو " فتذكر " بتخفيف الكاف ونصب الراء من أذكرته

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r5.claim: Because أذكرته is causative and takes two objects, the omitted second is testimony: one woman reminds the other of her testimony after forgetting.
