SAMIN-DURR:2:282#11/r5.anchor: وليس في الآية إلا مفعول واحد فلا بد من اعتقاد حذف الثاني

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r1.claim: An eccentric interpretation takes فتذكر to mean making the other woman a male witness, so their joint testimony equals a man's.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r1.anchor: وقد شذ بعضهم فقال: " معنى فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى أي: فتجعلها ذكرا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r2.speaker: الأصمعي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r2.claim: Al-Asma'i transmits from Abu Amr two readings of meaning: doubled فتذكر recalls after forgetting, while light فتذكر makes the second woman a reminder by joining her testimony.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r2.anchor: وروى الأصمعي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء قال: " فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى بالتشديد

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r3.speaker: المفسرون وأهل اللسان
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r3.claim: Exegetes and linguists reject the male-equivalence interpretation: forgetting pairs naturally with reminding, it does not fit the testimony rule's male witness, and it would imply wider legal equivalence.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r3.anchor: لم يرتض هذا من أبي عمرو المفسرون وأهل اللسان

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r4.claim: The author notes that the objection about not extending equivalence to every law also challenges the accepted reminder interpretation, so the response applies to both.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r4.anchor: وفيه نظر أيضا، إذ هو مشترك الإلزام

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r5.claim: Zamakhshari calls making one woman a male witness a far-fetched interpretation, without limiting the criticism to one reading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ومن بدع التفاسير: " فتذكر " فتجعل إحداهما الأخرى ذكرا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r6.claim: Nominative فتذكر is coordinated to أن تضل in the readings with أن; only Hamza raises the rāʾ, and the readers divide into three combinations of إن/أن, light/doubled kāf, and case.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#12/r6.anchor: وأما نصب الراء فنسق على " أن تضل " لأنهما يقرآن: " أن تضل "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r1.claim: The second object is omitted in this reading too; فعل and أفعل can be synonymous, while the more common doubled form is witnessed by the poet's يذكرنيك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r1.anchor: والتشديد في هذا اللفظ أكثر استعمالا من التخفيف

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r2.speaker: عيسى بن عمر والجحدري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r2.claim: They read تضل in the passive; al-Jahdari also reads tuḍillu, from أضل, with the omitted object الشهادة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r2.anchor: وقرأ عيسى بن عمر والجحدري: " تضل " مبنيا للمفعول، وعن الجحدري أيضا:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r3.speaker: حميد بن عبد الرحمن ومجاهد
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r3.claim: They read فتذكر with light kāf and nominative rāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r3.anchor: وقرأ حميد بن عبد الرحمن ومجاهد: " فتذكر " برفع الراء وتخفيف الكاف،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r4.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r4.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reads فتذاكر, the reciprocal form of mutual reminding.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r4.anchor: وزيد بن أسلم: " فتذاكر " من المذاكرة.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r5.claim: إحداهما is normally the subject and الأخرى the object, which grammar requires when case is unmarked; semantic clarity can also permit reversing them here.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r5.anchor: وقوله: { إحداهما } فاعل " والأخرى " مفعول، وهذا مما يجب تقديم الفاعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa says either woman can be parsed as subject because the semantic roles are recoverable, despite the usual ordering rule.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r6.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: ف " إحداهما " فاعل، و " الأخرى " مفعول، ويصح العكس، إلا أنه يمتنع

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r7.claim: The repeated إحداهما rather than a pronoun preserves ambiguity because either woman may forget and remind; the generic wording means if one forgets, the other reminds.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r7.anchor: ولما أبهم الفاعل في قوله: { أن تضل إحداهما } أبهم أيضا في قوله

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa gives two reasons for repeating the apparent noun: preserve role ambiguity, or replace a pronoun whose reference would make the forgetter also the reminder.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#13/r8.anchor: أعاد الظاهر ليدل على الإبهام في الذكر والنسيان

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r1.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r1.claim: Al-Farisi analyzes إحدى as an irregular feminine of الواحد; the author prefers it as the regular feminine of أحد, paired in eleven and twenty-one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r1.anchor: قال الفارسي: " أنثوه على غير بنائه، وفي هذا نظر، بل هو تأنيث " أحد "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r2.claim: إحدى pluralizes as إحد, like كسرة/كسر, because its final alif functions like feminine tāʾ; similar patterns include الكبرى/كبر and قصعاء/قواصع.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r2.anchor: قال أبو العباس: " جعلوا الألف في الإحدى بمنزلة التاء في " الكسرة " فقالوا في جمعها: إحد

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r3.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r3.claim: Ibn al-A'rabi cites إحدى الإحد as a poetic plural and notes expressions إحدى الإحد, أحد الأحدين, and واحد الآحاد for a unique one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r3.anchor: وأنشد ابن الأعرابي على إحدى وإحد قول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r4.claim: إحدى is used only in annexation, unlike its masculine counterpart أحد.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r4.anchor: واعلم أن " إحدى " لا تستعمل إلا مضافة إلى غيرها، فيقال:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r5.claim: الأخرى is feminine of comparative آخر and can mean آخرة, as in 7:38; both forms pluralize أخر, but their declension and meanings differ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#14/r5.anchor: و " الأخرى " تأنيث " آخر " الذي هو أفعل التفضيل، وتكون بمعنى آخرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r1.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another in debt; Ruʾba’s line illustrates the verb dāyantu.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r1.anchor: إذا داين بعضكم بعضا يقال داينت الرجل اذا عاملته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r2.claim: The debt may be owed by or to the person, as bāyaʿtuhu can mean selling to or buying from him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r2.anchor: معطيا أو آخذا كما تقول بايعته اذا بعته أو باعك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r3.claim: Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for ‘write it,’ improves the wording, and distinguishes deferred from immediate debt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r3.anchor: ذكر ليرجع الضمير إليه في قوله ﴿ فاكتبوه ﴾ إذ لو لم يذكر لوجب أن يقال فاكتبوا الدين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r4.claim: A specified term must be known; harvest, threshing, or pilgrims’ return is too indeterminate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r4.anchor: من حق الأجل ان يكون معلوما كالتوقيت بالسنة والأشهر والأيام ولو قال إلى الحصاد أو الدياس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r5.claim: Writing is recommended because it gives stronger security against forgetting and denial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r5.anchor: وإنما امر بكتبة الدين لأن ذلك اوثق وآمن من النسيان وأبعد من الجحود والأمر للندب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse concerns salam: after usury was forbidden, advance sale for a guaranteed term was permitted and the longest verse revealed for it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p351#2/r6.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أن المراد به السلم وقال لما حرم الله الربا أباح السلف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r1.claim: ‘With justice’ describes a trustworthy scribe who writes evenly and carefully, adding and omitting nothing; parties should choose a learned jurist who knows legal conditions.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r1.anchor: متعلق بكاتب صفة له أي كاتب مامون على ما يكتب يكتب بالسوية والاحتياط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r2.claim: The indefinite ‘a scribe’ generalizes the prohibition: no scribe should refuse to write.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r2.anchor: ولا يمتنع أحد من الكتاب وهو معنى تنكير كاتب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r3.claim: ‘As God taught him’ means to write documents without altering them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r3.anchor: مثل ما علمه الله كتابة الوثائق لا يبدل ولا يغير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r4.speaker: وقيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r4.claim: Alternatively, as in 28:77, the writer should benefit others through the skill God taught him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r4.anchor: وقيل هو كقوله تعالى ﴿ وأحسن كما أحسن الله إليك ﴾ القصص 77

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r5.speaker: الشعبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r5.claim: Al-Shaʿbī regards writing as a communal obligation.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r6.claim: ‘As God taught him’ may attach to ‘write’ in the prohibition or to the later command, producing different scopes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352/r6.anchor: كما علمه الله يجوز ان يتعلق بان يكتب وبقوله فليكتب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.claim: If the phrase attaches to ‘write,’ the scribe must use that taught form; if it attaches to ‘let him write,’ refusal is prohibited generally before writing is ordered with qualifications.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r1.anchor: يعني فليكتب تلك الكتابة لا يعدل عنها للتوكيد وإن علقته بقوله فليكتب فقد نهى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.claim: The debtor alone dictates because the debt is witnessed against him as fixed in his liability and acknowledged by him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r2.anchor: ولا يكن المملي الا من وجب عليه الحق لأنه هو المشهود على ثباته في ذمته وإقراره به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.claim: Imlāʾ and imlāl are two Arabic forms, both used in the Quran.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r3.anchor: والإملاء والإملال لغتان قد نطق بهما القرآن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r4.claim: Bakhsa means a reduction from a debt or right.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.claim: Readings omit the hamza in shayan or pronounce it with gemination.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r5.anchor: والبخس النقص وقرىء ( شيا ) بطرح الهمزة ( وشيا ) بالتشديد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r6.claim: A safīh is restricted for wastefulness and poor judgment; a weak person may be a child or confused elder, and inability to dictate may come from speech difficulty or muteness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.claim: The guardian dictates for a restricted or minor person, an agent for someone unable, or an interpreter for a person who confirms his translation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#2/r7.anchor: الذي يلي أمره من وصي إن كان سفيها أو صبيا أو وكيل إن كان غير مستطيع أو ترجمان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r1.claim: ‘He himself cannot dictate’ means he can dictate through another who interprets for him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r1.anchor: فيه انه غير مستطيع بنفسه ولكن بغيره وهو الذي يترجم عنه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r2.claim: Seek two male witnesses from believing men; most scholars require witnesses to be Muslim, free, and adult.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r2.anchor: من رجال المؤمنين والحرية والبلوغ شرط مع الاسلام عند عامة العلماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r3.speaker: علي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r3.claim: ʿAlī rules that an enslaved person’s testimony is invalid in any matter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r3.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه لا تجوز شهادة العبد في شيء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r4.speaker: شريح وابن سيرين وعثمان البتي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r4.claim: Shurayḥ, Ibn Sīrīn, and ʿUthmān al-Battī allow testimony by enslaved people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r4.anchor: وعند شريح وابن سيرين وعثمان البتي انها جائزة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa permits non-Muslims to testify within their own religious communities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r5.anchor: ويجوز عند أبي حنيفة شهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض على اختلاف الملل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r6.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; Abū Ḥanīfa accepts women’s testimony with men except in ḥudūd and retaliation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r6.anchor: فليشهد رجل وامرأتان وشهادة النساء مع الرجال مقبولة عند أبي حنيفة فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r7.claim: Acceptable witnesses are those whose uprightness is known.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r8.claim: ‘Lest one err’ means fail to recall the testimony; purpose is phrased by its cause and effect, like preparing a prop for a leaning wall or a weapon for an approaching enemy.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r8.anchor: أن لا تهتدي احداهما للشهادة بان تنساها من ضل الطريق اذا لم يهتد له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r9.claim: The cause-effect construction works because the two are closely linked; intent to remind is expressed as intent that one err.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r9.anchor: كانت ارادة الضلال المسبب عنه الإذكار إرادة للإذكار فكانه قيل إرادة ان تذكر احداهما الأخرى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r10.claim: Readings have fatadhakkara light or doubled, fatadhākarā, and Hamza’s conditional in tidilla with indicative fatadhakkaru.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p352#3/r10.anchor: وقرىء ( فتذكر ) بالتخفيف والتشديد وهما لغتان و ( فتذاكرا ) وقرأ حمزة ( إن تضل احداهما )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r1.claim: A passive feminine reading of ‘if one errs’ is reported; the gloss that two women together become one man is a bizarre interpretation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r1.anchor: ﴿ ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه ﴾ المائدة 95 وقرىء ( ان تضل احداهما ) على البناء للمفعول والتأنيث

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r2.claim: The explanation that the two women together count as a male is a bizarre gloss.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r2.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير فتذكر فتجعل احداهما الأخرى ذكرا يعني انهما اذا اجتمعتا كانتا بمنزلة الذكر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r3.claim: Witnesses must not refuse when summoned to give testimony.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r4.speaker: وقيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r4.claim: Another interpretation is that they are summoned to bear testimony; they may be called witnesses before bearing it because the imminent is named as present.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r4.anchor: وقيل ليستشهدوا وقيل لهم شهداء قبل التحمل تنزيلا لما يشارف منزلة الكائن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r5.speaker: قتادة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r5.claim: Qatāda says a verse was revealed after a man visited a large gathering and nobody followed him, illustrating refusal to respond.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r5.anchor: وعن قتادة كان الرجل يطوف في الحواء العظيم فيه القوم فلا يتبعه منهم أحد فنزلت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r6.claim: A Prophetic saying says a believer does not say ‘I am lazy’; weariness can mean laziness, a hypocrite’s trait.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r6.anchor: كني بالسأم عن الكسل لأن الكسل صفة المنافق ومنه الحديث 153 ( لا يقول المؤمن كسلت )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r7.claim: Frequent debtors may tire of preparing a separate document for each small or large debt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r7.anchor: ويجوز ان يراد من كثرت مدايناته فاحتاج ان يكسب لكل دين صغير أو كبير كتابا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r8.claim: ‘Write it’ can refer to the debt or right; small or large describes the debt, or the document’s concise or full length without omission.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353/r8.anchor: والضمير في ﴿ تكتبوه ﴾ للدين أو الحق ﴿ صغيرا أو كبيرا ﴾

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r1.claim: The agreed term is the time the parties named; dhālikum points to writing as a verbal noun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ إلى أجله ﴾ إلى وقته الذي اتفق الغريمان على تسميته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r2.claim: Aqsaṭ means more just, aqwam more supportive of testimony, and the directions make doubt less likely.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r2.anchor: أعدل من القسط ﴿ وأقوم للشهادة ﴾ وأعون على إقامة الشهادة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r3.claim: Following Sībawayh, aqsaṭ and aqwam may derive regularly from verbs or by analogy from qāsiṭ and qayyim, meaning possessed of justice and uprightness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r3.anchor: يجوز على مذهب سيبويه ان يكونا مبنيين من أقسط وأقام وان يكون أقسط من قاسط

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r4.claim: A reading has yāʾ for both occurrences of ‘they grow weary.’
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r4.anchor: وقرىء ( ولا يسأموا ان يكتبوه ) بالياء فيهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r5.claim: Present trade means exchanged goods and hand-to-hand exchange; an immediate sale need not be written because deferred-debt risks do not arise.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r5.anchor: اريد بالتجارة ما يتجر فيه من الابدال ومعنى إدارتها بينهم تعاطيهم إياها يدا بيد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r6.claim: Trade is read nominative with kāna complete or incomplete, or accusative in an excepted construction illustrated by poetry.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p353#2/r6.anchor: وقرىء تجارة حاضرة بالرفع على كان التامة وقيل هي الناقصة على ان الاسم ( تجارة حاضرة )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r1.claim: Witness any sale, immediate or deferred, as a precaution against disputes; alternatively, witnessing alone can suffice for immediate trade without writing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r1.anchor: امر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا ناجزا أو كالئا لأنه احوط وأبعد مما عسى يقع من الاختلاف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r2.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says one may choose whether to witness a sale.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r2.anchor: وعن الحسن ان شاء أشهد وإن شاء لم يشهد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r3.speaker: الضحاك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk considers witnessing obligatory even for a bunch of greens.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r3.anchor: وعن الضحاك هي عزيمة من الله ولو على باقة بقل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r4.claim: Ḍārr may be active or passive; ʿUmar’s and Ibn ʿAbbās’s readings clarify it. The ban covers refusing, falsifying, adding, or omitting testimony, or harming witnesses through coercion, unpaid work, and travel costs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r4.anchor: يحتمل البناء للفاعل والمفعول والدليل عليه قراءة عمر رضي الله عنه ( ولا يضارر ) بالإظهار والكسر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb with kasra.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r1.claim: ‘If you do so’ means if you harm one another; alternatively, it means doing anything forbidden in the passage.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r2.claim: On a journey means while travelling.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Ubayy read kitāban; Ibn ʿAbbās asks what if a scribe is found but paper and ink are not.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس وأبي رضي الله عنهما ( كتابا ) وقال ابن عباس أرأيت إن وجدت الكاتب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya reads kutuban; al-Ḥasan’s kitāban is glossed as the plural of kātib.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ أبو العالية ( كتبا ) وقرأ الحسن ( كتابا ) جمع كاتب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r5.claim: Pledge is a security; variants include ruhan and rihān, with different vowels and number.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r5.anchor: فالذي يستوثق به رهن وقرىء ( فرهن ) بضم الهاء وسكونها وهو جمع رهن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r6.claim: Travel is singled out because writing and witnesses may be unavailable; a pledge preserves property in their place, not because pledging is forbidden at home. The Prophet pledged his armor while not travelling.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r6.anchor: ليس الغرض تجويز الارتهان في السفر خاصة ولكن السفر لما كان مظنة لاعواز الكتب والإشهاد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk restrict pledging to travel by the apparent wording and require possession; Mālik validates it by offer and acceptance without possession.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p354#2/r7.anchor: وعن مجاهد والضحاك انهما لم يجوزاه الا في حال السفر أخذا بظاهر الآية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r1.claim: Some creditors trust a debtor because of their good opinion of him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r1.anchor: فإن أمن بعض الدائنين بعض المديونين لحسن ظنه به

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r2.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r2.claim: Ubayy reads the passive ‘if the debtor is trusted,’ describing a person known for reliability, fulfillment, and independence from collateral.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( فإن أومن ) أي آمنه الناس ووصفوا المديون بالأمانة والوفاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r3.claim: The debtor should honor the creditor’s trust by repaying the entrusted debt; it is called trust because the creditor relied on him without collateral.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r3.anchor: حث المديون على أن يكون عند ظن الدائن به وامنه منه وائتمانه له وان يؤدي اليه الحق

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r4.claim: The phrase has alternative pronunciations; ʿĀṣim’s assimilation in ittaman is rejected because its yāʾ derives from hamza and remains hamza-like.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356/r4.anchor: وعن عاصم انه قرأ ( الذي اتمن ) بإدغام الياء في التاء قياسا على اتسر في الافتعال من اليسر وليس بصحيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r1.claim: ‘His heart is sinful’ can make the heart the subject of āthim or the topic with a fronted predicate; both mean the heart itself sins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ قلبه ﴾ رفع بآثم على الفاعلية كانه قيل فإنه يأثم قلبه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r2.claim: Naming the heart emphasizes that concealment begins inwardly; the heart is the body’s chief organ and root of its deeds, so the sin is grave, not merely a failure of speech.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r2.anchor: فلما كان إثما مقترفا بالقلب أسند اليه لأن إسناد الفعل إلى الجارحة التي يعمل بها أبلغ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās counts association, false testimony, and concealing testimony among the greatest sins.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p356#2/r3.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أكبر الكبائر الاشراك بالله لقوله تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r1.claim: A reading puts qalbahu in the accusative, like safiha nafsahu in 2:130.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r1.anchor: وشهادة الزور وكتمان الشهادة وقرىء ( قلبه ) بالنصب كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r2.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r2.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads athima qalbuhu, meaning he made his heart sinful.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p357/r2.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة ( أثم قلبه ) أي جعله إثما

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r1.claim: Tadayantum means either mutually to settle debts or to transact with one another.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r1.anchor: في { تداينتم } تأويلان : أحدهما : تجازيتم . والثاني : تعاملتم

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r2.claim: Writing the debt is recommended, not compulsory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r2.anchor: أنه ندب , وهو قول أبي سعيد الخدري , والحسن , والشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r4.claim: A just scribe must neither add a term to harm the debtor nor omit one to harm the creditor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r4.anchor: وعدل الكاتب ألا يزيد [ فيه ] إضرارا بمن هو عليه , ولا ينقص منه , إضرارا بمن هو له

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r5.speaker: عامر
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r5.claim: The command that a scribe not refuse is a communal obligation, like jihad.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r5.anchor: أنه فرض على الكفاية كالجهاد , قاله عامر

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r6.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r6.claim: Writing is incumbent on a scribe when he is free to do it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r6.anchor: أنه واجب عليه في حال فراغه , قاله الشعبي أيضا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r7.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r7.claim: The command for a scribe to write is a recommendation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r8.claim: The command is abrogated by the later command not to harm a scribe or witness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r8.anchor: أن ذلك منسوخ بقوله تعالى : { ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r9.claim: The debtor dictates the amount to the scribe and acknowledges it before the witness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r9.anchor: يعني على الكاتب , ويقر به عند الشاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r10.claim: The debtor must not reduce any part of the debt.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r11.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r11.claim: A foolish debtor is one ignorant of the correct way to dictate what he owes.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r11.anchor: أنه الجاهل بالصواب فيما عليه أن يمله على الكاتب , وهو قول مجاهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r12.claim: A foolish debtor may be a child or a woman.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r13.speaker: الشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r13.claim: A foolish debtor may be one who squanders wealth and is corrupt in religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r13.anchor: أنه المبذر لماله , المفسد في دينه , وهو معنى قول الشافعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r14.claim: A foolish debtor may fail to understand the value of money and waste it instead of seeking to grow it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p354/r14.anchor: الذي يجهل قدر المال , ولا يمتنع من تبذيره ولا يرغب في تثميره

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r1.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r1.claim: A weak debtor may be dull or incompetent.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r2.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r2.claim: A weak debtor may be unable to dictate because of speech difficulty or muteness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r2.anchor: أنه العاجز عن الإملاء إما بعي أو خرس , قاله الطبري

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r3.claim: One who cannot dictate may be unable to speak or mute.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r3.anchor: أنه العيي الأخرس , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r4.claim: One who cannot dictate may be prevented by imprisonment or by a disability.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r4.anchor: أنه الممنوع عن الإملاء إما بحبس أو عيبة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r5.claim: One who cannot dictate may be mentally ill.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r6.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r6.claim: The guardian who dictates is the guardian of the person who owes the debt.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r6.anchor: ولي من عليه الحق , وهو قول الضحاك , وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r7.claim: The guardian who dictates may instead be the owner of the right, the creditor.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r7.anchor: ولي الحق , وهو صاحبه , قاله ابن عباس , والربيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r8.claim: The two men must be from your religious community.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r9.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r9.claim: The two men may be required to be free persons.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r10.speaker: الجمهور
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r10.claim: Acceptable witnesses are free, Muslim, upright people.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r10.anchor: أنهم الأحرار المسلمون العدول , وهو قول الجمهور

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r11.speaker: شريح وعثمان البتي وأبو ثور
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r11.claim: Acceptable Muslim witnesses may be upright even if enslaved.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r11.anchor: أنهم عدول المسلمين وإن كانوا عبيدا , وهو قول شريح , وعثمان البتي , وأبي ثور

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r12.speaker: أهل الكوفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r12.claim: An tadilla means “lest one of them err.”

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r13.speaker: أهل البصرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r13.claim: An tadilla means “because one of them might err.”
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r13.anchor: كراهة أن تضل , قاله أهل البصرة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r14.claim: The woman may err or forget; Sibawayh identifies forgetting as one meaning.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r14.anchor: أحدهما : أن تخطىء . والثاني : أن تنسى , قاله سيبويه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r15.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r15.claim: One woman reminding the other may mean making her count like a male witness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r15.anchor: أنها تجعلها كذكر من الرجال , قاله سفيان بن عيينة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r16.speaker: قتادة والسدي والضحاك وابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r16.claim: One woman reminds the other if she forgets.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r16.anchor: أنها تذكرها إن نسيت , قاله قتادة , والسدي , والضحاك , وابن زيد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r17.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r17.claim: Witnesses must answer a summons to have their testimony recorded in the document.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r17.anchor: لتحملها وإثباتها في الكتاب , قاله ابن عباس , وقتادة , والربيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r18.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r18.speaker: مجاهد والشعبي وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r18.claim: Witnesses must answer a summons to give testimony before a judge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r18.anchor: لإقامتها وأدائها عند الحاكم , قاله مجاهد , والشعبي , وعطاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r19.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r19.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r19.claim: The summons may be for both bearing and giving testimony.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r19.anchor: أنها للتحمل والأداء جميعا , قاله الحسن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r20.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r20.speaker: عطاء وعطية العوفي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r20.claim: Answering the summons is recommended, not obligatory.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r20.anchor: أنه ندب وليس بفرض , قاله عطاء , وعطية العوفي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r21.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r21.speaker: الشعبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r21.claim: Answering the summons is a communal obligation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r21.anchor: أنه فرض على الكفاية , قاله الشعبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r22.speaker: قتادة والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r22.claim: Answering the summons is an individual obligation.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r22.anchor: أنه فرض على الأعيان , قاله قتادة , والربيع

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r23.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r23.claim: Small or large debts should be written through their due date; “small” does not mean trivial amounts such as a qirat or daniq, outside customary usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r23.anchor: وليس يريد بالصغير ما كان تافها حقيرا كالقيراط والدانق لخروج ذلك عن العرف المعهود

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r24.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r24.claim: Aqsaṭ means more just; aqsaṭa is to act justly, while qasaṭa is to act unjustly, as the cited verses show.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r24.anchor: أعدل , يقال : أقسط إذا عدل فهو مقسط , قال تعالى : ^ { وأقسطوا إن الله يحب المقسطين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r25.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r25.claim: Aqwam for testimony means either more upright or better preserved, from qiyām meaning keeping watch.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r25.anchor: أحدهما : أصح لها , مأخوذ من الاستقامة . والثاني : أحفظ لها , مأخوذ من القيام , بمعنى الحفظ

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r26.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r26.claim: The writing makes doubt less likely either about the debtor denying what is owed or about a witness erring.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r26.anchor: ألا ترتابوا بمن عليه حق أن ينكره . والثاني : ألا ترتابوا بالشاهد أن يضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r27.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r27.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r27.claim: An immediate trade may be a cash sale with no deferred term in either price or merchandise, or goods the buyer takes into possession.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r27.anchor: أن الحاضرة ما تعجل ولم يداخله أجل في مبيع ولا ثمن

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r28.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r28.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r28.claim: Managing a trade between yourselves may mean passing the goods hand to hand or repeatedly trading them.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r28.anchor: تتناقلونها من يد إلى يد . والثاني : تكثرون تبايعها في كل وقت

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r29.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r29.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r29.claim: Not writing an immediate cash trade is permitted, though the command does not require its record.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r29.anchor: يعني أنه غير مأمور بكتبه وإن كان مباحا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r30.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r30.speaker: الضحاك وداود بن علي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r30.anchor: أنه فرض , وهو قول الضحاك , وداود بن علي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r31.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r31.speaker: الحسن والشعبي ومالك والشافعي
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r31.anchor: أنه ندب , وهو قول الحسن , والشعبي , ومالك , والشافعي

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r32.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r32.speaker: طاووس والحسن وقتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r32.claim: Harming a scribe or witness includes writing terms not dictated or testifying to what was not witnessed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r32.anchor: أن يكتب الكاتب ما لم يمل عليه , ويشهد الشاهد بما لم يستشهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r33.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r33.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r33.claim: Harming a scribe or witness includes preventing a scribe from writing or a witness from testifying.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r33.anchor: أن يمنع الكاتب أن يكتب , ويمنع الشاهد أن يشهد

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r34.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r34.speaker: عكرمة والضحاك والسدي والربيع
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r34.claim: Harming them may mean summoning a busy, excused scribe or witness.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r34.anchor: أن يدعى الكاتب والشاهد وهما مشغولان معذوران

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r35.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r35.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r35.claim: The harm prohibition may apply generally to writing and testimony.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r35.anchor: ويحتمل تأويلا رابعا : أن تكون المضارة في الكتابة والشهادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r36.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r36.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p355/r36.anchor: أن الفسوق المعصية , قاله ابن عباس , ومجاهد , والضحاك

MUJAHID:v1p118#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p118#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p118#2/r1.claim: The witnesses must not refuse when called if they had already witnessed the transaction.
MUJAHID:v1p118#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ﴾ يقول إذا كانوا قد شهدوا قبل ذلك

MUQATIL:2:282/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r1.claim: A deferred debt’s amount and due date should be written; a fair scribe writes between buyer and seller without increasing the debtor’s amount or reducing the creditor’s right; scribes were few in Muhammad’s time.
MUQATIL:2:282/r1.anchor: يعنى اكتبوا الدين والأجل، { وليكتب } الكاتب بين البائع والمشترى،

MUQATIL:2:282/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r2.claim: The debtor must dictate the record, fear God, and omit none of what is owed; the warning against shortchanging also appears in 7:85.
MUQATIL:2:282/r2.anchor: يعنى المطلوب، ثم خوف المطلوب، فقال عز وجل: { وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا }

MUQATIL:2:282/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r3.claim: If the debtor is ignorant, mentally impaired, weak, unable to dictate, or cannot speak, the creditor’s guardian dictates fairly, neither adding nor subtracting.
MUQATIL:2:282/r3.anchor: يعنى أو عاجزا، أو به حمق،

MUQATIL:2:282/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r4.claim: The right-holder’s representative dictates for an incapable debtor and must be fair, matching the same no-increase, no-decrease standard imposed on the debtor.
MUQATIL:2:282/r4.anchor: { فليملل وليه } ، يعنى ولى الحق، فليملل هو { بالعدل } ، يعنى بالحق،

MUQATIL:2:282/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r5.claim: For a debt, use two acceptable male witnesses or one man and two women; if one woman forgets, the other reminds her, and a summoned witness should serve when free.
MUQATIL:2:282/r5.anchor: يقول: ولا يشهد الرجل على حقه إلا مرضيا إن كان الشاهد رجلا أو امرأة.

MUQATIL:2:282/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282/r6.claim: Do not tire of recording even a small amount through its due date: writing better records the term and protects property, is just, reliable for testimony, and less likely to create doubt.
MUQATIL:2:282/r6.anchor: ولا تملوا، وكل شىء فى القرآن تسأموا، يعنى تملوا،

MUQATIL:2:282#2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r1.claim: Here “more likely” means more suitable: written evidence is more likely to bring testimony in 5:108 and to comfort the wives in 33:51.

MUQATIL:2:282#2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r2.claim: An immediate cash trade with no term may go unwritten; sales should be witnessed, but a scribe or witness should not be pressured when occupied if another can be found.
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r2.anchor: ليس فيها أجل، { فليس عليكم جناح } ، يعنى حرج،

MUQATIL:2:282#2/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r3.claim: Wronging a scribe or witness is sinful; God commands the parties to fear Him and knows all their deeds.
MUQATIL:2:282#2/r3.anchor: وإن تضاروا الكاتب والشاهد وما نهيتم عنه، فإنه إثم بكم،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r1.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another by debt, whether one lends or borrows.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r1.anchor: أى إذا داين بعضكم بعضا يقال داينت الرجل إذا عاملته بدين معطيا أو آخذا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r2.claim: A specified term is a known period, such as harvest, threshing, or the pilgrims' return.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r2.anchor: مدة معلومة كالحصاد أو الدياس أو رجوع الحاج

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r3.claim: Mentioning debt supplies the antecedent for فاكتبوه and clarifies deferred versus immediate debt; the phrasing is more elegant than repeating الدين.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r3.anchor: احتيج إلى ذكر الدين ولم يقل إذا تداينتم إلى اجل مسمى

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r4.claim: Writing a deferred debt is recommended because it better guards against forgetfulness and denial.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r4.anchor: أمر بكتابة الدين لأن ذلك أوثق وآمن من النسيان وأبعد من الجحود

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this concerns salam; after forbidding usury, God permitted a guaranteed advance sale for a known term and revealed the longest verse, requiring a term for salam.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r5.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما أن المراد به السلم وقال لما حرم الله الربا أباح السلف المضمون إلى أجل معلوم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r6.claim: The scribe must be trustworthy and precise, adding nothing and omitting nothing; the debtor's document should be legally valid.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r6.anchor: كاتب مأمون على ما يكتب يكتب بالاحتياط لا يزيد على ما يجب أن يكتب ولا ينقص

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r7.claim: The scribe should understand legal conditions, so the parties should select a learned, upright jurist who writes only what Islamic law accepts.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r7.anchor: وفيه دليل أن يكون الكاتب فقيها عالما بالشروط حتى يجئ مكتوبه معدلا بالشرع

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r8.claim: No scribe should refuse to write the document as God taught, altering or changing its form.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r8.anchor: كتابة الوثائق لا يبدل ولا يغير وكما متعلق بأن يكتب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r9.claim: The debtor, as the person liable and subject to testimony, must dictate, making the document his verbal admission; إملال and إملاء are synonymous forms.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r9.anchor: إلا من وجب عليه الحق لأنه هو المشهود على ثباته فى ذمته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r10.claim: The debtor must fear God, neither refusing to dictate in denial of the debt nor understating any part of it.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r10.anchor: الذى عليه الدين ربه فلا يمتنع عن الإملاء فيكون جحودا لكل حقه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r11.claim: Safīh may mean mentally impaired or legally restrained for wastefulness and poor judgment; ḍaʿīf means a child; inability includes stammering, muteness, or not knowing the language.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r11.anchor: أى مجنونا لأن السفه خفة فى العقل أو محجورا عليه لتبذيره وجهله بالتصرف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r12.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r12.claim: When the debtor cannot dictate, the guardian who manages his affairs dictates truthfully and justly.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r12.anchor: ﴿ فليملل وليه ﴾ الذى يلى امره ويقوم به ﴿ بالعدل ﴾ بالصدق والحق

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r13.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r13.claim: Two witnesses are sought from believing men; Islam, freedom, and adulthood are conditions, while the author's school accepts non-Muslims testifying among themselves.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r13.anchor: من رجال المؤمنين والحرية والبلوغ شرط مع الإسلام وشهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض مقبولة عندنا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r14.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r14.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; male testimony with women is accepted outside fixed punishments and retaliation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r14.anchor: فليشهد رجل وامرأتان وشهادة الرجال مع النساء تقبل فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r15.claim: The witnesses should be people whose uprightness is known; this implies some witnesses are not approved.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r15.anchor: ممن تعرفون عدالتهم وفيه دليل على أن غير المرضى شاهد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r16.claim: The two-witness clause explains that one woman may forget the testimony and the other remind her; Ḥamza reads the verb with nominative and gemination under the conditional, while Makki and Baṣri read it accusatively from dhikr.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p135#4/r16.anchor: إن تضل إحداهما على الشرط فتذكر بالرفع والتشديد حمزة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r1.claim: Witnesses are called witnesses before they testify because the anticipated event is treated as already actual; the first command is obligatory in principle and the second recommended.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r1.anchor: وسماهم شهداء قبل التحمل تنزيلا لما يشارف منزلة الكائن فالأول للفرض والثاني للندب

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r2.speaker: الشاعر
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r2.claim: A poet uses s-simt to express becoming weary with life after eighty years, supporting the sense of ولا تسأموا as do not tire.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r2.anchor: قال الشاعر سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش ثمانين حولا لا أبا لك يسأم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r3.claim: The pronoun in أن تكتبوه may refer to the debt or the document; small or large can describe the debt's value, supporting salam in textiles, or describe a concise or detailed record.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r3.anchor: والضمير فى ﴿ أن تكتبوه ﴾ للدين أو الحق ﴿ صغيرا أو كبيرا ﴾ على أى حال كان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r4.claim: Write the debt through its agreed due date; ذلك refers to the act of writing as a verbal noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r4.anchor: إلى وقته الذى اتفق الغريمان على تسميته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r5.claim: Writing is more equitable before God, better supports testimony, and reduces doubt about amount and qualities by providing a written reference.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r5.anchor: أقرب من انتفاء الريب للشاهد والحاكم وصاحب الحق فإنه قد يقع الشك فى المقدار والصفات

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r6.claim: The comparative forms أقسط and أقوم follow Sībawayh's derivation from the causative verbs اقسط and أقام.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r6.anchor: وبنى أفعلا التفضيل أى أقسط وأقوم من اقسط وأقام على مذهب سيبويه

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r7.speaker: عاصم
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim reads the phrase so تجارة is the noun of كان or an appositional clarification of trade.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r7.anchor: عاصم أى إلا أن تكون التجارة تجارة أو إلا أن تكون المعاملة تجارة حاضرة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r8.claim: Other readings analyze يكون as complete, meaning an immediate transaction occurs, or as incomplete with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and تديرونها as predicate.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r8.anchor: غيره تجارة حاضرة على كان التامة أى إلا أن تقع تجارة حاضرة أو هى ناقصة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r9.claim: Managing a spot trade means exchanging it hand to hand; there is no harm in leaving it unwritten because no debt-related suspicion arises.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r9.anchor: معنى إدارتها بينهم تعاطيها يدا بيد

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r10.claim: Witnessing sales is recommended for immediate and deferred exchanges as a precaution, or the command concerns immediate trade alone, where testimony suffices without writing.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r10.anchor: أمر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا ناجزا أو كالئا لأنه أحوط وأبعد من وقوع الإختلاف

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r11.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r11.claim: Makki reads تذكرة with accusative from dhikr rather than the other derivation.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r11.anchor: فتذكر بالنصب مكى وبصرى من الذكر لا من الذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r12.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r12.speaker: بصري
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r12.claim: Baṣri shares the accusative reading تذكرة from dhikr.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r12.anchor: فتذكر بالنصب مكى وبصرى من الذكر لا من الذكر

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r13.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r13.speaker: عمر
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r13.claim: ʿUmar reads يضارر in the active voice; Ibn ʿAbbās reads يضار in the passive.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r13.anchor: يحتمل البناء للفاعل لقراءة عمر رضى الله عنه ولا يضارر وللمفعول لقراءة ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ولا يضار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r14.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads the passive form ولا يضار, while ʿUmar's active form is ولا يضارر.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r14.anchor: لقراءة عمر رضى الله عنه ولا يضارر وللمفعول لقراءة ابن عباس رضى الله عنهما ولا يضار

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r15.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r15.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r15.claim: The active reading forbids a scribe or witness to refuse, distort, add, or omit; the passive forbids burdening them, rushing them from duties, withholding the scribe's fee, or making a witness bear travel costs.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r15.anchor: النهى عن الضرار بهما بأن يعجلا عن مهم ويلزا أولا يعطى الكاتب حقه من الجعل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r16.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r16.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r16.claim: Causing such harm is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty, and God teaches the laws of religion without forgetfulness or deficiency.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p137/r16.anchor: ﴿ وإن تفعلوا ﴾ و إن تضاروا ﴿ فإنه ﴾ فان

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r1.claim: Harming the scribe or witnesses is sinful conduct; fear God in this duty.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r1.anchor: ﴿ فسوق بكم ﴾ مأثم ﴿ واتقوا الله ﴾ فى مخالفة أ

NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r2.claim: God teaches the laws of religion and knows everything without forgetfulness or deficiency.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p138/r2.anchor: ﴿ ويعلمكم الله ﴾ شرائع دينه ﴿ والله بكل شيء عليم ﴾ لا يلحقه سهو ولا قصور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r1.claim: He says he was told that the debt verse was the latest Quranic revelation at the Throne.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r1.anchor: قال سعيد بن المسيب: بلغني أن أحدث القرآن بالعرش آية الدين.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r2.claim: He says the verse was revealed specifically about salam, prompted by the people of Medina, but by consensus it covers all deferred debt transactions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: هذه الآية نزلت في السلم خاصة. معناه أن سلم أهل المدينة كان سبب الآية،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r3.speaker: ابن خويزمنداد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r3.claim: He says the verse contains thirty legal rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r3.anchor: وقال ابن خويزمنداد: إنها تضمنت ثلاثين حكما.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r4.speaker: بعض علمائنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r4.claim: Some Maliki scholars infer that loans may be deferred because the verse does not distinguish loans from other debt contracts; the Shafiʿis reply that it only orders documentation of an already deferred debt and that term rules come from other evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r4.anchor: وقد استدل بها بعض علمائنا على جواز التأجيل في القروض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r5.claim: بدين is emphatic; a debt is a transaction with one present countervalue and another deferred in liability, since Arabs call what is present عين and what is absent دين.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r5.anchor:
بدين } تأكيد، مثل قوله
ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r6.claim: The wording إلى أجل مسمى states the required known, fixed term; two poetic lines use دين for a deferred rather than immediate obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r6.anchor: وقد بين الله تعالى هذا المعنى بقوله الحق { إلى أجل مسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r7.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r7.claim: He says إلى أجل مسمى proves salam with an unknown term is invalid, as also shown by Prophetic practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r7.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: دل قول الله «إلى أجل مسمى» على أن السلم إلى الأجل المجهول غير جائز،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r8.claim: He transmits the Prophet's rule for advance purchase of dates: specify measure, weight, and term; al-Qurṭubī says Bukhari, Muslim, and others recorded it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r8.anchor: ثبت أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة وهم يستلفون في الثمار السنتين والثلاث

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r9.claim: He says pre-Islamic buyers sold camel meat until the offspring of an offspring was born; the Prophet forbade this indeterminate term.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: كان أهل الجاهلية يتبايعون لحم الجزور إلى حبل الحبلة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r10.claim: Scholars agree valid salam specifies described, commonly available food, measure, term, payment in known currency before the parties separate, and delivery place; he knows no scholar who invalidates such a contract.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r10.anchor: وأجمع كل من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم على أن السلم الجائز أن يسلم الرجل إلى صاحبه في طعام معلوم موصوف،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r11.claim: Maliki scholars permit tying salam to harvest, fruit-picking, Nowruz, or Mihrajan because these mark known times.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282/r11.anchor: وقال علماؤنا: إن السلم إلى الحصاد والجذاذ والنيروز والمهرجان جائز إذ ذاك يختص بوقت وزمن معلوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r1.claim: Salam is a sale of a specified, described commodity in liability for present capital or its equivalent, due at a known term.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r1.anchor: هو بيع معلوم في الذمة محصور بالصفة بعين حاضرة أو ما هو في حكمها إلى أجل معلوم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r2.claim: Requiring liability excludes unknown goods and specified individual orchards whose fruit may fail; full description excludes unspecified kinds or qualities of dates, cloth, or fish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r2.anchor: ومن السلم في الأعيان المعينة مثل الذي كانوا يستلفون في المدينة حين قدم عليهم النبي عليه السلام فإنهم كانوا يستلفون في ثمار نخيل بأعيانها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r3.claim: Present capital excludes debt-for-debt; treating it as present permits a two- or three-day delay in paying salam capital, which Malik allows, while al-Shafiʿi and Kufans forbid any delay after contract and separation by analogy with currency exchange.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r3.anchor: تحرر من اليومين والثلاثة التي يجوز تأخير رأس مال السلم إليه،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r4.claim: Al-Qurṭubī distinguishes salam from currency exchange: exchange has many strict conditions, while salam more closely resembles ordinary transactions and tolerates more flexibility.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r4.anchor: فإن الصرف بابه ضيق كثرت فيه الشروط بخلاف السلم فإن شوائب المعاملات عليه أكثر.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r5.claim: A known term excludes spot salam, which is impermissible on the commonly held view, and excludes the pre-Islamic unknown terms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r5.anchor: وقولهم «إلى أجل معلوم» تحرز من السلم الحال فإنه لا يجوز على المشهور

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r6.claim: Salam and salaf refer to the same transaction, but salam is its specific name because salaf can also mean a loan; salam is a unanimously permitted sale excepted from the ban on selling what one does not possess.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r6.anchor: السلم والسلف عبارتان عن معنى واحد وقد جاءا في الحديث غير أن الاسم الخاص بهذا الباب «السلم»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r7.claim: Salam is licensed to meet mutual needs: the buyer needs the harvest and the grower needs money before it ripens; it is a sale for the needy, and an immediate sale would defeat that purpose.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r7.anchor: وأرخص في السلم لأن السلم لما كان بيع معلوم في الذمة كان بيع غائب تدعو إليه ضرورة كل واحد من المتبايعين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r8.claim: The agreed conditions are six for the goods—liability, description, measurement, deferral, known term, and availability at maturity—and three for capital—known kind, specified measure, and cash payment, with cash status disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r8.anchor: في شروط السلم المتفق عليها والمختلف فيها وهي تسعة: ستة في المسلم فيه، وثلاثة في رأس مال السلم.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r9.claim: He says the first requirement, liability, is self-evident because salam is a debt transaction sought for benefit and accommodation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وأما الشرط الأول وهو أن يكون في الذمة فلا إشكال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r1.claim: He alone allows salam in a designated item under two conditions: it comes from a secure village, and collection has begun, as with milk from a sheep or ripe fruit from a palm.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r1.anchor: بيد أن مالكا قال: لا يجوز السلم في المعين إلا بشرطين:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r2.claim: He accepts Malik's exceptions: a secure location makes non-delivery unlikely enough to tolerate slight uncertainty, and daily collection of milk or dates meets a recurring need when buyers lack cash or prices fluctuate and sellers need money.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#3/r2.anchor: وهاتان المسألتان صحيحتان في الدليل لأن التعيين امتنع في السلم مخافة المزابنة والغرر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r1.claim: The Prophetic wording إلى أجل معلوم settles the requirement for a known term; al-Qurṭubī allows one to three days when prices differ between towns, but not within one town where the price is stable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r1.anchor: يغني عن قول كل قائل. قلت الذي أجازه علماؤنا من السلم الحال ما تختلف فيه البلدان من الأسعار،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r2.claim: There is consensus that the term must be known; Malik alone also accepts harvest or fruit-picking as a sufficiently known deadline, discussed under the verse about lunar phases.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r2.anchor: وأما الشرط الخامس وهو أن يكون الأجل معلوما فلا خلاف فيه بين الأمة،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r3.claim: There is consensus that the goods must exist at maturity; if they fail to exist then through God's decree, the contract is dissolved according to all scholars.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r3.anchor: وأما الشرط السادس وهو أن يكون موجودا عند المحل فلا خلاف فيه بين الأمة أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r4.claim: The seller need not own the goods throughout the contract; reports from Ibn Abi Awfa and Ibn Abza say the Companions did not ask Syrian sellers whether they farmed the grain or oil they promised.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r4.anchor: ليس من شرط السلم أن يكون المسلم إليه مالكا للمسلم فيه خلافا لبعض السلف،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r5.claim: He requires the goods to exist continuously from contract through maturity, fearing that the promised goods may be unavailable when demanded; other jurists require existence only at maturity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r5.anchor: وشرط أبو حنيفة وجود المسلم فيه من حين العقد إلى حين الأجل،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r6.speaker: الكوفيون والثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r6.claim: They require the delivery location for goods involving transport and invalidate salam if it is omitted; al-Awzāʿī calls omission disliked.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r6.anchor: وشرط الكوفيون والثوري أن يذكر موضع القبض فيما له حمل ومؤنة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r7.claim: If the place is unstated, the contract remains valid and delivery defaults to the contract location, as held by Ahmad, Ishaq, and hadith scholars; the Ibn ʿAbbās report omits the place, although it specifies measure, weight, and term.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#4/r7.anchor: وعندنا لو سكتوا عنه لم يفسد العقد، ويتعين موضع القبض

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r1.claim: A report through ʿAṭiyya says the Prophet forbade redirecting an advance-purchase contract to a different commodity; ʿAbd al-Ḥaqq says the transmitter al-ʿAwfī is not an authority, despite prominent scholars transmitting from him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r1.anchor: من أسلف في شيء فلا يصرفه إلى غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r2.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r2.claim: If a salam seller cannot deliver at maturity and the buyer releases him, the buyer may take only the original currency or exact capital; exchanging it for another good before receipt would sell food before possession, which the Prophet forbade.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r2.anchor: قال مالك: الأمر عندنا فيمن أسلف في طعام بسعر معلوم إلى أجل مسمى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r3.claim: فاكتبوه commands recording the debt and its term; some say it also implies witnesses, since writing without witnesses is not legal proof, and it prevents forgetting.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r3.anchor: فاكتبوه } يعني الدين والأجل. ويقال: أمر بالكتابة ولكن المراد الكتابة والإشهاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r4.claim: A report says Adam first denied a written gift: God showed him David among his descendants, allowed forty years of Adam's thousand-year life to be added to David's sixty, recorded and witnessed the gift, then produced the document when Adam denied it; David received a hundred years and Adam completed his thousand.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r4.anchor:
عن ابن عباس قال:
" قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في قول الله عز وجل { إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r5.claim: The command to write calls for recording every detail that identifies the debt, preventing disputes and enabling a judge to decide if the parties later disagree.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r5.anchor: إشارة ظاهرة إلى أنه يكتبه بجميع صفته المبينة له المعربة عنه للاختلاف المتوهم بين المتعاملين،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r6.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r6.claim: He holds that documenting every debt, whether sale or loan, is obligatory to prevent forgetfulness or denial.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r6.anchor: ذهب بعض الناس إلى أن كتب الديون واجب على أربابها، فرض بهذه الآية،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r7.speaker: ابن جريج
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r7.claim: He says a lender should write while a seller should obtain witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r7.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: من أدان فليكتب، ومن باع فليشهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r8.speaker: الشعبي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r8.claim: He says people regarded the following clause about mutual trust as abrogating the order to write; Ibn Jurayj, Ibn Zayd, and a report from Abu Saʿid are similar.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r8.anchor: وقال الشعبي: كانوا يرون أن «قوله فإن أمن» ناسخ لأمره بالكتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r9.speaker: الربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r9.claim: He says writing was initially obligatory under these words, then God eased the requirement with the clause permitting trusted transactions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r9.anchor: وذهب الربيع إلى أن ذلك واجب بهذه الألفاظ، ثم خففه الله تعالى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r10.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r10.claim: The majority treat documentation as recommended protection against lost property and doubt; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this correct because a person may waive a financial claim, so there is no abrogation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r10.anchor: وقال الجمهور: الأمر بالكتب ندب إلى حفظ الأموال وإزالة الريب،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r11.speaker: عطاء وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r11.claim: They say the writer must write when asked if no other writer is available; al-Shaʿbī gives the same ruling.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#5/r11.anchor: قال عطاء وغيره: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب وقاله الشعبي، وذلك إذا لم يوجد كاتب سواه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r1.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r1.claim: He says the writer must do so when free.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r1.anchor: السدي: واجب مع الفراغ. وحذفت اللام من الأول وأثبتت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r2.claim: The imperative lam is omitted before a second-person verb but retained with a third-person verb; the text cites 10:58 and a poetic line to illustrate retention and omission.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r2.anchor: وحذفت اللام من الأول وأثبتت في الثاني لأن الثاني غائب والأول للمخاطب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r3.claim: Writing with justice means accurately recording the claim without adding or subtracting anything.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r3.anchor: بالعدل } أي بالحق والمعدلة، أي لا يكتب لصاحب الحق أكثر مما قاله ولا أقل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r4.claim: The impartial writer stands between debtor and creditor because each might suspect the other of biased documentation; alternatively, the command reflects that some people can write and some cannot.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r4.anchor: وإنما قال «بينكم» ولم يقل أحدكم لأنه لما كان الذي له الدين يتهم في الكتابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r5.claim: The phrase بالعدل attaches to the act of writing rather than the writer, since a child, slave, or careful layperson could write accurately; appointed notaries must still be upright, knowledgeable, and trusted, as Malik says.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r5.anchor: الباء في قوله تعالى { بالعدل } متعلقة بقوله: «وليكتب» وليست متعلقة ب «كاتب»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r6.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r6.claim: He says official document writers must be legally knowledgeable, upright, and trustworthy.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r6.anchor: قال مالك رحمه الله تعالى: لا يكتب الوثائق بين الناس إلا عارف بها عدل في نفسه مأمون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r7.speaker: الطبري والربيع
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r7.claim: They say the writer is obligated to write when asked.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r7.anchor: فقال الطبري والربيع: واجب على الكاتب إذا أمر أن يكتب.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r8.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r8.claim: He makes writing obligatory only where refusal would harm the creditor because no substitute writer is available; otherwise the writer has latitude.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r8.anchor: وقال الحسن: ذلك واجب عليه في الموضع الذي لا يقدر على كاتب غيره،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r9.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r9.claim: They say the order to write was abrogated by the prohibition against harming a writer or witness; al-Qurṭubī calls this remote because a universal obligation was never established and paid document-writing is permitted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r9.anchor: وحكى المهدوي عن الربيع والضحاك أن قوله { يأب } منسوخ بقوله { ولا يضآر كاتب ولا شهيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r10.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r10.claim: He says the command is guidance, so the writer need not write before being paid.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r10.anchor: ابن العربي: والصحيح أنه أمر إرشاد فلا يكتب حتى يأخذ حقه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r11.claim: The verb أبى يأبى is an unusual conjugation, grouped with a few other exceptional patterns.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#6/r11.anchor: وأبى يأبى شاذ، ولم يجىء إلا قلى يقلى وأبى يأبى وغسى يغسى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r1.claim: The كاف in كما علمه الله may attach to the command that he write as taught, to the meaning of not refusing because God taught him, or—if the clause ends at أن يكتب—to فليكتب in a new sentence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r1.anchor: الكاف في «كما» متعلقة بقوله { أن يكتب } المعنى كتبا كما علمه الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r2.claim: The person who owes the debt is the debtor, and must dictate it aloud so his obligation is known.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r2.anchor: وهو المديون المطلوب يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r3.claim: إملال and إملاء are two forms: Hijaz and Banu Asad say أمل, Tamim says أملى; the Quran uses both, including 25:5, and the second lām becomes yāʾ for ease.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r3.anchor: والإملاء والإملال لغتان، أمل وأملى فأمل لغة أهل الحجاز وبنى أسد،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r4.claim: The debtor dictates because the testimony follows his admission; he must fear God and not diminish the debt, since بَخْس means reduction, as also in 2:228.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r4.anchor: فأمر الله تعالى الذي عليه الحق بالإملاء لأن الشهادة إنما تكون بسبب إقراره.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r5.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r5.claim: Some say سفيها means a minor, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because an adult may also be financially foolish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r5.anchor: قال بعض الناس: أي صغيرا. وهو خطأ فإن السفيه قد يكون كبيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r6.claim: The verse distinguishes the independent debtor from three who cannot dictate: the fool, the weak-minded, and the person unable to dictate; debts can also arise through inheritance distributions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r6.anchor: جعل الله الذي عليه الحق أربعة أصناف: مستقل بنفسه يمل، وثلاثة أصناف لا يملون

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r7.claim: A fool has poor financial judgment and cannot manage giving or receiving; the word is likened to a loosely woven cloth, and can also describe crude speech associated with shallow minds.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r7.anchor: فالسفيه المهلهل الرأي في المال الذي لا يحسن الأخذ لنفسه ولا الإعطاء منها،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r8.claim: Arabic usage applies سفه to weakness of mind or body, as the cited lines demonstrate for judgment and weakened, swaying spear tops.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#7/r8.anchor: والعرب تطلق السفه على ضعف العقل تارة وعلى ضعف البدن أخرى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r1.claim: Some distinguish ḍamma for bodily weakness from fatḥa for weakness of judgment; another view treats both as dialects, but he prefers the distinction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r1.anchor: وقد قالوا: الضعف بضم الضاد في البدن وبفتحها في الرأي، وقيل: هما لغتان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r2.claim: He reports that a mentally impaired trader's family asked the Prophet to interdict him; the Prophet stopped him from selling, then allowed him to trade only if he said there was no deception. Al-Tirmidhī calls the report sound.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r2.anchor:
روى أبو داود عن أنس بن مالك
" أن رجلا على عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يبتاع وفي عقله ضعف

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r3.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r3.claim: His historical record gives a related wording requiring the trader to say there is no deception and granting three nights' option on each purchase.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r3.anchor:
وذكره البخاري في التاريخ وقال فيه:
" إذا بايعت فقل لا خلابة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r4.claim: The trader was Habban ibn Munqidh, though another account calls Munqidh the grandfather of Yahya and Wasiʿ; he lived 130 years and a battle wound to his head impaired his mind and speech.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r4.anchor: وهذا الرجل هو حبان بن منقذ بن عمرو الأنصاري والد يحيى وواسع ابني حبان:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r5.claim: Al-Dāraquṭnī transmits that Habban had poor sight and a head wound, so the Prophet gave him three days' option; his impaired speech rendered لا خلابة as لا خذابة.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r5.anchor:
وروى الدارقطني قال:
" كان حبان بن منقذ رجلا ضعيفا ضرير البصر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r6.claim: خلابة means deception, as in the proverb that if one cannot overcome someone, one should trick him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r6.anchor: الخلابة: الخديعة ومنه قولهم: «إذا لم تغلب فاخلب».

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r7.speaker: أحمد وإسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r7.claim: They support interdicting a person who is repeatedly cheated in sales because of inexperience or impaired judgment; other scholars oppose interdiction, and the Maliki school has both views.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r7.anchor: فقال بالحجر عليه أحمد وإسحاق. وقال آخرون: لا يحجر عليه. والقولان في المذهب،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r8.speaker: author
