QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r8.claim: He prefers interdiction under this verse and the family's request; the Prophet's concession was specific to Habban because he insisted on trading, while someone ordinarily cheated—especially through mental impairment—should be interdicted.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#8/r8.anchor: والصحيح الأول لهذه الآية، ولقوله في الحديث: يا نبي الله أحجر على فلان.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق عن محمد بن يحيى بن حبان
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r1.claim: The Prophet told Habban to say لا خلابة when selling and gave him three nights to keep or return each purchase; Habban invoked this right even when mocked by sellers, and Companions confirmed his claim. Al-Dāraquṭnī records it; Abu ʿUmar cites al-Bukhari's historical transmission.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r1.anchor: إذا بعت فقل لا خلابة ثم أنت في كل سلعة تبتاعها بالخيار ثلاث ليال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r2.claim: The weak debtor is someone impaired in reason or nature and unable to dictate because of stammering, muteness, or inability to express himself; his guardian may be a father or trustee.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r2.anchor: الضعيف هو المدخول العقل الناقص الفطرة العاجز عن الإملاء، إما لعيه أو لخرسه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r3.claim: The person unable to dictate includes a minor, whose guardian is a trustee or father, and an absent person unable due to illness or another excuse, whose guardian is an agent; a mute could fit either category but fits unable best.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r3.anchor: والذي لا يستطيع أن يمل هو الصغير، ووليه وصيه أو أبوه والغائب عن موضع الإشهاد،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r4.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r4.claim: He takes وليه to refer to the debt itself, with reports from al-Rabiʿ and Ibn ʿAbbās; al-Qurṭubī rejects this as unsound and says Ibn ʿAbbās's report is not reliable.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r4.anchor: ذهب الطبري إلى أن الضمير في { وليه } عائد على «الحق» وأسند في ذلك عن الربيع، وعن ابن عباس.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r5.claim: وليّه correctly refers to the debtor; having the creditor dictate a new liability for a fool would not be lawful, though a sick or mute person may hear a creditor's fair dictation and acknowledge it when complete.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو عائد على { الذي عليه الحق سفيها } وهو الصحيح.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r6.claim: Since the debtor is trusted to dictate, a pledgor's sworn account of the debt prevails while the collateral remains; most jurists and Ibn al-Mundhir agree because the creditor claims the excess, in keeping with the rule that the claimant bears proof and the defendant swears.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#9/r6.anchor: لما قال الله تعالى: { فليملل الذي عليه الحق } دل ذلك على أنه مؤتمن فيما يورده ويصدره،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r1.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r1.claim: He accepts the pledgee's sworn account only up to the collateral's value, treating the pledge and oath as supporting him; al-Qurṭubī says the verse instead favors the debtor, and collateral value need not match the debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r1.anchor: وقال مالك: القول قول المرتهن فيما بينه وبين قيمة الرهن ولا يصدق على أكثر من ذلك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r2.claim: If وليّه means guardian, the verse implies that a guardian's acknowledgment is valid for the orphan under his care.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r2.anchor: وإذا ثبت أن المراد الولي ففيه دليل على أن إقراره جائز على يتيمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r3.claim: A transaction by an interdicted fool without the guardian's permission is invalid by consensus; an unimpaired but foolish person who has not been interdicted is discussed under Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r3.anchor: وتصرف السفيه المحجور عليه دون إذن وليه فاسد إجماعا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r4.claim: Seeking witnesses is recommended, not obligatory, as al-Qurṭubī explains later.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r4.anchor: والصحيح أنه ندب على ما يأتي بيانه إن شاء الله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r5.claim: God generally requires two witnesses for financial and bodily claims and legal penalties, except adultery; شهيد is an intensive form suggesting repeated testimony and thus justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r5.anchor: رتب الله سبحانه الشهادة بحكمته في الحقوق المالية والبدنية والحدود وجعل في كل فن شهيدين إلا في الزنا،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r6.claim: He says رجالكم means free men; Shurayh, Uthman al-Batti, Ahmad, Ishaq, and Abu Thawr accept an upright slave's testimony, unlike Malik, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafiʿi, and the majority; al-Qurṭubī prefers the majority, while al-Shaʿbi and al-Nakhaʿi permit slaves' testimony in minor matters.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: المراد الأحرار، واختاره القاضي أبو إسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r7.claim: He rejects slave testimony because the address concerns transacting believers, while slaves do not own such assets independently; he also invokes the later restriction on witnesses refusing a summons.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r7.anchor: والصحيح قول الجمهور لأن الله تعالى قال: { يأيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r8.claim: He transmits the Prophet's instruction that a witness should testify only to what is as clear as seeing the sun, establishing direct certainty rather than inference.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#10/r8.anchor: مثل ما روي عن ابن عباس قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r1.claim: Witnesses must directly know what they attest: probable inference may suffice for ordinary acts such as accepting a gift or recognizing a spouse by voice, but not testimony about another's admission, sale, slander, or seizure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r1.anchor: وهذا يدل على اشتراط معاينة الشاهد لما يشهد به، لا من يشهد بالاستدلال الذي يجوز أن يخطىء.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r2.speaker: الشافعي وابن أبي ليلى وأبو يوسف
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r2.claim: They accept testimony after blindness when the witness already knew the person before losing sight, analogizing the impairment to absence or death; al-Qurṭubī sees no reason to reject testimony previously borne while sighted and accepts public knowledge for lineage.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r2.anchor: ولذلك قال الشافعي وابن أبي ليلى وأبو يوسف: إذا علمه قبل العمى جازت الشهادة بعد العمى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r3.claim: Some accept a blind person's voice-based testimony as certain, but al-Qurṭubī rejects this because it would imply that a sighted person could likewise rely on sound alone.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r3.anchor: ومن العلماء من قبل شهادة الأعمى فيما طريقه الصوت لأنه رأى الاستدلال بذلك يترقى إلى حد اليقين،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r4.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r4.claim: Malik permits an established voice-based testimony by a blind person, including on divorce; Ibn Qasim reports him accepting testimony from a man who heard his neighbor divorce through a wall, with several early jurists sharing the view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r4.anchor: قلت: مذهب مالك في شهادة الأعمى على الصوت جائزة في الطلاق وغيره إذا عرف الصوت.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r5.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r5.claim: If two male witnesses are not produced, the claimant should bring one man and two women; the male noun is nominative and the women coordinated, with the predicate omitted to mean they take the two men's place.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r5.anchor: المعنى إن لم يأت الطالب برجلين فليأت برجل وامرأتين هذا قول الجمهور.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r6.speaker: قول
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r6.claim: Another parsing says the female witnesses may be used only when no men can be found; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls this weak because the verse's apparent sense allows one man and two women even when two men are available.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r6.anchor: وقال قوم: بل المعنى فإن لم يكن رجلان، أي لم يوجدا فلا يجوز استشهاد المرأتين إلا مع عدم الرجال.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r7.speaker: الجمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r7.claim: The one-man-and-two-women arrangement applies to financial matters and requires a man, since financial transactions are common and have multiple safeguards: writing, witnesses, collateral, and guarantees.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#11/r7.anchor: فأجيزت في الأموال خاصة في قول الجمهور، بشرط أن يكون معهما رجل.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r1.claim: The debt-transactions clause does not encompass testimony about a marriage dowry or settlement for intentional homicide, because those testimonies concern marriage rather than debt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r1.anchor: ولا يتوهم عاقل أن قوله تعالى { إذا تداينتم بدين } يشتمل على دين المهر مع البضع،

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r2.claim: Women may testify alone in matters that no one else can observe, out of necessity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r2.anchor: وأجاز العلماء شهادتهن منفردات فيما لا يطلع عليه غيرهن للضرورة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r3.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r3.claim: Malik permits children's testimony in injuries among children if they have not disagreed or separated; at least two are required, and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr also judged by it, which Malik calls established practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r3.anchor: فأجازها مالك ما لم يختلفوا ولم يفترقوا.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r4.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r4.claim: They reject children's testimony because children lack the qualifications of men, approved witnesses, and just adults named elsewhere in scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r4.anchor: ولم يجز الشافعي وأبو حنيفة وأصحابه شهادتهم لقوله تعالى { من رجالكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r5.claim: Because two women replace one man, he reasons by analogy that their testimony can be accompanied by an oath just as one man's testimony can; al-Shafiʿi agrees, while Abu Hanifa and his companions reject the oath as an extra division beyond the text.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r5.anchor: لما جعل الله سبحانه شهادة امرأتين بدل شهادة رجل وجب أن يكون حكمهما حكمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r6.speaker: الثوري والأوزاعي وعطاء والحكم بن عتيبة وطائفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r6.claim: They oppose judgment by an oath with a witness; some call that practice abrogated by the Quran, and ʿAṭāʾ alleges ʿAbd al-Malik first ruled that way while al-Ḥakam attributes it to Muʿāwiya.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r6.anchor: وممن قال بهذا القول الثوري والأوزاعي وعطاء والحكم بن عتيبة وطائفة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r7.claim: Al-Qurṭubī calls those accusations mistaken: the verse does not negate the Prophet's ruling by an oath and one witness, and an exclusive reading would also invalidate claims proved when a defendant refuses to swear, contrary to consensus.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r7.anchor: وهذا كله غلط وظن لا يغني من الحق شيئا، وليس من نفى وجهل كمن أثبت وعلم!

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r8.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r8.claim: He argues that when a defendant denies a claim and refuses the oath, the claimant may swear and establish it; because this accepted procedure is absent from the Quran's witness list, its existence proves the list is not exhaustive and supports the oath with one witness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#12/r8.anchor: قال مالك: فمن الحجة على من قال ذلك القول أن يقال له: أرأيت لو أن رجلا ادعى على رجل مالا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r1.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rebukes those who reject judgment by an oath and one witness despite sound reports and early authorities' practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r1.anchor: مع شهرة الأحاديث وصحتها بدعوا من عمل بها حتى نقضوا حكمه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r2.claim: The Prophet ruled by an oath together with one witness; ʿAmr ibn Dīnār restricts the report to property cases.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أنه قضى باليمين مع الشاهد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r3.speaker: أبو عمرو
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r3.claim: Abū ʿAmr calls the report's chain the soundest and its transmitters trustworthy, citing Muslim and other critics.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r3.anchor: قال أبو عمرو: هذا أصح إسناد لهذا الحديث، وهو حديث لا مطعن

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r4.speaker: الزهري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r4.claim: One report from al-Zuhrī calls judgment by oath and witness an innovation and insists on two witnesses; another says he first ruled by it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r4.anchor: سألت الزهري عن اليمين مع الشاهد فقال هذا شيء أحدثه الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī endorses the majority position allowing an oath with one witness, based on transmitted reports and generations of Medinan practice; Mālik allowed it in every region.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r5.anchor: وهو الذي لا يجوز عندي خلافه، لتواتر الآثار به عن النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r6.speaker: يحيى بن يحيى
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r6.claim: In al-Andalus, Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā said he had not seen al-Layth issue a ruling or hold the doctrine, thereby opposing Mālik and Medinan practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#13/r6.anchor: فإن يحيى بن يحيى زعم أنه لم ير الليث يفتي به ولا يذهب إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r1.claim: Prophetic Sunnah may add rulings to the Qurʾān, as in prohibited marriage combinations, foods, and wiping over footwear alongside Qurʾānic wording.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r2.claim: The Qurʾān's general permission for sales cannot abrogate the Prophet's bans on uncertain and nonexistent sales; Sunnah explains scripture.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r2.anchor: عن المزابنة وبيع الغرر وبيع مالم يخلق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r3.claim: Although one might call the oath-and-witness ruling case-specific, al-Qurṭubī reads it as establishing a general legal rule.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r3.anchor: بل ذلك عبارة عن تقعيد هذه القاعدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r4.speaker: أبو داود
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r4.claim: A report of Ibn ʿAbbās transmitted by Abū Dāwūd expressly says the Prophet judged by one witness and an oath in rights cases.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r4.anchor: ما رواه أبو داود في حديث ابن عباس أن رسول الله

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r5.claim: By analogy, an oath has stronger evidentiary standing than two women because women have no role in mutual imprecation, whereas an oath does.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r5.anchor: أنا وجدنا اليمين أقوى من المرأتين، لأنهما لا مدخل لهما في اللعان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r6.claim: Once sound Sunnah is established, it must be followed and needs no supporting precedent; those who oppose it are answered by it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r6.anchor: وإذا صحت السنة فالقول بها يجب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو محمد عبد الوهاب
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r7.claim: Among jurists accepting oath-plus-witness, its use is limited by consensus to property and related rights, not bodily rights; property rights are lower because women's testimony is accepted there.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r7.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الوهاب: ذلك في الأموال وما يتعلق بها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r8.claim: Mālik has two reports about intentional injury: one allows a choice between retaliation and compensation, while the sounder report allows neither because bodily rights are involved.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r8.anchor: لا يجب به شيء لأنه من حقوق الأبدان. قال: وهو الصحيح.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r9.speaker: المازري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r9.claim: Al-Māzarī reports agreement on oath-plus-witness for pure money claims and rejection for marriage or divorce as such; claims leading only to money are disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r9.anchor: وقال المازري: يقبل في المال المحض من غير خلاف، ولا يقبل في النكاح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r10.speaker: المهدوي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r10.claim: Al-Mahdawī says most jurists reject women's testimony in criminal penalties, marriage, and divorce, and do not let them transmit testimony where they cannot testify directly.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#14/r10.anchor: وقال المهدوي: شهادة النساء في الحدود غير جائزة في قول عامة الفقهاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r1.claim: Mālik's school accepts two women's testimony in matters unavailable to other witnesses, such as childbirth and a newborn's first cry, though details are disputed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r1.anchor: ويقضى بأثنتين منهن في كل ما لا يحضره غيرهن كالولادة والاستهلال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r2.speaker: ابن بكير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r2.claim: Ibn Bukayr and others take the address requiring approved witnesses to be directed to judges.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r2.anchor: قال ابن بكير وغيره: هذه مخاطبة للحكام.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects limiting the address to judges: it addresses everyone, although judges carry out the case in practice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r3.anchor: ابن عطية: وهذا غير نبيل، وإنما الخطاب لجميع الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r4.speaker: جمهور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r4.claim: The majority infer that probity is an additional qualification beyond being Muslim, since the verse requires witnesses whom people approve.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r5.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa regards any apparently Muslim person free of manifest wrongdoing as upright, even when character is unknown.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r5.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة: كل مسلم ظاهر الإسلام مع السلامة من فسق ظاهر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r6.speaker: شريح وعثمان البتى وأبو ثور
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r6.claim: Shurayḥ, ʿUthmān al-Battī, and Abū Thawr count Muslims as upright witnesses even if enslaved.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r6.anchor: وقال شريح وعثمان البتى وأبو ثور: هم عدول المسلمين وإن كانوا عبيدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r7.claim: A Bedouin may testify for a town-dweller if upright: Qurʾānic general wording does not distinguish them, and al-Qurṭubī rejects a restrictive report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r7.anchor: والصحيح جواز شهادته إذا كان عدلا مرضيا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r8.speaker: مالك وأحمد بن حنبل
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r8.claim: Mālik in one report and Aḥmad reject a Bedouin's testimony for a town-dweller, relying on a report from Abū Hurayra.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r8.anchor: وذهب أحمد بن حنبل ومالك في رواية ابن وهب عنه إلى رد شهادة البدوي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r9.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r9.claim: Probity means religious steadiness: avoiding major sins, preserving respectable conduct and avoiding minor sins, while appearing trustworthy and alert; another definition stresses apparent integrity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r9.anchor: قال علماؤنا: العدالة هي الاعتدال في الأحوال الدينية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#15/r10.claim: Because testimony is a grave authority that makes another person liable, God requires approved and upright witnesses with distinguishing qualities.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r1.claim: The requirement of witness approval supports inference from signs and entrusts judges with discretion to detect carelessness or suspicion and reject testimony.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r1.anchor: دليل على جواز الاجتهاد والاستدلال بالأمارات والعلامات

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r2.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa accepts apparent Muslim status as enough in property cases but not criminal penalties.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r2.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة: يكتفى بظاهر الإسلام في الأموال دون الحدود

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r3.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r3.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī calls that distinction self-defeating: a property claim is a right and should not receive weaker witness scrutiny than a criminal penalty.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r3.anchor: فلا يكتفى في الشهادة عليه بظاهر الدين كالحدود قاله ابن العربي.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r4.claim: Upright witnesses are even more important for marriage than debt, given its effects on lawful status, punishment, and lineage; al-Qurṭubī rejects Abū Ḥanīfa's view.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r4.anchor: فاشتراطها في النكاح أولى، خلافا لأبي حنيفة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r5.claim: Apparent profession of Islam does not establish probity, since impressive speech or appearance may conceal disqualifying conduct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r5.anchor: ولا يغتر بظاهر قوله: أنا مسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayd glosses the verb for straying as forgetting; in testimony, a witness may recall one part while forgetting another and become uncertain.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r6.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: معنى تضل تنسى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r7.speaker: حمزة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r7.claim: Ḥamza reads the particle with kasra as a conditional; the following clause answers it and the phrase describes the witnesses.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#16/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «إن» بكسر الهمزة على معنى الجزاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r1.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r1.claim: Under Ḥamza's conditional reading, Sībawayh parses the following verb as a new clause; with the open particle it is an object of purpose with an omitted governor.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r1.anchor: هذا قول سيبويه. ومن فتح «أن» فهي مفعول له

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r2.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r2.claim: Al-Naḥḥās allows several vocalizations of the verb, including forms reflecting the dialect that says ḍalaltu taḍillu.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r2.anchor: قال النحاس ويجوز «تضل» بفتح التاء والضاد، ويجوز تضل

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r3.speaker: الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r3.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read the verb with a pattern meaning that one forgets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى بن عمر «أن تضل» بضم التاء وفتح الضاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r4.speaker: النقاش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r4.claim: Al-Naqqāsh reports another al-Jaḥdarī reading, with the testimony itself going astray or being lost.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r4.anchor: وحكى النقاش عن الجحدري ضم التاء وكسر الضاد بمعنى أن تضل الشهادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r5.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna and Abū ʿAmr understand the lighter reading of the reminder verb as returning a woman's testimony to memory, so two women's testimony totals a man's.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#17/r5.anchor: قال سفيان بن عيينة وأبو عمرو بن العلاء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r1.claim: Al-Qurṭubī finds the lighter reminder reading less apt: a reminder naturally answers forgetfulness, and the doubled reading means one woman alerts the other when she forgets.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r1.anchor: قلت: وإليها ترجع قراءة أبي عمرو، أي إن تنس إحداهما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r2.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command not to refuse witnesses covers both being asked to record testimony and to deliver testimony already held.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r2.anchor: قال الحسن: جمعت هذه الآية أمرين، وهما ألا تأبى إذا دعيت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r3.speaker: قتادة والربيع وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r3.claim: Qatāda, al-Rabīʿ, and Ibn ʿAbbās interpret the summons as a request to bear witness and enter it in writing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة والربيع وابن عباس: أي لتحملها وإثباتها في الكتاب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r4.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r4.claim: Mujāhid interprets the summons as a request to give testimony already held; he and others say an initial invitation to witness may be declined.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معنى الآية إذا دعيت إلى أداء شهادة وقد حصلت عندك

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r5.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya treats assistance as recommended when witnesses are plentiful, increasingly urgent when rights may be lost, and obligatory when delay will destroy a right.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والآية كما قال الحسن جمعت أمرين على جهة الندب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r6.claim: Al-Qurṭubī infers that a ruler may employ public witnesses and support them from the treasury to preserve people's rights; this is public support like judges' salaries, not a fee.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#18/r6.anchor: دليل على أن جائزا للإمام أن يقيم للناس شهودا ويجعل لهم من بيت المال كفايتهم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r1.claim: The verse indicates that witnesses go to the judge when summoned, a practice established across legal traditions and reflected in a proverb.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r1.anchor: دل على أن الشاهد هو الذي يمشي إلى الحاكم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r2.claim: An enslaved person is excluded from the witness class because he cannot independently answer a summons, just as he lacks independent authority in other duties.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r2.anchor: لأنه لا يمكنه أن يجيب، ولا يصح له أن يأتي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī rejects the view that testimony already held is merely recommended: it is obligatory when a right risks loss, supported by Qurʾānic commands and the Prophet's call to aid the wronged.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r3.anchor: والصحيح أن أداءها فرض وإن لم يسألها إذا خاف على الحق ضياعه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r4.speaker: ابن القاسم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r4.claim: Ibn al-Qāsim and others say refusing a required testimony damages the witness and testimony generally, whether the right belongs to God or a person.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī prefers general disqualification: wrongful refusal is misconduct that removes eligibility for testimony altogether.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#19/r5.anchor: والصحيح الأول لأن الذي يوجب جرحته إنما هو فسقه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r1.claim: Praise of witnesses who volunteer testimony does not conflict with a report condemning people who testify without being asked; the latter has three possible readings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r1.anchor: وهذا الحديث محمول على ثلاثة أوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r2.claim: Ibn Abī Shayba reports that ʿUmar warned of later false testimony, distinguishing corrupt witnesses from truthful help preserving rights.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r2.anchor: وذكر أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه خطب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r3.claim: One interpretation is that greed or bias makes a person eagerly present testimony before being asked; Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī reports that boys were warned against contracts and testimony.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r3.anchor: يحمله الشره على تنفيذ ما يشهد به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r4.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the verb for becoming weary as boredom and gives its verbal nouns; an unnamed poet illustrates weariness after eighty years of life.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#20/r4.anchor: معناه تملوا. قال الأخفش: يقال سئمت أسأم سأما

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r1.claim: The writing phrase is accusative after the verb, and small or large are circumstantial descriptions; small comes first for emphasis, since people might neglect tiny debts.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r2.speaker: علماؤنا
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r2.claim: The jurists except a tiny amount such as a qirat because people do not normally care to affirm or deny it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r2.anchor: قال علماؤنا: إلا ما كان من قيراط ونحوه لنزارته

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r3.claim: The verse's terms mean fairest, soundest and most protective for testimony, closer, and that people should not doubt.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r3.anchor: معناه أعدل، يعني أن يكتب القليل والكثير ويشهد عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r4.speaker: ابن المنذر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r4.claim: Ibn al-Mundhir says most scholars reject testimony based solely on handwriting when the witness no longer remembers; Mālik argues from Joseph's report.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r4.anchor: قال ابن المنذر: أكثر من يحفظ عنه من أهل العلم يمنع أن يشهد الشاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r5.speaker: ابن المبارك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r5.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak approves the report that a witness may testify from a document bearing his mark or handwriting even if he forgot the testimony.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r5.anchor: قال ابن المبارك: استحسنت هذا جدا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r6.claim: Reports of the Prophet's judgments and earlier prophets support accepting reliable signs and indications as evidence.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#21/r6.anchor: حكم في أشياء غير واحدة بالدلائل والشواهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r1.speaker: الأخفش أبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r1.claim: Al-Akhfash explains the exception as a sale that occurs immediately; other grammarians parse its predicate differently, while ʿĀṣim reads an implicit subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r1.anchor: قال الأخفش أبو سعيد: أي إلا أن تقع تجارة، فكان بمعنى وقع

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r2.claim: God lifts writing requirements for cash exchanges, commonly small purchases, because writing them would be burdensome; al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk specify hand-to-hand sales.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r2.anchor: نص على ترك ذلك ورفع الجناح فيه في كل مبايعة بنقد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r3.claim: Immediate reciprocal possession reduces disputes, while real estate and animals are less readily transferred or hidden; deferred transactions need written safeguards against changed circumstances and distrust.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r3.anchor: فكان الكتاب توثقا لما عسى أن يطرأ من اختلاف الأحوال وتغير القلوب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r4.speaker: الشافعي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r4.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī classifies sales as documented with witnesses, secured by a pledge, or based on trust, reading the verse as evidence for these forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r4.anchor: قال الشافعي: البيوع ثلاثة: بيع بكتاب وشهود، وبيع برهان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar would obtain witnesses for cash sales and write down deferred sales.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r5.anchor: وكان ابن عمر إذا باع بنقد أشهد، وإذا باع بنسيئة كتب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r6.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reads the witnessing command as covering small and large sales; Abū Mūsā, Ibn ʿUmar, and others hold it obligatory, and ʿAṭāʾ demands witnesses for tiny purchases.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r6.anchor: قال الطبري: معناه وأشهدوا على صغير ذلك وكبيره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r7.speaker: الشعبي والحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and al-Ḥasan treat witnessing as recommendation and guidance rather than a binding duty; Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and other jurists are also said to hold this.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r7.anchor: وذهب الشعبي والحسن إلى أن ذلك على الندب والإرشاد لا على الحتم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r8.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r8.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says the recommendation is the view of all jurists and is correct.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#22/r8.anchor: وزعم ابن العربي أن هذا قول الكافة، قال: وهو الصحيح

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r1.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r1.claim: Ibn al-ʿArabī says only al-Ḍaḥḥāk is reported to require witnessing; the Prophet made and recorded sales without witnesses and pledged his armor without them.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r1.anchor: ولم يحك عن أحد ممن قال بالوجوب إلا الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r2.claim: Al-Qurṭubī notes that the obligation was attributed to several authorities besides al-Ḍaḥḥāk, correcting Ibn al-ʿArabī's account.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r2.anchor: قلت: قد ذكرنا الوجوب عن غير الضحاك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds mandatory witnessing impractical for small sales and sometimes socially awkward; he treats it as recommended for its usual benefit unless an excuse intervenes.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r3.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو محمد بن عطية: والوجوب في ذلك قلق، أما في الدقائق فصعب شاق

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r4.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan, al-Ḥakam, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd are reported to say that the mutual-trust clause abrogated witnessing sales.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r4.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذا قول الحسن والحكم وعبد الرحمن بن زيد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r5.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects abrogation: the pledge clause addresses inability to find a scribe and an unrequired pledge, a different case from writing and witnessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#23/r5.anchor: قال الطبري: وهذا لا معنى له لأن هذا حكم غير الأول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r1.claim: Later rules for different situations do not abrogate earlier rules; some note both clauses may have been revealed together, since abrogation cannot occur simultaneously.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r1.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يرد الناسخ والمنسوخ معا جميعا في حالة واحدة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt verse is established, not abrogated, and writing, pledges, and witnesses are alternative means of securing debt; witnessing is recommended like pledging.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r2.anchor: قال: وقد روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال لما قيل له: إن آية الدين منسوخة قال: لا والله إن آية الدين محكمة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r3.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says explicit Sunnah showing the Prophet accepted a sale without witnesses is an even stronger argument against mandatory witnessing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r3.anchor: وأحسن منه ما جاء من صريح السنة في ترك الإشهاد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r4.speaker: طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r4.claim: Ṭāriq ibn ʿAbd Allāh recounts selling a camel to a man later identified as the Prophet; the Prophet sent word for the sellers to take dates and eat until satisfied, without witnesses at the sale.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#24/r4.anchor: وهو ما خرجه الدارقطني عن طارق بن عبد الله المحاربي قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r1.speaker: عمارة بن خزيمة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r1.claim: ʿUmāra ibn Khuzayma reports that his Companion uncle witnessed the Prophet's purchase of a horse from a Bedouin, and Khuzayma ibn Thābit testified from trust in the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r1.anchor: عن عمارة بن خزيمة أن عمه حدثه وهو من أصحاب النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r2.speaker: خزيمة بن ثابت
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r2.claim: The Prophet made Khuzayma's testimony count as that of two men because he testified on the basis of believing the Prophet.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r2.anchor: قال خزيمة بن ثابت: أنا أشهد أنك قد بعته. فأقبل النبي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r3.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وطاوس وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan, Qatāda, Ṭāwūs, and Ibn Zayd say a scribe must write only what is dictated and a witness must neither add to nor subtract from testimony.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r3.anchor: لا يكتب الكاتب ما لم يمل عليه، ولا يزيد الشاهد في شهادته ولا ينقص منها. قاله الحسن وقتادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ interpret the prohibition as forbidding a scribe or witness from refusing when asked to serve.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#25/r4.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وعطاء أن المعنى لا يمتنع الكاتب أن يكتب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r1.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r1.claim: Al-Naḥḥās reports Abū Isḥāq's preference for the reading that forbids falsifying a record or testimony, since the warning of sin fits dishonesty better than burdening a busy witness.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r1.anchor: قال النحاس: ورأيت أبا إسحاق يميل إلى هذا القول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وطاوس والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r2.claim: Mujāhid, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, Ṭāwūs, and al-Suddī understand the verse to forbid harassing a busy scribe or witness who gives a reasonable excuse; Ibn Masʿūd has a similar reading.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك وطاوس والسدي وروي عن ابن عباس: معنى الآية { ولا يضآر كاتب ولا شهيد }

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r3.claim: The reciprocal form encompasses both kinds of harm: dishonest additions and omissions wrongfully affect people and property, while imposing on busy witnesses violates God's command.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r3.anchor: ولفظ المضارة إذ هو من اثنين، يقتضي هذه المعاني

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r4.speaker: سفيان الثوري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r4.claim: Sufyān al-Thawrī explains 'it is wrongdoing by you' as meaning a sinful act; falsifying testimony and imposing on busy witnesses are both disobedience.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r4.anchor: أي معصية عن سفيان الثوري. فالكاتب والشاهد يعصيان بالزيادة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r5.claim: God promises that reverent people receive understanding and discernment to distinguish truth from falsehood, sometimes placed directly in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#26/r5.anchor: يجعل في قلبه نورا يفهم به ما يلقى إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#27/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#27/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#27/r1.claim: The promise that piety gives believers discernment is linked to the verse promising a criterion by which to distinguish right from wrong.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:282#27/r1.anchor: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إن تتقوا الله يجعل لكم فرقانا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r1.claim: The omitted object of ‘refuse’ is establishing the testimony.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r1.anchor: مفعوله محذوف لفهم المعنى، أي: لا يأبون إقامة الشهادة،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r2.claim: Alternatively, ‘refuse’ takes a deleted preposition because it means ‘refrain’; the sense is refraining from establishing testimony.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r2.anchor: وقيل: المحذوف مجرور لأن " أبى " بمعنى امتنع، فيتعدى تعديته

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r3.claim: ‘When they are summoned’ can be a temporal adverb modifying ‘refuse,’ meaning when called to perform or establish testimony.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r3.anchor: ظرف ل " يأب " أي: لا يمتنعون في وقت دعوتهم

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r4.claim: The phrase may instead be purely temporal, without conditional force.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r5.claim: Alternatively, it is conditional, with an omitted answer: when called, they should not refuse.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون شرطية والجواب محذوف أي: إذا دعوا فلا يأبوا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r6.claim: The infinitive clause is the direct object of ‘tire,’ which is directly transitive; a poetic line supports this construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r6.anchor: مفعول به والناصب له " تسأموا " لأنه يتعدى بنفسه قال

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r7.claim: Another analysis supplies the preposition min before the infinitive; a second poem shows ‘tire’ used with min.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r7.anchor: وقيل: بل يتعدى بحرف الجر، والأصل: من أن تكتبوه، فحذف حرف الجر

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r8.claim: Saʾam and saʾāma mean weariness, boredom, and annoyance with something.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r8.anchor: والسأم والسآمة: الملل من الشيء والضجر منه.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r9.claim: The pronoun in ‘write it’ may refer to the debt or the right; the latter is nearer, though it also means the debt.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r9.anchor: يجوز أن تكون للدين في أول الآية، وأن تكون للحق في قوله: " فإن كان الذي عليه الحق " وهو أقرب مذكور

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r10.claim: Zamakhshari says the pronoun may refer to the written document understood from ‘write it.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r10.anchor: يعود على الكتاب المفهوم من " يكتبوه " قاله الزمخشري.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r11.claim: ‘Small or large’ is circumstantial: either the debt is small or large, or the written record is brief or detailed.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r11.anchor: و " صغيرا أو كبيرا " حال، أي: على أي حال كان الدين قليلا أو كثيرا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r12.speaker: السجاوندي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r12.claim: Al-Sajawandi treats ‘small or large’ as the predicate of an implied kāna; the author says this is unnecessary and unsupported here.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r12.anchor: وجوز السجاوندي انتصابه على خبر " كان " مضمرة، وهذا لا حاجة تدعوا إليه

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r13.speaker: السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r13.claim: Al-Sulami reads both verbs with third-person yāʾ; the subject can be the witnesses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r13.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: { ولا يسأموا أن يكتبوه } بالياء من تحت فيهما. والفاعل على هذه القراءة ضمير الشهداء

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r14.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r14.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r14.claim: On the yāʾ reading, the subject may instead shift to the contracting parties or the scribe.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#15/r14.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون من باب الالتفات، فيعود: إما على المتعاملين وإما على الكتاب.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r1.claim: The phrase ‘until its term’ most clearly modifies an implied phrase: the debt remains established in liability until it falls due.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r1.anchor: أنه متعلق بمحذوف أي: أن تكتبوه مستقرا في الذمة إلى أجل حلوله.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r2.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r2.claim: Abu al-Baqa attaches ‘until its term’ directly to ‘write it.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه متعلق بتكتبوه، قاله أبو البقاء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r3.claim: The Shaykh rejects attachment to ‘write’: writing ends quickly and does not continue until the debt is due.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r3.anchor: رده الشيخ فقال: " هو متعلق بمحذوف لا ب " تكتبوه " لعدم استمرار الكتابة إلى أجل الدين

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r4.claim: A third analysis makes the phrase a circumstantial clause referring to the pronoun in ‘write it.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r4.anchor: والثالث: أن يتعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من الهاء، قاله أبو البقاء.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r5.claim: ‘That’ may refer only to writing, to writing and testimony, or to all the preceding instructions; the broadest reference is best.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r5.anchor: ذلكم } مشار به لأقرب مذكور وهو الكتب. وقيل إليه وإلى الإشهاد، وقيل: إلى جميع ما ذكر وهو أحسن.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r6.claim: One derivation takes ‘more equitable’ from quadriliteral aqsaṭ, ‘act justly’; this makes the hamza privative but requires an anomalous comparative from a quadriliteral.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r6.anchor: قيل: هو من أقسط إذا عدل، ولا يكون من قسط، لأن قسط بمعنى جار، وأقسط بمعنى عدل،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r7.claim: Zamakhshari says the comparatives may derive from aqsaṭ and aqāma, or from nisba forms meaning ‘possessing equity’ and ‘upright.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r7.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " إن قلت مم بني أفعلا التفضيل - أعني أقسط وأقوم؟ - قلت: يجوز على مذهب سيبويه أن يكونا مبنيين من " أقسط " و " أقام "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r8.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r8.claim: The Shaykh says Sibawayh did not explicitly state that comparatives derive from quadrilaterals; this is inferred from his rules for the exclamative form.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r8.anchor: قال الشيخ: لم ينص سيبويه على أن أفعل التفضيل يبنى من " أفعل " ، إنما يؤخذ ذلك بالاستدلال

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r9.claim: Grammarians differ among unrestricted permission, unrestricted prohibition, and permission only when the hamza is not causative; the last reading explains Sibawayh.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#16/r9.anchor: اختلف النحويون في بناء التعجب وأفعل التفضيل من أفعل على ثلاثة مذاهب

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r1.claim: Ibn Atiyya derives aqsaṭ from the triliteral qasuṭ with ḍamma, like akram from karuma.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r1.anchor: ونقل ابن عطية أنه مأخوذ من " قسط " بضم السين نحو: " أكرم " من " كرم ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r2.claim: Another derivation takes it from qist, ‘justice,’ a noun without a verb; this avoids deriving a comparative from ifʿāl.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r2.anchor: وقيل: هو من القسط بالكسر وهو العدل، وهو مصدر لم يشتق منه فعل،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r3.claim: These etymologies assume the triliteral means injustice and the quadriliteral means justice.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r3.anchor: بناء منهم على أن الثلاثي بمعنى الجور والرباعي بمعنى العدل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r4.claim: When al-Hajjaj asked his judgment, Saʿid b. Jubayr called him ‘qāsiṭ, ʿādil,’ making a pointed double-edged description.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r4.anchor: ويحكى أن سعيد بن جبير لما سأله الظالم [الحجاج] بن يوسف: ما تقول في؟ فقال: " أقول إنك قاسط عادل "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r5.claim: If q-s-ṭ can mean both justice and injustice, the ambiguity is straightforward; Ibn al-Qattaʿ records both opposite senses.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r5.anchor: قال ابن القطاع: " قسط قسوطا وقسطا: جار وعدل ضد ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r6.speaker: أبو عبيدة
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r6.claim: Abu Ubayda, as cited through Ibn al-Sikkit, distinguishes qasaṭ as injustice or justice by vocalization, while aqsaṭ always means justice.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة: " قسط: جار، وقسط: عدل، وأقسط بالألف عدل لا غير.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r7.speaker: الراغب الأصفهاني
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r7.claim: Al-Raghib says taking another’s share is qist and injustice, while giving that share is iqsaṭ and fairness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r7.anchor: وقال أبو القاسم الراغب الأصبهاني: " القسط أن يأخذ قسط غيره، وذلك جور، والإقساط أن يعطي قسط غيره، وذلك إنصاف،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r8.claim: ‘With God’ is an adverb modifying ‘more equitable,’ meaning in God’s judgment.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r8.anchor: ظرف منصوب ب " أقسط " أي: في حكمه.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r9.claim: The wāw in aqwam is valid because a comparative can follow the pattern of the exclamative, which functions like a noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r9.anchor: وقوله " وأقوم " إنما صحت الواو فيه لأنه أفعل تفضيل، وأفعل التفضيل يصح حملا على فعل التعجب،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r10.claim: Aqwam may come from transitive aqāma with its extra hamza removed, meaning firmer for establishing testimony; the analogy is 18:12.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r10.anchor: و " أقوم " يجوز أن يكون من " أقام " الرباعي المتعدي؛ لكنه حذف الهمزة الزائدة، ثم أتى بهمزة أفعل

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r11.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r11.claim: Abu al-Baqa derives aqwam from intransitive qāma, meaning that testimony itself is more firmly established.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r11.anchor: و " أقوم " يجوز أن يكون من " أقام " الرباعي المتعدي؛ لكنه حذف الهمزة الزائدة، ثم أتى بهمزة أفعل كقوله تعالى:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r12.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r12.claim: The lām in ‘for testimony’ attaches to aqwam and is semantically an object; it is extra if aqwam means ‘establish,’ but not if it means ‘be established.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r12.anchor: قوله: " للشهادة متعلق ب " أقوم " ، وهو مفعول في المعنى، واللام زائدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r13.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r13.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r13.claim: The lām cannot normally be dropped to make its complement an accusative after a comparative, except under poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#17/r13.anchor: ولا يجوز حذفها ونصب مجرورها بعد أفعل التفضيل إلا ضرورة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r1.claim: The cited poetic phrase has an accusative after a comparative; one analysis supplies an implied verb indicated by the comparative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r1.anchor: وقد قيل: إن " القوانس " منصوب بمضمر يدل عليه أفعل التفضيل، هذا معنى كلام الشيخ

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r2.claim: ‘So that you do not doubt’ has a deleted preposition; proposed choices are lām, ilā, or min, but min does not fit the sense.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r2.anchor: حرف الجر محذوف، فقيل: هو اللام أي: أدنى لئلا ترتابوا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r3.claim: Tartābū is form VIII from rayba; its original yāʾ becomes alif because it is vowelled after an open syllable.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r3.anchor: و " ترتابوا ": تفتعلوا من الريبة، والصل: " ترتيبوا " ، فقلبت الياء ألفا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r4.claim: The comparison’s second term is omitted because context supplies it: writing is more equitable, stable, and doubt-free than leaving the debt undocumented.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r4.anchor: والمفضل عليه محذوف لفهم المعنى، أي: أقسط وأقوم وأدنى لكذا من عدم الكتب، وحسن الحذف

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r5.claim: Omission is smoother when the comparative is a predicate than when it is an adjective or circumstantial phrase.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r5.anchor: وحسن الحذف كون أفعل خبرا للمبتدأ بخلاف كونه صفة أو حالا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r6.speaker: السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r6.claim: Al-Sulami reads the clause with third-person yāʾ, matching his reading of ‘they tire of writing.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#18/r6.anchor: وقرأ السلمين: { أن لا يرتابوا] بياء الغيبة كقراءة: { ولا يسأموا أن يكتبوه }

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r1.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r1.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats the trade exception as connected: from all transactions requiring testimony, it excludes the case of present trade.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r1.anchor: الجملة المستثناة في موضع نصب لأنه استثناء من الجنس لأنه أمر بالاستشهاد في كل معاملة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r2.speaker: مكي ابن أبي طالب
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r2.claim: Makki b. Abi Talib calls the exception disconnected; the author prefers this reading as the apparent sense, permitting omission of writing and witnesses for immediate trade.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r2.anchor: والثاني: أنه منقطع، قال مكي ابن أبي طالب: " و " أن " في موضع نصب على الاستثناء المنقطع " قلت: وهذا هو الظاهر،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r3.claim: ʿAsim reads ‘trade’ and its adjective in the accusative; in al-Nisaʾ the two other Kūfan readers agree, while the rest read both nominative.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r3.anchor: وقرأ عاصم هنا " تجارة " بالنصب، وكذلك " حاضرة " لأنها صفتها، وفي النساء وافقه الأخوان،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r4.claim: With nominative, kāna may be complete, meaning a trade occurs; ‘you circulate it’ is then an adjectival clause, a more idiomatic order.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r4.anchor: أنها التامة أي: إلا أن تحدث أو تقع تجارة، وعلى هذا فتكون " تديرونها " في محل رفع صفة لتجارة أيضا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r5.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r5.claim: Alternatively, kāna is incomplete: ‘trade’ is its subject and ‘you circulate it’ its predicate; al-Farraʾ and others adopt this.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r5.anchor: والثاني: ان تكون الناقصة، واسمها " تجارة " والخبر هو الجملة من قوله: " تديرونها "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r6.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r6.claim: For ʿAsim’s accusative reading, al-Zajjaj supplies an omitted subject for kāna, estimating ‘debt transaction.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r6.anchor: وقدره الزجاج إلا أن تكون المداينة، وهو أحسن.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r7.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r7.claim: Al-Farisi rejects ‘debt transaction’ as kāna’s subject because a debt is an obligation, unlike the present trade named in the predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r7.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون التداين اسم كان لأن التداين معنى، والتجارة الحاضرة يراد بها العين،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r8.claim: The author says al-Farisi’s objection does not answer al-Zajjaj, since trade too is a verbal noun and thus an abstract meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r8.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله الفارسي لا يظهر ردا على أبي إسحاق، لأن التجارة أيضا مصدر، فهي معنى من المعاني لا عين من الأعيان،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r9.speaker: الفارسي
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r9.claim: Al-Farisi also rules out ‘the right’ as kāna’s subject because it is a debt, so an omitted subject must be supplied.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#19/r9.anchor: وقال الفارسي أيضا: " ولا يجوز أيضا أن يكون اسمها " الحق " الذي في قوله: " فإن كان الذي عليه الحق "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r1.claim: One possible omitted subject of kāna is ‘transaction,’ understood from the preceding commands; Sibawayh gives a similar contextual ellipsis.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r1.anchor: فدى لبني ذهل بن شيبان ناقتي إذا كان يوما ذا كواكب أشهبا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r2.claim: A poem using ‘when there was stabbing and embracing’ supplies an omitted ‘matter’ as the subject of kāna.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r2.anchor: أعيني هلا تبكيان عفاقا إذا كان طعنا بينهم وعناقا

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r3.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r3.claim: Another analysis supplies ‘trade’ twice: ‘unless there is trade, as a trade’; al-Farraʾ and al-Zamakhshari cite poetic parallels with an understood repeated noun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r3.anchor: والثاني: أن يكون أضمر التجارة كأنه قيل: إلا أن تكون التجارة تجارة، ومثله ما أنشده الفراء:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r4.claim: ‘Between you’ is an adverb modifying ‘you circulate it.’

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r5.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r5.claim: Abu al-Baqa says the fāʾ in ‘there is no blame’ signals that the following clause depends on the preceding one.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r5.anchor: قال أبو البقاء: " دخلت الفاء في " فليس " إيذانا بتعلق ما بعدها بما قبلها " قلت:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r6.claim: The author analyzes the fāʾ as conjunction to the whole exception clause, with clear causal force: the immediate transaction explains the dispensation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r6.anchor: هي عاطفة هذه الجملة على الجملة من قوله: { إلا أن تكون تجارة } إلى آخرها، والسببية فيها واضحة

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r7.claim: ‘That you do not write it’ means ‘in not writing it’; the preposition is omitted, leaving the two constructions discussed for an infinitive after its deletion.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#20/r7.anchor: وقوله: { ألا تكتبوها } أي: " في أن لا " ، فحذف حرف الجر فبقي في موضع " أن " الوجهان:

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r1.claim: ‘When you trade’ may be conditional, answered by a preceding clause or an omitted ‘then bear witness’; alternatively it is purely temporal.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r1.anchor: يجوز أن/ تكون شرطية، وجوابها: إما متقدم عند قوم، وإما محذوف لدلالة ما تقدم عليه تقديره: إذا تبايعتم فأشهدوا،

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r2.claim: On the temporal reading, the instruction is to witness at the time of trading.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ظرفا محضا أي: افعلوا الشهادة وقت التبايع.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r3.claim: The common reading has fatḥ on the final rāʾ in the jussive prohibition; lā is prohibitive, and the vowel follows the rule seen in the reading of ‘if one errs.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r3.anchor: العامة على فتح الراء جزما، و " لا " ناهية، وفتح الفعل لما تقدم في قراءة حمزة: " إن تضل ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r4.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r4.claim: On the active reading, the scribe and witness are forbidden to harm the beneficiary by altering or withholding documentation; al-Zajjaj prefers it because such conduct is clearly sinful.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r4.anchor: واختاره الزجاج، ورجحه بأن الله تعالى قال: { فإنه فسوق بكم }

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وطاووس
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Tawus are reported to explain the active reading as the scribe or witness harming the party entitled to the record.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r5.anchor: ونقل في التفسير عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وطاووس هذا المعنى

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r6.speaker: عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد وابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r6.claim: Al-Dani reports these authorities reading the first rāʾ with kasra, supporting the active interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r6.anchor: ونقل الداني عن عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد وابن أبي إسحاق أنهم قرؤوا الراء الأولى بالكسر

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r7.claim: On the passive reading, no one may harm the scribe or witness; its context concerns those receiving the writing and testimony, and the consequence would otherwise address two people.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r7.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون الفعل فيها مبنيا للمفعول، والمعنى: أن أحدا لا يضارر الكاتب ولا الشاهد، ورجح هذا بأنه لو كان النهي متوجها نحو الكاتب والشهيد

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r8.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وطاووس
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r8.claim: The passive interpretation is also transmitted in tafsir from Ibn Abbas and the other named authorities.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r8.anchor: ونقل في التفسير هذا المعنى عن ابن عباس ومن ذكر معه

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r9.speaker: عمر وابن عباس ومجاهد وابن أبي إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r9.claim: Al-Dani reports these authorities reading the first rāʾ with fatḥa, matching the passive interpretation.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r9.anchor: وذكر الداني أيضا عنهم أنهم قرؤوا الراء الأولى بالفتح

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r10.claim: The readings and explanations alternate because the verse permits both interpretations.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r10.anchor: إذ الآية عندهم محتملة للوجهين فسروا وقرؤوا بهذا المعنى تارة وبالآخر أخرى

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r11.speaker: أبو جعفر وعمرو بن عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r11.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read the doubled rāʾ sākin in connected speech; the author notes the three-consonant cluster is weak, tolerated by lengthening and by analogy to pause.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وعمرو بن عبيد: " ولا يضار " بتشديد الراء ساكنة وصلا، وفيها ضعف من حيث الجمع بين ثلاث سواكن

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r12.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r12.speaker: عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r12.claim: ʿIkrima reads the form with both rāʾs separated and the first kasra; the implied subject is the rights-holder, who must not coerce the scribe or witness.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#21/r12.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة/: " ولا يضارر كاتبا ولا شهيدا " بالفك وكسر الراء الأولى، والفاعل ضمير صاحب الحق

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r1.speaker: ابن محيصن
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r1.claim: Ibn Muhaysin reads the rāʾ nominative as a negation whose report-like form conveys a prohibition, as in 2:197.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن محيصن: " ولا يضار " برفع الراء، وهو نفي فيكون الخبر بمعنى النهي

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r2.speaker: عكرمة
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r2.claim: In a report from Miqsam, ʿIkrima reads doubled rāʾ with kasra, reflecting the original meeting of two sukūns.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r2.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة في رواية مقسم: " ولا يضار " بكسر الراء مشددة على أصل التقاء الساكنين.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r3.claim: The related grammatical and reading issues were discussed under the prohibition against a mother being harmed in 2:233.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r3.anchor: وقد تقدم لك تحقيق هذه الأشياء عند قوله لا تضار والدة بولدها

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r4.claim: ‘If you do’ means any act forbidden by God; its object is omitted because context supplies it.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r4.anchor: أي: تفعلوا شيئا مما نهى الله عنه، فحذف المفعول به للعلم به.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r5.claim: The pronoun in ‘it is’ may refer to refusal or to harm.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r5.anchor: والضمير في " فإنه " يعود على الامتناع أو الإضرار.

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r6.claim: Abu al-Baqa supplies ‘incumbent upon you’ after ‘upon you’; the author instead supplies an unrestricted state as an adjective of ‘transgression.’
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r6.anchor: فقدره أبو البقاء: " لاحق بكم " وينبغي أن يقدر كونا مطلقا، لأنه صفة ل " فسوق "

SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r7.claim: ‘God teaches you’ is most likely an independent sentence; Abu al-Baqa also allows a circumstantial clause, but the author objects that a positive present verb does not directly follow the circumstantial wāw.
SAMIN-DURR:2:282#22/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون حالا من الفاعل في " اتقوا " قال أبو البقاء: " تقديره: واتقوا الله مضمونا لكم التعليم

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.claim: Malik and one Shafi'i view restore guardianship if a released person becomes wasteful; Abu Hanifa says it cannot return, but al-Qurtubi cites the Quran's protection of wealth and its provision for a guardian when a debtor becomes foolish or weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#8/r3.anchor: ثم عاد إلى السفه بظهور تبذير وقلة تدبير عاد إليه الحجر عندنا

RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.claim: The detailed debt-recording rule follows commands to give charity, avoid usury, and remain mindful of God: preserving lawful wealth enables those duties and protects worldly and religious interests.
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r1.anchor: ندبه إلى كيفية حفظ المال الحلال وصونه عن الفساد والبوار فإن القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.claim: Al-Qaffal sees the verse’s unusually repeated instructions as deliberate emphasis: careful documentation preserves lawful wealth needed for charity and avoidance of forbidden gain.
RAZI-FULL:v7p93#2/r2.anchor: ألفاظ القرآن جارية في الأكثر على الاختصار ، وفي هذه الآية بسط شديد

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r1.speaker: قوم من المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r1.claim: Some exegetes take the debt transaction here as salam, which provides the benefits sought through usury by a lawful route; the author approves this as a second coherent link.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r1.anchor: والوجه الثاني : أن قوما من المفسرين قالوا : المراد بالمداينة السلم

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r2.claim: A second account of the passage’s arrangement says the ban on usury is followed by permission for salam, which offers the same desired benefits through lawful means.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r2.anchor: لما منع الربا في الآية المتقدمة أذن في السلم في جميع هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r3.claim: The commentators distinguish a loan, which they say cannot stipulate a term, from a debt sale whose payment may be deferred; the verse’s specified term therefore points beyond a loan.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r3.anchor: القرض غير الدين ، لأن القرض أن يقرض الإنسان دراهم ، أو دنانير

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r4.speaker: الأحمر
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r4.claim: Al-Ahmar cites a line using dāna for borrowing and repayment to illustrate the verb’s debt-related meanings.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r4.anchor: ندين ويقضي الله عنا وقد نرى

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed about forward sales: people in Medina prepaid for dates two or three years ahead, and the Prophet required known measure, weight, and term.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أنها نزلت في السلف لأن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r6.claim: Al-Razi rejects interpreting the debt as a loan because he says a loan cannot stipulate the deferred term specified in the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r6.anchor: القرض وهو ضعيف لما بينا أن القرض لا يمكن أن يشترط فيه الأجل

RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r7.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r7.claim: Most exegetes include both a sale of present goods for deferred payment and salam, while excluding cash-for-cash and debt-for-debt exchanges.
RAZI-FULL:v7p94/r7.anchor: قول أكثر المفسرين : أن البياعات على أربعة أوجه

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r1.claim: Although reciprocal form tadāyantum might suggest each party incurs a debt, al-Razi reads it broadly as transacting in a way that results in a debt.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r1.anchor: المراد من تداينتم تعاملتم ، والتقدير : إذا تعاملتم بما فيه دين

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says bidayn specifies the financial sense of tadāyantum, since the verb can also mean reciprocal recompense.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r2.anchor: التداين يكون لمعنيين أحدهما : التداين / بالمال ، والآخر التداين بمعنى المجازاة

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r3.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r3.claim: The author of al-Kashshaf explains that bidayn supplies the antecedent for the pronoun in فاكتبوه and improves the sentence’s ordering.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r3.anchor: إنما ذكر الدين ليرجع الضمير إليه في قوله { فاكتبوه }

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r4.claim: The word bidayn may be emphatic, as in the Qur’anic phrases فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون and ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r4.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكره للتأكيد ، كقوله تعالى : { فسجد الملائكة كلهم أجمعون }

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r5.claim: Bidayn can also generalize the rule to small or large transactions and to loans, salam, or deferred sales.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r5.anchor: فإذا تداينتم أي دين كان صغيرا أو كبيرا

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r6.claim: Al-Razi’s own explanation is that adding bidayn limits the reciprocal form to transactions producing one debt, thereby excluding invalid debt-for-debt exchange.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r6.anchor: لما قال : { إذا تداينتم بدين } كان المعنى : إذا تداينتم تداينا يحصل فيه دين واحد

RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r7.claim: Although idha alone does not express universal scope, the stated rationale applies to every debt transaction: documentation prevents mistaken claims of increase or loss.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95/r7.anchor: كلمة { إذا } وإن كانت لا تقتضي العموم ، إلا أنها لا تمنع من العموم

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.claim: An appointed term is a future time at which the period ends; its root conveys delay, and a specified debt term must be objectively known, such as by year, month, or days.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r1.anchor: الأجل في اللغة هو الوقت المضروب لانقضاء الأمد ، وأجل الإنسان

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.claim: Terms such as harvest, threshing, or the pilgrims’ arrival are invalid because they do not specify a determinate date.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r2.anchor: ولو قال : إلى الحصاد ، أو إلى الدياس ، أو إلى قدوم الحاج

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r3.claim: Writing and witnesses protect both sides when payment is deferred: the creditor avoids premature or excessive demands, and the debtor avoids denial and can prepare payment.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r3.anchor: فائدة الكتبة والإشهاد أن ما يدخل فيه الأجل ، تتأخر فيه المطالبة

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r4.speaker: عطاء وابن جريج والنخعي والطبري
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r4.claim: ʿAtaʾ, Ibn Jurayj, al-Nakhaʿi, and al-Tabari hold that writing and witnessing deferred debts are obligatory; al-Nakhaʿi even requires witnessing a tiny vegetable purchase.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r4.anchor: فقال قوم بالوجوب وهو مذهب عطاء ، وابن جريج والنخعي

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r5.speaker: جمهور الفقهاء المجتهدين
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r5.claim: Most jurists treat the commands as recommendations, citing Muslims’ customary deferred sales without records and the hardship obligatory documentation would cause.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r5.anchor: هذا الأمر محمول على الندب ، وعلى هذا جمهور الفقهاء المجتهدين

RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r6.speaker: الحسن والشعبي والحكم وابن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r6.claim: A group says documentation was once obligatory and was abrogated by the permission to rely on mutual trust in the following verse; al-Razi later rejects abrogation without proof.
RAZI-FULL:v7p95#2/r6.anchor: وقال قوم : بل كانت واجبة ، إلا أن ذلك صار منسوخا بقوله

RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r1.claim: The command to write does not require every person to write; it requires that the record be made by someone, as the command to cut a thief’s hand is fulfilled by an authorized agent.
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r1.anchor: المقصود منه أنه لا بد من حصول قطع اليد من إنسان واحد

RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r2.claim: A just record must neither inflate nor reduce the debt and must protect either party’s claim when needed.
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r2.anchor: أن يكتب بحيث لا يزيد في الدين ولا ينقص منه ، ويكتبه بحيث يصلح

RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r3.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r3.claim: Some jurists define justice in drafting as balanced protection for both disputants, agreement with recognized scholarly positions, and avoidance of ambiguous wording that invites dispute.
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r3.anchor: قال بعض الفقهاء : العدل أن يكون ما يكتبه متفقا عليه بين أهل العلم

RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r4.claim: Meeting those standards requires a writer skilled in jurisprudence and in distinguishing similar expressions.
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r4.anchor: لا يمكن رعايتها إلا إذا كان الكاتب فقيها عارفا بمذاهب المجتهدين

RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r5.claim: One reading treats the ban on a writer’s refusal as guidance: writing for another Muslim is gratitude for God’s gift of literacy and legal knowledge.
RAZI-FULL:v7p96/r5.anchor: على سبيل الارشاد إلى الأولى لا على سبيل الإيجاب

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r1.speaker: الشعبي
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbi regards writing as a communal obligation: one writer must act if no others are available, while one among several suffices.
