RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r1.anchor: وهو قول الشعبي : أنه فرض كفاية ، فإن لم يجد أحدا يكتب

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r2.claim: Another view says the writer’s duty was obligatory but later abrogated by the prohibition on harming writers and witnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r2.anchor: والقول الثالث : أن هذا كان واجبا على الكاتب ، ثم نسخ بقوله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r3.claim: A further interpretation makes the duty conditional: whoever writes must follow God’s taught rules and preserve every safeguard for the parties.
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r3.anchor: أن متعلق الإيجاب هو أن يكتب كما علمه الله ، يعني أن بتقدير أن يكتب

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r4.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj gives two grammatical attachments for كما علمه الله: it can complete the preceding ban on refusal or introduce the following command to write.
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r4.anchor: فيه احتمالان الأول : أن يكون متعلقا بما قبله / ولا يأب كاتب عن الكتابة التي علمه الله إياها

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r5.claim: The debtor must dictate an acknowledgment of the amount, kind, description, and due date so that the written contract is complete.
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r5.anchor: فليدخل في جملة إملائه اعترافه بما عليه من الحق في قدره

RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r6.claim: Al-Farraʾ notes that amlal and amla are dialectal alternatives: the first is associated with Hijaz and Banu Asad, the second with Tamim and Qays.
RAZI-FULL:v7p97/r6.anchor: أمللت عليه الكتاب لغة أهل الحجاز وبني أسد ، وأمليت لغة تميم وقيس

RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r1.claim: The debtor must dictate without diminishing any amount owed; if the debtor is not competent to make a valid acknowledgment, the guardian’s acknowledgment counts.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r1.anchor: وهذا أمر لهذا المملى الذي عليه الحق بأن يقر بمبلغ المال الذي عليه

RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r2.claim: The conjunction أو marks three distinct conditions: an adult with deficient judgment, someone lacking capacity such as a child or incapacitated elder, and someone unable to dictate because of speech or knowledge limitations.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r2.anchor: إدخال حرف { أو } بين هذه الألفاظ الثلاثة ، أعني السفيه ، والضعيف

RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r3.claim: For each of those three classes, the relevant guardian dictates fairly; the guardian of an incapacitated person can acknowledge debts as in the person’s other affairs.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r3.anchor: والمراد ولي كل واحد من هؤلاء الثلاثة ، لأن ولي المحجور السفيه

RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r4.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل والربيع
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, Muqatil, and al-Rabiʿ say the wali is the creditor, but al-Razi rejects this because a claimant’s assertion alone would make documentation and witnesses pointless.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس ومقاتل والربيع : المراد بوليه ولي الدين يعني أن الذي له الدين

RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r5.claim: The purpose of witnesses is to let the creditor establish the claim if the debtor later denies it; istashhidu means make someone testify, and shahidayn means two witnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98/r5.anchor: المقصود من الكتابة هو الاستشهاد لكي يتمكن بالشهود عند الجحود

RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r1.claim: Min rijalikum is variously read as men of the Muslim community, free men, or men considered fit to testify because of justice.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r1.anchor: فيه وجوه الأول : يعني من أهل ملتكم وهم المسلمون والثاني : قال بعضهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r2.speaker: شريح وابن سيرين وأحمد
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r2.claim: Shurayh, Ibn Sirin, and Ahmad accept an enslaved man’s testimony, arguing that the verse is general and that intellect, religion, and justice—not legal status—prevent lying.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r2.anchor: عند شريح وابن سيرين وأحمد تجوز شهادة العبد ، وعند الشافعي وأبي حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي وأبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r3.claim: Al-Shafiʿi and Abu Hanifa reject an enslaved person as a witness, reasoning that the command to attend testimony cannot be obligatory for slaves.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r3.anchor: حجة الشافعي وأبي حنيفة رضي الله عنهما قوله تعالى : { ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا }

RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi calls the argument against slave testimony strong, while noting that the general wording can be restricted to people already recognized as qualified witnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r4.anchor: وهذا الاستدلال حسن . وأما قوله تعالى : { واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم }

RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r5.speaker: علي بن عيسى
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r5.claim: Ali ibn ʿIsa gives four permissible implied predicates for the nominative phrase رجل وامرأتان, including let there be, let testify, or the witnesses are.
RAZI-FULL:v7p98#2/r5.anchor: وفي ارتفاع رجل وامرأتان أربعة أوجه الأول : فليكن رجل وامرأتان

RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r1.claim: The qualification ممن ترضون and the parallel divorce instruction show that not everyone may testify; jurists enumerate ten conditions, including freedom, adulthood, Islam, justice, knowledge, and lack of personal conflict or benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r1.anchor: هذه الآية تدل على أنه ليس كل أحد صالحا للشهادة والفقهاء قالوا

RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r2.claim: Al-Razi explains the two-women provision by saying a second woman can prompt the first if she forgets, which he attributes to women’s bodily temperament.
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r2.anchor: النسيان غالب طباع النساء لكثرة البرد والرطوبة في أمزجتهن

RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r3.speaker: حمزة
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r3.claim: Hamza reads إن with kasra and فتذكر as a raised, doubled form, taking the construction as conditional; the jussive of تضل is obscured by its doubled consonant.
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r3.anchor: قرأ حمزة { أن تضل } بكسر إن { فتذكر } بالرفع والتشديد

RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r4.speaker: سائر القراء
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r4.claim: Other readers use accusative أن, parsed either as لأن تضل with an elided preposition or as a purpose clause.
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r4.anchor: وأما سائر القراء فقرؤا بنصب { ءان } وفيه وجهان

RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r5.claim: Al-Razi answers the objection that testimony aims at remembrance by saying the wording serves both reliable testimony and the stated comparative legal treatment of men and women.
RAZI-FULL:v7p99/r5.anchor: ولا سبيل إلى ذلك إلا بضلال إحداهما وتذكر الأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r1.claim: Ḍalāl in the clause can mean forgetting, as in the verse about what vanished from people, or failing to find one’s way; Abu ʿAmr says its root sense is disappearance.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r1.anchor: الضلال في قوله { أن تضل إحداهما } فيه وجهان أحدهما : أنه بمعنى النسيان

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r2.speaker: نافع وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r2.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn ʿAmir, ʿAsim, and al-Kisaʾi read فتذكر with doubling and the subjunctive; Hamza doubles it with the indicative, while Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr use the lighter form.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r2.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم والكسائي { فتذكر } بالتشديد والنصب

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna interprets the second woman as making the first a male-equivalent witness, rather than reminding her of forgotten testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r3.anchor: إلا ما يروى عن سفيان بن عيينة أنه قال في قوله { فتذكر إحداهما الاخرى } أن تجعلها ذكرا

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r4.claim: Al-Razi rejects that interpretation as contrary to the general exegetical view: without a man, women’s testimony is not accepted, so the second woman does not simply make the first a witness.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه باطل باتفاق عامة المفسرين ، ويدل على ضعفه وجهان

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r5.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlaʾ also transmits the male-equivalent reading, explaining that the second woman’s testimony joins the first to make one man’s testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه منقول عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء ، قال : إذا شهدت المرأة ثم جاءت الأخرى

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r6.claim: Al-Razi says the sounder reading of the phrase forbidding witnesses to refuse is a ban on withholding testimony when the rights-holder needs it.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r6.anchor: وهو الأصح : أنه نهى الشاهد عن الامتناع عن أداء الشهادة عند احتياج صاحب الحق إليها

RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r7.speaker: قتادة والقفال
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r7.claim: Qatada and al-Qaffal instead understand the command as requiring a person to accept the burden of witnessing, so rights are not lost through lack of records or witnesses.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100/r7.anchor: وهو قول قتادة واختيار القفال ، قال : كما أمر الكاتب أن لا يأبى الكتابة

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r1.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads the command as covering both accepting testimony beforehand and giving it afterward.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r1.anchor: الثاني : أن ظاهر قوله { ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا } النهي عن الامتناع

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi favors testimony performance: the witnesses are already called witnesses, and the command is obligatory for all, whereas accepting testimony is not required of everyone.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r2.anchor: متأكد بقوله تعالى : { ولا تكتموا الشهادة } فكان هذا أولى

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r3.claim: Accepting testimony is already included in the command to appoint two witnesses, so reading the later command as performance gives it a distinct legal function; concealing testimony is separately forbidden.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r3.anchor: فصار الأمرر بتحمل الشهادة داخلا في قوله { واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم }

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r4.claim: If the witness is uniquely available, giving testimony is an individual duty; if many can testify, it is a communal duty.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r4.anchor: فإن كان متعينا وجب عليه أداء الشهادة / وإن كان فيهم كثرة صار ذلك فرضا على الكفاية

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r5.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r5.claim: Al-Shafiʿi permits judgment on one witness plus the claimant’s oath, citing the Prophet’s practice; Abu Hanifa rejects it because the verse specifies two men or one man and two women.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r5.anchor: قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : يجوز القضاء بالشاهد واليمين ، وقال أبو حنيفة رضي الله عنه : لا يجوز

RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r6.claim: The verse repeats the writing instruction after commanding it earlier as reinforcement of the documentation rule.
RAZI-FULL:v7p100#2/r6.anchor: أعاد ذلك مرة أخرى على سبيل التأكيد

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r1.claim: Saʾāma means weariness or irritation; the instruction encourages writing small and large debts because even a small dispute can grow into serious conflict.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r1.anchor: السآمة الملال والضجر ، يقال : سئمت الشيء سأما وسآمة

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r2.claim: The command does not conventionally extend to trivial amounts such as a grain or qirat, since such things are not normally written down.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r2.anchor: لا لأن هذا محمول على العادة ، ليس في العادة أن يكتبوا التافه

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r3.claim: The accusative أن can be construed with the following verb as a verbal noun or with an omitted preposition meaning from writing it until its term.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r3.anchor: إن شئت جعلته مع الفعل مصدرا فتقديره : ولا تسأموا كتابته

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r4.claim: The pronoun in أن تكتبوه must refer back to either the debt or the right mentioned earlier.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r4.anchor: الضمير في قوله { أن تكتبوه } لا بد وأن يعود إلى المذكورر سابقا

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r5.claim: A variant reading has ياء in both instances of ولا.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r5.anchor: المسألة الرابعة : قرىء { ولا } بالياء فيهما

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r6.claim: Al-Qaffal takes ذالكم as referring to the commanded writing and witnessing; writing is more just because it is closer to certainty and truth and further from ignorance and falsehood.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r6.anchor: الفائدة الأولى : قوله { ذالكم أقسط عند * الله } وفي قوله { ذالكم } وجهان

RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r7.claim: Qist is justice and iqsat its verbal noun; the related forms mean acting justly or acting unjustly, as illustrated by other Qur’anic passages.
RAZI-FULL:v7p101/r7.anchor: ومعنى { أقسط عند الله } أعدل عند الله ، والقسط اسم ، والإقساط مصدر

RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r1.claim: Aqwam means more upright; writing supports accurate testimony through preservation and memory, serving worldly benefit, while the first benefit serves religion and is placed first to prioritize religion.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r1.anchor: واعلم أن الكتابة إنما كانت أقوم للشهادة ، لأنها سبب للحفظ والذكر

RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r2.claim: Writing also reduces doubt and protects both parties from uncertain recollection and accusations that can lead to backbiting or slander.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r2.anchor: والفائدة الثالثة : هي قوله { وأدنى * أن لا * ترتابوا } يعني أقرب إلى زوال الشك

RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r3.claim: The exception for immediate trade may be connected to the debt-writing command or to the writer’s duty, or disconnected as a separate concession; ease and immediate exchange explain the concession.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r3.anchor: فيه وجهان أحدهما : أنه استثناء متصل والثاني : أنه منقطع

RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r4.claim: The exception is justified by the frequency of everyday cash exchanges and the absence of denial risk when both parties exchange their due in the same sitting.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102/r4.anchor: وإنما رخص تعالى في ترك الكتبة والإشهاد في هذا النوع من التجارة

RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r1.claim: An takuna may use kāna for occurrence, or incomplete kāna with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and تديرونها as predicate; al-Farraʾ gives the latter parse.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r1.anchor: قوله { أن تكون } فيه قولان أحدهما : أنه من الكون بمعنى الحدوث والوقوع

RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r2.speaker: عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r2.claim: ʿAsim reads تجارة in the accusative, while the other readers use the nominative.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r2.anchor: قرأ عاصم { تجارة } بالنصب ، والباقون بالرفع

RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the accusative by supplying مداينة as the subject, while Abu ʿAli al-Farisi objects that a debt transaction cannot be immediate trade.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج : التقدير إلا أن تكون المداينة تجارة حاضر ، قال أبو علي الفارسي : هذا غير جائز

RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi answers that a sale payable within an hour can still be called immediate commerce despite creating a debt.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r4.anchor: بأن المداين إذا كانت إلى أجل ساعة ، صح تسميتها بالتجارة الحاضرة

RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r5.claim: Commerce means dealing in property for profit, while تديرونها means exchanging directly hand to hand; the exemption removes hardship rather than declaring that omission is sinful.
RAZI-FULL:v7p102#2/r5.anchor: التجارة عبارة عن التصرف في المال سواء كان حاضرا أو في الذمة لطلب الربح

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r1.claim: Most exegetes say immediate trade is exempt from writing but remains subject to witnessing, which is easier and avoids later memory failure.
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r1.anchor: أكثر المفسرين قالوا : المراد أن الكتابة وإن رفعت عنهم في التجارة إلا أن الاشهاد ما رفع عنهم

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r2.claim: The commands to record and witness are guidance toward prudent protection of rights.
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r2.anchor: المقصود من هذا الأمر الإرشاد إلى طريق الاحتياط

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r3.speaker: أكثر المفسرين والحسن وطاوس وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r3.claim: Most exegetes, al-Hasan, Tawus, and Qatada read ولا يضار as forbidding the writer or witness from harming the rights-holder through falsification, omission, or ineffective testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r3.anchor: الأول : قول أكثر المفسرين والحسن وطاوس وقتادة ، والثاني : قول ابن مسعود وعطاء ومجاهد

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود وعطاء ومجاهد
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud, ʿAtaʾ, and Mujahid instead understand the clause as forbidding the rights-holder from burdening or obstructing the writer and witness.
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r4.anchor: قراءة عمر رضي الله عنه { ولا } بالإظهار والكسر ، وقراءة ابن عباس { ولا } بالإظهار والفتح

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r5.speaker: عمر وابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r5.claim: The ambiguity comes from assimilation in يضارر: the subject may inflict harm or suffer it; Umar’s kasra and Ibn ʿAbbas’s fatḥa with explicit pronunciation preserve both readings.

RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r6.speaker: الزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj prefers the reading that writers and witnesses must not harm the claimant, while the opposing reading points to the plural address and the ensuing plural verb.
RAZI-FULL:v7p103/r6.anchor: وإذا كان هذا خطابا للذين يقدمون على المداينة فالمنهيون عن الضرار هم والله أعلم

RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r1.claim: فسوق بكم may refer specifically to committing the prohibited harm, or generally to doing anything forbidden or omitting any commanded duty.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r1.anchor: يحتمل أنه يحمل على هذا الموضع خاصة والمعنى : فإن تفعلوا ما نهيتكم عنه من الضرار

RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r2.claim: The call to fear God may likewise refer narrowly to avoiding harm in this transaction or broadly to all commands and prohibitions.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r2.anchor: يعني فيما حذر منه هاهنا ، وهو المضارة ، أو يكون عاما

RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r3.claim: God teaches people guidance and safeguards for worldly dealings as well as religious guidance; His knowledge encompasses the interests of both lives.
RAZI-FULL:v7p104/r3.anchor: يعلمكم ما يكون إرشادا واحتياطا في أمر الدنيا ، كما يعلمكم ما يكون إرشادا في أمر الدين

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r1.claim: This is the Quran’s longest single verse.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r1.anchor: This is the longest single verse in the Quran

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r2.speaker: Ṭ, IK, Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r2.claim: Although associated with agricultural forward sales, the rule generally applies to agreements including loans when payment and delivery are not simultaneous.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r2.anchor: It is said to have been revealed in connection with agricultural forward sales, but is generally applicable to all agreements, including loans

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r3.claim: In Madinah, forward sales allowed payment for agricultural goods due one to three years later; the Prophet required fixed quantity, weight, and delivery time.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r3.anchor: Whosoever contracts a forward sale, let it be for a set amount, a set weight, and a set time

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r4.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r4.claim: Forward sale is an exception to the ban on selling what one does not possess because agricultural sellers need funds for seeds and crop care on an annual cycle.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r4.anchor: This represents an exception to the general rule that one is prohibited from selling what one does not possess

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r5.claim: Though risky, forward sale is not gambling; its social benefit is considered greater than its possible harm and uncertainty.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r5.anchor: the social benefit is thought to outweigh the potential harm and uncertainty

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r6.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r6.claim: A seller must own production means and specify the product’s attributes, quantity, delivery time, and feasible place of delivery.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r6.anchor: the product should be of known traits and attributes

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r7.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r7.claim: The buyer should pay fungible or monetary material because agricultural sellers lack liquid wealth and hold assets not easily converted to money.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r7.anchor: they should pay in fungible or monetary material

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r8.claim: The debtor, broadly including a forward-sale seller, dictates the terms; commentators say the creditor may inflate the amount and the seller is usually weaker.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r8.anchor: The one who has to deliver the product or repay a loan, the debtor (used in the general sense

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r9.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r9.claim: Writing records the agreement’s terms for memory; it does not replace a living witness, since testimony was primarily oral and secondarily written.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r9.anchor: the writing was meant to serve as a means of remembering the terms of the agreement

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r10.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r10.claim: A scribe’s duty to write contracts is communal: society must provide someone, but each individual need not do it.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r10.anchor: which means that someone in society must be available to carry out what is a solemn duty

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r11.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r11.claim: The debtor described as feeble-minded, weak, or unable to dictate is interpreted respectively as mentally disabled, a minor, or incapacitated by illness.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r11.anchor: someone who is mentally disabled, a minor, or someone who is sick to the point of incapacitation

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r12.speaker: IK, Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r12.claim: The one-man-and-two-women witness provision is specific to these commercial transactions and differs from other testimony.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r12.anchor: this provision is peculiar to the commercial transactions mentioned in this verse

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r13.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r13.claim: Other verses give equal consideration to male and female testimony in accusations of adultery by either spouse.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r13.anchor: where accusations of adultery are given equal consideration whether they are made by the husband or the wife

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r14.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r14.claim: Classical law generally excluded women’s testimony in corporal punishment and qiṣāṣ cases, though this appears to be preference because women could testify without a male witness.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r14.anchor: in the absence of a male witness, women’s testimony would be accepted

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r15.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r15.claim: A judge cannot strictly quantify testimony’s value and needs all relevant evidence; the preferences likely reflect social aversion to involving women in these matters.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r15.anchor: a judge simply needs all the relevant evidence to come to a decision

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r16.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r16.claim: To err means to forget an aspect of the contract.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r16.anchor: “to err” means to forget some aspect of the contract

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r17.claim: Commentators differ over whether the reminded woman becomes legally equal to a man or the two women together equal one man; the latter view was more widely accepted.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r17.anchor: The latter was more widely accepted

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r18.claim: Some commentators infer women’s essential inability to judge objectively and intrinsic unreliability as witnesses.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r18.anchor: some commentators, but not all, understood this verse to indicate an essential inferiority in women’s ability to judge objectively

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r19.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r19.claim: The verse does not demand an inference of female inferiority; its described transaction allows two women to arrange a sale and use two men as witnesses.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r19.anchor: Nothing in the verse demands such a reading, however

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r20.claim: Women may conduct sales and loans for themselves, including transactions without witnesses; the witness provision therefore serves another purpose.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r20.anchor: women, like men, can transact any sale or loan on their own behalf

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r21.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r21.claim: Because women of the time generally lacked experience with complex finance, two women could make testimony more practical and protect them from bullying or manipulation, rather than indicting their reliability.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r21.anchor: accepting two women in the place of one man would have been more practical

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r22.speaker: Abū Bakr ibn ʿArabī
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r22.claim: In Aḥkām al-Qur’ān he wondered why one man could not remind one woman if she erred, and found no answer.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r22.anchor: jurists such as Abū Bakr ibn ʿArabī, inAḥkām al-Qur’ān, wondered why

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r23.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r23.claim: The testimony stipulation is particular to this circumstance and addresses social or communal difficulties; the approval of witnesses also suggests competence in this specialized area.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r23.anchor: from among those whom you approve as witnesses suggests that it is a matter of competence in a specific area

STUDYQURAN:2:282/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r24.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r24.claim: Forward contracts could span years, and women might be less socially available to witness them over time; spot sales need no written contract because delivery and payment are simultaneous.
STUDYQURAN:2:282/r24.anchor: The trade of present goods refers to a transaction where delivery is made at the time of payment

TAB-FULL:v5p69/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r1.claim: Tadayantum covers deferred sales and purchases, lending, and other debt exchanges due at a known, fixed time; it includes loans, forward sales, and permissible sales with deferred payment.
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r1.anchor: يعني إذا تبايعتم بدين أو اشتريتم به، أو تعاطيتم، أو أخذتم به

TAB-FULL:v5p69/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed specifically about forward purchase of wheat by known measure and due date.
TAB-FULL:v5p69/r2.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية: {إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه} [البقرة: 282] في السلم في الحنطة

TAB-FULL:v5p72/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas again identifies the setting as forward purchase of wheat, with its measure and date specified.
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r1.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية: {يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى} [البقرة: 282] في السلف في الحنطة

TAB-FULL:v5p72/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r2.speaker: قتادة عن ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas affirms that a guaranteed forward sale with a specified term is lawful and authorized by God.
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r2.anchor: أشهد أن السلف المضمون، إلى أجل مسمى أن الله عز وجل قد أحله

TAB-FULL:v5p72/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r3.claim: The added phrase bidain clarifies the intended legal sense because tadayantum can mean mutual repayment or general giving and taking, not only a debt transaction.
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r3.anchor: أبان الله بقوله {بدين} [البقرة: 282] المعنى الذي قصد تعريفه

TAB-FULL:v5p72/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r4.claim: Some call bidain mere emphasis, as in 15:30, but al-Tabari says that explanation has no merit here.
TAB-FULL:v5p72/r4.anchor: ولا معنى لما قال من ذلك في هذا الموضع

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r1.claim: Al-Tabari takes write it to mean documenting the debt due at the appointed time, whether from a sale or loan, then introduces a dispute about whether writing is obligatory or recommended.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r1.anchor: ذكر من قال ذلك: حدثني المثنى، قال: ثنا إسحاق

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r2.claim: A reported position holds that documentation, though originally obligatory, was later abrogated by the mutual-trust provision.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان اكتتاب الكتاب بالدين فرضا، فنسخه قوله:

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r3.claim: Anyone selling for a fixed future date was commanded to document the transaction, whether small or large.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r3.anchor: من باع إلى أجل مسمى أمر أن يكتب صغيرا كان أو كبيرا

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r4.claim: A borrower should write the debt, while a seller should obtain witnesses.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r4.anchor: فمن ادان دينا فليكتب، ومن باع فليشهد

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r5.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r5.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the writing requirement was initially obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r5.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، في قوله: " {إذا تداينتم بدين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه} [البقرة: 282] فكان هذا واجبا

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r6.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r6.claim: A second report from al-Rabiʿ says the trust provision in the next verse granted a concession.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r6.anchor: عن أبيه، عن الربيع، بمثله، وزاد فيه: قال: ثم قامت الرخصة والسعة

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r7.speaker: أبو سليمان المرعشي
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r7.claim: A seller who failed to document or witness a debt and was later denied it had sinned, so his prayer against the debtor would not be answered.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r7.anchor: رجل باع شيئا فلم يكتب ولم يشهد، فلما حل ماله

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r8.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r8.claim: Another view treats the writing rule as relaxed when parties trust one another, allowing them not to document or witness the transaction under the next verse.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r8.anchor: لا بأس إذا أمنته أن لا تكتب، ولا تشهد

TAB-FULL:v5p73/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r9.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r9.claim: The trust provision grants permission for anyone who chooses to entrust the other party without documentation.
TAB-FULL:v5p73/r9.anchor: رخص في ذلك، فمن شاء أن يأتمن صاحبه فليأتمنه

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r1.claim: The command means to write down any debt due at a fixed term, whether it arose from a sale or a loan.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r1.anchor: لم يبح لأحد أن يدان بدين إلا بكتاب وشهداء

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r2.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says that if the parties trust one another, neither witnessing nor writing is needed.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r2.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: «إن ائتمنه فلا يشهد عليه ولا يكتب»

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reports that people treated the trust clause as abrogating prior writing and witness requirements, making them a concession and mercy.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r3.anchor: فكانوا يرون أن هذه، الآية: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا} [البقرة: 283] نسخت ما قبلها

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r4.speaker: غير عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r4.claim: An unnamed authority other than ʿAṭāʾ says the trust clause abrogated writing and testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r4.anchor: قال غير عطاء: " نسخت الكتاب والشهادة: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا} [البقرة: 283]

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the trust clause replaced all documentation, witnesses, and pledges with reliance on the entrusted person's honesty.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " نسخ ذلك قوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته} [البقرة: 283]

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r6.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r6.claim: When asked whether every sale needs a witness, al-Ḥasan points to the instruction that a trusted party must return what was entrusted to him.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r6.anchor: سألت الحسن قلت: كل من باع بيعا ينبغي له أن يشهد؟ قال: " ألم تر أن الله عز وجل يقول

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r7.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r7.claim: ʿĀmir understands the trust clause as permission: whoever wishes may trust the other party without documentation.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r7.anchor: رخص في ذلك، فمن شاء أن يأتمن صاحبه فليأتمنه

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r8.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r8.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says witnessing is prudent, but leaving it is lawful and allowed.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r8.anchor: عن الشعبي، في قوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا} [البقرة: 283] قال: «إن أشهدت فحزم، وإن لم تشهد ففي حل وسعة»

TAB-FULL:v5p75/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r9.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r9.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the trust clause abrogated the preceding command.
TAB-FULL:v5p75/r9.anchor: فقرأ إلى قوله: {فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا} [البقرة: 283] «قد نسخ ما كان قبله»

TAB-FULL:v5p76/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
TAB-FULL:v5p76/r1.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī says the trust clause abrogated what preceded it in the debt passage.
TAB-FULL:v5p76/r1.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري: أنه قرأ

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.claim: The scribe is to record the debt between creditor and debtor fairly, without diminishing the creditor's due or falsely imposing a debt on the debtor.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] قال: «اتقى الله كاتب في كتابه، فلا يدعن منه حقا

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.claim: Qatāda says a God-fearing scribe omits no right and adds nothing false.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] قال: «اتقى الله كاتب في كتابه، فلا يدعن منه حقا، ولا يزيدن فيه باطلا»

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.claim: The refusal prohibition addresses a scribe asked to write a debt contract; God granted him writing knowledge that many people lack.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r3.anchor: ولا يأبين كاتب استكتب ذلك أن يكتب بينهم كتاب الدين، كما علمه الله كتابته

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says it is obligatory for a scribe to write when asked.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قول الله عز وجل: {ولا يأب كاتب} [البقرة: 282] قال: «واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب»

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.claim: ʿAṭāʾ answers that a scribe is indeed obligated not to refuse.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r5.anchor: قلت لعطاء: قوله: {ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب} [البقرة: 282] أواجب أن لا يأبى أن يكتب؟ قال: «نعم»

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.claim: Mujāhid likewise calls the scribe's duty obligatory.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r6.anchor: وقال مجاهد: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r7.speaker: عامر وعطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r7.claim: ʿĀmir and ʿAṭāʾ say a person summoned to write must not refuse when no other scribe is available.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r7.anchor: عن عامر، وعطاء، قوله: {ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله} [البقرة: 282] قالا: «إذا لم يجدوا كاتبا فدعيت فلا تأب

TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r8.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the original obligation to write was abrogated by the prohibition on harming a scribe or witness.
TAB-FULL:v5p76#2/r8.anchor: عن الضحاك: {ولا يأب كاتب} [البقرة: 282] قال: " كانت عزيمة فنسختها: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد}

TAB-FULL:v5p78/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r1.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the command made writing obligatory on scribes.
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r1.anchor: عن الربيع: {وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله} [البقرة: 282] «فكان هذا واجبا على الكتاب»

TAB-FULL:v5p78/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says a scribe must not refuse when he is free.
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «لا يأب كاتب أن يكتب إن كان فارغا»

TAB-FULL:v5p78/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rules that recording a fixed-term debt and the scribe's duty to write are binding unless proof establishes recommendation; the trust exception applies when writing or a scribe is unavailable, so it does not abrogate the ordinary rule.
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r3.anchor: فذلك فرض عليهم لا يسعهم تضييعه

TAB-FULL:v5p78/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects abrogation by the trust clause: a conditional concession does not cancel a rule that can coexist with it, just as travel ablution and expiation alternatives do not cancel their ordinary rules.
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r4.anchor: وإنما يكون الناسخ ما لم يجز اجتماع حكمه وحكم المنسوخ في حال واحدة

TAB-FULL:v5p78/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī also rejects treating the commands to write and not refuse as mere guidance without evidence, challenging that standard's inconsistent application to other divine commands.
TAB-FULL:v5p78/r5.anchor: وأما الذين زعموا أن قوله: {فاكتبوه} [البقرة: 282] وقوله: {ولا يأب كاتب} [البقرة: 282] على وجه الندب والإرشاد

TAB-FULL:v5p81/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r1.claim: The debtor must dictate the debt to the scribe and fear God by not diminishing the creditor's right; cheating the creditor will be answered for on the Day of Judgment.
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r1.anchor: عن الربيع: {فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق} [البقرة: 282] فكان هذا واجبا

TAB-FULL:v5p81/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the debtor's dictation is obligatory and he must wrong the creditor in no amount.
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r2.anchor: عن الربيع: {فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق} [البقرة: 282] فكان هذا واجبا، {وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا}

TAB-FULL:v5p81/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd explains that the debtor must not reduce any part of the other man's right while dictating.
TAB-FULL:v5p81/r3.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ولا يبخس منه شيئا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «لا ينقص من حق هذا الرجل شيئا إذا أملى»

TAB-FULL:v5p82/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r1.claim: Mujāhid explains the fool as someone ignorant about dictation and practical affairs.
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها} [البقرة: 282] " أما السفيه: فالجاهل بالإملاء والأمور

TAB-FULL:v5p82/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r2.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the fool here as a young child.
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها} [البقرة: 282] " أما السفيه: فهو الصغير

TAB-FULL:v5p82/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk also identifies the fool as a young child.
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا} [البقرة: 282] قال: " هو الصبي الصغير

TAB-FULL:v5p82/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers ignorance of right and wrong in dictation as the meaning of foolishness; it can describe any uninformed person, but the verse most directly concerns competent adults rather than children, who cannot transact debts.
TAB-FULL:v5p82/r4.anchor: السفيه في هذا الموضع: الجاهل بالإملاء وموضع صواب ذلك من خطئه

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r1.claim: The fool can dictate but lacks sound judgment; the weak cannot dictate through a speech impediment or muteness; one unable to dictate is prevented by confinement or absence. In these cases the creditor dictates fairly.
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r1.anchor: فليملل وليه بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] يعني ولي الحق

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects interpreting the fool as a child and the weak as an adult idiot: a sane adult, even if mute or absent, has no guardian who can dispose of his property without authorization.
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r2.anchor: ولا وجه لقول من زعم أن السفيه في هذا الموضع هو الصغير، وأن الضعيف هو الكبير الأحمق

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r3.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r3.claim: Al-Rabīʿ identifies the person who dictates for the debtor as the creditor entitled to the right.
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r3.anchor: عن الربيع: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «ولي الحق»

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says that when the debtor cannot dictate, the creditor dictates fairly.
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو فليملل وليه بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] قال: يقول: «إن كان عجز عن ذلك أمل صاحب الدين بالعدل»

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the guardian of a foolish or weak debtor is ordered to dictate fairly.
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r5.anchor: عن الضحاك: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو} [البقرة: 282] قال: «أمر ولي السفيه أو الضعيف أن يمل بالعدل»

TAB-FULL:v5p84/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r6.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p84/r6.claim: Al-Suddī interprets the weak person as an idiot.

TAB-FULL:v5p85/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r1.claim: Mujāhid likewise says the weak person is an idiot.

TAB-FULL:v5p85/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd describes a weak debtor as unable to recognize and establish the other party's right, so his guardian acts in his place.
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا} [البقرة: 282] «لا يعرف فيثبت لهذا حقه ويجهل ذلك، فوليه بمنزلته

TAB-FULL:v5p85/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the guardian's dictation is to be done truthfully and in accordance with the right.
TAB-FULL:v5p85/r3.anchor: وأما قوله: {فليملل وليه بالعدل} [البقرة: 282] فإنه يعني بالحق

TAB-FULL:v5p86/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p86/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p86/r1.claim: The command is to appoint two witnesses over one's rights; “your men” means free Muslim men, excluding slaves and free non-Muslims.

TAB-FULL:v5p86/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p86/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p86/r2.claim: Mujāhid glosses “your men” as free men.
TAB-FULL:v5p86/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم} [البقرة: 282] قال: «الأحرار»

TAB-FULL:v5p87/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r1.claim: If two men cannot be found, the clause permits a man and two women; several nominative and accusative parses are grammatically possible. Approved witnesses are upright in religion and character.
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r1.anchor: فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان

TAB-FULL:v5p87/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the witness formula concerns debts and that approved witnesses are just.
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم} [البقرة: 282] «يقول في الدين»

TAB-FULL:v5p87/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says God commands two just men, or, if unavailable, one man and two approved women.
TAB-FULL:v5p87/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك: {واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم} [البقرة: 282] «أمر الله عز وجل أن يشهدوا ذوي عدل من رجالهم»

TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r1.claim: Most Hijaz, Medina, and some Iraqi reciters read “an taḍilla” with open أن and subjunctive verbs, meaning the second woman reminds the first if she errs; the wording places the reminder after the error for its intended sense.
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r1.anchor: فقرأ عامة أهل الحجاز والمدينة وبعض أهل العراق: {أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} [البقرة: 282] بفتح الألف من «أن» ونصب «تضل» و «تذكر»

TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r2.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r2.claim: Some readers of the light-kāf form interpret the two women's testimony together as equivalent to one man's, so each woman makes the other a “male” witness; this is reported from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah.
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r2.anchor: حدثت عن سفيان بن عيينة، أنه قال: " ليس تأويل قوله: {فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} [البقرة: 282] من الذكر بعد النسيان

TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r3.claim: Other readers of the light-kāf form take it to mean ordinary remembering after forgetfulness.
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r3.anchor: وكان آخرون منهم يوجهونه إلى أنه بمعنى الذكر بعد النسيان

TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r4.speaker: قراء آخرون
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r4.claim: Another group reads إن with kasra and raises the doubled verb, treating the clause as an independent statement: if one forgets, the other reminds her.
TAB-FULL:v5p87#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ ذلك آخرون: (إن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى) بكسر «إن» من قوله: (إن تضل) ورفع «تذكر» وتشديده

TAB-FULL:v5p90/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r1.speaker: الأعمش
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r1.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads إن with kasra, puts تضل in the conditional jussive, and raises فتذكر as its response, yielding an independent statement about one witness reminding the other if she forgets.
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r1.anchor: وهذه قراءة كان الأعمش يقرؤها ومن أخذها عنه

TAB-FULL:v5p90/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the widely transmitted open-أن reading with a doubled kāf and subjunctive verbs: one woman reminds the other if she errs; فتذكر is coordinated with تضل and أن stands where كي would.
TAB-FULL:v5p90/r2.anchor: والصواب من القراءة عندنا في ذلك قراءة من قرأه بفتح «أن» من قوله: {أن تضل إحداهما} [البقرة: 282] وبتشديد الكاف

TAB-FULL:v5p91/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rejects Ibn ʿUyaynah's “making her male” interpretation: it contradicts the exegetes and misunderstands error in testimony as forgetfulness, when the forgetful witness needs reminding.
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r1.anchor: فتأويل خطأ لا معنى له لوجوه شتى

TAB-FULL:v5p91/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says that even if Ibn ʿUyaynah meant strengthening the forgetful woman's recall, that approaches his own interpretation, but no one reports that reading-based explanation and the light reading remains unsupported.
TAB-FULL:v5p91/r2.anchor: فإن كان ابن عيينة هذا أراد، فهو مذهب من مذاهب تأويل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p93/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r1.claim: Qatāda urges reliance on God's assurance in documenting rights: writing protects property, benefits the pious, and makes even a wicked debtor more likely to pay because witnesses exist.
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} [البقرة: 282] «علم الله أن ستكون حقوق

TAB-FULL:v5p93/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ explains that one woman may forget and the other reminds her.
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r2.anchor: عن الربيع: {أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «أن تنسى إحداهما فتذكرها الأخرى»

TAB-FULL:v5p93/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says one woman may forget the testimony and the other reminds her.
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r3.anchor: عن السدي، " {أن تضل إحداهما} [البقرة: 282] يقول: تنسى إحداهما الشهادة فتذكرها الأخرى

TAB-FULL:v5p93/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk likewise interprets the clause as one woman forgetting and the other reminding her.
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك: {أن تضل إحداهما} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «إن تنس إحداهما تذكرها الأخرى»

TAB-FULL:v5p93/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the two forms are synonymous dialects and that he reads فتذكر with a doubled kāf.
TAB-FULL:v5p93/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} [البقرة: 282] قال: " كلاهما لغة وهما سواء

TAB-FULL:v5p94/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r1.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r1.claim: Qatāda says the clause forbids refusing an initial request to witness rights; he recounts a man calling through a large encampment with no one answering, and reads the verse as testifying for one person against another.
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله تعالى: " {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] كان الرجل يطوف في الحواء العظيم فيه القوم

TAB-FULL:v5p94/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r2.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r2.claim: Al-Rabīʿ reports the same setting: people summoned in a large gathering would not follow the caller to testify.
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r2.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: " كان الرجل يطوف في القوم الكثير يدعوهم ليشهدوا

TAB-FULL:v5p94/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r3.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says answering an initial request is optional when others are available, but obligatory if no other witness can be found.
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، قال: {لا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إن شاء شهد، وإن شاء لم يشهد، فإذا لم يوجد غيره شهد»

TAB-FULL:v5p94/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan glosses the command as carrying out testimony and giving testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p94/r4.anchor: عن الحسن: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: قال الحسن: «الإقامة والشهادة»

TAB-FULL:v5p96/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command covers both giving testimony when one has it and answering an initial invitation to testify.
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r1.anchor: قال: كان الحسن يقول: «جمعت أمرين لا تأب إذا كانت عندك شهادة أن تشهد

TAB-FULL:v5p96/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a Muslim whose testimony is needed must give it and may not refuse when summoned.
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] «يعني من احتيج إليه من المسلمين شهد على شهادة إن كانت عنده

TAB-FULL:v5p96/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains the command as not refusing either to give testimony already held or to become a witness when asked.
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r3.anchor: عن الحسن: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «لإقامتها، ولا يبذأ بها

TAB-FULL:v5p96/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r4.claim: Mujāhid generally takes the command to concern carrying out testimony already given or held, not refusing a summons to perform it.
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إذا شهد»

TAB-FULL:v5p96/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r5.claim: Mujāhid also distinguishes existing testimony, which must be performed, from a new invitation to witness, which one may accept or decline.
TAB-FULL:v5p96/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إذا كانت شهادة فأقمها، فإذا دعيت لتشهد، فإن شئت فاذهب، وإن شئت فلا تذهب»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r1.speaker: أبو مجلز
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r1.claim: Abū Mujliz says a person may decline an initial invitation he dislikes, but must respond if summoned after giving testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r1.anchor: لأبي مجلز: ناس يدعونني لأشهد بينهم، وأنا أكره أن أشهد بينهم؟ قال: «دع ما تكره، فإذا شهدت فأجب إذا دعيت»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r2.speaker: عامر
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r2.claim: ʿĀmir says a witness may choose freely until he has testified.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r2.anchor: عن عامر، قال: «الشاهد بالخيار ما لم يشهد»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r3.claim: ʿIkrima says the command concerns carrying out testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «لإقامة الشهادة»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r4.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ likewise says the command concerns performing testimony already held.

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r5.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a person who dislikes an initial invitation to testify may decline it.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r5.anchor: عن الحسن: أنه سأله سائل قال: أدعى إلى الشهادة وأنا أكره أن أشهد عليها، قال: «فلا تجب إن شئت»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r6.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r6.claim: Ibrāhīm says a person afraid of forgetting may decline an initial request to testify.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r6.anchor: عن مغيرة، قال: سألت إبراهيم قلت: أدعى إلى الشهادة وأنا أخاف أن أنسى، قال: «فلا تشهد إن شئت»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr understands the verse to concern witnesses who have already testified.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r7.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إذا كانوا قد شهدوا»

TAB-FULL:v5p98/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r8.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r8.claim: Al-Suddī says an available witness should not refuse an initial request to come forward and testify.
TAB-FULL:v5p98/r8.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «لا يأب الشاهد أن يتقدم فيشهد إذا كان فارغا»

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r1.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says those summoned are people who already testified; an initial invitation may be declined because witnesses are plentiful, unlike the scribe's binding duty to write.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r1.anchor: قلت لعطاء: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «هم الذين قد شهدوا»

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says a witness who has testified must answer a summons to deliver and perform that testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إذا شهد فلا يأب إذا دعي أن يأتي يؤدي شهادة ويقيمها»

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r3.claim: Qatāda says al-Ḥasan interpreted the verse as requiring a person who already has testimony to perform it when summoned.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r3.anchor: عن قتادة: {ولا يأب الشهداء} [البقرة: 282] قال: «كان الحسن يتأولها إذا كانت عنده شهادة فدعي ليقيمها»

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk includes witnesses who were formally engaged and scribes who wrote a record: when called to adjudicate a right, they must answer and report what they were entrusted with.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إذا كتب الرجل شهادته

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r5.speaker: عطية العوفي
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r5.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī treats the rule as a recommendation for a man or woman invited to give new testimony, not as an obligation.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r5.anchor: عن عطية العوفي، في قوله: {ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا} [البقرة: 282] قال: «أمرت أن تشهد، فإن شئت فاشهد، وإن شئت فلا تشهد»

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r6.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ is also reported to say that an invitation to give new testimony is a recommendation that may be accepted or declined.

TAB-FULL:v5p100/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the verse obligates an already appointed witness to perform testimony before an authority or judge who can secure the right owed.
TAB-FULL:v5p100/r7.anchor: وأولى هذه الأقوال بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: ولا يأب الشهداء من الإجابة إذا دعوا لإقامة الشهادة وأدائها عند ذي سلطان أو حاكم

TAB-FULL:v5p101/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reasons that “the witnesses” names identifiable people already entrusted with testimony, as established by the earlier command to appoint them; it cannot mean everyone merely capable of witnessing.
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r1.anchor: وغير جائز أن يلزمهم اسم الشهداء إلا وقد استشهدوا قبل ذلك

TAB-FULL:v5p101/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says an initial request to witness is obligatory only when no other suitable witness is available, by broader duties to preserve a fellow Muslim's right, not by this verse itself.
TAB-FULL:v5p101/r2.anchor: فإن الفرض عليه إجابة داعيه إليها كما فرض على الكاتب إذا استكتب بموضع لا كاتب به سواه

TAB-FULL:v5p103/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r1.claim: Do not grow weary of recording a small or large debt until its term; a written record keeps track of both the due date and amount.

TAB-FULL:v5p103/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r2.claim: Mujāhid says the object to be written is the debt.
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد: {ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله} [البقرة: 282] قال: «هو الدين»

TAB-FULL:v5p103/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r3.claim: The verb تسأموا means “do not tire”; Labīd and Zuhayr use سئمت in the sense of becoming weary.

TAB-FULL:v5p103/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r4.claim: A Basran grammarian construes “to its term” as the term for the witness, meaning the time during which testimony is valid.
TAB-FULL:v5p103/r4.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي البصريين: تأويل قوله: {إلى أجله} [البقرة: 282] إلى أجل الشاهد

TAB-FULL:v5p104/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p104/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p104/r1.claim: “That” means recording the debt through its due date; أَقْسَط means more just and comes from the verb for judging equitably, unlike قَسَط, which means to act unjustly.

TAB-FULL:v5p104/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p104/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p104/r2.claim: Al-Suddī glosses أَقْسَط as “more just in God's sight.”
TAB-FULL:v5p104/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {ذلكم أقسط عند الله} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «أعدل عند الله»

TAB-FULL:v5p104#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p104#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p104#2/r1.claim: Written documentation makes testimony more accurate because it preserves the parties' exact acknowledged words, keeps witnesses' accounts aligned, and makes judgment clearer; obeying God's command is itself more just than abandoning it.
TAB-FULL:v5p104#2/r1.anchor: الدين والمستدين على نفسه، فلا يقع بين الشهود اختلاف

TAB-FULL:v5p105/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r1.claim: أدنى means nearer, and the writing brings the parties closer to certainty rather than doubt about the testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r1.anchor: وأقرب لكم أن لا تشكوا فيما شهد به شهودكم عليكم من الحق والأجل إذا كان مكتوبا

TAB-FULL:v5p105/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r2.claim: Al-Suddī explains the phrase as ensuring that people will not doubt the testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r2.anchor: عن السدي: {ذلك أدنى أن لا ترتابوا} يقول: «أن لا تشكوا في الشهادة»

TAB-FULL:v5p105/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r3.claim: Writing every debt, large or small, makes the transaction more just, gives witnesses a sounder basis, and helps prevent doubt about the amount and due date.
TAB-FULL:v5p105/r3.anchor: فإن كتابكم ذلك أعدل عند الله وأصوب لشهادة شهودكم عليه، وأقرب لكم أن لا تشكوا

TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r1.claim: The exception permits leaving a written record for immediate cash trade because each party receives what is due before parting; it does not cover deferred or credit transactions.
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r1.anchor: لا أجل فيها ولا تأخير ولا نساء

TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r2.claim: Al-Suddī describes the exempt trade as local, visible goods exchanged directly, for which the parties need not write a record.
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r2.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة تديرونها بينكم} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «معكم بالبلد ترونها فتؤخذ وتعطى

TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says debts due at a term must be documented, while immediate hand-to-hand trades should be witnessed though writing is waived.
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك: {ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه صغيرا أو كبيرا إلى أجله} [البقرة: 282] إلى قوله: {فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها}

TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r4.claim: Most Hijaz, Iraqi, and other reciters raise تجارة حاضرة; some Kufans use the accusative, which is grammatically possible, but al-Ṭabarī prefers the widespread nominative reading.
TAB-FULL:v5p105#2/r4.anchor: فقرأته عامة قراء الحجاز والعراق وعامة القراء: (إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة) بالرفع

TAB-FULL:v5p108/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r1.claim: Arabic permits an indefinite noun with its adjective after kāna to appear either nominative or accusative; poets attest both constructions, so a feminine noun does not require kāna to be feminine.
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r1.anchor: وإنما تفعل العرب ذلك في النكرات لما وصفنا من اتباع أخبار النكرات أسماءها

TAB-FULL:v5p108/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r2.claim: Two anonymous poetic examples attest the Arabic construction of an indefinite feminine noun with kāna in these case patterns.
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r2.anchor: أعيني هل تبكيان عفاقا … إذا كان طعنا بينهم وعناقا

TAB-FULL:v5p108/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r3.speaker: بعض الناس
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r3.claim: Some assume the accusative reading requires the masculine form يكون, as though its sense were “unless it be a trade.”
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r3.anchor: وقد ظن بعض الناس أن من قرأ ذلك: {إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة} [البقرة: 282] إنما قرأه على معنى: إلا أن يكون تجارة حاضرة

TAB-FULL:v5p108/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r4.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r4.claim: Some Basran grammarians treat kāna here as a complete verb meaning “exist” or “occur,” with تجارة حاضرة as its subject and no predicate.
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r4.anchor: وقد زعم بعض نحويي البصرة أن قوله: (إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة) مرفوعة فيه التجارة الحاضرة لأن يكون بمعنى التمام

TAB-FULL:v5p108/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the complete-verb analysis is grammatically possible but less apt; تديرونها بينكم can be the predicate in the accusative or follow the indefinite تجارة حاضرة in the nominative.
TAB-FULL:v5p108/r5.anchor: والذي قال من حكينا قوله من البصريين غير خطأ في العربية، غير أن الذي قلنا بكلام العرب أشبه، وفي المعنى أصح

TAB-FULL:v5p109/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r1.claim: Even when cash trades need not be written, both parties should have witnesses for every sale, large or small, immediate or deferred, to prevent either buyer or seller from losing a right through denial and lack of proof.
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r1.anchor: ليس بإرخاص مني لكم في ترك الإشهاد منكم على من بعتموه شيئا

TAB-FULL:v5p109/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the risk to the buyer: the seller may deny the sale and prevail on oath because the buyer cannot prove the purchase; the seller likewise risks losing the unpaid price if the buyer denies it.
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r2.anchor: أما على المشتري، فأن يجحد البائع المبيع، وله بينة على ملكه ما قد باع

TAB-FULL:v5p109/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r3.speaker: الحسن والشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan and al-Shaʿbī treat witnessing at sale as recommended or optional, citing the permission to rely on trust.
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r3.anchor: عن الشعبي، في قوله: {وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إن شاء أشهد، وإن شاء لم يشهد»

TAB-FULL:v5p109/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r4.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says witnessing protects one's claim, but omitting it is not blameworthy.
TAB-FULL:v5p109/r4.anchor: قلت للحسن: أرأيت قول الله عز وجل: {وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم} [البقرة: 282] ؟ قال: «إن أشهدت عليه فهو ثقة

TAB-FULL:v5p110/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r1.speaker: الشعبي
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says the parties may choose whether to witness their sale.
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r1.anchor: عن الشعبي: {وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم} [البقرة: 282] قال: «إن شاءوا أشهدوا، وإن شاءوا لم يشهدوا»

TAB-FULL:v5p110/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says immediate cash sales may go unwitnessed, but deferred sales must be written and witnessed while the parties are settled.
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، قال: «ما كان من بيع حاضر، فإن شاء أشهد، وإن شاء لم يشهد، وما كان من بيع إلى أجل، فأمر الله أن يكتب ويشهد عليه

TAB-FULL:v5p110/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī rules that witnessing every purchase and sale is an obligatory duty, because divine commands bind unless evidence shows a recommendation; he rejects abrogation by the trust clause.
TAB-FULL:v5p110/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب أن الإشهاد على كل مبيع ومشتري حق واجب وفرض لازم

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r1.speaker: ابن طاوس
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r1.claim: Ibn Ṭāwūs says the writer must not record anything the person dictating did not say, nor may the witness attest to anything he was not asked to witness.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r1.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه، في قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] «ولا يضار كاتب فيكتب ما لم يمل عليه

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says a scribe must not add or distort, and a witness must not conceal testimony or attest except to truth.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r2.anchor: كان الحسن يقول: " {لا يضار كاتب} [البقرة: 282] فيزيد شيئا أو يحرف، {ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] ، قال: لا يكتم الشهادة

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r3.claim: Qatāda says the scribe and witness must preserve every right accurately, adding nothing false and omitting no right.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: " اتقى الله شاهد في شهادته لا ينقص منها حقا ولا يزيد فيها باطلا

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r4.claim: Ibn Zayd says the scribe harms people by changing what was dictated, while a witness harms them by altering testimony and thereby voiding their rights.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r4.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قال: " لا يضار كاتب فيكتب غير الذي أملي عليه

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r5.claim: On the first interpretation, the underlying form is ولا يضارر; the two identical rāʾ letters assimilate, with fatḥa used despite the jussive because it is the lightest vowel.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r5.anchor: فأصل الكلمة على تأويل من ذكرنا من هؤلاء: ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد

TAB-FULL:v5p112/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r6.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r6.claim: ʿAṭāʾ offers another interpretation: the writer and witness must not be harmed by having to withhold the knowledge or testimony they possess.
TAB-FULL:v5p112/r6.anchor: عن عطاء، في قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «أن يؤديا ما قبلهما»

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r1.speaker: عطاء
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r1.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says the writer and witness should deliver the knowledge they hold.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r1.anchor: قلت لعطاء: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قال: «لا يضار» أن يؤديا ما عندهما من العلم

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the harm as summoning a writer or witness who has a need, only for them to be told to ignore it and come anyway.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: {لا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قال: " أن يدعوهما فيقولان: إن لنا حاجة

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also describes harm as compelling a person despite there being enough other witnesses, simply because the caller invokes the command to answer summonses.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: {لا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282]

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r4.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r4.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and Mujāhid say the writer must write when asked, while a witness must perform testimony already entrusted to him.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r4.anchor: عن عطاء، ومجاهد: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قالا: «واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب»

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r5.claim: Mujāhid says a requester harms a busy scribe or witness by insisting “fear God, you were commanded” when other people can be found; they need not interrupt their work or feel pressured.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه كان يقرأ: (ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد) وأنه كان يقول في تأويلها

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r6.speaker: عمر
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r6.claim: ʿUmar is reported to have read the phrase with an unassimilated doubled rāʾ, ولا يضارر.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r6.anchor: عن عكرمة، قال: كان عمر يقرأ: (ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد)

TAB-FULL:v5p114/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is reported to have read the phrase as ولا يضارر.
TAB-FULL:v5p114/r7.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، قال: كان ابن مسعود يقرأ: (ولا يضارر)

TAB-FULL:v5p116/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says a writer or witness with an unavoidable need should be allowed to leave.
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: " إنه يكون للكاتب والشاهد حاجة ليس منها بد

TAB-FULL:v5p116/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r2.claim: ʿIkrima says a person who is ill or occupied must not be harassed.
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، في قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قال: " يكون به العلة، أو يكون مشغولا

TAB-FULL:v5p116/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r3.claim: Mujāhid describes harassment as pressing an occupied scribe or witness to comply by invoking God's command when the person has asked that someone else be found.
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، أنه كان يقول: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: " لا يأت الرجل فيقول: انطلق فاكتب لي واشهد لي

TAB-FULL:v5p116/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r4.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says callers must not harm writers or witnesses who explain they have a need; the caller should seek another person instead.
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك، في قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: " يدعو الرجل الكاتب أو الشهيد

TAB-FULL:v5p116/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says one must not keep a busy writer or witness from his own need when another is available.
TAB-FULL:v5p116/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: " ليس ينبغي أن تعترض رجلا له حاجة

TAB-FULL:v5p118/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r1.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r1.claim: Al-Rabīʿ reports that after the duty not to refuse writing was revealed, people pressured busy scribes and witnesses despite being able to find others; this harassment occasioned the prohibition on harming them.
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r1.anchor: عن الربيع، قوله: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] قال: " لما نزلت هذه الآية: {ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله}

TAB-FULL:v5p118/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r2.speaker: ابن طاوس
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r2.claim: Ibn Ṭāwūs says the writer or witness should not be harmed when saying “I have a need; let me go” by a claimant insisting “write for me.”
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r2.anchor: عن ابن طاوس، عن أبيه: {ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد} [البقرة: 282] يقول: " إن لي حاجة فدعني، فيقول: اكتب لي

TAB-FULL:v5p118/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the prohibition addresses the rights-holder summoning a busy scribe or witness and insisting they comply when occupied; the surrounding commands address those arranging debts, and the plural warning “if you do” confirms that addressee.
