TAB-FULL:v5p118/r3.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب قول من قال: معنى ذلك: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد، بمعنى: ولا يضارهما من استكتب هذا أو استشهد هذا

TAB-FULL:v5p118/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r4.claim: If the scribe and witness themselves were the addressees, the verse would say “if the two do it, it is wrongdoing for them”; instead it uses a plural warning to the parties arranging the transaction.
TAB-FULL:v5p118/r4.anchor: لو كانا هما المنهيين عن الضرار لقيل: وإن يفعلا فإنه فسوق بهما

TAB-FULL:v5p119/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r1.claim: Fusūq here means sin and disobedience: whoever harms the scribe or witness has disobeyed God and committed what is forbidden.
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r1.anchor: وأن من يضارهما فقد عصى ربه وأثم به، وركب ما لا يحل له

TAB-FULL:v5p119/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r2.claim: The verse calls it transgression whenever people do other than what God commanded.
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك: {وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم} [البقرة: 282] يقول: «إن تفعلوا غير الذي آمركم به

TAB-FULL:v5p119/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: {وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم} [البقرة: 282] " الفسوق: المعصية

TAB-FULL:v5p119/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r4.claim: He also glosses fusūq as disobedience.
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r4.anchor: عن الربيع: {وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم} [البقرة: 282] " الفسوق: العصيان

TAB-FULL:v5p119/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r5.claim: He instead reads fusūq as lying: a scribe distorts the dictated record or a witness changes testimony.
TAB-FULL:v5p119/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد: {وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم} [البقرة: 282] " الفسوق: الكذب، قال: هذا فسوق

TAB-FULL:v5p120/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r1.claim: God teaches by clarifying the rules so people can act on them.
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r1.anchor: وعليكم، فاعملوا به {والله بكل شيء عليم} [البقرة: 282] يعني من أعمالكم وغيرها

TAB-FULL:v5p120/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r2.claim: God knows deeds and other matters, records people's actions, and will repay them.
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r2.anchor: من أعمالكم وغيرها، يحصيها عليكم ليجازيكم بها

TAB-FULL:v5p120/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r3.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r3.claim: He describes these rules as instruction from God that people should follow.
TAB-FULL:v5p120/r3.anchor: عن الضحاك، قوله: {ويعلمكم الله} [البقرة: 282] قال: «هذا تعليم علمكموه فخذوا به

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.claim: He defines the key terms: mutual debt, dictation, shortchanging, weariness, causing harm, disobedience, and the two plural forms for pledged collateral.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r1.anchor: والاملال والاملاء إلقاء الرجل للكاتب ما يكتبه

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r2.claim: Using “the one who owes the right” instead of a pronoun removes possible confusion with the previously mentioned writer.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r2.anchor: لرفع اللبس برجوع الضمير إلى الكاتب السابق ذكره

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r3.claim: The explicit pronoun in “he cannot dictate” makes the debtor share the work with his guardian; unlike earlier cases, the guardian handles only what the debtor cannot.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r3.anchor: فإن هذه الصورة تغاير الصورتين الأوليين بأن الولي في الصورتين الأوليين هو المسؤول بالأمر المستقل فيه

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r4.claim: “Lest one of them err” elliptically means fearing that one woman will err; repeating “one of them” distinguishes the initially unspecified woman from the one who reminds after the other errs.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r4.anchor: والنكتة فيه اختلاف معنى اللفظ في الموضعين

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r5.claim: The command to fear God concerns obeying the instructions in the verse; “God teaches you” begins a separate statement of favor, teaching religious rules and lawful and unlawful matters.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r5.anchor: فالمراد به الامتنان بتعليم شرائع الدين ومسائل الحلال والحرام

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r6.claim: Although piety can bring divine teaching elsewhere, the verse does not establish that causal rule: the conjunction and the passage’s structure do not support it.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r6.anchor: فيه أنه وإن كان حقا يدل عليه الكتاب والسنة،

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r7.claim: Repeating God’s name shows that “God teaches you” is independent; the final name emphasizes the reason for His instruction, that He knows everything.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r7.anchor: أظهر الاسم أولا وثانيا لوقوعه في كلامين مستقلين، وأظهر ثالثا

TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.claim: The two verses contain nearly twenty legal rulings, including rules for debt and pledges; detailed legal debate belongs in jurisprudence, so he leaves it aside here.
TABATABAI:2:282-283/r8.anchor: واعلم أن الآيتين تدلان على ما يقرب من عشرين حكما من أصول أحكام الدين والرهن وغيرهما

ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r2.claim: داينت someone means dealing with him through a debt, giving and taking; تداينا is used similarly, while دنت and أدنت distinguish borrowing from lending.
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r2.anchor:
يقال داينت الرجل إذا عاملته بدين، أخذت منه وأعطيته. وتداينا على
داينته، قال الشاعر:

ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r3.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses داينت ليلى for dealing with Layla in debts, then describes delay in repayment and partial payment.
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r3.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
- داينت ليلى والديون تقضى. . . فمطلت بعضا وأدت بعضا

ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r4.claim: دنت means I borrowed and أدنت means I lent; a cited poem illustrates أدان and المدان, the lender and debtor vocabulary.
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r4.anchor: ويقال دنت وأدنت أي اقترضت، وأدنت إذا أقرضت.

ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r5.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r5.claim: A poet’s line about أدان and المدان illustrates the verb for lending and the indebted person.
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r5.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أدان وأنبأه الأولون. . . بأن المدان مليء وفي

ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r6.claim: Writing debt preserves people’s property; witnesses and proof discourage a creditor from being tempted to deny or erase the debt, so God commands recording and testimony.
ZAJJAJ:v1p360/r6.anchor:
فالمعنى إذا كان لبعضكم على بعض دين إلى أجل مسمى فاكتبوه فأمر
الله - عز وجل - بكتب الدين، حفظا منه للأموال

ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r1.claim: The command to disperse after Friday prayer likewise permits people to resume business once prayer ends.
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r1.anchor: وكما قال: (فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض).

ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r2.claim: The analogy fails: those commands permit actions after a prohibition on hunting in ihram or trading during prayer, whereas the debt verse has no preceding prohibition to lift.
ZAJJAJ:v1p361/r2.anchor: وهذا خلاف ما أمر الله به في كتاب الدين والإشهاد لأن هذين جميعا إباحة بعد تحريم

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r1.claim: If two men are unavailable, one man and two women may witness; ‘whom you approve’ means people whose standing or judgment you approve, implying some witnesses are not acceptable.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r1.anchor:
وقوله عز وجل: (فرجل وامرأتان ممن ترضون من الشهداء).
أي فالذي يشهد - إن لم يكن - رجلان - رجل وامراتان

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r2.claim: With kasra on إن, the clause is conditional: if one forgets, the remembering woman reminds her; فتذكر is indicative in this reading.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r2.anchor:
من كسر (أن) فالكلام على لفظ الجزاء، ومعناه: المعنى في (إن تضل)
إن تنسى إحداهما، تذكرها الذاكرة فتذكر.

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r3.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r3.claim: For the majority’s open أن reading, some grammarians posit a condition moved forward: appoint two women so the remembering one can remind the forgetful one.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r3.anchor: لا غير - ومن قرأ "أن تضل قتذكر " وهي قراءة أكثر الناس، فزعم بعض أهل اللغة فيها أن الجزاء فيها مقدم أصله التاخير

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r4.claim: The author says he does not understand why advancing the conditional should require فتح on أن.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r4.anchor:
ولست أعرف لم صار الجزاء إدا تقدم - وهو في مكانه أو في غير
مكانه وجب أن يفتح (أن) معه.

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r5.speaker: سيبويه والخليل وجميع النحويين الموثوق بعلمهم
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r5.claim: The reliable grammarians take أن as purpose: appoint two women so one can remind the other; forgetting is mentioned because it causes the reminder.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r5.anchor:
وذكر سيبويه والخليل " وجميع النحويين الموثوق بعلمهم أن المعنى
استشهدوا امراتين لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخري، ومن أجل أن تذكر إحداهما

ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r6.speaker: سيبويه
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r6.claim: Sibawayh explains that the cause of reminding is mentioned as its purpose, like preparing a beam to support a wall if it begins to lean.
ZAJJAJ:v1p363/r6.anchor: قال سيبويه: فإن قال إنسان فلم جاز (أن تضل) وإنما أعد هذا للإذكار، فالجواب أن الإذكار لما كان سببه الإضلال

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r1.speaker: الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says witnesses must not refuse when summoned to begin giving testimony.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r1.anchor: يروى عن الحسن أنه قال (ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا) لابتداء الشهادة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r2.claim: The author endorses al-Hasan’s interpretation: refusing to begin testimony would forfeit rights and undermine transactions that require safeguards.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r2.anchor:
وهذا الذي قال الحسن هو الحق - والله أعلم - لأن الشهداء إذا أبوا -
وكان ذلك لهم - أن يشهدوا تويت حقوقهم

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r3.speaker: غير الحسن
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r3.claim: Another view applies the command only to witnesses already holding testimony who are summoned to deliver it; those not yet witnesses may choose whether to accept an initial request.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r3.anchor:
وقال غير الحسن: (ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا) - وكانت في أعناقهم
شهادة - أن يقيموها.

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r4.claim: The author argues that the next command not to tire of writing reinforces that giving testimony from the outset is obligatory.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r4.anchor:
أي لا تملوا أن تكتبوا ما أشهدتم عليه، فقد أمروا بهذا، فهذا يؤكد أن
أمر الشهادة في الابتداء واجب

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r5.speaker: الراجز
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r5.claim: A rajaz poet uses السآمة for weariness, illustrating the verb سئمت.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r5.anchor:
قال الراجز:
لما رأيت أنه لا قامة. . .وأنني ساق على السآمة
نزعت نزعا زعزع الدعامة

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r6.claim: Most readers raise تجارة: the exception means ‘unless a cash trade takes place’; ʿĀṣim’s accusative reading means ‘unless the debt transaction is a cash trade.’
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r6.anchor:
أكثر القراء على الرفع (تجارة حاضرة) على معنى: إلا أن تقع تجارة
حاضرة.

ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r7.claim: Writing may be omitted for frequent cash dealings, often involving small sums, but testimony is still emphatically commanded when people trade.
ZAJJAJ:v1p364/r7.anchor: فرخص الله عز وجل في ترك كتابة ما يديرونه بينهم لكثرة ما تقع المعاملة فيه

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r1.claim: The view under discussion also bars summoning a witness when his attendance would harm him.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r1.anchor: لا يدعى الشاهد ومجيئه للشهادة يضر به والأول أبين

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r2.claim: The author says asking a busy writer or witness to attend does not itself count as fisq.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r2.anchor: ليشهد، ودعا كاتبا ليكتب، وهو مشغول فليس يسمى هذا فاسقا

ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r3.claim: The first interpretation is clearer because فسوق describes lying in testimony or distorting a document, not merely calling a busy witness or writer.
ZAJJAJ:v1p366/r3.anchor:
والأول أبين
لقوله: (وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم)
فالفاسق أشبه بغير العدل وبمن حرف الكتاب

TABRISI:2:282/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r1.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:2:282/r1.claim: Ḥamza alone reads إن تضل with kasra, as a conditional particle whose جواب is فتذكر.
TABRISI:2:282/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة وحده إن تضل بكسر الهمزة

TABRISI:2:282/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r2.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وقتيبة
TABRISI:2:282/r2.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Qutayba read فتذكر lightly and in the subjunctive.
TABRISI:2:282/r2.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وقتيبة فتذكر بالتخفيف والنصب

TABRISI:2:282/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r3.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:2:282/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads فتذكر with doubled dhāl and indicative mood.

TABRISI:2:282/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r4.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:2:282/r4.claim: The remaining readers read فتذكر with doubled dhāl and subjunctive mood.

TABRISI:2:282/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r5.speaker: عاصم
TABRISI:2:282/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim alone reads تجارة حاضرة in the accusative; the others read it nominative.
TABRISI:2:282/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحده تجارة حاضرة بالنصب

TABRISI:2:282/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABRISI:2:282/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar reads لا يضار with a doubled, quiescent rāʾ; the remaining readers use the doubled rāʾ in the accusative form.
TABRISI:2:282/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر ولا يضار بتشديد الراء وتسكينها

TABRISI:2:282/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282/r7.claim: For Ḥamza's conditional reading, رجل وامرأتان forms a nominative description of the two women, while ممن ترضون refers back to that nominative pair rather than accusative شهيدين.
TABRISI:2:282/r7.anchor: وهو أنه جعل أن للجزاء والفاء في قوله فتذكر جواب الجزاء

TABRISI:2:282#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r1.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:282#2/r1.claim: A third analysis supplies an omitted predicate for the subject فرجل وامرأتان, understood as فرجل وامرأتان يشهدون.
TABRISI:2:282#2/r1.anchor: والثالث: أن يضمر خبر المبتدأ الذي هو فرجل وامرأتان

TABRISI:2:282#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#2/r2.claim: On this analysis يشهدون governs أن; its omission is placed before the conditional with fatḥ and after it with kasra.
TABRISI:2:282#2/r2.anchor: فيكون يشهدون العامل في أن وموضع إضماره فيمن فتح الهمزة

TABRISI:2:282#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#2/r3.claim: The particle أن is accusative here, with the sense “because one woman may forget, then the other remind her.”
TABRISI:2:282#2/r3.anchor: وأما موضع أن هذه فنصب وتقديره لأن تضل إحداهما فتذكر

TABRISI:2:282#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
TABRISI:2:282#2/r4.claim: Sībawayh says testimony is requested so one woman may remind the other; possible forgetfulness is the reason for reminding, like shoring a wall because it may lean.
TABRISI:2:282#2/r4.anchor: أمر بالإشهاد لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى وإنما ذكر أن تضل لأنه سبب الأذكار

TABRISI:2:282#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#2/r5.claim: With the nominative reading, كان means “occur” or “happen,” so the phrase means that a present trade occurs.
TABRISI:2:282#2/r5.anchor: بالرفع فالوجه فيها أن يكون كان بمعنى وقع وحدث

TABRISI:2:282#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#2/r6.claim: One analysis derives لا يضار from doubled ر, with the writer and witness forbidden to depart from the truth.
TABRISI:2:282#2/r6.anchor: أن أصله لا يضارر فادغمت الراء في الراء

TABRISI:2:282#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#2/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#2/r7.claim: The first interpretation of لا يضار is clearer; Abū Jaʿfar's doubled quiescent rāʾ is unusual and explained by treating connected recitation like pause.

TABRISI:2:282#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r1.claim: داينت and تداينت mean transacting in debt, either by borrowing or lending; the cited poem shows this usage.

TABRISI:2:282#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r2.claim: The verb دنت means borrowing while أدنت means lending; أمل and أملى are both used for dictating.

TABRISI:2:282#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r3.claim: بخس is unjust diminution; safīh means ignorant or light-minded, named for the lightness of reason.
TABRISI:2:282#3/r3.anchor: والبخس النقص ظلما يقال بخسه حقه يبخسه بخسا

TABRISI:2:282#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r4.claim: The otherwise unusual pattern أَبَى يَأبى is explained by the hamza behaving like a guttural consonant.
TABRISI:2:282#3/r4.anchor: والقول فيه أن الألف من أبى أشبهت الهمزة

TABRISI:2:282#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r5.claim: Ḍalāl originally means loss or going where something cannot be found; saʾam is weariness, and أقسط means acted justly while قسط means acted unjustly.
TABRISI:2:282#3/r5.anchor: والضلال أصله الهلاك تقول العرب ضل الماء في اللبن

TABRISI:2:282#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r6.claim: The opening continues the previous direction to defer an insolvent debtor by explaining rules for deferred claims and debt transactions.
TABRISI:2:282#3/r6.anchor: لما أمر سبحانه بإنظار المعسر وتأجيل دينه عقبه ببيان أحكام الحقوق المؤجلة

TABRISI:2:282#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#3/r7.claim: بدين may reinforce the meaning of تداينتم; alternatively it distinguishes debt transactions from تداينتم understood as mutual requital.
TABRISI:2:282#3/r7.anchor: أحدهما: أنه على وجه التأكيد وتمكين المعنى في النفسي

TABRISI:2:283/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283/r1.claim: One analysis takes تداينتم as mutual requital, while another takes it as dealing in debt; adding بدين resolves this lexical ambiguity.
TABRISI:2:283/r1.anchor: إنما قال بدين لأن تداينتم قد يكون بمعنى تجازيتم

TABRISI:2:283/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:283/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the verse was revealed specifically concerning forward sale and testifies that God permitted a guaranteed sale to a known term.
TABRISI:2:283/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إن الآية وردت في السلم خاصة

TABRISI:2:283/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283/r3.claim: Although Ibn ʿAbbās specifies forward sale, the verse's apparent scope includes every deferred debt, which commentators and jurists accept.
TABRISI:2:283/r3.anchor: وظاهر الآية يقع على كل دين مؤجل سلما كان أو غيره

TABRISI:2:283/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283/r4.claim: Writing the debt protects against forgetting or denial and secures the rights of creditor, debtor, and witnesses for the reasons explained.
TABRISI:2:283/r4.anchor: فاكتبوا الدين في صك لئلا يقع فيه نسيان أو جحود وليكون ذلك توثقة للحق

TABRISI:2:283/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي
TABRISI:2:283/r5.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, al-Ḥasan, and al-Shaʿbī say writing the debt is recommended, the majority's preferred view.
TABRISI:2:283/r5.anchor: مندوب إليه عن أبي سعيد الخدري والحسن والشعبي وهو الأصح

TABRISI:2:283/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r6.speaker: الربيع وكعب
TABRISI:2:283/r6.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and Kaʿb regard writing as obligatory; the author cites the permission to rely on trust as evidence against obligation.
TABRISI:2:283/r6.anchor: وقيل هو فرض عن الربيع وكعب

TABRISI:2:283/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283/r7.claim: A just scribe records the debt or sale accurately, without changing its terms, amount, or anything that harms either party without consent.
TABRISI:2:283/r7.anchor: بالقسط والإنصاف والحق لا يزيد فيه ولا ينقص منه في صفة ولا مقدار

TABRISI:2:283/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:283/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:283/r8.claim: The scribe must not refuse to write; كما علمه الله may mean writing justly as God taught, or that the scribe must not hoard the skill God gave him.
TABRISI:2:283/r8.anchor: وقيل كما فضله الله تعالى بتعليمه إياه فلا يبخل على غيره بالكتابة

TABRISI:2:282#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r1.speaker: الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين
TABRISI:2:282#4/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī and other commentators treat writing as a communal duty; al-Rummānī and al-Jubbāʾī choose that view.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r1.anchor: فقيل على الكفاية كالجهاد ونحوه عن الشعبي وجماعة من المفسرين

TABRISI:2:282#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r2.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:2:282#4/r2.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī allows a scribe and witness to take payment, while al-Ṭūsī says their school does not permit it; paper costs belong to the creditor.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r2.anchor: وجوز الجبائي أن يأخذ الكاتب والشاهد الأجرة على ذلك

TABRISI:2:282#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r3.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:2:282#4/r3.claim: Al-Suddī says a scribe must write when free of other work.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r3.anchor: وقيل واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب في حال فراغه عن السدي

TABRISI:2:282#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r4.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
TABRISI:2:282#4/r4.claim: Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ say writing becomes obligatory when the scribe is asked.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r4.anchor: وقيل واجب عليه أن يكتب إذا أمر عن مجاهد وعطاء

TABRISI:2:282#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r5.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:2:282#4/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says refusal is obligatory to avoid only when there is no alternative scribe and refusal would harm the creditor; otherwise the scribe has latitude.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r5.anchor: فإذا كان كذلك فهو فريضة وإن قدر على كاتب غيره فهو في سعة

TABRISI:2:282#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TABRISI:2:282#4/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says writing was originally obligatory but was abrogated by the ban on harming a scribe or witness.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r6.anchor: وقيل كان واجبا ثم نسخ بقوله ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد

TABRISI:2:282#4/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#4/r7.claim: The command is emphasized because scribes were scarce in the Prophet's time; combining a command with a prohibition against neglect makes compliance more likely.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r7.anchor: وكانت الكتبة على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فيهم قلة فلذلك أكد

TABRISI:2:282#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#4/r8.claim: The debtor dictates and must fear God, reducing neither the amount nor the quality of what is owed.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r8.anchor: يعني المديون يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه

TABRISI:2:282#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#4/r9.claim: The debtor may be a fool through ignorance, childhood, or impaired understanding; weak may mean intellectual disability or senility, and inability may mean madness, stammering, or muteness.

TABRISI:2:282#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r10.speaker: القاضي
TABRISI:2:282#4/r10.claim: Al-Qāḍī differentiates the three: the foolish person squanders, the weak person is an adolescent, and the one unable to dictate is insane.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r10.anchor: السفيه المبذر والضعيف الصبي المراهق ومن لا يستطيع أن يمل المجنون

TABRISI:2:282#4/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#4/r11.claim: The debtor's guardian may dictate; alternatively, Ibn ʿAbbās says the guardian here is the creditor, who knows the debt best.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r11.anchor: وقيل معناه ولي الحق وهو الذي له الحق عن ابن عباس لأنه أعلم بدينه

TABRISI:2:282#4/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#4/r12.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:282#4/r12.claim: Mujāhid limits the two male witnesses to free, adult, Muslim men; al-Ṭabrisī rejects freedom as a condition, requiring Islam and probity instead.
TABRISI:2:282#4/r12.anchor: وقال مجاهد: معناه من الأحرار العالمين البالغين المسلمين

TABRISI:2:282#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#5/r1.claim: If two men are unavailable, the witness set is one man and two women whose outward probity and trustworthiness the parties accept; this makes justice a condition of testimony.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r1.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن العدالة شرط في الشهود

TABRISI:2:282#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#5/r2.claim: The wording requires witnesses acceptable to the parties, since people cannot know whom God approves except from outward reliability and integrity.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r2.anchor: ولم يقل من المرضيين لأنه لا طريق لنا إلى معرفة من هو مرضي عند الله

TABRISI:2:282#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r3.speaker: الربيع والسدي والضحاك وأكثر المفسرين
TABRISI:2:282#5/r3.claim: Most commentators take تضل as one woman forgetting the testimony she and the other woman heard; the light reading likewise means prompting her to recall it.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r3.anchor: قيل هو من الذكر الذي هو ضد النسيان عن الربيع والسدي والضحاك

TABRISI:2:282#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r4.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
TABRISI:2:282#5/r4.claim: Sufyān b. ʿUyayna reads the doubled form as making one woman equivalent to a man; al-Ṭabrisī says the memory-based reading is stronger.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r4.anchor: وقيل هو من الذكر أي يجعلها كذكر من الرجال عن سفيان بن عيينة

TABRISI:2:282#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r5.speaker: حسين بن علي المغربي
TABRISI:2:282#5/r5.claim: Al-Maghribī says تضل concerns a lost or forgotten testimony, not a woman herself going astray; this avoids needless repetition of إحداهما.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r5.anchor: ما قاله حسين بن علي المغربي أن معناه أن تضل إحدى الشهادتين

TABRISI:2:282#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#5/r6.claim: The repeated إحداهما may put the subject before its object and avoid separating verb and subject, or may clarify that a testimony is lost rather than a person straying.
TABRISI:2:282#5/r6.anchor: أحدهما: أنه إنما كرر ليكون الفاعل مقدما على المفعول

TABRISI:2:282#6/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r1.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير
TABRISI:2:282#6/r1.claim: One reported view says summoned witnesses must not refuse to give testimony they know without doubt, provided doing so causes them no harm.
TABRISI:2:282#6/r1.anchor: ولا يمتنع الشهداء إذا دعوا لإقامة الشهادة عن مجاهد وعطاء وسعيد بن جبير

TABRISI:2:282#6/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r2.speaker: قتادة والربيع
TABRISI:2:282#6/r2.claim: Qatāda and al-Rabīʿ say the witnesses must not refuse when summoned to establish and carry the testimony.
TABRISI:2:282#6/r2.anchor: أن معناه إذا دعوا لاثبات الشهادة وتحملها عن قتادة والربيع

TABRISI:2:282#6/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r3.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
TABRISI:2:282#6/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Ḥasan understand the summons as covering both bearing and delivering testimony; the author prefers this broader reading.

TABRISI:2:282#6/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#6/r4.claim: Do not weary of recording a debt, small or large, until its term; this is fairer, steadier testimony, and less likely to leave doubts about amount or term.

TABRISI:2:282#6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#6/r5.claim: The command may address witnesses and mean not to tire of recording testimony; the stronger referent of its term is the debt's due date, not the witness's allowable period.
TABRISI:2:282#6/r5.anchor: أي إلى أجل الدين وقيل معناه إلى أجل الشاهد

TABRISI:2:282#6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#6/r6.claim: Writing the debt or testimony is more just before God, more reliable for testimony, and closer to preventing doubt; قسط means fairness and الأقسط means acting justly.

TABRISI:2:282#6/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#6/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#6/r7.claim: A spot transaction exchanged hand to hand can be left unwritten because documentation is needed for deferred payment, not cash trade.
TABRISI:2:282#6/r7.anchor: فليس عليكم إثم في ترك كتابتها لأن الكتابة للوثيقة

TABRISI:2:282#7/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r1.speaker: الحسن وجميع الفقهاء
TABRISI:2:282#7/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan and the jurists regard witnessing sales as recommended; the Ẓāhirīs make it obligatory.
TABRISI:2:282#7/r1.anchor: وهذا أمر على الاستحباب والندب عن الحسن وجميع الفقهاء

TABRISI:2:282#7/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r2.speaker: الحسن وقتادة وعطاء وابن زيد
TABRISI:2:282#7/r2.claim: With kasra on the first rāʾ, the prohibition addresses the writer and witness: do not change dictated terms, testify to matters not requested, or refuse to testify.
TABRISI:2:282#7/r2.anchor: أصله يضارر بكسر الراء الأولى عن الحسن وقتادة وعطاء وابن زيد

TABRISI:2:282#7/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود ومجاهد
TABRISI:2:282#7/r3.claim: With fatḥ on the first rāʾ, the prohibition tells people not to impose writing on a busy scribe or summon a witness when excused, or to mistreat either.
TABRISI:2:282#7/r3.anchor: وقيل الأصل فيه لا يضارر بفتح الراء الأولى عن ابن مسعود ومجاهد

TABRISI:2:282#7/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r4.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:282#7/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the first reading is clearer because deliberate falsification makes someone a wrongdoer more plausibly than summoning a busy witness does.

TABRISI:2:282#7/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:282#7/r5.claim: The verse threatens that harming a scribe or witness in writing or testimony is a departure from God's commands; fear God, who teaches what is needed and knows all.
TABRISI:2:282#7/r5.anchor: معناه وإن تفعلوا مضارة الكاتب والشهيد فإن المضارة في الكتابة والشهادة فسوق بكم

TABRISI:2:282#7/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:282#7/r6.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
TABRISI:2:282#7/r6.claim: ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim's tafsīr counts five hundred legal rulings in al-Baqara and fifteen in this verse alone.
TABRISI:2:282#7/r6.anchor: وذكر علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم في تفسيره أن في البقرة خمسمائة حكم

THALABI:v2p290/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p290/r1.claim: When God prohibited usury, He permitted deferred sale; tadayantum means you transact debt with one another, including loans, forward sales, and other deferred obligations.
THALABI:v2p290/r1.anchor: ابن عباس: لما حرم الله الربا، أباح السلم، فقال: يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا تداينتم

THALABI:v2p290/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p290/r2.claim: Dayn is deferred while ʿayn is present; dāna means to lend, the lender is dā'in, and the recipient is madin or madyun.
THALABI:v2p290/r2.anchor: والدين ما كان مؤجلا والعين ما كان حاضرا، يقال: دان فلانا يدينه

THALABI:v2p290/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p290/r3.claim: Although mutual dealing can already imply debt, bidayn clarifies it because tadayun can also mean exchange or spot barter.
THALABI:v2p290/r3.anchor: فإنما قال: بدين والمداينة لا تكون إلا بدين لأن المداينة قد [تكون] مجازاة

THALABI:v2p290/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p290/r4.claim: Alternatively, the repeated word emphasizes the point, like saying a bird flies with its wings or all the angels prostrated.
THALABI:v2p290/r4.anchor: وقيل: هو بمعنى التأكيد كقوله: ولا طائر يطير بجناحيه

THALABI:v2p290/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p290/r5.claim: A specified term is a known time; write the sale, loan, or other debt to prevent denial, forgetting, or dispute.
THALABI:v2p290/r5.anchor: اكتبوا الذي تداينتم به بيعا كان أو قرضا

THALABI:v2p290/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p290/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p290/r6.claim: Jurists disagree whether writing is obligatory; Ibn Jurayj says a borrower should write and a seller obtain witnesses, the view chosen by al-Tabari and supported by a prophetic report that begins by naming three unanswered supplications.
THALABI:v2p290/r6.anchor: فقال بعضهم: فرض واجب، قال ابن جريج: من أدان فليكتب

THALABI:v2p291/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p291/r1.claim: A warning example links failure to document a debt and entrusting wealth to a fool with the preceding injunction against giving fools property.
THALABI:v2p291/r1.anchor: رجل كان له دين فلم يشهد، ورجل أعطى سفيها مالا، وقد قال الله تعالى

THALABI:v2p291/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r2.speaker: قوم
THALABI:v2p291/r2.claim: Writing the debt is recommended and discretionary: documenting it is good, but leaving it carries no blame.
THALABI:v2p291/r2.anchor: قال قوم: هو أمر استحباب وتخيير فإن كتب فحسن وإن ترك فلا بأس.

THALABI:v2p291/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r3.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v2p291/r3.claim: Al-Farra chooses the discretionary reading, comparing the writing command to commands to hunt after ihram and disperse after Friday prayer.
THALABI:v2p291/r3.anchor: كقوله: وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا . وقوله: فإذا قضيت الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض . هو اختيار الفراء.

THALABI:v2p291/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r4.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v2p291/r4.claim: The debt record, witnesses, and pledge were initially obligatory, then the trust clause abrogated that requirement.
THALABI:v2p291/r4.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان كتاب الدين والإشهاد والرهن فرضا ثم نسخ ذلك بقوله تعالى: فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي اؤتمن أمانته وهو قول الشعبي.

THALABI:v2p291/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r5.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p291/r5.claim: Al-Hasan reads وليكتب with a kasra on the command lām; the lām is ordinarily for an absent subject, and after conjunctions Arabs often sukun it for ease while some retain the original kasra.
THALABI:v2p291/r5.anchor: ثم بين كيفية الكتابة فقال عز من قائل: وليكتب بينكم كاتب بالعدل وقرأ الحسن وليكتب بكسر اللام، وهذه اللام، لام الأمر ولا يؤمر بها غير الغائب،

THALABI:v2p291/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p291/r6.claim: The writer records the debt agreement for seller, buyer, creditor, and debtor, accurately and impartially without changing amount, due date, or either party's rights.
THALABI:v2p291/r6.anchor: كاتب بالعدل أي بالحق والإنصاف فلا يزيد فيه ولا ينقص منه ولا يقدم الأجل

THALABI:v2p291/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p291/r7.claim: A writer must not refuse to write as God taught; this command mattered because trained writers were few in the Prophet's time.
THALABI:v2p291/r7.anchor: ولا يأب ولا يمتنع كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب وذلك إن الكتاب كانوا قليلا

THALABI:v2p291/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r8.speaker: مجاهد والربيع
THALABI:v2p291/r8.claim: Mujahid and al-Rabiʿ hold that a writer is obliged to write when asked.
THALABI:v2p291/r8.anchor: فقال مجاهد والربيع: واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب إذ أمر.

THALABI:v2p291/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r9.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p291/r9.claim: Al-Hasan makes writing obligatory when refusing would harm the creditor because no other writer is available, but optional when another can do it.
THALABI:v2p291/r9.anchor: ذلك في الموضع الذي لا يقدر فيه على كاتب غيره فيضر صاحب الدين إن امتنع

THALABI:v2p291/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r10.speaker: الضحاك
THALABI:v2p291/r10.claim: Al-Dahhak says the command originally bound writers and witnesses, then the prohibition on harming them abrogated it.
THALABI:v2p291/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كانت هذه عزيمة واجبة على الكاتب والشاهد فنسخها قوله: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد.

THALABI:v2p291/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r11.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v2p291/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says writing is obligatory when the writer is free from other work.
THALABI:v2p291/r11.anchor: السدي: هو واجب عليه في حال فراغه.

THALABI:v2p291/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p291/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p291/r12.claim: The debtor should dictate and acknowledge the debt himself because he knows what he owes; imlāl and imlāʾ are both proper Arabic forms.
THALABI:v2p291/r12.anchor: وليملل الذي عليه الحق. المديون والمطلوب يقر على نفسه بلسانه ليعلم ما عليه، والإملال والإملاء لغتان فصيحتان

THALABI:v2p292/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r1.claim: The Qurʾanic use of imlāʾ is echoed by the description of scripture being dictated morning and evening.
THALABI:v2p292/r1.anchor: قال الله تعالى: فهي تملى عليه بكرة وأصيلا .

THALABI:v2p292/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r2.claim: Imlāl originally means repeating something insistently; a cited poem uses أمل to describe time wearing down dwellings.
THALABI:v2p292/r2.anchor: أصل الإملال: إعادة الشيء مرة بعد مرة والإلحاح عليه. قال الشاعر:

THALABI:v2p292/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r3.claim: The debtor must fear God and not reduce any part of what he owes.
THALABI:v2p292/r3.anchor: ثم خوفه فقال: وليتق الله ربه ولا يبخس منه شيئا. أي لا ينقص من الحق الذي عليه شيئا،

THALABI:v2p292/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p292/r4.claim: Mujahid interprets a foolish debtor as someone ignorant about money.
THALABI:v2p292/r4.anchor: فإن كان الذي عليه الحق. يعني وإن كان المطلوب الذي عليه المال سفيها. جاهلا بالمال. قاله مجاهد،

THALABI:v2p292/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r5.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
THALABI:v2p292/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak and al-Suddi include a child or a weak person, such as an elderly person, among those needing a guardian to dictate.
THALABI:v2p292/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك والسدي: طفلا صغيرا أو ضعيفا. أو شيخا كبيرا.

THALABI:v2p292/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r6.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
THALABI:v2p292/r6.claim: Al-Suddi and Ibn Zayd explain inability to dictate as incapacity caused by muteness, confusion, absence, foreign speech, disability, confinement, or ignorance of the debt.
THALABI:v2p292/r6.anchor: السدي وابن زيد: يعني عاجزا أحمق أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو. لخرس أو عي أو غيبة أو عجمة

THALABI:v2p292/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r7.claim: The debtor's wali is his guardian or heir, who dictates impartially when the debtor cannot.

THALABI:v2p292/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r8.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل
THALABI:v2p292/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Rabiʿ, and Muqatil instead identify the person who dictates as the creditor, who knows the debt best.
THALABI:v2p292/r8.anchor: ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل: يعني فليملل ولي الحق وصاحب الدين لأنه أعلم بدينه بالعدل

THALABI:v2p292/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r9.claim: The sīn in استشهدوا marks a request: call for two witnesses.
THALABI:v2p292/r9.anchor: استشهدوا. هذا السين للسؤال والطلب شهيدين. شاهدين من رجالكم.

THALABI:v2p292/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r10.speaker: مالك والشافعي وأبو حنيفة وسفيان وأكثر الفقهاء
THALABI:v2p292/r10.claim: The required male witnesses are free adult Muslims, excluding slaves, minors, and free non-Muslims.
THALABI:v2p292/r10.anchor: يعني الأحرار البالغين دون العبيد والصبيان ودون أحرار الكفار. وهذا مذهب مالك

THALABI:v2p292/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r11.speaker: شريح وابن سيرين وأنس بن مالك
THALABI:v2p292/r11.claim: Shurayh, Ibn Sirin, and Anas permit testimony by a slave; some jurists accept it only in minor matters.
THALABI:v2p292/r11.anchor: وأجاز شريح وابن سيرين بشهادة العبد وهو قول أنس بن مالك. وأجاز بعضهم شهادتهم

THALABI:v2p292/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r12.claim: If two men are unavailable, the transaction may be witnessed by one man and two women.
THALABI:v2p292/r12.anchor: فإن لم يكونا رجلين. يعني فإن لم يكن الشاهدان رجلين فرجل وامرأتان. أو فليشهد رجل وامرأتان.

THALABI:v2p292/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p292/r13.claim: Jurists agree that women may testify alongside men in property matters, but dispute other matters: Malik and several others limit them to property, while Abu Hanifa and Sufyan allow them generally except in fixed penalties and retaliation.
THALABI:v2p292/r13.anchor: وأجمع الفقهاء على أن شهادة النساء جائزة مع الرجال في الأموال، واختلفوا في غير الأموال.

THALABI:v2p292/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p292/r14.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
THALABI:v2p292/r14.claim: Umar says judges infer a person's character from visible conduct, and should not doubt someone whose neighbors, relatives, and companions praise him.
THALABI:v2p292/r14.anchor: من أظهر لنا خيرا ظننا به خيرا فأجبناه عليه ومن أظهر لنا شرا ظننا به شرا

THALABI:v2p293/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r1.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي
THALABI:v2p293/r1.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi defines uprightness as having no apparent cause for suspicion.
THALABI:v2p293/r1.anchor: وقال إبراهيم النخعي: العدل: من لم يظهر منه ريبة.

THALABI:v2p293/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r2.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v2p293/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbi defines an upright witness as one not accused of sexual or financial misconduct.
THALABI:v2p293/r2.anchor: وقال الشعبي: العدل: من لم يطعن عليه في بطن ولا فرج.

THALABI:v2p293/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r3.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p293/r3.claim: Al-Hasan defines uprightness as having no known disgrace.
THALABI:v2p293/r3.anchor: وقال الحسن: هو من لم يعلم له خزية.

THALABI:v2p293/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p293/r4.claim: A prophetic report disqualifies a treacherous witness, someone punished for a ḥadd, a hostile witness, a known perjurer, a household dependent, and a suspect relative or client.
THALABI:v2p293/r4.anchor: لا يجوز شهادة خائن ولا خائنة ولا مجلود حدا ولا ذي غمر على أخيه

THALABI:v2p293/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p293/r5.claim: An acceptable witness must meet ten conditions: freedom, adulthood, Islam, uprightness, knowledge of the matter, no personal gain or avoidance of harm, few errors, proper social conduct, no excessive leniency, and no adverse testimony from his slave.
THALABI:v2p293/r5.anchor: وجملة القول فيمن تقبل شهادته: أن تجتمع فيه عشر خصال: يكون حرا بالغا مسلما عدلا

THALABI:v2p293/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p293/r6.claim: Women may testify without men in four matters: women's bodily defects, nursing, childbirth, and the first cry after birth; bodily evidence is limited to the specified private areas.
THALABI:v2p293/r6.anchor: وتقبل شهادة النساء على الانفراد لا رجل معهن في أربع مواضع: عيوب النساء

THALABI:v2p293/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
THALABI:v2p293/r7.claim: The sole disagreement about those four matters concerns nursing: Abu Hanifa requires either two men or one man and two women for it.
THALABI:v2p293/r7.anchor: ولا خلاف في ذلك كله إلا في الرضاع. وان أبا حنيفة ذهب إلى أن شهادة النساء

THALABI:v2p293/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p293/r8.claim: Asked about testimony, the Prophet says a witness should testify only to something as evident as seeing the sun.
THALABI:v2p293/r8.anchor: وأما صفة الشهادة فروى طاوس عن ابن عباس قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن الشهادة

THALABI:v2p293/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p293/r9.claim: The Prophet urges honoring witnesses because God uses them to establish rights and repel injustice.
THALABI:v2p293/r9.anchor: أكرموا الشهود فإن الله عز وجل يستخرج بهم الحقوق ويدفع بهم الظلم

THALABI:v2p293/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v2p293/r10.claim: A report warns that withholding a rightful testimony for three days after being entrusted with it incurs a qīrāṭ of sin.
THALABI:v2p293/r10.anchor: من حبس ذكر حق بعد ما تقبض ما فيه ثلاثا فعليه قيراط من الإثم

THALABI:v2p293/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p293/r11.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة
THALABI:v2p293/r11.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Hamza read إن with kasra and فتذكر in the nominative, construing the clause conditionally or as a new beginning.
THALABI:v2p293/r11.anchor: قرأ الأعمش وحمزة: «إن» بكسر الألف (فتذكر) رفعا، ومعناه الجزاء والابتداء

THALABI:v2p294/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p294/r1.claim: The common reading has إن with fatḥa and فتذكر accusative, linked to the preceding clause through an understood causal preposition: one woman may err so the other reminds her.
THALABI:v2p294/r1.anchor: وقراءة العامة بنصب الألف، فالفاء على الاتصال بالكلام الأول وموضع (أن) نصب

THALABI:v2p294/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p294/r2.claim: The construction places cause before effect, like the cited verse whose sense is that they would ask for a messenger if calamity struck them.
THALABI:v2p294/r2.anchor: وهذا من المقدم والمؤخر، كقولك: إنه ليعجبني أن يسأل فيعطى، يعني:

THALABI:v2p294/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p294/r3.claim: Here tadilla means to forget, as in verses that pair ضلال with not knowing or forgetting and describe losing something in the earth.
THALABI:v2p294/r3.anchor: ومعنى قوله (أن تضل) : أي تنسى، كقوله: لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى .

THALABI:v2p294/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r4.speaker: عاصم الجحدري
THALABI:v2p294/r4.claim: Asim al-Jahdari reads tadilla in the passive, with taḍalla's tāʾ vowelled in ḍamma and dāl in fatḥa.
THALABI:v2p294/r4.anchor: وقرأ عاصم الجحدري: أن تضل أحداهما بضم التاء وفتح الضاد

THALABI:v2p294/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r5.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
THALABI:v2p294/r5.claim: Zayd ibn Aslam reads فتذكر as mutual reminding.
THALABI:v2p294/r5.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن أسلم: فتذكر من المذاكرة.

THALABI:v2p294/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r6.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وقتيبة
THALABI:v2p294/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Yaqub, Abu Hatim, and Qutayba read فتذكر without doubling; the remaining readers double the consonant.
THALABI:v2p294/r6.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ويعقوب وأبو حاتم وقتيبة: فتذكر خفيفه، وقرأ الباقون مشددا.

THALABI:v2p294/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p294/r7.claim: Dhakkara and adhkara can both mean remind, like the paired forms nuzzila/anzala and karuma/akrama; a poem uses the sun as a reminder.
THALABI:v2p294/r7.anchor: وذكر وأذكر بمعنى واحد كما يقال: نزل وأنزل وكرم وأكرم،

THALABI:v2p294/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r8.speaker: أبو عبيد
THALABI:v2p294/r8.claim: Abu Ubayd transmits Sufyan ibn Uyayna's view that a woman's testimony joined to another woman's becomes like a man's testimony.
THALABI:v2p294/r8.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: حدثت عن سفيان بن عينية أنه قال: هو من الذكر،

THALABI:v2p294/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p294/r9.claim: The author rejects that reading of the rationale because the reminder is conjoined to forgetting, not to male remembrance.
THALABI:v2p294/r9.anchor: قلت: هذا القول لا يعجبني لأنه معطوف على النسيان والله أعلم.

THALABI:v2p294/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r10.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v2p294/r10.claim: Some read the summons command as requiring people to accept the burden of serving as witnesses.
THALABI:v2p294/r10.anchor: ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا. قال بعضهم: هذا في محمل الشهادة وهو أمر إيجاب.

THALABI:v2p294/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r11.speaker: قتادة والربيع
THALABI:v2p294/r11.claim: Qatada and al-Rabiʿ report that people once refused when asked to witness in a large neighborhood, prompting this verse.
THALABI:v2p294/r11.anchor: كان الرجل يطوف في الحي العظيم فيه القوم فيدعوهم إلى الشهادة فلا يتبعه أحد

THALABI:v2p294/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r12.speaker: الشعبي
THALABI:v2p294/r12.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says accepting a witness role is optional when another witness is available and obligatory when the person is the only one.
THALABI:v2p294/r12.anchor: وقال الشعبي: هو مخير في تحمل الشهادة إذا وجد غيره، فإن شاء شهد وإن شاء لم يشهد،

THALABI:v2p294/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p294/r13.speaker: عطاء وعطية
THALABI:v2p294/r13.claim: Ata and Atiyya take the summons as recommendation, leaving a person free whether or not to testify.
THALABI:v2p294/r13.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا أمر ندب وهو مخير في جميع الأحوال إن شاء شهد وإن شاء لم يشهد.

THALABI:v2p295/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r1.speaker: أبو بحرية
THALABI:v2p295/r1.claim: Abu Bahriyya says al-Hasan told a reluctant person summoned to testify that he need not attend and may choose.
THALABI:v2p295/r1.anchor: وقال أبو بحرية: قلت للحسن: أدعى إلى الشهادة وأنا كاره، قال: فلا تجب ولا تشهد إن شئت.

THALABI:v2p295/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r2.speaker: مغيرة
THALABI:v2p295/r2.claim: Mughira reports that Ibrahim advised him not to testify if he feared forgetting and did not wish to.
THALABI:v2p295/r2.anchor: وقال مغيرة: قلت لإبراهيم: إني أدعى إلى الشهادة وإني أخاف أن أنسى، قال: فلا تشهد أن تحب.

THALABI:v2p295/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وعكرمة وسعيد بن جبير والضحاك والسدي
THALABI:v2p295/r3.claim: Mujahid and these scholars say the prohibition concerns establishing testimony already witnessed: a witness must not refuse when called to give it.
THALABI:v2p295/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم: هذا في إقامة الشهادة وأدائها، ومعنى الآية: ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا لإقامة الشهادة

THALABI:v2p295/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r4.speaker: عامر
THALABI:v2p295/r4.claim: Amir says a witness remains free to decline until he has actually testified.
THALABI:v2p295/r4.anchor: روى سفيان عن جابر عن عامر قال الشاهد بالخيار ما لم يشهد

THALABI:v2p295/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r5.speaker: الحسن والسدي
THALABI:v2p295/r5.claim: Al-Hasan and al-Suddi apply the command to both bearing and giving testimony when the witness is available.
THALABI:v2p295/r5.anchor: هذه الآية في الأمرين جميعا في التحمل والاقامة إذا كان فارغا

THALABI:v2p295/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p295/r6.claim: Tasʾamu means grow weary; the cited lines by Zuhayr and Labid attest the verb for tiring of life or its length.
THALABI:v2p295/r6.anchor: ولا تسئموا. ولا تملوا يقال: سئمت أسأم سأما وسأمة، قال زهير:

THALABI:v2p295/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p295/r7.claim: An may be a verbal noun object, meaning tire of writing it, or governed by an omitted preposition, meaning tire of writing it.
THALABI:v2p295/r7.anchor: وأن في محل النصب من وجهين: إن شئت جعلته مع الفعل مصدرا وأوقعت السآمة عليه،

THALABI:v2p295/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r8.speaker: السلمي
THALABI:v2p295/r8.claim: Al-Sulami reads ولا يسأموا with a third-person yāʾ.

THALABI:v2p295/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p295/r9.claim: Small or large describes whether the debt or amount is slight or substantial; the forms can be parsed as circumstantial modifiers or as predicates of an implied kāna.
THALABI:v2p295/r9.anchor: صغيرا. كان الحق أو كبيرا. قليلا كان المال أو كثيرا،

THALABI:v2p295/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p295/r10.claim: A written record is more just, steadier for testimony, and less likely to leave doubt about the amount or term; the author compares this with another verse about giving testimony properly.
THALABI:v2p295/r10.anchor: إلى أجله . إلى محل الحق ذلكم. الكتاب أقسط. أعدل عند الله. لأنه أمر به،

THALABI:v2p295/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p295/r11.speaker: عاصم
THALABI:v2p295/r11.claim: Asim reads the immediate-trade exception in the accusative as a predicate of kāna with its subject omitted; the syntax is explained further in the next segment.
THALABI:v2p295/r11.anchor: قرأها عاصم بالنصب على خبر كان وأضمر الاسم

THALABI:v2p296/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r1.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v2p296/r1.claim: Al-Farra cites lines using كان يوما and كان طعنا to show that kāna may take an omitted noun understood as the occasion or event.
THALABI:v2p296/r1.anchor: إذا كان يوما ذا كواكب أشنعا أي إذا كان اليوم يوما

THALABI:v2p296/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p296/r2.claim: The majority reading raises tijāra under either an existential sense of kāna or as its subject, with تديرونها بينكم as predicate.
THALABI:v2p296/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالرفع على وجهين: أحدهما: أن يكون معنى الكون الوقوع،

THALABI:v2p296/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p296/r3.claim: The exception means an immediate, hand-to-hand transaction without a deferred term or credit need not be written.
THALABI:v2p296/r3.anchor: تجارة حاضرة يدا بيد تديرونها بينكم ليس فيها أجل ولا نسيئة

THALABI:v2p296/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p296/r4.claim: The exemption from writing applies to the cash transaction, while witnesses are still commanded when a sale takes place.
THALABI:v2p296/r4.anchor: فليس عليكم جناح ألا تكتبوها. يعني التجارة وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم.

THALABI:v2p296/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r5.speaker: الضحاك ومحمد بن جرير
THALABI:v2p296/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak treats witnessing as a firm divine command for every transaction, small or large and cash or deferred; Muhammad ibn Jarir prefers this view.
THALABI:v2p296/r5.anchor: قال الضحاك: هو عزم من الله عز وجل، والاشهاد واجب في صغير الحق وكبيره

THALABI:v2p296/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
THALABI:v2p296/r6.claim: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri says the decision to witness depends on mutual trust, citing the following verse.
THALABI:v2p296/r6.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد الخدري: الأمر فيه إلى الامانة. قال الله فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا.

THALABI:v2p296/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r7.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v2p296/r7.claim: Other scholars treat witnessing sales as recommended, leaving the parties free to call witnesses or not.
THALABI:v2p296/r7.anchor: وقال الآخرون: هو أمر ندب إن شاء أشهد وإن لم يشاء لم يشهد

THALABI:v2p296/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p296/r8.claim: The prohibition has assimilated doubled rāʾ letters from yudār ir, with fatḥa resolving the two adjacent sukūns.
THALABI:v2p296/r8.anchor: وأصله يضارر فأدغمت الراء في الراء ونصبت لحق التضعيف

THALABI:v2p296/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r9.speaker: طاوس والحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
THALABI:v2p296/r9.claim: On the active reading, a writer must not alter the dictated record and a witness must not invent testimony or refuse to establish what he saw.
THALABI:v2p296/r9.anchor: ولا شهيد فيشهد ما لم يشهد عليه أو يمتنع من إقامة الشهادة،

THALABI:v2p296/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p296/r10.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v2p296/r10.claim: On the passive reading, the parties must not harass a busy writer or witness; if they are occupied, the requester should find someone else.
THALABI:v2p296/r10.anchor: وأجراه آخرون على الفعل المجهول وجعلوا الكاتب والشهيد مفعولين

THALABI:v2p297/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297/r1.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
THALABI:v2p297/r1.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas reports that people sometimes pressured busy writers and witnesses by invoking the command, even when alternatives existed, so the verse prohibited harming them.
THALABI:v2p297/r1.anchor: وقال الربيع بن أنس: لما نزلت هذه الآية ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله فليكتب

THALABI:v2p297/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297/r2.speaker: عمر وأبي وابن مسعود ومجاهد
THALABI:v2p297/r2.claim: Umar, Ubayy, Ibn Masʿud, and Mujahid read ولا يضارر with the doubled consonants made explicit, supporting the interpretation that the writer or witness is not to be harmed.
THALABI:v2p297/r2.anchor: ودليل هذا التأويل قراءة عمر وأبي وابن مسعود ومجاهد: ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد

THALABI:v2p297/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v2p297/r3.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads ولا يضار in a light, jussive form with one rāʾ.
THALABI:v2p297/r3.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: ولا يضار، مجزوما مخففا القى راء واحدة

THALABI:v2p297/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297/r4.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v2p297/r4.claim: Al-Hasan reads ولا يضار with a doubled rāʾ and kasra.
THALABI:v2p297/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ولا يضار بكسر الراء مشددا

THALABI:v2p297/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p297/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p297/r5.claim: The prohibited harm is disobedience and departure from God's command; the passage closes by commanding reverence and affirming God's knowledge.
THALABI:v2p297/r5.anchor: وإن تفعلوا. ما نهيتكم عنه من الضراء فإنه فسوق بكم. خروج عن الأمر واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n269/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n269/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n269/r1.claim: The credit rule covers loans and commercial transactions, and tadayantum grammatically includes both the giver and receiver of credit.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n269/r1.anchor: any transaction on the basis of credit, be it an outright loan or a commercial deal

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n270/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n270/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n270/r1.claim: The scribe is to write in accordance with the laws laid down in the Qur’an.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n270/r1.anchor: in accordance with the laws promulgated in the Qur'an

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n271/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n271/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n271/r1.claim: The instruction literally says not to diminish any part of the undertaking, whose wording is entrusted to the debtor as the weaker party.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n271/r1.anchor: the formulation of the undertaking is left to the weaker party, i.e., to the one who contracts the debt

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n272/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n272/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n272/r1.claim: A debtor may be unable to dictate because of physical disability, difficulty understanding business terms, or unfamiliarity with the contract language; weakness of understanding or body includes minors and mentally diminished elders.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n272/r1.anchor: does not fully understand the business terminology used in such contracts, or is not acquainted with the language

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n273/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n273/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n273/r1.claim: The two-women provision does not question women’s moral or intellectual ability; Asad, citing ‘Abduh, attributes it to women’s usual lack of experience with business procedures and greater risk of mistakes.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n273/r1.anchor: it is obviously due to the fact that, as a rule, women are less familiar with business procedures than men

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n274/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n274/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n274/r1.claim: Writing down the contract means recording all rights and obligations that arise from it.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n274/r1.anchor: all rights and obligations arising from the contract

ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n275/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n275/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n275/r1.claim: A scribe or witness must not be harmed by being held responsible for the contract’s consequences or either party’s failure to perform.
ASAD-NOTES:2:282#n275/r1.anchor: held responsible for the eventual consequences of the contract as such, or for the non-fulfilment

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās connects the verse with God forbidding usury while permitting salam, or advance purchase on credit.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم حرم الله تعالى الربا أباح السلم فقال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r2.claim: Tadāyun is reciprocal dealing in debt, such as selling to one another on credit; loans are distinct from deferred debts, since classical loans cannot have a term but debts can.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r2.anchor: التداين: تفاعل، من الدين، ومعناه: داين بعضكم بعضا وتبايعتم بدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r3.claim: Dāna may mean selling on credit, lending, borrowing, or being heavily indebted; tadayyana and istadāna mean taking debt, illustrated by poetry.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r3.anchor: ويقال من الدين: ادان: إذا باع سلعته (¬1) بثمن إلى أجل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r4.claim: The exegetes say every right whose due date is deferred is covered by this verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: كل حق مؤجل فهو داخل تحت قوله: {إذا تداينتم بدين}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī explains the explicit word dayn after tadāyantum by distinguishing financial dealing from moral recompense, since dayn can mean requital too.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p483/r5.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: إنما ذكر الدين مع أن {تداينتم} يدل عليه؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r1.claim: An ajal is the time set for an interval to end; a person’s ajal is death, while a debt’s ajal is its due date, and the root conveys delay.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r1.anchor: معنى الأجل في اللغة: الوقت المضروب لانقضاء الأمد، وأجل الإنسان هو الوقت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r2.speaker: عطاء وابن جريج وإبراهيم وابن جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r2.claim: A group, chosen by Ibn Jarīr, treat writing and witnessing deferred debts as obligatory to protect wealth and deter denial; Ibrāhīm says even a tiny handful of greens should be documented.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r2.anchor: وهذا مذهب عطاء (¬2) وابن جريح (¬3) وإبراهيم (¬4) واختيار محمد بن جرير (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ regards writing and witnesses as recommendation and permission like the commands in 5:2 and 62:10: documenting is good but leaving it is harmless.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: هذا أمر ندب وإباحة كقوله: {وإذا حللتم فاصطادوا}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī agrees that the command is nonbinding because most scholars hold this and obligatory documentation would impose severe hardship; the Prophet described his mission as easy and tolerant.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r4.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: وهو اختيارنا؛ لاتفاق أكثر العلماء عليه،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.speaker: آخرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.claim: Others say writing, witnesses, or collateral were initially obligatory but were abrogated by the trust clause in 2:283, which permits leaving documentation when the parties trust each other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r5.anchor: وقال آخرون: كانت الكتابة والإشهاد أو الرهن فرضا، ثم نسخ ذلك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.claim: Asked by al-Taymī, al-Ḥasan said the parties may witness or omit witnesses, citing the clause that some may trust others.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r6.anchor: قال التيمي: سألت الحسن عنها فقال: إن شاء أشهد، وإن شاء لم يشهد،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says scholars in the Ḥijāz and Iraq agree that sale witnesses are not mandatory and that buyers can choose; they treat the following trust clause as abrogating the obligation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p485/r7.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: والعلماء اليوم من أهل الحجاز وأهل العراق وغيرهم على هذا القول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r1.claim: The fair scribe records the debt with equity, granting neither party an advantage, altering neither the amount nor due date, and writing nothing that secretly defeats either party’s right.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r1.anchor: أي: بالحق والإنصاف، لا يكتب لصاحب الدين فضلا على الذي عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r2.claim: A writer must not refuse to document the debt as God taught him; abā means to refuse, and the source also records its use for refusing food.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r2.anchor: أي: لا يمتنع، يقال: أبى فلان الشيء يأباه، إذا امتنع عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r3.speaker: مجاهد والربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r3.claim: Mujāhid and al-Rabīʿ say the scribe must write when asked because God ordered him not to refuse; al-Farrāʾ says there were few literate people in the Prophet’s time.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r3.anchor: قال مجاهد (¬8) والربيع (¬9): واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب إذا أمر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r4.speaker: الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan limits the duty to cases where no other scribe is available, because refusal would harm the creditor.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r4.anchor: وقال الحسن: ذاك إذا لم يقدر على كاتب سواه فيضر بصاحب الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r5.speaker: الضحاك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r5.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the command initially imposed an obligation on scribe and witness, later abrogated by the ban on harming either one.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p487/r5.anchor: وقال الضحاك: كانت هذه عزيمة واجبة على الكاتب والشاهد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r1.claim: As God taught him may attach to write, meaning write as God commanded, or begin a new clause, meaning write as God favored him with literacy; al-Zajjāj gives both parses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r1.anchor: ويحتمل أن يتم الكلام عند قوله: {أن يكتب} ثم قال: {كما علمه الله فليكتب}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as what God enabled the person to understand and says one known to write should not refuse the good deed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كما أفهمه الله، ولا يمنعن المعروف بكتابة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says imlāl is the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad form, while imlāʾ is used by Tamīm and Qays; the Qur’an has both forms, as in 25:5.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: أمللت عليه الكتابة لغة الحجاز وبني أسد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r4.claim: The debtor dictates because the debt is being testified against him and his own words reveal what he owes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p488/r4.anchor: أن (¬4) الذي عليه الدين يملي؛ لأنه المشهود عليه، فيقر على نفسه بلسانه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r1.claim: Bakhs means diminution; the debtor must acknowledge the amount owed without reducing any part of it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r1.anchor: البخس: النقصان، يقال: بخسه حقه، إذا نقصه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r2.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r2.claim: Mujāhid interprets safīh as someone ignorant about dictating the debt.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r3.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r3.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī interpret safīh as a young child.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r4.speaker: السدي وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r4.claim: Al-Suddī and Ibn Zayd explain weak as incapable or mentally deficient.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r4.anchor: يعني: عاجزا أحمق، عن السدي (¬1) وابن زيد (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r5.claim: Someone unable to dictate may be mute, impaired, or ignorant of what he owns and owes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r5.anchor: لخرس أو عي أو (¬3) جهل بما له وعليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r6.speaker: الضحاك وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Ibn Zayd say the wali is the guardian of a child, incapable person, or fool: a trustee, heir, or other person acting for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r6.anchor: قال الضحاك (¬5) وابن زيد (¬6): أي: ولي السفيه والعاجز والطفل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r7.speaker: ابن عباس والربيع ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Rabīʿ, and Muqātil instead say the wali is the creditor, who knows the debt best.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس (¬7) والربيع (¬8) ومقاتل (¬9): يعني: ولي الحق، وهو صاحب الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r8.speaker: الزجاج وصاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r8.claim: Al-Zajjāj and the author of al-Naẓm prefer the guardian interpretation: 4:5 calls for guardians to manage dependents’ assets, and taking the creditor as wali would let a claimant’s assertion replace writing and witnesses.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r8.anchor: والقول الأول اختيار الزجاج (¬10) وصاحب النظم، وهو الأظهر والأصح

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r9.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r9.claim: The passage’s syntax confirms the dependent’s guardian: the debtor is the one who dictates, so his wali must be his representative; a creditor’s representative would have been framed like the earlier scribe.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r9.anchor: وقال صاحب "النظم": الذي يدل عليه نظم هذا الفصل أنه ولي السفيه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r10.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p489/r10.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows both interpretations of who the wali is.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r1.claim: Istashhidū means ashhidū, to call someone as witness; the saying that people testify but are not istushhidūn is explained as saying that they do not testify.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r1.anchor: أي: أشهدوا، يقال: أشهدت الرجل واستشهدته بمعنى (¬7)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r2.claim: The two men are free, adult members of the believers’ community, excluding children and enslaved people.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r2.anchor: يعني: من أهل ملتكم من الأحرار البالغين، دون الصبيان والعبيد (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r3.speaker: الزجاج والفراء وصاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r3.claim: The phrase one man and two women can mean the witnesses sought should be one man and two women, let there be that combination, or let that number suffice; each syntactic paraphrase is sound.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r4.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r4.claim: Al-Akhfash supplies an implicit kāna; it may take a predicate or be complete, with the complete verb preferred because it requires fewer omitted words, though either reading implies testimony by one man and two women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون (¬9) (كان) المضمرة في الآية الناصبة للخبر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r5.claim: There is consensus that women’s testimony is admissible in matters of property.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p491/r5.anchor: واجماع أن شهادة النساء جائزة (¬7) في الأموال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses those whom you approve as people of virtue and religion, like the just witnesses in 65:2; this implies some witnesses should not be accepted.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد: من # أهل الفضل والدين (¬1)، كما في الطلاق

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r2.claim: The source lists ten qualities for an admissible witness: freedom, adulthood, Islam, uprightness, knowledge, no self-serving interest or self-protective motive, no frequent error, no breach of propriety, and no enmity with the party testified against.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r2.anchor: وجملة القول فيمن تقبل شهادته، أن يجتمع فيه عشر خصال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r3.claim: The purpose clause an taḍilla attaches to an implied command to seek one man and two women; it may attach to an implicit verb or to a supplied predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p493/r3.anchor: وذلك أن قوله: {فإن لم يكونا رجلين فرجل وامرأتان} يدل على: فاستشهدوا رجلا وامرأتين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r1.speaker: ابن عباس وجميع أهل التفسير والمعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and exegetes and language scholars take taḍilla as forget, since the forgetful turns away from recall; 26:20 and al-Farazdaq’s verse illustrate it, while Abū ʿAmr says the root means disappearance.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس (¬1) وجميع أهل التفسير والمعاني: تضل: تنسى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r2.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r2.claim: Abū ʿAlī says iḥdā is a feminine form of wāḥid that is used only in an annexed phrase, not by itself.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: أنثوه على غير بنائه، و (إحدى) لا تستعمل إلا مضمومة إلى غيرها ومضافة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r3.speaker: أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās transmits Ibn al-Aʿrābī’s forms for pluralizing iḥdā as iḥd, with analogies to kubr/kubrā and poetic attestation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r3.anchor: وروى أبو العباس عن ابن الأعرابي قال: (¬5) يقال: أحد في جمع إحدى.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r4.claim: An is accusative with a purpose sense: call two women as witnesses so that one can remind the other.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r4.anchor: وموضع (أن) نصب، لأن المعنى: استشهدوا امرأتين، لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r5.speaker: سيبويه والبصريون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p495/r5.claim: Sibawayh and the Basran grammarians explain that the verse names forgetting because it causes the needed reminder, as preparing a support because a wall may lean.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r1.claim: Because the clause also says fatudhakkira, the interpretation of an taḍilla as the stated purpose fails: fear of forgetting makes sense, but fear of reminding does not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r1.anchor: ولما عطف قوله: {فتذكر} على {أن تضل} فسد هذا القول؛

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r2.speaker: حمزة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r2.claim: Ḥamza reads in taḍilla with kasra and fatudhakkira in the indicative; inna is conditional, taḍilla is jussive with a joining fatḥa, and the fāʾ introduces the apodosis.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة (إن تضل) بكسر الألف (فتذكر) بالرفع (¬2)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r3.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r3.claim: By analogy with 5:95, Sibawayh posits a deleted subject after the apodosis fāʾ, meaning in the matter that one woman reminds the other; the condition and answer modify the indefinite two women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r3.anchor: وقياس قول سيبويه في قوله: {ومن عاد فينتقم الله منه} [المائدة: 95]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r4.claim: A conditional clause can describe an indefinite noun, as in 22:41; here condition and answer qualify the two women.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p499/r4.anchor: لأن الشرط والجزاء جملة يوصف # بها، كما يوصف (¬1) بها في نحو قوله: {الذين إن مكناهم في الأرض أقاموا الصلاة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r1.claim: Fatudhakkira is read with either gemination or a light consonant; gemination makes dhakara transitive to a second object, supported by 51:55, 88:21 and a poem, while the light form uses hamza-transitivity and omits the object, meaning the testimony.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r2.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r2.claim: Most exegetes understand the other woman to remind her after she forgets.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r2.anchor: وعامة المفسرين على أن هذا التذكير والإذكار من النسيان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r3.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna instead interprets it as making the other woman a male witness, so their joint testimony counts as a man’s; this is also attributed to Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and reported through a narration.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r3.anchor: إلا ما يروى عن سفيان بن عيينة أنه قال في قوله: {فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r4.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes the readings: geminated means reminding after forgetting; light means one woman reminds the other because the two together stand in a man’s place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r4.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلا: من قرأ: {فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى} بالتشديد فهو من طريق التذكير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r5.claim: Exegetes reject the male-equivalence interpretation: women without a man still cannot testify, forgetting should be paired with its opposite, remembering, and equal male status would apply across all legal rulings.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p500/r5.anchor: وأنكر المفسرون هذا التفسير، وضعفوه، من حيث إن النساء لو بلغن ما بلغن

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r1.speaker: قتادة والربيع
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r1.claim: Qatāda and al-Rabīʿ say the ban on refusing applies when asked to undertake testimony; al-Shaʿbī makes it obligatory only if no one else can do so.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, through ʿAṭāʾ, applies it to giving testimony: after entrusting someone with testimony, one may need him to attend court and deliver it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس، في رواية عطاء: يريد: إذا استودعته الشهادة ثم احتجت إلى شهادة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r3.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة والسدي وسعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r3.claim: Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, al-Suddī, and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr also understand the verse as testimony’s performance and delivery.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r3.anchor: وهو قول مجاهد (¬2) وعكرمة (¬3) والسدي (¬4) وسعيد بن جبير (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r4.speaker: الحسن وأبو إسحاق
