WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the duty covers both undertaking and delivering testimony when the person is available and has no excuse; Abū Isḥāq chooses this view, supported by the adjacent command not to tire of documenting what one witnessed.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r4.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن (¬6) واختيار أبي إسحاق.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r5.claim: Saʾāma means weariness or annoyance; the infinitive clause is accusative as the object of that weariness, and the pronouns in write it and its due date refer to the debt.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r5.anchor: والسآمة: الملالة والضجر، يقال: سئمت الشيء أسأمه سأما وسآمة (¬8)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r6.claim: The command not to tire of writing is best addressed to creditors: document the rights they lend, small or large, with due date and term; the passage begins by addressing asset and debt holders, while trivial amounts are not normally recorded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p502/r6.anchor: وأظهر من هذا أن يجعل قوله: {ولا تسأموا أن تكتبوه} خطابا لأولياء الحق،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r1.claim: Dhālikum refers to the documentation; it is more equitable with God because following God’s command is more just than neglecting it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r1.anchor: أي: الكتاب {أقسط عند الله} أي: أعدل (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r2.claim: Written records make testimony more reliable because they remind witnesses, instead of leaving them to impressions; aqwam means more fully upright, and adnā means closer to removing doubt about amount and term.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r2.anchor: {وأقوم للشهادة} لأن الكتاب يذكر الشهود، فتكون شهادتهم (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r3.claim: A current sale that the parties transact hand to hand can omit documentation because the risks of deferred payment and term are absent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r3.anchor: فلا جناح في ترك ذلك فيه؛ لأن ما يخاف في النساء والتأجيل يؤمن في البيع يدا بيد (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r4.claim: Here kāna means occur or come into being, as in the usage discussed at 2:280.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r4.anchor: والكون هنا بمعنى: الوقوع والحدوث، كما بينا في قوله: {وإن كان ذو عسرة}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r5.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows tadīrūnahā to be accusative as the predicate of kāna; otherwise it is nominative describing a present transaction in circulation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء (¬6): وان شئت جعلت {تديرونها} في موضع نصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r6.speaker: عاصم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r6.claim: ʿĀṣim reads tijāratan ḥāḍiratan in the accusative; Abū Isḥāq understands an implied present debt transaction.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r7.speaker: أبو علي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r7.claim: Abū ʿAlī rejects treating tadāyun or the debt in a person’s liability as the name of kāna, since neither is the concrete trade meant here.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p504/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي: لا يجوز أن يكون التداين اسم كان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r1.claim: The command to witness transactions was discussed at the beginning of the verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r1.anchor: قد ذكرنا ما في هذا في أول الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r2.speaker: طاوس والحسن وقتادة وابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r2.claim: One reading prohibits harming a scribe or witness through falsifying or altering the record, bearing false testimony, or refusing to testify; the active form has the writer and witness as agents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r2.anchor: وهذا قول طاوس (¬4) والحسن (¬5) وقتادة (¬6) وابن زيد (¬7)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وعطاء ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd, ʿAṭāʾ, and Mujāhid instead say not to summon a busy scribe or witness when attending would harm him; on this reading the verb is passive.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود (¬1) وعطاء (¬2) ومجاهد (¬3): معنى الآية: لا يدعى الكاتب وهو مشغول

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj chooses the first interpretation because fisq suits a false witness or person who alters writing, not someone who merely summoned a busy witness; defenders of the second read fisq as sin and disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r4.anchor: والقول الأول اختيار الزجاج، قال: لقوله: {وإن تفعلوا فإنه فسوق بكم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r5.speaker: عمر وأبي وابن مسعود ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r5.claim: A reading attributed to ʿUmar, Ubayy, Ibn Masʿūd, and Mujāhid vocalizes the verb as passive, supporting the interpretation that a busy witness must not be burdened.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v4p508/r5.anchor: ويؤكد هذا الثاني: قراءة عمر (¬7) وأبي (¬8) وابن مسعود (¬9) # ومجاهد (¬1)

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r2.claim: After prohibiting usury, God permits forward-credit sales and commands writing and witnessing deferred debts to protect property; the trust exception in 2:283 abrogates this command.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r2.anchor: فلما حرم الله تعالى الربا أباح السلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r3.claim: A just scribe writes without altering amount or term and must not refuse when asked; this was first obligatory for writer and witness, then abrogated by the prohibition on harming them.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r3.anchor: بالحق والإنصاف، ولا يزيد في المال والأجل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r4.claim: “As God taught him” recognizes God’s favor of literacy; the debtor dictates because he is liable and must acknowledge the debt aloud without reducing it.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r5.claim: A child, incapacitated fool, mute, or speech-impaired debtor has a guardian—an heir or representative—dictate truthfully on his behalf.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r5.anchor: { أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r6.claim: Witnesses are two free adult men of the believers, acceptable for their merit and religion; if one woman forgets, the other reminds her of the testimony.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r6.anchor: أي: من أهل ملتكم من الأحرار البالغين

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r7.claim: Witnesses must not refuse when summoned to bear or give testimony; parties should not let irritation keep them from recording a small or large debt through its due date.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r8.claim: Writing is fairest before God, makes testimony more reliable because the record reminds witnesses, and best prevents doubt about amount or due date.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r9.claim: An immediate exchange of goods is exempt from writing because the risks of delayed payment are absent; witnessing spot sales is also no longer obligatory under the abrogated ruling.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r9.anchor: وذلك أن ما يخاف في النساء والتأجيل

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r10.claim: The ban on harming a scribe or witness forbids altering records, false testimony, and refusing to testify; doing so is sinful.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:281-282/r10.anchor: وهو أن يزيد الكاتب أو ينقص أو يحرف

ELMALILI:2:282/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r1.claim: The verse's readings differ on the forms of an tadilla and fa-tudhakkira; Hamza reads with the hamza's kasra, while Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, and Yaqub use a still zā and an ungeminated kāf.
ELMALILI:2:282/r1.anchor: Hamza kıraatinde hemzenin kesriyle فَتُذَكِّرَ;أَن تَضِلَّ İbn Kesîr, Ebû Amr, Ya‘kūb kıraatlerinde zâl’in sükûnu

ELMALILI:2:282/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r2.claim: Hamza also reads the relevant form with rāʾ in the nominative, whereas readings other than Asim's use the nominative for wa-la yudārra.
ELMALILI:2:282/r2.anchor: Hamza kıraatinde de râ’nın zammıyla تِجَٰرَةً حَاضِرَةًۭ;فَتُذَكِّرَ Âsım kıraatinden mâ‘adâsında ref‘ile

ELMALILI:2:282/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r3.claim: Abu Jaafar reads tijāratan hāḍiratan with an ungeminated rāʾ; Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read furuhun with both rāʾ and hāʾ vocalized and without the alif.
ELMALILI:2:282/r3.anchor: râ ve he’nin zammıyla elifsiz فَرُهُنٌ okunur

ELMALILI:2:282/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r4.claim: Called the Verse of Debt, this is the Quran's longest verse.
ELMALILI:2:282/r4.anchor: Bu birinci âyete “Âyet-i Müdâyene” tâbir olunur ki Kur’an’da en uzun âyet budur

ELMALILI:2:282/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r5.claim: One report gives the occasion of revelation as salam, paying in advance for goods delivered later, though the ruling covers every kind of sale and debt transaction.
ELMALILI:2:282/r5.anchor: Bir rivayette sebeb-i nüzûlü selem, yani peşin semen ile veresi mal almak ise de

ELMALILI:2:282/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r6.claim: Linguists distinguish a loan from debt, so the verse's condition need not cover a pure loan; jurisprudence treats a loan first as a trust and finally as a currency exchange, with no fixed repayment date.

ELMALILI:2:282/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r7.claim: Any debt transaction with a specified, known due date should be written; credit trading remains permissible despite the ban on usury, provided the due date is known and documented.
ELMALILI:2:282/r7.anchor: Borçlaşabilirsiniz, fakat alışverişte borcun vadesi mâlum olmalı, bir de yazılarak tevsik edilmelidir

ELMALILI:2:282/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r8.claim: A neutral scribe should record both parties' rights equally; parties may keep private records, but those do not replace the impartial written contract.
ELMALILI:2:282/r8.anchor: tarafeynden hiçbirine meyl etmeyecek, ‘ale’s-seviyye iki tarafın da hukūkunu olduğu gibi gözeterek yazabilecek bîtaraf bir kâtib-i adl aranızda yazsın

ELMALILI:2:282/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r9.claim: A scribe must write as God taught, following proper documentary practice, justice, or gratitude for the gift of literacy; writing is a collective duty that becomes an individual duty when assigned.
ELMALILI:2:282/r9.anchor: Bunu yazmak farz-ı kifâyedir, ta‘ayyün edince farz-ı ‘ayn olur

ELMALILI:2:282/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r10.claim: Appointing legal document scribes is among the government's duties, and such scribes must write when asked.
ELMALILI:2:282/r10.anchor: hükûmetin kâtib-i vesâik, ta‘bîr-i âharla kâtib-i adl tâyin etmesi de vezâifindendir

ELMALILI:2:282/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282/r11.claim: The debtor dictates the note because its contents constitute the debtor's acknowledgment and the witness statement is against that party.
ELMALILI:2:282/r11.anchor: Çünkü yazılacak senedin mazmûnu onun ikrârı bulunacak, şehadet de onun aleyhine olacaktır

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r1.claim: He defines imlāl as dictating from memory and infers that the debtor should propose and dictate the written debt record.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r1.anchor: İmlâl; “imlâ” kelimesinin aslı veya mürâdifidir ki ezbere söyleyip yazdırmak demektir.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r2.claim: While dictating, the debtor must fear God rather than the scribe and must not reduce any part of the creditor’s right.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r2.anchor: borçlu taraf teklif etmeli, o yazdırmalıdır. Binâen‘aleyh tamamen imlâ etsin

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r3.claim: The debtor must not use deception or insert defensive clauses that alter the legal course of the transaction now or later.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r3.anchor: ifadesinde hîle ve hud‘aya saparak veya bazı kuyûd-ı müdâfi‘a derc ederek vak‘anın hâlen

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r4.claim: A debtor unable to dictate includes a spendthrift fool, a minor or mentally deficient person, or anyone unable because of muteness, stammering, ignorance, or another cause.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r4.anchor: malını israf ve telef eder hafif akıllı bir sefih yahut sagīr veya ma‘tuh bir zaîf

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r5.claim: The debtor’s guardian, trustee, agent, translator, or the creditor as debt-holder may dictate in the debtor’s place, fairly and justly.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r5.anchor: velîsi, yani onun yerine işine bakan veliyy-i umûru, vasîsi, vekîli, tercümanı yahut veliyy-i deyn olan dâin adl ü hakkāniyet vechile imlâ etsin

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r6.claim: The wording “your men” excludes children and non-Muslim men’s testimony against Muslims as sufficient testimony.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r6.anchor: مِنَ الرِّجَالِ buyurulmayıp da مِن رِّجَالِكُمْ buyurulması çocukların

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r7.claim: The witnesses must be people whose testimony is accepted and whose justice and reliability are known; a random pairing is not valid.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r7.anchor: şehadetlerine râzı olacağınız, sizce adalet ve mevsûkiyetleri mâlum şâhidlerden bulunsunlar

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r8.claim: Justice is also required by the instruction in 65:2 to appoint two just witnesses from among you.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r9.claim: On Hamza’s reading, if one woman forgets or errs, the other reminds her.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r9.anchor: yahut –Hamza kıraatine göre– birisi unutur, şaşırırsa birisi diğerine hatırlatır.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r10.claim: Witness competence requires sound retention; witnesses lacking moral probity or reliable acquisition or retention of evidence are not admissible.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r10.anchor: şehâdete ehliyetin şartlarından birisi de hakkıyla zapt u hıfzdır. Ahlâk-ı marziyyesi olmayanların şehâdeti muteber olmayacağı

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r11.claim: A witness need not remember the event continuously, provided they can properly recall it when giving testimony.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r11.anchor: Fakat zabt için evvelinden âhirine kadar

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r12.claim: Someone who recorded an event, later forgot it, and then recalls it clearly by consulting the record may testify.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r12.anchor: Demek ki bir vakayı defterine kaydeden bunu bir müddet unutsa da sonra o deftere müracaat ettiği zaman zihninden iyice hatırlarsa şehadet edebilir.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r13.claim: Someone who only knows they made a record but still cannot recall the event must not testify.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r13.anchor: Kendi kendine “kaydetmişim, amma hâlâ iyi hatırlayamıyorum” diyorsa edemez.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r14.claim: Witnesses should not be prompted; one who has forgotten should be able to remember independently.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r14.anchor: Şâhidlerin ihtâra tâbi‘olması da iyi olmaz, unutan şâhid kendiliğinden hatırlayabilmeli.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r15.claim: Requiring at least two witnesses removes suspicion and the possibility of error or forgetfulness, displaying the strength of their retention and justice.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r15.anchor: Nisâb-ı şehâdetin lâekal iki olması da reyb ü töhmeti, ihtimâl-i hatâ ve nisyânı bertaraf ederek zabtın ve adâletin kuvvetini

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r16.claim: He generalizes that women’s retention is weaker and forgetfulness more likely than men’s, while allowing individual exceptions and treating gender and the majority as the legal reference.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r16.anchor: İşte sûret-i umûmiyede mülâhaza edildiği zaman erkeklere nisbetle kadınlarda kuvvet-i zabt nâkıs ve ihtimâl-i nisyan gālibdir. Böyle olmayanları bulunabilirse de itibar cinse ve ekseredir.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r17.claim: He attributes women’s alleged forgetfulness partly to greater sensitivity and emotional impressions, which can weaken recall even in intelligent people.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r17.anchor: Evvelâ kadınlık fıtratında hassâsiyet gālibdir ve galebe-i hassâsiyet, kesret-i teessürâtı istilzam eder. Kesret-i teessür ise esbâb-ı nisyandandır

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r18.claim: He says women are more inwardly oriented and less engaged with external affairs such as commerce and debts, which he regards as primarily men’s work.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r18.anchor: Hâdisât-ı âfâkiye onu derece-i sâniyede alâkadar eder.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r19.claim: He says modesty and reserve predominate in women and should do so, and that even a small engagement diminishes their distinct worth and leaves fewer reminders of events.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r19.anchor: Sâlisen kadında hayâ ve hicab gālibdir ve gālib olmalıdır. Onun kıymet-i nev‘iyyesi en cüz’î bir meşgūliyetle zâyi‘olur.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r20.claim: He calls a woman’s becoming manlike a degradation and says both feminized men’s and masculinized women’s testimony is inadmissible because they depart from their sex-specific perfection and may distort truth.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r21.claim: He treats women’s comparatively lower retention of external events as a consequence of their sex-specific nature, while saying a woman who later recalls an event fully can testify.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r21.anchor: Şu hâlde fıtrat-ı hak kadının kemâliyle erkeğin kemâlini bi’l-vücûh tefrik etmiş bulunduğundan kadının vâkı‘ât-ı hâriciyeye ait zabtında noksan ihtimâli fazla bulunması kemâl-i nev‘îsinin muktezâsıdır.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r22.claim: It is unjust to compel women to record events or, after a human lapse of memory, to make them recover recollection through outside prompts.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r22.anchor: Kadını re’sen zabt-ı vâkı‘aya mecbur tutmak revâ-yı hak olmadığı gibi lede’l-îcâb üzerine tahmil edilen şehâdeti de hasbe’l-beşeriyye unuttuğu zaman da onu hâricî muhtıralarla tahattura sevketmek de revâ-yı hak değildir.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r23.claim: Two women can confer before testifying and remind one another without outside prompting, strengthening their recall and preserving both their dignity and the right entrusted to them.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r23.anchor: bunlar edâ-yı şehâdetten evvel hâricî hiçbir ihtâra tâbi‘ve muhtaç olmaksızın yekdiğeriyle hasbihâl ederek kendi kendilerine mütekābil ihtârât ile zabtlarını takviye ve tesbit edebilir

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r24.claim: If neither woman forgot, their evidentiary position is stronger; the mutual reminder need not happen in court, where it could prevent acceptance of testimony.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r24.anchor: Şayet hiç unutmamış bulunurlarsa vaziyetleri daha kuvvetli olur. Şu hâlde bu tezkîr ü ihtar mahkemede edâ-yı şehâdet sırasında olacak diye anlaşılmamalıdır.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r25.claim: Where men can know the matter, women should not be made witnesses; if no man is available and a woman must be called, two women should serve for one man.

ELMALILI:2:282#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r26.claim: For matters men cannot witness, women’s reports alone may suffice, sometimes even one woman’s report, as with an incident in a women’s bath or a midwife’s report of birth.
ELMALILI:2:282#2/r26.anchor: erkeklerin muttali‘olmaları câiz olmayan husûsâtta yalnız kadınların ihbârıyla ve hatta sırasına göre bir kadının ihbârıyla da amel câiz olur.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r1.claim: A summons to bear or give testimony must not be refused: testimony is a collective duty, and becomes individually obligatory when nobody else can meet the need or particular people are required.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r1.anchor: gerek tahammül ve gerek edâ olsun, şehadet için vukū‘bulan davete icâbet farz-ı kifâyedir. Hiç kimse gitmezse herkes âsim olur.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r2.claim: Some scholars restrict the prohibition to accepting testimony, others to giving it, and many choose the latter; the author follows the view that the wording is unrestricted and includes both.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r2.anchor: Bazı ulemâ bu nehyin yalnız tahammüle, bazıları da yalnız edâya ait olduğunu beyan etmişler ve birçokları ikinciye hükmeylemişler ise de

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r3.claim: Qatada relates that the verse was revealed after a man went from camp to camp seeking a witness and no one paid attention.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r3.anchor: Katâde’den “bu hususta bir adam oba oba dolaşır kimse aldırmazdı, bu nâzil oldu” diye rivayet edilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r4.claim: Although giving testimony is especially important, necessity can make both accepting and giving testimony individually obligatory.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r4.anchor: edâ farîzası daha mühim olmakla beraber ihtiyaç vukû‘unda gerek tahammül ve gerek edâ-yı şehâdet farz-ı ‘ayn olur.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r5.claim: Every debt, large or small, should be documented in detail through its due date, including all particulars and qualities, rather than dismissed as too minor to write.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r5.anchor: büyük olsun küçük olsun o deyni veya hakkı eceline varıncaya kadar yazmaktan usanmayınız, az olsun çok olsun yazınız ve ecel ü müddetine varıncaya kadar bütün müfredât ve evsâfıyla mufassalan

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r6.claim: Some read the command to keep writing as an explanation and emphasis of the earlier command, directed to scribes; the author finds the broader contextual reading more fitting.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r6.anchor: Bu fıkra bâlâdaki فَٱكْتُبُوهُ emrinin bir tavzih ve te’kîdi olmak üzere kâtiblere hitab gibi tefsir olunuyor. Fakat bunun daha şümullü

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r7.claim: He prefers understanding the command to address both parties, scribes, and witnesses, urging them to keep their own records and, where possible, write down testimony they have undertaken.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r7.anchor: gerek dâyin ve gerek medyun tarafından deynin ayrıca kendi defterlerine kaydını

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r8.claim: Detailed documentation has three benefits: it is most just before God, supports the establishment of testimony, and most nearly prevents doubt.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r8.anchor: Allah ‘indinde a‘deldir, en ziyade adl ü istikāmettir.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r9.claim: A complete record secures confidence about the debt’s kind, amount, term, witnesses, testimony, and the parties’ moral, legal, and social relations.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r10.claim: The exception is a fully cash, hand-to-hand commercial transaction; in that case leaving it unwritten causes no blame.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r10.anchor: meğer ki yaptığınız iş aranızda yed-be-yed alıp vereceğiniz tamamen peşin hâzır bir ticaret muâmelesi olsun

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r11.claim: Even a cash sale may be written privately or in a short memorandum, though the burden on people who cannot write may outweigh the benefit.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r11.anchor: her ihtimâle karşı husûsî bir surette veya icmâlen yekdiğerine bir muhtıra olmak üzere mümkin olduğu kadar yazılıverirse fena da olmaz.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r12.claim: For any sale, including a cash sale, make it openly in the presence of witnesses rather than secretly; this precaution protects property and legal security.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r12.anchor: velev peşin olsun bir mübâya‘a, bir alım satım yaptığınızda işhâd ediniz, şâhid huzurunda alenen yapınız

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r13.claim: The majority of exegetes regard witnessing a sale here as a recommendation for precaution.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r13.anchor: Cumhûr-ı müfessirîn beyan ediyorlar ki bu âyetteki nedb ihtiyat içindir.

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r14.claim: The command not to harm a scribe or witness can mean they must not harm rights-holders by refusing a request or falsifying or altering the writing or testimony.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r14.anchor: ‘inde’l-mürâca‘a icâbet etmemek veya kitâbet ü şehâdeti tahrif ve tağyir eylemek gibi ahlâksızlıkla ashâb-ı hukūku zararlandırmasın

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r15.claim: Alternatively, on the passive reading, scribes and witnesses themselves must not be harmed by excessive demands, interruption of important work, or denial of a scribe’s fee.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r15.anchor: ne kâtib, ne şâhid ızrar edilmesin, bunlara kitabet veya şehadet gibi bir vazîfe-i dîniye tahmil olunurken kendilerince mühim olan işlerinden alıkonulmak

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r16.claim: Causing such harm is a transgression against God’s obedience.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r16.anchor: bu her hâlde sizin için bir fısktır,

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r17.claim: God will teach people more knowledge and rulings that serve their welfare.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r17.anchor: Allah size daha ziyade ilimler öğretecek, mesâlihinizi tazammun eden ahkâmını, ma‘ârifini belletecektir

ELMALILI:2:282#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r18.claim: Because God knows everything, believers should obey commands, avoid prohibitions, trust His promise, honor Him, and secure their dealings; piety is the foundation of that security.
ELMALILI:2:282#3/r18.anchor: tevsik din ve takva olduğunu unutmayınız.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r1.claim: Because ordinary borrowing is necessary and abuse led to usury, the Qur'an permits loans and other lawful deferred contracts after forbidding interest; writing, witnesses, collateral, and trust help ensure timely full repayment and prevent forgetting or denial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r1.anchor: faizi haram kılan Kur’an, gerek ödünç almak ve gerekse diğer meşrû akidleri yapmak suretiyle borçlanmayı helâl kılmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r2.speaker: İbn Abbas
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse was revealed about salam, a sale paid for in advance with goods delivered later, for example at harvest.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r2.anchor: İbn Abbas bu âyetin selem (peşin parayla sonradan, meselâ hasat mevsiminde teslim edilecek mal satma) işlemiyle ilgili olarak geldiğini söylemiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r3.claim: Exegetes correctly generalize the rule to every deferred debt, since a specific occasion of revelation does not confine the ruling.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r3.anchor: âyetin geliş sebebinin özel olması hükmünün genel olmasına engel teşkil etmediğini göz önüne alan tefsirciler, haklı olarak bu âyetin bütün vadeli borç ilişkilerini kapsadığını ifade etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r4.speaker: Dört mezhebin imamlarının içinde bulunduğu çoğunluk
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r4.claim: Most jurists, including the four school imams, and Ibn Atiyya treat the documentation measures as recommended safeguards, not binding commands.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r4.anchor: Dört mezhebin imamlarının içinde bulunduğu çoğunluğa göre burada, borcu güvence altına almak için öngörülen tedbirleri ihtiva eden emirler tavsiye niteliğindedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r5.speaker: Taberî, Dâvûd ez-Zâhirî, Atâ
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r5.claim: Tabari, Dawud al-Zahiri, and Ata consider the command binding: writing is obligatory and abandoning it is sinful.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r5.anchor: Taberî, Dâvûd ez-Zâhirî, Atâ gibi fıkıhçı ve tefsircilere göre bu emir bağlayıcı hüküm getirmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r6.claim: The command for a scribe to write has been read as having literate parties write and exchange documents, while an able writer records the debt for illiterate parties; the verse supports written documents as evidence in Islamic law.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r6.anchor: Yazma emri aynı zamanda İslâm hukukunda yazının delil olduğuna, yazılı vesikanın ispat vasıtası olarak kullanılacağına dayanak kılınmıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r7.claim: Jurists differ on whether an approached scribe must write: some say it is individually obligatory, others say a collective duty when time allows; Jassas says writing itself is not obligatory, but one should teach it or find another writer to prevent rights being lost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r7.anchor: Hanefî fıkıhçısı Cessâs’a göre yazmanın aslı bile farz olmadığına göre kâtibin yazmasının farz olması düşünülemez

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r8.claim: Whether a scribe may charge depends on whether writing is obligatory, since religious duties cannot be paid work but optional acts may be; the author deems abstention impermissible when capable writers are available, especially if no substitute exists and rights may be lost.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r8.anchor: özellikle başkası bulunmadığında ve hakkın zayi olması ihtimali de söz konusu olduğunda yazmaktan geri durmalarının câiz olmadığını söylemek isabetli olsa gerektir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r9.claim: Writing and witnessing are both required because they complement one another in securing the transaction rather than substitute for one another.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r9.anchor: Yazma ve tanık tutma birbirinin yerine geçmek üzere öngörülmemiş, amacı gerçekleştirmeye daha uygun ve yardımcı olacağından ikisi birden istenmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r10.claim: The requirement for witnesses from among your men means they must be adults and Muslim men; jurists generally exclude non-Muslims from witnessing Muslim legal relations except a dying Muslim's will while travelling, arguing Muslims cannot reliably identify which non-Muslims will protect their rights.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r10.anchor: Şahitler çocuk olmayacak, ergenlik çağına gelmiş kimselerden olacaktır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r11.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r11.claim: Financial testimony requires either two men or one man and two women, as a precaution to protect rights rather than because women are intellectually or morally deficient; the second woman helps the first remember, and a woman counts as one witness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r11.anchor: Diğer kadının işi, hemcinsinin unutması veya yanılması halinde ona hatırlatmaktan, hatırlamasına yardımcı olmaktan ibarettir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r12.claim: When a cash transaction is immediately completed, the writing requirement is lifted though witnesses remain recommended, because disputes can arise even without a term.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r12.anchor: Borç doğuran akidlerin peşin usulüyle yapılması, akdin hemen sonunda alacak ve borcun kapanması halinde yazma yükümlülüğü kaldırılmakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r13.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r13.claim: Parties must not inconvenience or harm scribes and witnesses, even with unnecessary calls, pressure, or threats to distort the record; the verse forbids such conduct and calls them to fear God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:282/r13.anchor: İlgili âyet bütün bunları yasaklamakta ve tarafları Allah’tan korkmaya davet etmektedir

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r1.claim: Hamza alone reads إن تضل with kasra and فتذكر geminated in the nominative; the others open أن and use accusative فتذكر, with Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr lightening its kāf.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r1.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وحده: أن تضل بكسر الألف فتذكر بالتشديد والرفع وكسر إن.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r2.claim: أن تضل cannot attach directly to استشهدوا شهيدين; the following alternative of one man and two women signals an omitted command to call those witnesses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r2.anchor: لا يكون متعلقا بقوله: واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r3.claim: Abu al-Hasan supplies فليكن رجل وامرأتان; Abu Ali calls this a good analysis because it gives أن تضل an implied verb that raises the indefinite and governs the clause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن في قوله تعالى : فرجل وامرأتان [البقرة/ 282] التقدير: فليكن رجل وامرأتان، وهذا قول حسن

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r4.claim: Both an auxiliary كان with a predicate and a complete كان meaning occurrence can be supplied; the complete verb requires less ellipsis.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p418/r4.anchor: أن كل واحد منهما يجوز أن يقدر إضماره

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r1.claim: A predicate-taking كان may be omitted because its mention is recoverable from earlier wording; an existential كان is also possible and is simpler because it requires only one omitted element.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r1.anchor: ويجوز أن تضمر التامة التي بمعنى الحدوث والوقوع

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r2.claim: On either analysis, the phrase means that testimony by one man and two women should occur, not that the man and women themselves should occur; the noun testimony is omitted and its complement stands for it.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r2.anchor: ولكن لتحدث شهادتهما، أو تقع، أو تكن شهادة رجل وامرأتين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r3.claim: A third attachment is possible: أن تضل may depend on the predicate of an implied nominal clause, in addition to the implied command to witness or the verb فليشهد.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p420/r3.anchor: فقد جاز في: أن تضل أن يتعلق بأحد ثلاثة أشياء:

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r1.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r1.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya records الواحد، الوحد، and الأحد as synonymous forms.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r1.anchor: وحكى أحمد بن يحيى: أن الواحد والوحد والأحد، بمعنى

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r2.speaker: أبو عمر
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r2.claim: Abu Amr says replacing a kasra-bearing wāw with hamza is limited to attested forms; other grammarians treat the replacement as productive.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r2.anchor: فإن أبا عمر يزعم أن ذلك لا يجاوز به المسموع

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r3.claim: The replacement is phonologically expected because kasra acts like yāʾ beside wāw, just as ḍamma acts like another wāw; a noninitial position need not follow an established initial replacement pattern.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p423/r3.anchor: فالواو إذا وقعت قبلها الياء أعلت، وكذلك إذا وقعت بعدها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r1.claim: The continuation glosses losing the sense of a matter; Abu Zayd then distinguishes a lost road or house from causing an animal or thing to go missing.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r1.anchor: ضللت وجه الأمر. وقال أبو زيد: ضللت الطريق والدار أضله ضلالا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r2.claim: Abu Zayd distinguishes ضللت الطريق or a house, becoming lost, from أضللت an animal or thing, causing it to go missing; a stationary animal is treated like a place.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r2.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: ضللت الطريق والدار أضله ضلالا، وأضللت الفرس والناقة والشيء إضلالا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r3.speaker: أبو الحسن
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r3.claim: Abu al-Hasan says ضللت دار فلان; al-Farazdaq's verse uses it for losing the way while searching for Darim.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r3.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: تقول: ضللت دار فلان، وقال الفرزدق:

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r4.claim: In 20:52, لا يضل ربي means the book does not go astray from my Lord. Here أن is accusative and attaches to one of the previously proposed implied verbs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r4.anchor: وفي كتاب الله تعالى: في كتاب لا يضل ربي ولا ينسى [طه/ 52] أي: لا يضل الكتاب عن ربي.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r5.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r5.claim: The testimony is called so one woman may forget and the other remind her; as Sibawayh explains, forgetting is the cause that makes reminding necessary, not the intended outcome.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p424/r5.anchor: أمر بالإشهاد لأن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى، ومن أجل أن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r1.claim: ممن ترضون describes the nominative رجل وامرأتان, not the earlier accusative شهيدين; the case mismatch rules out the earlier noun phrase as its antecedent.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r1.anchor: علمت أن الوصف الذي هو ظرف إنما هو وصف لقوله: «فرجل وامرأتان» دون من تقدم ذكرهما

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r2.claim: Under Hamza's conditional reading, the clause and response describe the two women; the lām in لأن تضل is jussive, opened to resolve adjacent sukūns, though kasra is also analogically possible.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r2.anchor: والشرط وجزاؤه وصف للمرأتين؛ لأن الشرط وجزاءه جملة يوصف بها كما يوصل بها

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r3.claim: Following Sibawayh, the fa-clause can include an omitted subject and be expanded as فيما تذكر إحداهما الأخرى; the pronoun in إحداهما then refers back to that subject.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427/r3.anchor: أن يكون بعد الفاء في: فتذكر إحداهما مبتدأ محذوف ولو أظهرته لكان فيما تذكر إحداهما الأخرى

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r1.claim: ذكر means either remembering, the opposite of forgetting, or utterance; utterance can be neutral invocation or speech intended to reproach, as Qur'anic examples and poetry show.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r1.anchor: والذكر الذي هو قول يستعمل على ضربين: قول لا ثلب فيه للمذكور، والآخر يراد به ثلب المذكور.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r2.claim: ذكرى can be treated as an indefinite verbal noun, making its following noun accusative, or as a construct governing a genitive object; the cited poets illustrate both analyses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r2.anchor: فمن قدر في «ذكرى» التنوين، نصب الاسم بعده، ومن لم يقدر فيه التنوين جر الاسم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r3.claim: قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا رسولا has two parses: an omitted possessor of remembrance, with ذكرا meaning honor or Qur'an, or a verbal noun governing رسولا as its object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r3.anchor: فأما قوله: قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا رسولا [الطلاق/ 10] فإن قوله: ذكرا، يحتمل أمرين

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r4.claim: Sibawayh records verbal-noun variants such as ذكرته ذكرا, comparing them with حفظته حفظا.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p427#2/r4.anchor: قال سيبويه: قالوا ذكرته ذكرا كحفظته حفظا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r1.claim: If ذكرا رسولا contains an omitted noun, sending down means bringing into being, as with God creating livestock and iron; the omitted noun can mean an honored reminder or scripture.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r1.anchor: فإذا قدرت حذف المضاف كان المعنى في أنزل: الإحداث والإنشاء، كما قال: وأنزل لكم

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r2.claim: Without an omitted noun, ذكرا governs رسولا as its object: God has sent a messenger to be followed and obeyed; ذِكر also means the Qur'an in the cited verses.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r2.anchor: فإن لم تقدر حذف المضاف، كان المعنى: قد أنزل الله إليكم ذكرا رسولا فيكون: رسولا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r3.claim: The source construction is supported by other examples where a verbal noun governs its object; a strengthened or hamzated form of ذكر adds a second object.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p430/r3.anchor: ومثل ذلك في إعمال المصدر قوله تعالى : ما لا يملك لهم رزقا من السماوات والأرض شيئا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r1.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr read فتذكر lightly, using the hamzated causative pattern; the other readers geminate it, using the intensive pattern, and both are valid.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r1.anchor: وقول ابن كثير وأبي عمرو مثل أغرمته وأفرحته، وقول الباقين على غرمته

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r2.claim: The second object of فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى is omitted; the meaning is that one woman reminds the other of the testimony they undertook.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r2.anchor: والمفعول الثاني من قوله سبحانه : فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى محذوف. المعنى: فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى الشهادة

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r3.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r3.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyayna interprets the phrase as one woman making the other a reminder, but Abu Ali judges this weak because women still need a man for a valid testimony.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r3.anchor: وروي عن سفيان بن عيينة في قوله: فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى، أي: تجعلها ذكرا

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r4.claim: Since Abu Ubayda glosses ضلال as forgetting, the natural opposite in context is remembering or reminding; this supports the ordinary reading of the clause.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p432/r4.anchor: ومما يبعد قوله: أن تضل إحداهما، والضلال قد فسره أبو عبيدة: بالنسيان

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r1.claim: The theory that a fronted conditional caused أن to open has no evidence: changing a particle's vowel need not change its syntax or meaning, as open لام remains a preposition.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r1.anchor: كذلك ينبغي أن لا يتغير أن، بل أن أجدر أن لا تتغير

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r2.claim: Fronting does not alter a particle's work; examples of altered vowels, deletion, and letter substitution likewise preserve the particles' established syntax and meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p435/r2.anchor: كذلك ينبغي أن لا يتغير أن، بل أن أجدر أن لا تتغير

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r1.claim: Asim alone reads تجارة منصوب; the rest read it nominative, though Abu Bakr is unsure about Ibn Amir.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r1.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وحده تجارة نصبا. وقرأ الباقون: بالرفع.

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r2.claim: كان can mean an event occurred, can be a temporal auxiliary with an accusative predicate, can mean became, or can be redundant without adding meaning.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r2.anchor: قال أبو علي: كان كلمة استعملت على أنحاء: أحدها: أن تكون بمنزلة حدث، ووقع،

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r3.claim: The exception means the debt need not be written when an immediate hand-to-hand sale occurs, because same-session exchange requires no documentary or pledged security.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r3.anchor: أي: يدا بيد لا أجل فيه، فلا يحتاج في تبايع ذلك إلى التوثق باكتتاب الكتاب

FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r4.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r4.claim: أن in إلا أن تكون تجارة عن تراض منكم is accusative and governed by لا تأكلوا through إلا; both exceptions are disconnected. Sibawayh reports an accusative reading of تجارة.
FARISI-HUJJA:v2p436/r4.anchor: وكلا الاستثناءين منقطع. وزعم سيبويه: أنه قد نصب في القراءة تجارة عن تراض منكم

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r1.claim: Kasra in إن تضل makes a conditional clause with a jussive verb; fatḥa in أن تضل treats it as a complement after an understood li, meaning lest one err.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r1.anchor: فالحجة لمن كسر أنه جعلها حرف شرط وجزم بها تضل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r2.claim: فتذكر may be doubled or light and jussive, indicative, or subjunctive: it can continue the conditional, begin a clause after fa, or be governed by the open أن.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p104/r2.anchor: والحجة لمن نصب أنه عطفه على تضل وقد عملت فيه أن المفتوحة

IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r2.claim: Hamza alone reads إن تضل with kasra and فتذكر with doubled kāf and indicative ending; the others use open أن and a subjunctive verb, except Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr, who lighten the verb.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r2.anchor: فقرأ حمزة وحده ﴿ أن تضل ﴾ بكسر الألف ﴿ فتذكر ﴾ بتشديد الكاف ورفع الراء

IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r3.speaker: عاصم
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r3.claim: Asim alone reads إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة with both words accusative; the other readers use nominative, though Abu Bakr hesitates about Ibn Amir.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p193/r3.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وحده ﴿ إلا أن تكون تجارة حاضرة ﴾ نصبا

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:64#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:64#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:64#1/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar has a quiescent hāʾ in hwa rather than huwa, a rapid-recitation reduction with no semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:64#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on hāʾ — هْوَ (hwa) instead of هُوَ (huwa)

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:89#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:89#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:89#1/r1.claim: Reading in as a conditional yields if one of them errs; an instead makes the phrase purposive, so that or lest one errs. Both are canonical.

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#1/r1.claim: Form IV tudhkira is a simpler causative than Form II tudhakkira; both are canonical readings with related causative senses.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#1/r1.anchor: Form IV (afʿala) instead of Form II (faʿʿala): tudhkira vs tudhakkira

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#2/r1.claim: The indicative ending presents her reminding as an independent fact; the subjunctive makes it a purpose or result. Both are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:93#2/r1.anchor: Indicative instead of subjunctive: -u ending vs -a. Changes from purpose/result

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:128#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:128#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:128#1/r1.claim: Nominative tijāratun makes kāna complete, meaning that a present trade exists, rather than taking an accusative predicate; both are canonical.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:128#1/r1.anchor: Nominative instead of accusative: tijāratun ḥāḍiratun. Changes kāna from defective verb

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:129#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:129#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:129#1/r1.claim: Nominative ḥāḍiratun agrees with the nominative tijāratun reading and the complete-verb analysis of kāna.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:129#1/r1.anchor: Nominative, matching the tijāratun variant above. Same logic: complete kāna reading

QIRAAT-ER:2:282:144#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:144#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:144#1/r1.claim: Abu Jaʿfar and Yaʿqub quiesce the final rāʾ in yuḍār; the source treats it as phonetic, with the same morphological analysis.
QIRAAT-ER:2:282:144#1/r1.anchor: Sukūn on final rāʾ (Abū Jaʿfar, Yaʿqūb). Phonetic variant

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r1.claim: Qatada says a witness must not refuse when called to give testimony.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ﴾ قال لا تأب أن تشهد إذا دعيت إلى الشهادة

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says the prohibition covers both withholding testimony one already has and refusing to testify when summoned.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r2.anchor: وكان الحسن يقول مثل ذلك ويقول جمعت الأمرين لا تأب إن كانت عندك شهادة أن تشهد بها

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the summons as applying to witnesses who have already testified.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا ﴾ قال إذا كانوا قد شهدوا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r4.claim: Mujahid, as reported by Jabir al-Ju‘fi, says a witness may choose whether to testify until he has testified.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r4.anchor: وقال جابر الجعفي عن مجاهد الشاهد بالخيار ما لم يشهد

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r5.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r5.claim: Ata and Mujahid say the scribe is obliged to write, while the witness clause concerns someone who has already witnessed the matter.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r5.anchor: عن عطاء ومجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد ﴾ قال واجب على الكاتب أن يكتب

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r6.claim: Qatada says a scribe is harmed by being made to write what was not dictated, and a witness by being made to attest what he did not witness.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد ﴾ قال لا يضار كاتب فيكتب ما لم يمل عليه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r7.speaker: عطاء
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r7.claim: Ata says the scribe and witness must deliver what is entrusted to them.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r7.anchor: عن عطاء في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد ﴾ يقول أن يؤديا ما قبلهما

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r8.speaker: عمر
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r8.claim: Ikrima reports Umar reciting the verb with a doubled r, as ‘ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد.’
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p110#2/r8.anchor: عن عمرو عن عكرمة قال كان عمر يقرأ ولا يضارر كاتب ولا شهيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p720#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p720#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p720#2/r1.claim: Tadāyantum is a reciprocal verb from debt, applying whether one lends or borrows, as reciprocal sale can mean giving or taking.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p720#2/r1.anchor: تداين: تفاعل من الدين، يقال: داينت الرجل عاملته بدين معطيا أو آخذا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r1.speaker: رؤبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r1.claim: Ruʾba's verse about Arwā paying some debts and delaying others illustrates dāyantu as lending or dealing in debt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r1.anchor: داينت أروى والديون تقضى ... فمطلت بعضا وأدت بعضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r2.claim: Dāntuhu means I sold to him on credit; adantu means I borrowed on credit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r2.anchor: ويقال: دنت الرجل إذا بعته بدين، وادنت أنا أي: أخذت بدين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r3.claim: Amala and amlā are dialect variants for dictating: the first belongs to the Ḥijāz and Banū Asad, the second to Tamīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r3.anchor: أمل وأملى لغتان: الأولى لأهل الحجاز وبني أسد، والثانية لتميم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r4.claim: The verb for dictating means casting words for another to write and originally connoted repeating them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r4.anchor: يقال: أمليت وأمللت على الرجل أي: ألقيت عليه ما يكتبه، وأصله في اللغة الإعادة مرة بعد أخرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r5.claim: A poetic line uses umlī to mean wearing something down over time; another account derives the form from amlal with lām changed to yāʾ for ease.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r5.anchor: ألا يا ديار الحي بالسبعان ... أمل عليها بالبلى الملوان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r6.claim: Bakhs means reduction or shortchanging; it can also mean an eye injury, and metaphorically applies to depriving someone of a right or cheating in sale.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r6.anchor: البخس: النقص، يقال منه: بخس يبخس، ويقال بالصاد، والبخس: إصابة العين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r7.claim: Saʾm and saʾāma mean boredom or irritation with something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r7.anchor: السأم والسآمة: الملل من الشيء والضجر منه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r8.claim: Ṣaghīr is the active participle of ṣaghura and means small in amount, also used for abstract things.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r8.anchor: الصغير: اسم فاعل من صغر يصغر، ومعناه قلة. الجرم، ويستعمل في المعاني أيضا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r9.claim: Qisṭ with kasra means justice or an allotted share; with fatḥa it means injustice.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r9.anchor: القسط: بكسر القاف: العدل، يقال منه: أقسط الرجل أي عدل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r10.claim: Rahn is the security given to a creditor; the verbal noun can name the pledged item, and rahana can also mean to remain or continue.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r10.anchor: الرهن: ما دفع إلى الدائن على استيثاق دينه، ويقال: رهن يرهن رهنا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r11.claim: Poetry shows rāhin as something retained and arhana as lasting; Ibn Sīda records ra-hana as making something last, while arhana in a sale can mean bidding it up.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r11.anchor: قال ابن سيده: ورهنه، أي: أدامه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r12.speaker: همام بن مرة وابن الأعرابي والزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r12.claim: Hammām ibn Murra illustrates pledging property with a line; Ibn al-Aʿrābī and al-Zajjāj accept both rahana and arh an a for giving collateral.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r12.anchor:
قال همام بن مرة:
فلما خشيت أظافيرهم ... نجوت وأرهنتهم مالكا
وقال ابن الأعرابي، والزجاج: يقال في الرهن رهنت وأرهنت.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r13.speaker: الأعشى
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r13.claim: Al-Aʿshā's verse uses rahīna for something pledged, and the author notes rahantu lisānī is said for pledging one's word, not arhantu.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p721/r13.anchor:
وقال الأعشى:
حتى يقيدك من بنيه رهينة ... نعش ويرهنك السماك الفرقدا
وتقول: رهنت لساني بكذا، ولا يقال فيه: أرهنت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the debt-document verse was revealed specifically about forward-sale transactions in Medina; consensus extends it to all debts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: نزلت في السلم خاصة، يعنى: أن سلم أهل المدينة كان السبب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r4.claim: After commands to spend in God's path and leave usury, this verse offers a lawful way to grow wealth and gives detailed rules for protecting it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r4.anchor: ومناسبة هذه الآية لما قبلها أنه لما أمر بالنفقة في سبيل الله، وبترك الربا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r5.claim: The word dَayn supplies the pronoun in fa-ktubūhu; it also disambiguates tadāyantum, emphasizes the reference, and generalizes to any size or type of debt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r5.anchor: وذكر قوله: بدين، ليعود الضمير عليه في قوله: فاكتبوه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r6.claim: A specified term is not a restrictive condition because every valid debt must have a known term; harvest, threshing, or pilgrims' return are too indefinite.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r6.anchor: إلى أجل مسمى ليس هذا الوصف احترازا من أن الدين لا يكون إلى أجل مسمى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r7.claim: Ila ajal can modify tadāyantum directly or be an adjective phrase for dayn.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r7.anchor: و: إلى أجل، متعلق: بتداينتم، أو في موضع الصفة لقوله: بدين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r8.claim: Writing protects against forgetfulness and denial; although its command appears obligatory, the majority treat it as recommended preservation that reduces doubt and supports acknowledgment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r8.anchor: فاكتبوه أمر تعالى بكتابته لأن ذلك أوثق وآمن من النسيان، وأبعد من الجحود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r9.claim: Writing acts as a substitute for the tongue, just as the tongue conveys what is in the heart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p722/r9.anchor: فإن الكتاب خليفة اللسان، واللسان خليفة القلب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري وابن زيد والشعبي وابن جريج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r1.claim: They held that the trust clause abrogated the command to write; al-Rabīʿ instead says writing was first required and then eased by the trust clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r1.anchor: وروي عن أبي سعيد الخدري، وابن زيد، والشعبي، وابن جريج أنهم كانوا يرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r2.speaker: عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r2.claim: ʿAṭāʾ and others say the command that a scribe write is a collective duty, while some say the scribe must write in every circumstance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r2.anchor: قال عطاء، وغيره: يجب على الكاتب أن يكتب على كل حال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r3.speaker: الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r3.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says a scribe must write if no other scribe is available; elsewhere he says the duty applies when the scribe is free.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r3.anchor: وقال الشعبي، أيضا: إذا لم يوجد كاتب سواه فواجب عليه أن يكتب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r4.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says writing is obligatory when the scribe has time.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: هو واجب مع الفراغ.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r5.speaker: الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib prefers a collective duty: the parties need not always document a deal, but a scribe approached for it must write, like a scholar asked to explain a non-obligatory prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r5.anchor: واختار الراغب أن الصحيح كون الكتابة فرضا على الكفاية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r6.claim: Between you means between creditor and debtor, seller and buyer, or lender and borrower; both should be present so neither side is suspected of dictating a biased record.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r6.anchor: ومعنى: بينكم، أي: بين صاحب الدين والمستدين، والبائع والمشتري، والمقرض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r7.claim: Writing justly means truthfully and impartially, without favoring either side in the scribe's mind or pen.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r7.anchor: ومعنى: بالعدل، أي: بالحق والإنصاف بحيث لا يكون في قلبه ولا في قلمه ميل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī attaches bi-l-ʿadl to kātib: the scribe must be trustworthy, write evenly, and know legal conditions, so the parties should select a learned, pious writer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r8.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: بالعدل، متعلق بكاتب صفة له، أي: بكاتب مأمون على ما يكتب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya attaches the preposition to yaktub rather than kātib: even a child or enslaved person can write a sound deed if legally informed, though officials must choose just, trusted scribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والباء متعلقة بقوله تعالى: وليكتب، وليست متعلقة بكاتب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r10.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r10.claim: A third grammatical view treats bāʾ as extra, yielding the sense let the just scribe write.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p723/r10.anchor: وقيل: الباء زائدة، أي فليكتب بينكم كاتب العدل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r1.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r1.claim: Al-Qaffāl says justice requires wording accepted by legal scholars and not so ambiguous that a judge could find grounds to invalidate the document.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r1.anchor: وقال القفال في معنى بالعدل: أن يكون ما يكتبه متفقا عليه بين أهل العلم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the imperative lām in wa-lyaktub with kasra, its original vowel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: وليكتب، بكسر لام الأمر، والكسر الأصل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r3.claim: The prohibition lā yaʾba kātib an yaktub forbids a scribe from refusing to write.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r3.anchor: ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب كما علمه الله نهى الكاتب عن الامتناع من الكتابة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r4.claim: Because kātib is indefinite under a prohibition, the command is general.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r4.anchor: و: كاتب، نكرة في سياق النهي، فتعم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r5.claim: On the apparent reading, as God taught him means to write documentation as taught, without alteration; it urges the scribe to use his full knowledge of its conditions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r5.anchor: ومعنى: كما علمه الله، أي: مثل ما علمه الله من كتابة الوثائق، لا يبدل ولا يغير،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r6.claim: Another gloss takes ʿallamahu as made known and understands the phrase as writing in the way God commanded, in truth.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r6.anchor: وقيل: المعنى كما أمره الله به من الحق، فيكون: علم، بمعنى: أعلم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r7.claim: A further gloss makes the kaaf causal: write because God favored you with the skill, as in the command to do good because God did good to you.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r7.anchor: وقيل: المعنى كما فضله الله بالكتاب، فتكون الكاف للتعليل، أي: لأجل ما فضله الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r8.claim: The kaaf most naturally modifies an yaktub; ending the clause there and attaching it to fa-lyaktub is awkward because of the fa and the reversed order.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r8.anchor: والظاهر تعلق الكاف بقوله: أن يكتب، وقيل: تم الكلام عند قوله: أن يكتب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r9.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya suggests as may instead qualify the refusal: just as God gave the scribe writing, he should not refuse and should favor others; the author says this is not the apparent reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: ويحتمل أن يكون: كما، متعلقا بما في قوله: ولا يأب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r10.speaker: الربيع والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r10.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the ban on a scribe refusing was abrogated by the later ban on harming a scribe or witness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r10.anchor: وقال الربيع، والضحاك: ولا يأب، منسوخ بقوله: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r11.claim: The debtor must dictate because the debt is owed from him and the written record safeguards the obligation against him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p724/r11.anchor: فليكتب وليملل الذي عليه الحق أي: فليكتب الكاتب، وليملل من وجب عليه الحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r1.claim: Pairing Allah with Lord reminds the debtor that God nurtures, repairs, and favors him; Allah comes first because divine authority precedes the reminder of favors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r1.anchor: وليتق الله ربه، فيما يمليه ويقربه، وجمع بين اسم الذات وهو: الله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r2.claim: The debtor must not diminish any amount through deception or resistance; the person ordered to dictate is assumed to control himself.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r2.anchor: ولا يبخس منه شيئا أي: لا ينقص بالمخادعة أو المدافعة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r3.claim: Breaking the doubled lām in yumlil is a Ḥijāzī form when the final syllable is jussive or at pause, not in nominative or accusative; one reading doubles shayʾan's yāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r3.anchor: وفك المضاعفين في قوله: وليملل، لغة الحجاز،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r4.speaker: مجاهد وابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r4.claim: Mujāhid and Ibn Jubayr define safīh as someone ignorant of practical matters and dictation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r4.anchor: فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها قال مجاهد، وابن جبير: هو الجاهل بالأمور والإملاء.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r5.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says safīh means a child or a woman.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r6.speaker: الضحاك والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and al-Suddī interpret safīh as a minor.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r7.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r7.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī defines safīh as someone who squanders wealth and corrupts his religion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r7.anchor: وقال الشافعي: المبذر لماله المفسد لدينه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says safīh is one ignorant of Islam; other glosses call him a fool or someone who does not value or grow money.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r9.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r9.claim: They interpret ḍaʿīf as an incapacitated person, a mute, or someone mentally impaired.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r9.anchor: أو ضعيفا قال ابن عباس: وابن جبير: إنه العاجز، والأخرس، ومن به حمق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r10.speaker: مجاهد والسدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r10.claim: Mujāhid and al-Suddī also describe the weak person as a fool; others say a minor or one with diminished faculties.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r11.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says weak refers to someone unable to dictate because of speech difficulty or muteness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r11.anchor: وقال الطبري: العاجز عن الإملاء لعي أو لخرس.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says inability to dictate can come from speech difficulty, muteness, or absence; others mention madness, ignorance of the account, or childhood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r12.anchor: أو لا يستطيع أن يمل هو قال ابن عباس: لعي أو خرس أو غيبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r13.claim: The three categories are distinct: safīh is profligate or poor at managing money, weak has bodily impairment from childhood or advanced age, and inability to dictate is speech impairment or muteness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r13.anchor: والذي يظهر تباين هؤلاء الثلاثة، فمن زعم زيادة: أو، في قوله: أو ضعيفا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r14.claim: The author rejects claims that either or is redundant, since the coordinating particle is not added without meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r14.anchor: فمن زعم زيادة: أو، في قوله: أو ضعيفا، أو زيادتها في هذا، وفي قوله: أو لا يستطيع، فقوله ساقط،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r15.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p725/r15.claim: The author's preferred distinctions largely follow al-Zamakhsharī's explanation.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r1.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r1.claim: The verse covers three recurrent cases: the financially incompetent spendthrift, the mentally deficient, and one unable to dictate because absent or ill; their guardians are respectively a guardian or executor, father or executor, and agent, with the mute among the weak or unable.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r1.anchor: ذكر تعالى ثلاثة أنواع تقع نوازلهم في كل زمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r2.claim: Emphasizing “he himself” removes a possible figurative reading and specifies that the debtor cannot dictate personally.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r2.anchor: وفيه من الفصاحة ما لا يخفى، لأن في التأكيد به رفع المجاز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r3.claim: A rare reading quiesces the hāʾ of huwa after a word ending in a vowel, treating a separated form like a connected one; this is more exceptional than a reading after thumma.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r3.anchor: وقرىء شاذا بإسكان هاء: هو، وإن كان قد سبقها ما ينفصل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r4.claim: The pronoun in “his guardian” refers to the debtor, one of the three vulnerable cases; al-Zamakhsharī identifies an executor, agent, or interpreter who dictates with the debtor's approval.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r4.anchor: الضمير في وليه عائد على أحد هؤلاء الثلاثة، وهو الذي عليه الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r5.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the pronoun to refer to the debt, making the guardian the creditor; this is also related from Ibn ʿAbbās and al-Rabīʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r5.anchor: وذهب الطبري إلى أن الضمير في وليه يعود على الحق، فيكون الولي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r6.speaker: ابن عطية، الراغب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejects attributing the creditor-as-guardian view to Ibn ʿAbbās because a creditor's dictation cannot establish a debt against a spendthrift; al-Rāghib likewise says a claimant's assertion has no force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ولا يصح عن ابن عباس، وكيف تشهد البينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r7.claim: The bāʾ in “with justice” may attach to the dictation verb or mark its state or manner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p726/r7.anchor: و: بالعدل، متعلق بقوله: فليملل، ويحتمل أن تكون الباء للحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r1.claim: “With justice” urges fairness toward both creditor and ward; the verse supports legal interdiction of a minor and transactions by a spendthrift under guardianship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r1.anchor: بالعدل، حث على تحريه لصاحب الحق، والمولى عليه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r2.speaker: author
