ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r2.claim: “Seek two witnesses” is a request for testimony or equivalent to “make two witnesses”; shahīd is intensive, suggesting experienced witnesses whose repeated use indicates acceptance and integrity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r2.anchor: واستشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم أي: اطلبوا للإشهاد شهيدين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r3.claim: Addressing believers as “your men” indicates non-Muslims are not witnesses here; the verse does not address testimony among non-Muslims, which Abū Ḥanīfa allows even across religions. It also indicates adult male witnesses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r3.anchor: من رجالكم، الخطاب للمؤمنين، وهم المصدر بهم الآية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r4.speaker: شريح، ابن سيرين، ابن شبرمة، عثمان البتي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r4.claim: They accept a slave's testimony; reports also attribute acceptance to ʿAlī, with Ibrāhīm permitting testimony in trivial matters and Anas saying he knows no one who rejected it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r4.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه: يجوز شهادة العبد، وهو مذهب شريح،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r5.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r5.claim: The majority, including leading Ḥanafīs, Mālik, and al-Shāfiʿī, reject slave testimony in all matters; this is also narrated from ʿAlī, Ibn ʿAbbās, and al-Ḥasan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r5.anchor:
وقال الجمهور:
أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r6.speaker: الثوري، أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، ابن شبرمة، الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r6.claim: They say children's testimony is not considered; Ibn Abī Laylā permits children's mutual testimony, and Mālik permits it in injuries under conditions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p727/r6.anchor: وظاهر الآية يدل على أن شهادة الصبيان لا تعتبر، وبه قال الثوري،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r1.claim: The apparent requirement is simply that the two principal witnesses be men; jurists disagree over testimony by a blind witness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r1.anchor: وظاهر الآية اشتراط الرجولية فقط في الشاهدين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة، محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r2.claim: They categorically reject testimony by a blind witness; the same view is narrated from ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, and Iyās b. Muʿāwiya.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r2.anchor: ذهب أبو حنيفة، ومحمد إلى أنه لا يجوز بحال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r3.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، أبو يوسف، الشافعي، زفر، شريح، الشعبي، مالك، الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r3.claim: They differ: Ibn Abī Laylā, Abū Yūsuf, and al-Shāfiʿī accept testimony learned before blindness; Zufar permits only lineage; Shurayḥ and al-Shaʿbī accept it generally; Mālik and al-Layth rely on voice recognition in some matters but reject testimony in adultery or false accusation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r3.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى، وأبو يوسف، والشافعي: إذا علم قبل العمى جازت،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r4.claim: Some accept a mute witness through gestures and some reject the testimony; deaf witnesses are rejected for spoken claims but accepted for other sensory matters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r4.anchor: ولو كان الشاهد أخرس، فقيل: تقبل شهادته بإشارة، وسواء كان طارئا أم أصليا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r5.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r5.claim: Reports from Mālik restrict a Bedouin's testimony against a settled person to injuries, with another report allowing specified travel-related testament and sale cases.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r5.anchor: ولو شهد بدوي على قروي، فروى ابن وهب عن مالك أنها لا تجوز إلا في الجراح.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r6.claim: “If the two are not men” may mean the creditor failed or chose not to obtain two men; another view requires that two men be unavailable before two women may be called.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r6.anchor: فإن لم يكونا رجلين الضمير عائد على الشهيدين أي: فإن لم يكن الشهيدان رجلين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r7.claim: “One man and two women” admits several ellipses and parses: an omitted witness, a subject with omitted predicate, or a man as subject or passive object of an implied verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p728/r7.anchor: فرجل وامرأتان ارتفاع رجل على أنه خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: فلشاهد،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r1.claim: A nonstandard reading quiesces the hamza in wa-imraʾatān, perhaps easing successive vowels; a poetic line illustrates the sound change.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r1.anchor: وقرىء شاذا: وامرأتان، بهمزة ساكنة، وهو على غير قياس،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r2.claim: The apparent wording permits one man's and two women's testimony in all debt contracts, including consideration, marriage, benefits, and intentional blood claims; excluding a contract requires evidence.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r2.anchor: وظاهر الآية يقتضي جواز شهادة المرأتين مع الرجل في سائر عقود المداينات،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r3.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r3.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī rejects women's testimony with men outside property matters; for wills he accepts men for nonfinancial dispositions and women for financial dispositions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r3.anchor: وقال الشافعي: لا تجوز شهادة النساء مع الرجال في غير الأموال،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r4.speaker: الليث، الأوزاعي، الحسن بن حيي، الثوري، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r4.claim: Their positions differ on wills, emancipation, marriage, divorce, penalties, retaliation, agency, and lineage: al-Layth allows wills and emancipation; al-Awzāʿī bars marriage; al-Ḥasan b. Ḥayy bars penalties; al-Thawrī bars only penalties; Mālik excludes penalties and personal-status matters.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r4.anchor: وقال الليث: تجوز شهادة النساء في الوصية والعتق، ولا تجوز في النكاح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r5.speaker: الحسن، الضحاك؛ عمر، عطاء، الشعبي؛ شريح؛ عمر وابنه عبد الله؛ علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r5.claim: Other reported views limit women to debt, allow divorce, allow emancipation, allow one man with two women in marriage, or allow testimony in a contract, respectively.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن، والضحاك: لا تجوز شهادتهن إلا في الدين.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r6.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد، زفر، عثمان البتي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r6.claim: They reject women's testimony with men in penalties and retaliation but accept it for other rights.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r6.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر، وعثمان البتي: لا تقبل شهادة النساء مع الرجال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r7.claim: There is no disagreement that women may testify alone about childbirth, virginity, a newborn's first cry, women's defects, and comparable matters specific to women.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729/r7.anchor: وأما قبول شهادتهن مفردات فلا خلاف في قبولها في: الولادة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r1.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r1.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa accepts one upright woman's testimony for moon sighting as information, and also accepts a midwife alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r1.anchor: وأجاز أبو حنيفة شهادة الواحدة العادلة في رؤية الهلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r2.claim: “Among witnesses whom you approve” most likely modifies “seek witnesses,” applying approval to all combinations; adjective and substitution analyses are weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r2.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه متعلق بقوله: واستشهدوا، أي: واستشهدوا ممن ترضون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r3.claim: The address in “you approve” is apparently to believers, implying that witnesses are not presumed upright by status alone; other views address judges or creditors.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r3.anchor: والخطاب في ترضون ظاهره أنه للمؤمنين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، الشعبي، الحسن، النخعي، الخصاف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r4.claim: They define approved witnesses as people of merit, religion, and competence; untainted in sex or lineage; not known for misconduct or suspicion; or with good deeds outweighing bad deeds while avoiding major sins.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r4.anchor: ابن عباس: من أهل الفضل والدين والكفاءة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r5.claim: Another view requires ten traits: freedom, adulthood, Islam, integrity, knowledge, no personal gain or self-protection, no habitual error, preserved social decency, and no enmity toward the accused.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: المرضي من الشهود من اجتمعت فيه عشر خصال:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r6.speaker: أبو يوسف
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r6.claim: Abū Yūsuf accepts a person whose good conduct outweighs minor sins and who avoids major offenses; he excludes gamblers, habitual prayer neglecters, notorious liars, and those who insult the Companions or neighbors, among other conduct.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p729#2/r6.anchor: وذكر بشر بن الوليد عن أبي يوسف: أن من سلم من الفواحش

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r1.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r1.claim: They accept upright witnesses from sectarian groups except the Khaṭṭābiyya among the Rāfiḍa; Muḥammad rejects Kharijites but accepts Ḥarūriyya because he distinguishes their treatment of Muslims' property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r1.anchor: وقال ابن أبي ليلى، وأبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف: تقبل شهادة أهل الأهواء العدول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة، إياس بن معاوية، بلال بن أبي بردة، عمر بن عبد العزيز، شريح، أبو هريرة، محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r2.claim: Reports reject witnesses for miserliness, sea-trading, eating clay, plucking or hiding the beard, answering a disparaging nickname, slave dealing, frivolity, effeminacy, or flying pigeons; Shurayḥ's anecdote illustrates the nickname ruling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r2.anchor: وعن إياس بن معاوية لا يجيز شهادة الأشراف بالعراق ولا البخلاء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r3.speaker: ابن أبي ليلى، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r3.claim: Ibn Abī Laylā rejects a poor witness because poverty may prompt desire for money; Mālik rejects beggars in substantial matters but accepts testimony in trivial ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r3.anchor: ابن أبي ليلى شهادة الفقير، وقال: لا يؤمن أن يحمله فقره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r4.speaker: الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r4.claim: One report rejects a witness whose usual conduct is sinful or indecent; another accepts one whose usual conduct is obedience and who has committed no major sin.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r4.anchor: وعن الشافعي: إذا كان الأغلب من حاله المعصية وعدم المروءة ردت شهادته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r5.claim: Muruwwa means restraint, dignified bearing, respect for social obligations, and avoiding vulgarity and frivolity, not fine clothing, mounts, tools, or appearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r5.anchor: وينبغي أن تفسر المروءة بالتصاون، والسمت الحسن، وحفظ الحرمة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r6.speaker: عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r6.claim: In his letter to Abū Mūsā, ʿUmar says Muslims are upright for one another unless punished, known for false testimony, suspect, or disqualified by kinship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r6.anchor: ففي كتاب عمر لأبي موسى: والمسلمون عدول بعضهم على بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r7.speaker: الحسن، ابن شبرمة، محمد، أبو يوسف، مالك، الليث، الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r7.claim: They differ over investigating witnesses: al-Ḥasan accepts unless impeached; Ibn Shubrumah investigates if challenged; Muḥammad and Abū Yūsuf always investigate; Mālik requires private inquiry; al-Layth lets the opponent produce discrediting evidence; al-Shāfiʿī adds public attestation after private clearance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p731/r7.anchor: وقال محمد، وأبو يوسف: يسأل عنهم، وإن لم يطعن فيهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r1.claim: Regional jurists agree testimony for a child or parent is invalid, apart from reported exceptions; the dominant view bars either spouse testifying for the other.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r1.anchor: وأما ما ذكر من اعتبار نفي التهمة عن الشاهد إذا كان عدلا، فاتفق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r2.speaker: البتي، إياس بن معاوية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r2.claim: Al-Battī permits a child for parents and a father for child and wife; Iyās is reported to permit testimony for one's son.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r2.anchor: إلا ما حكي عن البتي، قال: تجوز شهادة الولد لوالديه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، محمد، زفر، مالك، الأوزاعي، الليث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r3.claim: They reject testimony by either spouse for the other; employee testimony is also disputed, with Mālik requiring notable integrity, al-Awzāʿī rejecting it, and al-Thawrī allowing it absent personal benefit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r3.anchor: وذهب أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، ومحمد، وزفر، ومالك، والأوزاعي، والليث إلى أنه: لا يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r4.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r4.claim: The Ḥanafīs do not readmit testimony rejected for sinfulness or marriage but accept after rejection for slavery, unbelief, or childhood; Mālik also bars readmission after slavery or childhood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r4.anchor: قال أبو حنيفة، وأصحابه: لا تقبل إذا ردت لفسق أو زوجية،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r5.claim: The verse's apparent rules require two men or one man and two women, and thus do not allow judgment on one witness plus an oath; the Ḥanafīs and others agree.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r5.anchor: وظاهر الآية: أن الشهود في الديون رجلان، أو رجل وامرأتان،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r6.speaker: مالك، الشافعي، أحمد، إسحاق، أبو عبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r6.claim: They permit one witness plus an oath in financial claims, citing the four caliphs and Medinan practice; reports from al-Zuhrī differ on whether this was innovation and when it began.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732/r6.anchor:
وقال مالك، والشافعي وأتباعهما، وأحمد، وإسحاق، وأبو عبيد:
يحكم به في الأموال خاصة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r1.speaker: الأعمش، حمزة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r1.claim: They read in tadhilla with a kasra as a conditional particle and fa-tudhakkiru with doubled dhāl and a jussive response.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r1.anchor: قرأ الأعمش، وحمزة: إن تضل بكسر الهمزة، جعلها حرف شرط.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r2.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r2.claim: Most readers use subjunctive an and coordinate fa-tudhakkira; Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr lighten the kāf, while others double it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح همزة: أن، وهي الناصبة، وفتح راء فتذكر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r3.speaker: الجحدري، عيسى بن عمران، حميد بن عبد الرحمن، مجاهد، زيد بن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r3.claim: Variants include passive tadhalla “be forgotten,” a form meaning testimony goes astray, fa-tudhakkiru “then she reminds,” and reciprocal fa-tadhākara.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الجحدري وعيسى بن عمران: تضل، بضم التاء وفتح الضاد مبنيا للمفعول،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r4.claim: On the conditional reading, the clause may describe the two women as an adjective, though its placement after the earlier descriptor raises a syntactic concern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r4.anchor: قال ابن عطية: في موضع رفع بكونه صفة للمذكر، وهما المرأتان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r5.claim: With open an, the clause is a purpose-cause: the possibility of forgetting is expressed as the reason for the other to remind, carried by meaning like preparing a prop for a wall that may lean.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p732#2/r5.anchor: وأما: أن تضل، بفتح الهمزة، فهو في موضع المفعول من أجله،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r1.claim: Forgetfulness means failing to find one's way in testimony through forgetting or inattention, answered by reminding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r1.anchor: ومعنى الضلال هنا هو عدم الاهتداء للشهادة لنسيان أو غفلة، ولذلك قوبل بقوله: فتذكر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء، سفيان بن عيينة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r2.claim: They explain the light reading as making the two women's combined testimony equivalent to a man's; al-Zamakhsharī calls this aberrant and Ibn ʿAṭiyya distant and wrong.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r2.anchor: وأما ما روي عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء، وسفيان بن عيينة من أن قراءة التخفيف، فتذكر، معناه:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r3.claim: He agrees with al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya: the reading fails linguistically because the verb is not recorded with that causative sense, and logically because both women's testimony, not one woman's reminder, would make the equivalent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r3.anchor: وما قالاه صحيح، وينبو عنه اللفظ من جهة اللغة ومن جهة المعنى،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r4.claim: Either woman may forget and either may remind, so “one of them” is generic; the ordinary parse makes the other woman the one reminded, though object-first order is possible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r4.anchor: والمعنى: إن ضلت هذه أذكرتها هذه، وإن ضلت هذه أذكرتها هذه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r5.claim: An interpretation links women's forgetfulness to cold and moisture, says one woman's forgetting is more likely than both forgetting, and infers men's superiority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r5.anchor: أن النسيان غالب على طباع النساء لكثرة البرد والرطوبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r6.speaker: النحاس عن علي بن سليمان عن أبي العباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās analyzes it as “for fear that one forget”; Abū Jaʿfar rejects this because it would make the purpose that the other woman remind her.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p733/r6.anchor: وقال النحاس: سمعت علي بن سليمان يحكي عن أبي العباس أن التقدير:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r1.claim: Tudhakkiru takes an omitted object, “the testimony”; the wording implies a witness must remember testimony and cannot rely only on writing, supported by 43:86.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r1.anchor: وفي قوله فتذكر إحداهما الأخرى دلالة على أن من شرط جواز إقامة الشهادة ذكر الشاهد لها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r2.speaker: أبو حنيفة، أبو يوسف، الشافعي، ابن أبي ليلى، الثوري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r2.claim: The first three require recollection beyond handwriting; Ibn Abī Laylā allows recognition of the handwriting, and al-Thawrī allows testimony if the witness recalls witnessing but not the amount.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة، وأبو يوسف، والشافعي: إذا كتب خطه بالشهادة فلا يشهد حتى يذكرها،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r3.claim: Qatāda relates an occasion of revelation in which a man passed through a large gathering at Ḥirāʾ and no one accompanied him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r3.anchor: قال قتادة: سبب نزولها أن الرجل كان يطوف في الحراء العظيم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r4.speaker: ابن عباس، قتادة، الربيع؛ عطاء، الحسن؛ الشعبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Rabīʿ read the summons as initial bearing; ʿAṭāʾ and al-Ḥasan consider it advisory, while al-Shaʿbī requires it when no other witness exists.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r4.anchor: قاله ابن عباس، وقتادة، والربيع وغيرهم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r5.speaker: مجاهد، عطاء، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، الضحاك، السدي، إبراهيم، ابن زيد، النقاش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r5.claim: They read the summons as performing testimony already witnessed; al-Naqqāsh attributes this to the Prophet and says, if authentic, it makes the prohibition binding.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r5.anchor: وقيل: المعنى: ولا يأب الشهداء إذا ما دعوا لأداء الشهادة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya combines both readings: assistance is recommended when witnesses are plentiful, nearly obligatory in necessity, and obligatory if delay would destroy the right, especially when summoned to perform testimony already borne.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p735/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: والآية كما قال الحسن، جمعت الأمرين،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r1.claim: Recording every debt and due date protects property and prevents disputes; “small” comes first to stress that minor debts matter, and the due date is the parties' agreed term.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r1.anchor: نهى أيضا عن السآمة في كتابة الدين، كل ذلك ضبط لأموال الناس، وتحريض على أن لا يقع النزاع،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r2.speaker: الماتريدي، author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r2.claim: Al-Māturīdī infers advance sale of clothing from “small or large”; Abū Ḥayyān objects that these words mean little or much, including amounts of grain.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r2.anchor: وقال الماتريدي: فيه دلالة على جواز السلم في الثياب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r3.claim: “Become weary” is explained as “be lazy” or “be annoyed”; grammarians debate whether saʾima takes its object directly or through a preposition. A hadith and 4:142 are parallels for laziness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r3.anchor: قيل: ومعنى: ولا تسأموا، أي لا تكسلوا، وعبر بالسأم عن الكسل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r4.speaker: لبيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r4.claim: Labīd's line about tiring of life witnesses the construction saʾima min.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r4.anchor: ولقد سئمت من الحياة وطولها ... وسؤال هذا الناس كيف لبيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r5.claim: The pronoun in “write it” refers to the earlier debt or nearby right, equivalent in sense; those with many debts might tire of documentation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p736/r5.anchor: وضمير النصب في: تكتبوه، عائد على الدين، لسبقه، أو على الحق لقربه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī suggests the pronoun means the document, which may be concise or detailed without being deficient; Abū Ḥayyān calls this far-fetched.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ويجوز أن يكون الضمير للكتاب،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r2.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r2.claim: Al-Sulamī reads “they should not tire” and “they should write”; the plural likely refers to witnesses, but may shift to parties or scribes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r2.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: ولا يسأموا، بالياء وكذلك: أن يكتبوه،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r3.claim: “Small or large” is a state of the debt being written; supplying omitted kāna is misplaced. “Until its due date” means the debt remains established in liability until maturity, not that writing lasts the entire term.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r3.anchor: والتقدير: أن تكتبوه مستقرا في الذمة إلى أجل حلوله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r4.claim: “That is more just” points either to writing alone or to writing, testimony, and all prior means of documentation; aqsaṭ means more equitable, though its derivation is debated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r4.anchor: ذلكم أقسط عند الله الإشارة إلى أقرب مذكور وهو الكتابة، وقيل الكتابة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r5.speaker: الزمخشري، ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī derives aqsaṭ from aqsaṭa, while Ibn ʿAṭiyya questions its derivation; the author discusses comparative morphology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737/r5.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: مم بني أفعلا التفضيل. أعني: أقسط. وأقوم؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r1.claim: He prefers deriving aqsaṭ from triliteral qasaṭa meaning “act justly,” avoiding the alleged morphological irregularity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r1.anchor: والذي ينبغي أن يحمل عليه أقسط هو أن يكون مبنيا من قسط الثلاثي بمعنى عدل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r2.speaker: ابن السيد عن ابن السكيت عن أبي عبيدة، ابن القطاع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r2.claim: Lexicographers report qasaṭa as both just and unjust, while aqsaṭa with hamza means only just, making aqsaṭ regular.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r2.anchor: حكى ابن السكيت في كتاب الأضداد عن أبي عبيدة: قسط جار، وقسط عدل،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r3.claim: “More just with God” means more just under God's judgment because it prevents oppression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r3.anchor: ومعنى: أقسط عند الله. أعدل في حكم الله أن لا يقع التظالم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r4.claim: “More reliable for testimony” means firmer and sounder; deriving aqwam from aqāma is irregular to some grammarians, while qāma avoids that issue.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows aqwam to derive from aqāma under Sibawayh's approach or as a relational form from qawīm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r5.anchor: وتقدم قول الزمخشري إنه جائز على مذهب سيبويه أن يكون من أقام، وقال أيضا: يجوز

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r6.claim: The lām in “for testimony” attaches to aqwam with object-like meaning; omitting it and using a direct accusative is restricted to poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r6.anchor: ويتعلق: للشهادة، بأقوم، وهو من حيث المعنى مفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r7.speaker: السلمي، author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r7.claim: Al-Sulamī reads “that they do not doubt” with a masculine plural verb; the omitted comparison after “closer” is “than not writing.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p737#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ السلمي: أن لا يرتابوا بالياء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r1.claim: The sequence moves from obedience to God's just judgment, to reliable testimony, to eliminating doubt; writing and witnessing reassure the parties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r1.anchor: ونسق هذه الأخبار في غاية الحسن، إذ بدىء أولا بالأشرف،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r2.claim: Doubt may concern denial by the debtor, a witness forgetting, the testimony, amount or due date, or uncertainty for witness, judge, and parties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r2.anchor:
قيل:
والمعنى: أن لا ترتابوا بمن عليه الحق أن ينكر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r3.claim: Present trade means either cash sale without a term or a movable-goods sale, usually small; al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk specify hand-to-hand exchange.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r3.anchor: في التجارة الحاضرة قولان: أحدهما: ما يعجل ولا يدخله أجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r4.claim: “You circulate it among yourselves” means passing goods hand to hand or repeated trading, implying taking possession.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r4.anchor: وفي معنى الإدارة، قولان: أحدهما: يتناولونها من يد إلى يد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r5.claim: The exception is disconnected because immediate sales are not deferred debts; writing may be omitted because it protects against uncertainty about amount, description, and term. Other views connect the exception to the debt or writing command.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r5.anchor: وهذا الاستثناء في قوله: إلا أن تكون، منقطع لأن ما بيع لغير أجل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r6.speaker: عاصم، الباقون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r6.claim: ʿĀṣim reads “trade, present” in the accusative, with kāna incomplete; others use nominative and a complete verb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p738/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: تجارة حاضرة، بنصبهما على أن كان ناقصة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r1.claim: For most exegetes, “no blame” means no harm in omitting writing because writing is not obligatory; those who require it interpret the phrase as “no sin.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r1.anchor: ونفي الجناح هنا معناه لا مضرة عليكم في ترك الكتابة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r2.claim: Witnessing all sales, immediate or deferred, is safer against disagreement; another interpretation limits the command to present trade.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r2.anchor: وأشهدوا إذا تبايعتم هذا أمر بالإشهاد على التبايع مطلقا، ناجزا أو كالئا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r3.speaker: الجحدري، الحسن، عبد الرحمن بن يزيد، الحكم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r3.claim: They say the witnessing command was abrogated by the permission to trust one another.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r3.anchor: قيل: وهذه الآية منسوخة بقوله: فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r4.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري، ابن عمر، الضحاك، ابن المسيب، جابر بن زيد، مجاهد، عطاء، إبراهيم، الشعبي، النخعي، داود بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r4.claim: They hold witnessing obligatory; al-Ḍaḥḥāk requires it even for greens and ʿAṭāʾ for any price. Al-Ṭabarī says an unwitnessed sale defies God's Book.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r4.anchor: وقيل: هي محكمة، والأمر في ذلك على الوجوب قال ذلك أبو موسى الأشعري،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r5.speaker: الحسن وجماعة، ابن العربي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r5.claim: They treat the command as recommendation and guidance, not compulsion; Ibn al-ʿArabī identifies this as the majority position.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r5.anchor: وذهب الحسن وجماعة إلى أن هذا الأمر على الندب والإرشاد لا على الحتم.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r6.claim: An active reading forbids a writer altering the document or a witness concealing, changing, or withholding testimony; al-Zajjāj prefers this. Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, and ʿAṭāʾ also explain harm as refusing with excuses about being busy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p740/r6.anchor: واحتمل هذا الفعل أن يكون مبنيا للفاعل فيكون الكاتب والشهيد قد نهيا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r1.speaker: ابن عباس، مجاهد، طاووس، الضحاك، السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r1.claim: Under the passive reading, they say others must not harm the writer or witness by burdening them, disrupting their work, or making unreasonable demands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r1.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون مبنيا للمفعول، فنهي أن يضارهما أحد بأن يعنتا،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r2.speaker: الطبري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers the passive reading, supported by ʿUmar's unassimilated reading: the opening addresses transaction parties, not writers and witnesses, and the warning fits parties forbidden to cause harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r2.anchor: واختاره الطبري لأن الخطاب من أول الآيات إنما هو للمكتوب له،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r3.speaker: عمر، ابن عباس، مجاهد، ابن أبي إسحاق
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r3.claim: Their reading is reported with the first rāʾ unassimilated and either kasra or fatḥa; unassimilated pronunciation is Ḥijāzī and assimilation Tamīmī.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r3.anchor: وحكى أبو عمرو عن عمر، وابن عباس، ومجاهد، وابن أبي إسحاق: أن الراء الأولى مكسورة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r4.speaker: ابن القعقاع، عمرو بن عبيد، عكرمة، ابن محيصن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r4.claim: Their variants include a jussive rāʾ, an unassimilated verb with accusative kātiban, and a raised doubled rāʾ used as a negative form that strengthens the prohibition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r4.anchor: وقرأ ابن القعقاع، وعمرو بن عبيد: ولا يضار، بجزم الراء،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r5.claim: Under the active reading, “if you do so” means causing harm; fusūq bikum means transgression attached to you or located within you, the latter more emphatic.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741/r5.anchor: وإن تفعلوا لمضارة أو الضرار فإنه، أي الضرار، فسوق بكم أي: ملتبس بكم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r1.claim: The warning addresses writer and witness under an active reading, the parties under the passive reading, or everyone regarding all commands and prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r1.anchor: والخطاب في: تفعلوا، عائد على الكاتب والشاهد، إذ كان قوله: ولا يضار،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r2.claim: “Fear God” means avoiding harm or observing all commands and prohibitions; it follows the warning of transgression.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r2.anchor: واتقوا الله أي: في ترك الضرار، أو: في جميع أوامره ونواهيه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r3.claim: “God teaches you” is an independent sentence reminding of the blessing of knowledge; taking it as circumstantial is very weak because imperfect circumstantial verbs ordinarily do not take this waw.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r3.anchor: ويعلمكم الله هذه جملة تذكر بنعم الله التي أشرفها: التعليم للعلوم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r4.claim: God's knowledge encompasses all and signals recompense; repeating “God” makes three independent statements: command to piety, reminder of grace, and promise or threat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r4.anchor: وأعيد لفظ الله في هذه الجمل الثلاث على طريق تعظيم الأمر،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r5.claim: Some ascetics invoke the verse to avoid legal sciences; Abū Ḥayyān objects that knowledge is needed to know piety.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p741#2/r5.anchor: وكثيرا ما يتمثل بهذه بعض المتطوعة من الصوفية الذين يتجافون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.claim: The passage uses contrasting paronomasia in debt/indebtedness, writer/writing, and entrustment/trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p746/r4.anchor: التجنيس المغاير في قوله: إذا تداينتم بدين، وفي قوله: وليكتب بينكم كاتب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r2.claim: Repetition stresses following the right: “right” recurs, while ʿalā signals the creditor's position and claim.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r2.anchor: كرر الحق للدعاء إلى اتباعه، وأتى بلفظة على للإعلام أن لصاحب الحق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r3.claim: The passage pairs opposites in forgetting/reminding and small/large; it also uses comparison, specification, and repetition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r3.anchor: والطباق في قوله: أن تضل إحداهما فتذكر، لأن الضلال هنا بمعنى النسيان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.claim: The closing catalogue identifies ellipsis and explains implied subjects and objects in writing, dictation, testimony, repayment, and not concealing testimony.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p747/r4.anchor: والحذف في قوله: يا أيها الذين آمنوا، حذف متعلق الإيمان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r1.claim: The verse varies address between direct presence and third-person reference, then shifts repeatedly to heighten its rhetorical movement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r1.anchor: وتلوين الخطاب، وهو الانتقال من الحضور إلى الغيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r2.claim: The forms شهيد and كاتب shift from an active participle pattern to an intensive pattern.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r2.anchor: والعدول من فاعل إلى فعيل، في قوله: شهيدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r3.claim: The verse uses fronting, delay, and ellipsis: writing precedes dictation, and the witness phrases imply the omitted relation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r3.anchor: والتقديم والتأخير في قوله: فليكتب، وليملل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r4.claim: A long series of commands, safeguards, warnings, and reminders emphatically protects wealth in transactions from loss and breach of trust.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r4.anchor: وفيها من التأكيد في حفظ الأموال في المعاملات ما لا يخفى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r5.claim: The Prophet paired safeguarding wealth with safeguarding lives and bloodshed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p748/r5.anchor: وقد قرنها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالنفوس والدماء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r1.claim: After directing that an insolvent debtor be given time, the passage sets out how to document deferred rights and debt contracts.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r1.anchor: ولما أمر سبحانه بإنظار المعسر وتأجيله عقبه ببيان أحكتم الحقوق المؤجلة وعقود المداينة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r2.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing with one another; adding bi-dayn makes explicit that the shared transaction is a debt, since the verb can also mean reciprocal recompense. Al-Alusi rejects reliance on context alone for legal clarity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r2.anchor: فائدة ذكره تخليص المشترك ودفع الإيهام نصا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r3.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r3.claim: Some say dayn is mentioned to provide an explicit antecedent for the later pronoun; others say it improves the wording, but the objection that tadāyantum already supplies the sense is answered because it does not clearly identify the debt itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r3.anchor: وقيل : ذكر ليرجع اليه الضمير إذ لولاه لقيل : فاكتبوا الدين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r4.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r4.claim: A further view says the indefinite debt denotes debt generally and allows its division into current and deferred kinds; without the word, one might think debt is always deferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r4.anchor: وقيل : ذكر لأنه أبين لتنويع الدين إلى مؤجل وحال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r5.claim: A specified term is a known time expressed in days, months, or comparable units; a harvest date is too uncertain and would undermine the agreement.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r5.anchor: بالأيام أو الأشهر أو نظائرهما مما يفيد العلم ويرفع الجهالة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r6.claim: Writing the debt with its due date is more convenient and secure; most treat the instruction as recommended in view of the later trust exception.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r6.anchor: أي الدين بأجله لانه أرفق وأوثق والجمهور على استجابة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās restricts the debt here to forward-sale debt, reporting that God set and permitted such a deferred transaction before reciting the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r7.anchor: فقد أخرج البخارى عنه أنه قال : أشهد أن السلف المضمون إلى أجل مسمى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r8.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r8.claim: Imām Mālik uses the verse as evidence that a loan may have a deferred repayment date.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r8.anchor: واستدل الإمام مالك بها على جواز تأجيل القرض

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r9.claim: The command to have a just scribe specifies how to write and who does it; keeping either contracting party from writing prevents suspicion, and the scribe should be learned in law as well as fair and trustworthy.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r9.anchor: بيان لكيفية الكتابة المأمور بها وتعيين من يتولاها إثر الأمر بها إجمالا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r10.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r10.claim: Al-Ṭībī sees a stated meaning plus an embedded implication: the writer must be legally knowledgeable to balance consequential matters; some infer that rulers should bar unqualified people from drafting legal documents.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p55/r10.anchor: كما قال الطيبي مسوق لمعنى ومدمج فيه آخر بإشارة النص

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r1.claim: The writer must not refuse to document the debt; 'as God taught him' means because God taught and favored him with documentary skill, like the command to do good as God did good to you.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r1.anchor: أي لأجل ما علمه الله تعالى من كتابه الوثائق وتفضل به عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r2.claim: The phrase 'as God taught him' may modify the act of writing as an adverbial or circumstantial phrase, or attach to 'let him write'; the fāʾ can still connect because it functions semantically as a relative clause.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن يتعلق الكاف بأن يكتب على أنه نعت لمصدر محذوف أو حال

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r3.claim: If the second command repeats the earlier writing order, it emphasizes it because forbidding refusal does not explicitly command its opposite; some infer a communal obligation, but al-Alusi says this reading would impose hardship on the believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r3.anchor: والأمر بالكتابة بعد النهى عن الأداء منها على الأول للتأكيد وإحتيج إليه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r4.claim: On another parsing, the command requires writing in the taught, just manner after forbidding refusal of writing generally; this is not a repetition. Al-Alusi rejects the claim that repetition must follow, calling the distinction arbitrary when unrestricted and restricted commands concern one event.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56/r4.anchor: وأما على الوجه الثانى فلا تأكيد وإنما هو أمر بالكتابة المقيدة بعد النهي عن الإمتناع من المطلقة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.claim: The mā in 'as God taught him' may be a verbal noun, particle of emphasis, relative pronoun, or adjective; pronoun reference changes accordingly, and some supply 'document writing' as the second object of 'taught.'
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r1.anchor: قيل : إما مصدرية أو كافة وجوز أن تكون موصولة أو موصوفة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.claim: Imlāl means dictating to a scribe; the form alternates with imlāʾ through sound changes involving the doubled consonant and final hamza.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r2.anchor: من الإملال بمعنى الإلقاء على الكاتب ما يكتبه وفعله أمللت

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.claim: The person owing the debt must dictate because that person is the one against whom a claim is made and must acknowledge it; attaching the command to that description implies a restriction to the debtor.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r3.anchor: وهو المطلوب لأنه المشهود عليه فلا بد أن يكون هو المقر لا غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.claim: Pairing God's majestic name with 'his Lord' combines majesty and gracious care to intensify the debtor's admonition to fear God.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r4.anchor: جمع بين الإسم الجليل والوصف الجميل مبالغة في الحث على التقوى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.claim: The prohibition on reducing any part of the dictated debt, even a small amount, is the transmitted interpretation from Saʿīd b. Jubayr; variant readings omit or double the hamza in shayʾan.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r5.anchor: وإن كان حقيرا وقرئ شيا بطرح الهمزة وشيا بالتشديد وهذا هو التفسير المأثور عن سعيد بن جبير

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.claim: Some refer 'let him fear' to the scribe, but al-Alusi rejects this: the debtor is particularly liable to reduce the amount, whereas the scribe might add or subtract, and fairness already governs the scribe.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r6.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يرجع ضمير يتق للكاتب وليس بشئ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.claim: The debtor receives both a positive command to fear God and a prohibition on reducing the debt because self-interest naturally drives people to repel harm from themselves.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r7.anchor: وإنما شدد في تكليف المملى حيث جمع فيه بين الأمر بالإتقاء والنهي عن البخس

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.claim: Minhu can attach directly to 'reduce,' with min marking origin, or be a fronted circumstantial phrase; shayʾan can be its object or a cognate accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r8.anchor: وجهان : أحدهما أن يكون متعلقا بيبخس و من لإبتداء الغاية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.claim: The phrase about an incapable debtor restates the topic for clarity; 'foolish' can mean incompetent or foolish (Ibn Zayd), unable to dictate (Mujāhid), or wasteful and religiously corrupt (al-Shāfiʿī).
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r9.anchor: قاله ابن زيد أو جاهلا بالإملال قاله مجاهد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r10.claim: 'Weak' means a child or senile elder; inability to dictate may be muteness, as reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, or any impediment including unfamiliarity with the language.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.claim: The pronoun hu either emphasizes inability to dictate personally, excluding figurative attribution, or serves as the subject with changed syntax to stress negation; his guardian then dictates fairly.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r11.anchor: والضمير البارز توكيد للضمير المستتر في أن يمل وفائدة التوكيد به رفع المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.claim: The representative is whoever manages the incapable person's affairs, not only a formal guardian: the term includes a curator, agent, and translator; admitting for another here is valid, unlike admitting against another.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r12.anchor: أي متولي أمره وإن لم يكن خصوص الولي الشرعي فيشمل القيم والوكيل والمترجم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.speaker: ابن الفرس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.claim: Ibn al-Faras infers that guardians may not be unbelievers or sinners but may be enslaved or women because the verse requires only justice; al-Alusi dismisses this inference.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p56#2/r13.anchor: ذكره ابن الفرس وليس بشيء كما لا يخفى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r1.speaker: الشعبي والجبائي والرماني
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r1.claim: Al-Shaʿbī, al-Jubbāʾī, and al-Rummānī infer from 'let him write' and 'let no scribe refuse' that writing is a communal obligation; al-Ḥasan's position inclines that way.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r1.anchor: وإلى ذلك ذهب الشعبي والجبائي والرماني إلا أنهم قالوا : إنها واجبة على الكفاية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r2.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r2.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the individual scribe must write when asked; another position recommends writing, and a report from al-Ḍaḥḥāk says its original obligation was later abrogated.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r2.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك : واجب عليه أن يكتب إذا أمر وقيل : هي مندوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r3.claim: Istashhidū means request two people to bear witness to the transaction; alternatively its extra sīn and tāʾ may be redundant and mean simply 'witness.' The intensive noun suggests experienced, capable witnesses and may hint at recognized reliability.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r3.anchor: أي إطلبوهما ليتحملا الشهادة على ما جرى بينكما وجوز أن تكون السين والتاء زائدتين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r4.claim: The command to seek witnesses is considered recommended or obligatory according to the broader disagreement over these commands.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r4.anchor: والأمر للندب أو للوجوب على الخلاف في ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r5.claim: The expression 'from your men' is linked to the command or describes the witnesses partitivally; its address to believers is taken to imply Muslim, adult, male, and free witnesses, based on the customary sense of complete men.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r5.anchor: وفي ذكر الرجال مضافا إلى ضمير المخاطبين دلالة على إشتراط الإسلام والبلوغ والذكورة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r6.speaker: الإمامية
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r6.claim: The Imāmīs, along with Shurayḥ, Ibn Sīrīn, Abū Thawr, and ʿUthmān al-Battī, do not require a witness to be free, provided he is Muslim and upright; this differs from the report that ʿAlī rejected slave testimony entirely.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r6.anchor: وذهب الإمامية إلى عدم إشتراط الحرية في قبول الشهادة وإنما الشرط فيه عندهم الإسلام و العدالة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r7.speaker: أبو حنيفة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r7.claim: The verse does not address unbelievers testifying among themselves, but Abū Ḥanīfa allows this by analogy even when their religious communities differ.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r7.anchor: ولم تتعرض الآية لشهادة الكفار بعضهم على بعض وأجاز ذلك قياسا الإمام أبو حنيفة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r8.claim: 'If the two are not men' means the parties do not intend to summon two men, even if two are available; it negates the combined case rather than universally negating men, or the replacement clause would fail.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r8.anchor: أي لم يقصد إشهادهما ولو كانا موجودين والحكم من قبيل نفي العموم لا عموم النفي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r9.claim: If two men are not sought, the alternatives can be parsed elliptically as one man and two women testifying, serving as witnesses, or being requested as witnesses.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r9.anchor: أي فإن لم يكونا رجلين مجتمعين فليشهد رجل وإمرأتان أو فرجل وإمرأتان يشهدون

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r10.claim: A man and two women suffice in testimony outside ḥudūd and qiṣāṣ according to al-Alusi's school, while al-Shāfiʿī confines it to property cases and excludes matters such as marriage.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r10.anchor: وكفاية الرجل والمرأتين في الشهادة فيما عدا الحدود والقصاص عندنا وعند الشافعى في الأموال خاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r11.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r11.claim: Mālik excludes such testimony from ḥudūd, qiṣāṣ, clientage, and proof of chastity, but accepts it for agency and wills where emancipation is not involved; women alone may testify in matters such as birth or virginity.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r11.anchor: وقال مالك : لا تجوز شهادة أولئك فدى الحدود ولا القصاص ولا الولاء ولا الإحصان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r12.claim: A rare reading gives the initial hamza of imraʾatān sukūn, apparently to avoid a sequence of moving consonants.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r12.anchor: وقرئ وإمرأتان بهمزة ساكنة ولعل ذلك لإجتماع المتحركات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r13.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r13.claim: The phrase 'from those you approve' can modify the male-and-female pair, the two male witnesses, or all solicited witnesses; Abū Ḥayyān attaches it to 'seek witnesses,' which al-Alusi says awkwardly separates the women's provision from its rationale.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r13.anchor: وإختار أو حيان تعلقه بإستشهدوا ليكون قيدا في الجميع ويلزمه الفصل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r14.claim: The verse names people whose outward reliability you approve, rather than implying access to their inward state; God judges the hidden reality. 'Among the witnesses' is a circumstantial phrase, with women included in the masculine plural by convention.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p57/r14.anchor: ولم يقل من المرضيين لإفهامه إشتراط كونهم كذلك في نفس الأمر و لا طريق لنا إلى معرفته

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r1.claim: The two-woman provision explains the testimony rule: if one forgets, the other reminds her; al-Alusi attributes forgetfulness to women’s temperaments.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r1.anchor: شرع ذلك إرادة أن تذكر إحداهما الأخرى إن ضلت إحداهما لما أن النسيان غالب على طبع النساء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r2.claim: An objection says God’s legal will should not target forgetfulness; al-Alusi answers that the will targets the reminder consequent on it, not the lapse itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r2.anchor: لم تتعلق بالضلال نفسه أعنى عدم الإهتداء للشهادة بل بالضلال المرتب عليه الإذكار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r3.claim: The construction with an means reminder is so strongly desired that the normally unwanted lapse appears to be sought as its means; this is better than calling lapse a metonym for reminder.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r3.anchor: الإيماء إلى شدة الإهتمام بشأن الإذكار بحيث صار ما هو مكروه كأنه مطلوب لأجله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r4.claim: The second one of them can be the subject of remind, or its object while the other is subject; neither parse forces a misplaced explicit noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r4.anchor: يجوز أن تكون فاعل تذكر وليس من وضع المظهر موضع المضمر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r5.claim: Putting the explicit object before the subject foregrounds reminding the woman who forgot; repeating the noun also avoids assigning forgetfulness to one particular woman.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r5.anchor: والسبب في تقديم المفعول على الفاعل التنبيه على الإهتمام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r6.claim: Ibn Masud’s reading, transmitted by al-Aʿmash, has her remind her; other grammarians say the canonical wording intensifies ambiguity about which woman forgets.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r6.anchor: وهي قراءة ابن مسعود كما رواه الأعمشى إلى ما في النظم الكريم لتأكيد الإبهام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r7.speaker: حسين بن علي المغربي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r7.claim: Al-Maghribi takes the first one of them as one of the two testimonies and the second as one of the two women, so one woman recalls the forgotten testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p58/r7.anchor: فجعل ضمير ( إحدهما ) الأولى راجعا إلى الشهادتين

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r1.claim: Al-Alusi rejects al-Maghribi’s testimony-as-subject reading: it breaks the syntax and leaves no sensible second one; al-Tabarsi’s lexical support is weak because Arabic calls a forgetful person ضال.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r1.anchor: وليس بشئ إذ لا يكون لإحداهما أخرى في الكلام مع حصول التفكيك وعدم الإنتظام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والضحاك والربيع والسدي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r2.claim: These early authorities are reported as using ضل for a person who forgets, supporting the ordinary reading of the verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r2.anchor: وقد روي ذلك في الآية عن سعيد بن جبير والضحاك والربيع والسدي

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r3.speaker: ابن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r3.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna is reported to interpret the two women together as equivalent to a male witness; al-Alusi rejects this as strained in meaning and syntax.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r3.anchor: ما حكي عن ابن عيينة أن معنى ( فتذكر ) الخ فتجعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r4.claim: Al-Alusi says making two women into one figurative male witness requires layered metaphors and still fails to explain the need for a male witness if both women are present.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r4.anchor: لأن الإحتياج إلى اقتران ذكر البتة معهما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r5.speaker: شهاب الدين الغزنوي
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r5.claim: In the Khafaji anecdote, the judge answers that repeating one of them preserves ambiguity; a pronoun would wrongly identify a particular woman as the one subject to the ruling.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r5.anchor: تضل إحداهما ) فالقول محتمل كليهما فهي للاظهار

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r6.claim: A passive feminine reading of an tadilla is reported, along with the variant فتذاكر.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r6.anchor: وقرئ ( أن تضل ) بالبناء للمفعول والتأنيث وقرئ فتذاكر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r7.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب وأبو عمرو والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r7.claim: These readers recite فتذكر with a still dhal and kasra on kaf.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ويعقوب وأبو عمرو والحسن فتذكر بسكون الذال وكسر الكاف

ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r8.speaker: حمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r8.claim: Hamza reads an tadilla as a conditional clause and فتذكر in the indicative; its syntax is discussed in the next segment.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p59/r8.anchor: وحمزة ( أن تضل ) على الشرط فتذكر بالرفع

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r1.claim: Grammarians variously supply an omitted subject after the conditional fa; one analysis supplies the remembered woman, while other accounts supply a story pronoun or a pronoun for testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r1.anchor: وقيل : الأوجه أن يقدر المبتدأ ضمير الذاكرة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r2.speaker: بعض المحققين
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r2.claim: Some exacting grammarians prefer an implicit dual pronoun after the fa: then the two women remind one another.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r2.anchor: الأوجه من هذا كله تقدير ضمير التثنية أي فهما تذكر إحداهما الأخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r3.claim: Al-Alusi says later grammarians misunderstood al-Zamakhshari’s analogy to 5:95: the point is an omitted pronoun supplied by context, not whether it is singular or dual.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r3.anchor: ولم يتفطنوا بأن ذلك إنما هو من جهة تقدير ضمير بعد الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r4.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan are cited for interpreting the witnesses’ refusal as refusal either to give testimony or to undertake it.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r4.anchor: وهو المروي عن ابن عباس والحسن رضي الله تعالى عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r5.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Jubayr restrict the prohibition to refusing to give testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r5.anchor: وخص ذلك مجاهد وابن جبير بالأول

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r6.claim: Al-Alusi finds refusal to give testimony the more apparent sense because it avoids figurative interpretation, though al-Rabiʿ’s reported occasion points to being asked to testify.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r6.anchor: وهو الظاهر لعدم إحتياجه إلى إرتكاب المجاز

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r7.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r7.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the verse came when a man went around asking many people to witness and nobody responded.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r7.anchor: أن الآية نزلت حين كان الرجل يطوف في القوم الكثير فيدعوهم إلى الشهادة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r8.claim: The particle ma after idha is an extra particle, a regular construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r8.anchor: صلة وهى قاعدة مطردة بعد ( إذا )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r9.claim: Saʾama means to tire of or become annoyed by something; the verse discourages weariness over recording debt.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r9.anchor: ولا تسئموا ( أي تملوا أو تضجروا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r10.speaker: زهير
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r10.claim: Zuhayr’s line supplies poetic evidence for the sense of saʾima, growing weary.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r10.anchor:
ومنه قول زهير :
سئمت تكاليف الحياة ومن يعش

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r11.claim: The object of writing may be the debt, right, or written record implied by the verb; the verb can take it directly, or an understood preposition may be omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r11.anchor: أي الدين أو الحق أو الكتاب المشعر به الفعل

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r12.claim: Some take saʾama as laziness by euphemism, since the Qurʾan describes hypocrites as praying lazily; a hadith says a believer should say prayer feels burdensome, not lazy.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r12.anchor: وقيل : المراد من السأم الكسل إلا أنه كني به عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r13.claim: A variant reads both occurrences of yasʾamu in the plural masculine form.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r13.anchor: وقرئ ولا يسأموا أن يكتبوه بالياء فيهما

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r14.claim: Small and large describe the debt’s amount or its level of detail; alternatively they are predicates of an omitted kāna, with the smaller stated first for emphasis and progression.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r14.anchor: حالان من الضمير أي على كل حال قليلا أو كثيرا مجملا أو مفصلا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r15.claim: The phrase to its term describes the debt remaining due until its agreed maturity, not the writing, which takes little time.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r15.anchor: حال من الهاء في تكتبوه أي مستقرا في ذمة المدين إلى وقت حلوله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r16.claim: That may refer to writing, testimony, or, best, all the preceding practices; the demonstrative addresses the believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r16.anchor: أي الكتب وهو الأقرب أو الأشهاد وهو الأبعد أو جميع ما ذكر وهو الأحسن

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r17.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r17.claim: Sibawayh allows the comparatives aqsaṭ and aqwam to be formed directly from verbs, without treating them as irregular.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r17.anchor: مبينان من أقسط وأقام على رأى سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r18.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r18.claim: Abu Hayyan, citing Ibn al-Qattaʿ, says qasṭ means justice, so aqsaṭ needs no special derivation from a noun.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60/r18.anchor: وقيل من قاسط بمعنى ذى قسط وقويم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r1.claim: Aqwam retains its wāw because the root is frozen in the exclamatory form; the comparative has a meaning that supports this form.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r1.anchor: وإنما صحت الواو فى أقوم ولم يقل أقام

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r2.claim: Writing and witnessing make doubts about a debt’s kind, amount, and maturity less likely; the omitted preposition before an taرتابوا is variously understood as ila, lam, min, or fi.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r2.anchor: أقرب إلى انتقاء ريبكم وشككم في جنس الدين وقدره وأجله

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r3.claim: The cash-trade exception is best read as a detached exception from the writing command: immediate exchange of both countervalues permits leaving the transaction unwritten.

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r4.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r4.claim: The Dur al-Masun allows a connected exception from witnessing: cash trade is exempt from witnessing in every case.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r4.anchor: يجوز أن يكون استثناءا متصلا من الاستشهاد

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r5.claim: Other analyses make the exception detached from both writing and witnessing, or attach it to both; al-Alusi favors the first analysis.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : إنه استثناء من هذا وذاك وهو منقطع أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r6.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r6.claim: Asim reads tijaratan in the accusative as the predicate of kāna, with an implicit subject referring to trade.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r6.anchor: ونصب عاصم تجارة على أنها خبر تكون واسمها مستتر فيها يعود إلى التجارة

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r7.claim: Other grammarians make the implied subject refer to the transaction and treat trade as a verbal noun; most readers use the nominative, with trade as subject and the clause as predicate, or take kāna as complete.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r7.anchor: ورفعها الباقون على أنها اسم ( تكون ) ولخبر جملة ( تديرونها )

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r8.claim: There is no harm or sin in omitting written records for immediate exchanges, because they are less exposed to dispute and forgetfulness or because writing them is burdensome.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r8.anchor: أي فلا مضرة عليكم أو لا إثم في عدم كتابتكم لها لبعد ذلك عن التنازع والنسيان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r9.claim: Witness when you make the specified sale, or, according to a broader reading, whenever a sale is made.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r9.anchor: أي هذا التبايع المذكور أو مطلقا

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r10.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r10.claim: Umar’s uncontracted reading with kasra supports the active interpretation of the prohibition against harming a scribe or witness.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r10.anchor: قراءة عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه ولا يضار بالفك والكسر

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas’s uncontracted reading with fatha supports the passive interpretation, forbidding others to harm the scribe or witness.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r11.anchor: وقراءة ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما بالفك والفتح

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r12.claim: If active, the verse forbids witnesses and scribes to refuse, distort, add, or subtract; if passive, it forbids burdening them, withholding the fee, or requiring costly travel.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r12.anchor: نهى الكاتب والشاهد عن ترك الإجابة إلى ما يطلب منهما وعن التحريف والزيادة والنقصان

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r13.speaker: الربيع
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r13.claim: Al-Rabiʿ reports that requesters sometimes forced busy scribes to write and would not let them decline; this occasion explains the command not to harm them.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r13.anchor: ما أخرجه ابن جريح عن الربيع قال : لما نزلت هذه الآية

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r14.claim: Al-Alusi rejects making the صيغة carry both active and passive meanings at once.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r14.anchor: وحمل بعضهم الصيغة على المعنيين وليس بشئ

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r15.speaker: الحسن
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r15.claim: Al-Hasan is reported to read the verb with kasra; a nominative variant treats the negative as a prohibition.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r15.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ولا يضار بالكسر وقرئ بالرفع على أنه نفي بمعنى النهى

ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r16.claim: The warned-against act is the prohibited harm or another breach; فسوق بكم means disobedience attached to you, or more forcefully a state in which you are immersed.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p60#2/r16.anchor: منكم ( فإنه ( أى ذلك الفعل ( فسوق بكم

ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r1.claim: God knows every matter and will repay people for their conduct.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r1.anchor: فلا يخفى عليه حاكم وهو مجازيكم بذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r2.claim: Repeating the divine name in three successive independent clauses is laudable when it magnifies the subject; here the clauses exhort piety, promise divine instruction, and glorify God’s knowledge.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r2.anchor: المستحسن كل تكرير يقع على طريق التعظيم أو التحقير في جمل متواليات

ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r3.claim: The clauses differ as exhortation, promise, and declaration, which explains their connective pattern; treating the middle clause as a circumstantial clause is possible but less preferred.
ALUSI-FULL:v3p61/r3.anchor: لأن ( اتقوا الله ) حث على تقوى الله تعالى ( ويعلمكم الله ) وعد بإنعامه سبحانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.claim: After forbidding usury, God permitted salam, an advance purchase secured to a fixed term, in this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما لما حرم الله الربا أباح السلم وقال: أشهد أن السلف المضمون إلى أجل مسمى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.claim: Tadāyantum means dealing by debt; dayn specifies this sense because debt transactions may mean repayment or immediate exchange, or it is emphatic like saying a bird flies with its wings.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r2.anchor: قوله: {إذا تداينتم} أي تعاملتم بالدين، يقال: داينته إذا عاملته بالدين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.claim: A specified term has a known beginning and end; in sale or salam it prevents the creditor demanding payment before its due date, while a loan's term is not binding according to most scholars.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r3.anchor: الأجل مدة معلومة الأول والآخر، والأجل يلزم في الثمن في البيع وفي السلم حتى لا يكون لصاحب الحق الطلب قبل محله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r4.claim: Write the debt whether it arises from a sale, salam, or loan.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r4.anchor: {فاكتبوه} أي اكتبوا الذي تداينتم به، بيعا كان أو سلما أو قرضا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r5.claim: Some consider writing obligatory, but most deem the command recommendatory; al-Shaʿbi says writing, witnessing, and pledging were obligatory then abrogated by the trust provision.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r5.anchor: واختلفوا في هذه الكتابة: فقال بعضهم: هي واجبة، والأكثرون على أنه أمر استحباب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r6.claim: Some say writing is obligatory, while the majority recommend it and say omission is harmless, comparing the command with the call to disperse after Friday prayer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r6.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه أمر استحباب فإن ترك فلا بأس كقوله تعالى "فإذا قضيتم الصلاة فانتشروا في الأرض" (10-الجمعة)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r7.speaker: الشعبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r7.claim: Al-Shaʿbi holds that writing, witnessing, and pledging were initially obligatory and that the instruction to fulfill a trusted deposit abrogated all three.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم كانت كتابة الدين والإشهاد والرهن فرضا ثم نسخ الكل بقوله "فإن أمن بعضكم بعضا فليؤد الذي ائتمن أمانته" وهو قول الشعبي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r8.claim: A just scribe records the debt agreement for both creditor and debtor without adding, subtracting, or altering its term.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r8.anchor: ثم بين كيفية الكتابة فقال جل ذكره {وليكتب بينكم} أي ليكتب كتاب الدين بين الطالب والمطلوب {كاتب بالعدل} أي بالحق من غير زيادة ولا نقصان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r9.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r9.claim: A scribe must write when asked; al-Hasan requires it only when no other scribe is available, while others regard it as recommended.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r9.anchor: واختلفوا في وجوب الكتابة على الكاتب وتحمل الشهادة على الشاهد، فذهب قوم إلى وجوبها إذا طولب وهو قول مجاهد، وقال الحسن تجب إذا لم يكن كاتب غيره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r10.speaker: الضحاك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r10.claim: He says the writer's and witness's duties were binding, then abrogated by the ban on harming either.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r10.anchor: وقال الضحاك كانت عزيمة واجبة على الكاتب والشاهد فنسخها قوله تعالى "ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r11.claim: As God taught him means according to the law God ordained and commanded.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r11.anchor: {كما علمه الله} أي كما شرعه الله وأمره

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r12.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r12.claim: The debtor must dictate his own admission so his obligation is clear; imlāl and imlāʾ are two eloquent synonyms used in the Qur'an.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r12.anchor: وليملل الذي عليه الحق} يعني: المطلوب يقر على نفسه بلسانه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r13.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r13.claim: The one dictating must fear God and not reduce any part of the debt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p348#2/r13.anchor: {وليتق الله ربه} يعني الممل {ولا يبخس منه شيئا} أي ولا ينقص منه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r1.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r1.claim: Safīh means someone ignorant of how to dictate; al-Dahhak and al-Suddi say it means a young child; al-Shafiʿi says a squanderer who corrupts his property or religion.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r1.anchor: {فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها} أي جاهلا بالإملاء، قاله مجاهد، وقال الضحاك والسدي: طفلا صغيرا، وقال الشافعي رحمه الله، السفيه:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r2.claim: Ḍaʿīf may mean an elderly man or someone mentally weak from impairment or madness.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r2.anchor: قوله {أو ضعيفا} أي شيخا كبيرا وقيل هو ضعيف العقل لعته أو جنون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r3.claim: Unable to dictate may mean mute, impaired, unable to speak Arabic, imprisoned, absent from the scribe, or ignorant of what is owed and owned.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r3.anchor: لخرس أو عي أو عجمة أو حبس أو غيبة لا يمكنه حضور الكاتب أو جهل بما له وعليه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r4.claim: His guardian may mean his custodian; Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil identify the guardian as the creditor, who knows the claim and dictates fairly if the debtor cannot.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r4.anchor: {فليملل وليه} أي قيمه {بالعدل} أي بالصدق والحق، وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنه ومقاتل: أراد بالولي صاحب الحق

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p349/r5.speaker: author
