ITQAN:v1p163/r13.anchor: فأرسل إلى حفصة أن أرسلي إلينا الصحف ننسخها في المصاحف ثم نردها إليك فأرسلت بها حفصة إلى عثمان فأمر زيد بن ثابت وعبد الله بن الزبير وسعيد بن العاص وعبد الرحمن بن الحارث بن هشام

ITQAN:v1p163/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p163/r14.speaker: عثمان
ITQAN:v1p163/r14.claim: After copying, ʿUthman returned Hafsa’s sheets, sent a codex to each region, and ordered other Qur’anic sheets and codices burned.
ITQAN:v1p163/r14.anchor: حتى إذا نسخوا الصحف في المصاحف رد عثمان الصحف إلى حفصة وأرسل إلى كل أفق بمصحف مما نسخوا وأمر بما سواه من القرآن في كل صحيفة ومصحف أن يحرق

ITQAN:v1p130/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p130/r1.claim: Al-Suyuti says the hadith about seven ahruf has roughly forty interpretations.
ITQAN:v1p130/r1.anchor: اختلف في معنى هذا الحديث على نحو أربعين قولا

ITQAN:v1p130/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r2.speaker: ابن سعدان النحوي
ITQAN:v1p130/r2.claim: Ibn Saʿdan regards the hadith as obscure because harf can mean a letter, word, meaning, or aspect.
ITQAN:v1p130/r2.anchor: أنه من المشكل الذي لا يدرى معناه لأن الحرف يصدق لغة على حرف الهجاء وعلى الكلمة وعلى المعنى وعلى الجهة قاله ابن سعدان النحوي

ITQAN:v1p130/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r3.speaker: عياض
ITQAN:v1p130/r3.claim: Qadi ʿIyad and followers take seven as a nonliteral number signifying ease, latitude, and abundance, as seven, seventy, and seven hundred can mean many.
ITQAN:v1p130/r3.anchor: الثاني أنه ليس المراد بالسبعة حقيقة العدد بل المراد التيسير والتسهيل والسعة ولفظ السبعة يطلق على إرادة الكثرة

ITQAN:v1p130/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p130/r4.claim: The Ibn Abbas report in both Sahihs supports an actual count: Gabriel began with one mode, and the Prophet kept asking for more until there were seven.
ITQAN:v1p130/r4.anchor: ويرده ما في حديث ابن عباس في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ITQAN:v1p130/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p130/r5.claim: Ubayy’s Muslim report likewise recounts successive easing from one to two and ultimately seven ahruf.
ITQAN:v1p130/r5.anchor: وفي حديث أبي عند مسلم إن ربي أرسل إلي أن أقرأ القرآن على حرف

ITQAN:v1p130/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v1p130/r6.claim: A Nasaʾi wording has Gabriel and Michael ask the Prophet to keep requesting more until the allowance reaches seven.
ITQAN:v1p130/r6.anchor: وفي لفظ عنه عند النسائي إن جبريل وميكائيل أتياني فقعد جبريل عن يميني وميكائيل عن يساري

ITQAN:v1p130/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r7.speaker: أبو بكرة
ITQAN:v1p130/r7.claim: In Abu Bakra’s Nasaʾi report, Michael’s silence signals that the fixed count has ended.
ITQAN:v1p130/r7.anchor: وفي حديث أبي بكرة عنده اقرأه فنظرت إلى ميكائيل فسكت فعلمت أنه قد انتهت العدة

ITQAN:v1p130/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p130/r8.claim: A third view takes seven ahruf to mean seven readings; its objection is that few words, such as عبد الطاغوت and أف, have seven forms.
ITQAN:v1p130/r8.anchor: الثالث أن المراد بها سبع قراءات وتعقب بأنه لا يوجد في القرآن كلمة تقرأ على سبعة أوجه إلى القليل مثل

ITQAN:v1p130/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p130/r9.claim: A fourth view says each word may have one or more readings up to seven, but this is challenged because some words have more than seven.
ITQAN:v1p130/r9.anchor: وأجيب بأن المراد أن كل كلمة تقرأ بوجه أو وجهين أو ثلاثة أو أكثر إلى سبعة ويشكل على هذا أن في الكلمات ما قرئ على أكثر

ITQAN:v1p130/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r10.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ITQAN:v1p130/r10.claim: Ibn Qutayba’s first variation type changes case or vowel without changing meaning or form, illustrated by two readings of ولا يضار كاتب.
ITQAN:v1p130/r10.anchor: ذكره ابن قتيبة قال فأولها ما يتغير حركته ولا يزول معناه وصورته مثل

ITQAN:v1p130/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r11.speaker: ابن قتيبة
ITQAN:v1p130/r11.claim: His second type changes the verb form, illustrated by باعد read as past tense or as a command.

ITQAN:v1p130/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r17.speaker: قاسم بن ثابت
ITQAN:v1p130/r17.claim: Qasim ibn Thabit objects that the license arose when most people neither wrote nor knew the rasm, but knew letter sounds and articulations.
ITQAN:v1p130/r17.anchor: وتعقب هذا قاسم بن ثابت بأن الرخصة وقعت وأكثرهم يومئذ لا يكتب ولا يعرف الرسم وإنما كانوا يعرفون الحروف ومخارجها

ITQAN:v1p130/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p130/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p130/r18.claim: The response says Qasim’s objection does not weaken Ibn Qutayba: the listed variation types may have arisen incidentally and been recognized by induction.
ITQAN:v1p130/r18.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا يلزم من ذلك توهين ما قاله ابن قتيبة لاحتمال أن يكون الانحصار المذكور في ذلك وقع اتفاقا وإنما اطلع عليه بالاستقراء

ITQAN:v1p231/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p231/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p231/r2.claim: The pause after ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب and the pause after كما علمه الله are likewise mutually exclusive.
ITQAN:v1p231/r2.anchor: وكالوقف على ﴿ ولا يأب كاتب أن يكتب ﴾ فإن بينه وبين ﴿ كما علمه الله ﴾ مراقبة

ITQAN:v1p231/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p231/r4.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p231/r4.claim: Ibn al-Jazari credits Abu al-Fadl al-Razi as the first to identify pause-muraqaba, borrowing the notion from prosodic meter.
ITQAN:v1p231/r4.anchor: قال ابن الجزري وأول من نبه على المراقبة في الوقف أبو الفضل الرازي أخذه من المراقبة في العروض

ITQAN:v3p84/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p84/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p84/r8.claim: A word shared between two literal senses, or literal and figurative senses, may carry both; if polysemous use is denied, the wording can be understood as addressed twice with each sense intended.
ITQAN:v3p84/r8.anchor: وقد يكون مشتركا بين حقيقتين أو حقيقة ومجاز ويصح حمله عليهما جميعا سواء قلنا بجواز إستعمال اللفظ في معنييه أو لا

ITQAN:v3p84/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p84/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p84/r9.claim: The verse can mean that the scribe and witness must not wrong the claimant, or that the claimant must not harm them by imposing undue work or coercing them.
ITQAN:v3p84/r9.anchor: ومن أمثلته ﴿ ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد ﴾ فإنه يحتمل لا يضارر الكاتب والشهيد صاحب الحق بجور في الكتابة والشهادة

ITQAN:v3p84/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p84/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p84/r10.claim: On the alternate vocalization, the verse forbids the claimant from injuring the scribe or witness by burdening them improperly or compelling them to act.
ITQAN:v3p84/r10.anchor: أي لا يضرهما صاحب الحق بإلزامهما مالا يلزمهما وإجبارهما على الكتابة والشهادة

ITQAN:v3p134/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p134/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p134/r1.claim: Hasr or qasr restricts one matter to another by a particular method, affirming the stated ruling and negating it of everything else.
ITQAN:v3p134/r1.anchor: أما الحصر ويقال له القصر فهو تخصيص أمر بآخر بطريق مخصوص ويقال أيضا إثبات الحكم للمذكور ونفيه عما عداه

ITQAN:v3p134/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p134/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p134/r2.claim: Restriction divides into restricting a described subject to a quality or a quality to a subject; either can be literal or figurative.
ITQAN:v3p134/r2.anchor: وينقسم إلى قصر الموصوف على الصفة وقصر الصفة على الموصوف وكل منهما إما حقيقي وإما مجازي

ITQAN:v3p134/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p134/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p134/r3.claim: Literal restriction of a subject to one quality, such as Zayd is only a writer, is exceptionally rare and absent from the Qur’an because exhaustive knowledge of every quality is difficult.
ITQAN:v3p134/r3.anchor: وهو عزيز لا يكاد يوجد لتعذر الإحاطة بصفات الشيء

ITQAN:v3p137/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r1.speaker: أهل البيان
ITQAN:v3p137/r1.claim: Rhetoricians list coordination with لا or بل as a fourth construction of restriction and report no disagreement on it.
ITQAN:v3p137/r1.anchor: الرابع العطف بلا أو بل ذكره أهل البيان ولم يحكوا فيه خلافا

ITQAN:v3p137/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r2.speaker: بهاء الدين
ITQAN:v3p137/r2.claim: Baha al-Din disputes restriction by لا: saying Zayd is a poet, not a writer denies one quality only, whereas restriction must deny every quality besides the one affirmed.
ITQAN:v3p137/r2.anchor: ونازع فيه الشيخ بهاء الدين في عروس الأفراح فقال أي قصر في العطف بلا إنما فيه نفي وإثبات فقولك زيد شاعر لا كاتب لا تعرض فيه لنفي صفة ثالثة

ITQAN:v3p137/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r3.speaker: بهاء الدين
ITQAN:v3p137/r3.claim: He objects that coordination with بل is even less suitable because negation and affirmation do not consistently continue through it.
ITQAN:v3p137/r3.anchor: وأما العطف ببل فأبعد منه لأنه لا يستمر فيها النفي والإثبات

ITQAN:v3p137/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p137/r4.claim: A fifth construction is fronting the object, as in إياك نعبد and لإلى الله تحشرون; some scholars disagree that this conveys restriction.
ITQAN:v3p137/r4.anchor: وخالف فيه قوم وسيأتي بسط الكلام فيه قريبا

ITQAN:v3p137/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p137/r9.speaker: عبد القاهر
ITQAN:v3p137/r9.claim: The seventh proposed construction is fronting the subject to restrict it to a verbal predicate; ʿAbd al-Qahir describes this function.
ITQAN:v3p137/r9.anchor: السابع تقديم المسند إليه على ما قال الشيخ عبد القاهر قد يقدم المسند إليه ليفيد تخصيصه بالخبر الفعلي

ITQAN:v4p453/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p453/r1.claim: Writing the Qur’an neatly, clearly, and precisely without undue effort is recommended; hanging a mushaf and writing it on a small object are disliked.
ITQAN:v4p453/r1.anchor: يستحب كتابة المصحف وتحسين كتابته وتبيينها وإيضاحها وتحقيق الخط دون مشقة وتعليقه فيكره وكذا كتابته في الشيء الصغير

ITQAN:v4p453/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r2.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v4p453/r2.claim: ʿUmar rebuked and struck a man for writing a mushaf in very fine script, telling him to honor God’s Book; he was pleased to see a large mushaf.
ITQAN:v4p453/r2.anchor: عن عمر أنه وجد مع رجل مصحفا قد كتبه بقلم دقيق فكره ذلك وضربه وقال عظموا كتاب الله وكان عمر إذا رأى مصحفا عظيما سر به

ITQAN:v4p453/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r3.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p453/r3.anchor: وأخرج عبد الرزاق عن علي أنه كان يكره أن تتخذ المصاحف صغارا

ITQAN:v4p453/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r4.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p453/r4.claim: A second report says Ali disliked writing the Qur’an on a small object.
ITQAN:v4p453/r4.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عنه أنه كره أن يكتب القرآن في الشيء الصغير

ITQAN:v4p453/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r5.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p453/r5.claim: Ali told Abu Hakim al-Abdi to sharpen his pen; after he trimmed it, Ali approved and said to illuminate the script as God had illuminated it.
ITQAN:v4p453/r5.anchor: عن أبي حكيم العبدي قال مر بي علي وأنا أكتب مصحفا فقال أجل قلمك فقضمت من قلمي قضمة ثم جعلت أكتب فقال نعم هكذا نوره كما نوره الله

ITQAN:v4p453/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r6.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v4p453/r6.claim: A report attributed to Ali says a person who carefully embellishes the basmala is forgiven.
ITQAN:v4p453/r6.anchor: عن علي موقوفا قال تنوق رجل في ( بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ) فغفر له

ITQAN:v4p453/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ITQAN:v4p453/r7.claim: A raised report from Anas promises forgiveness to anyone who writes the basmala beautifully.
ITQAN:v4p453/r7.anchor: من طريق أبان عن أنس مرفوعا ( من كتب بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم مجودة غفر الله له )

ITQAN:v4p453/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r8.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
ITQAN:v4p453/r8.claim: ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz instructed his officials to extend the word الرحمن when writing the basmala.
ITQAN:v4p453/r8.anchor: عن عمر بن عبد العزيز أنه كتب إلى عماله

ITQAN:v4p453/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r9.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ITQAN:v4p453/r9.claim: Zayd ibn Thabit disliked writing the basmala without its letter sin.
ITQAN:v4p453/r9.anchor: وأخرج عن زيد بن ثابت أنه كان يكره أن تكتب ( بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ليس لها سين )

ITQAN:v4p453/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r10.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v4p453/r10.claim: ʿUmar struck ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs’s scribe for writing bismillah without the sin, explaining that the blow was for that letter.
ITQAN:v4p453/r10.anchor: وأخرج عن يزيد بن أبي حبيب أن كاتب عمرو بن العاص كتب إلى عمر فكتب ( بسم الله ) ولم يكتب لها سنا فضربه عمر فقيل له فيم ضربك أمير المؤمنين قال ضربني في سين

ITQAN:v4p453/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r11.speaker: ابن سيرين
ITQAN:v4p453/r11.claim: Ibn Sirin disliked extending the basmala’s initial baʾ through the mim before writing the sin.
ITQAN:v4p453/r11.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن سيرين أنه كان يكره أن تمد الباء إلى الميم حتى تكتب السين

ITQAN:v4p453/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r12.speaker: ابن سيرين
ITQAN:v4p453/r12.claim: Ibn Sirin disliked writing the mushaf in mashq, explaining that it involves a deficiency.
ITQAN:v4p453/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي داود في المصاحف عن ابن سيرين أنه كره أن يكتب المصحف مشقا قيل لم قال لأن فيه نقصا

ITQAN:v4p453/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p453/r13.claim: Writing the Qur’an with an impure substance is forbidden; writing it in gold is considered good by al-Ghazali.
ITQAN:v4p453/r13.anchor: وتحرم كتابته بشيء نجس وأما بالذهب فهو حسن كما قاله الغزالي

ITQAN:v4p453/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r14.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v4p453/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas, Abu Dharr, and Abu al-Dardaʾ are reported to have disliked writing the Qur’an in gold.
ITQAN:v4p453/r14.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عن ابن عباس وأبي ذر وأبي الدرداء أنهم كرهوا ذلك

ITQAN:v4p453/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p453/r15.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p453/r15.claim: Ibn Masʿud said the best adornment of a gold-decorated mushaf is reciting it truthfully.
ITQAN:v4p453/r15.anchor: وأخرج عن ابن مسعود أنه مر عليه مصحف زين بالذهب فقال إن أحسن ما زين به المصحف تلاوته بالحق

ITQAN:v4p496/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r1.claim: Al-Bukhari often cites Ibn Abi Talha’s Ibn Abbas tafsir through Abu Salih; al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Mundhir transmit it through intermediaries.
ITQAN:v4p496/r1.anchor: وهي عند البخاري عن أبي صالح وقد اعتمد عليها في صحيحه كثيرا فيما يعلقه عن ابن عباس

ITQAN:v4p496/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r2.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v4p496/r2.claim: Some say Ibn Abi Talha did not hear Ibn Abbas’s tafsir and instead received it from Mujahid or Sa'id ibn Jubayr.
ITQAN:v4p496/r2.anchor: وقال قوم لم يسمع ابن أبي طلحة من ابن عباس التفسير وإنما أخذه عن مجاهد أو سعيد بن جبير

ITQAN:v4p496/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r3.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v4p496/r3.claim: Ibn Hajar answers that the intermediary is known and trustworthy, so the missing direct hearing causes no problem.
ITQAN:v4p496/r3.anchor: قال ابن حجر بعد أن عرفت الواسطة وهو ثقة فلا ضير في ذلك

ITQAN:v4p496/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r4.speaker: الخليلي
ITQAN:v4p496/r4.claim: Al-Khalili describes the Ibn Abbas tafsir as transmitted from Ali ibn Abi Talha through Mu'awiya ibn Salih and Abu Salih, the scribe of al-Layth.
ITQAN:v4p496/r4.anchor: تفسير معاوية بن صالح قاضي الأندلس عن علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس رواه الكبار عن أبي صالح

ITQAN:v4p496/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r5.speaker: الحفاظ
ITQAN:v4p496/r5.claim: Hadith critics agree Ibn Abi Talha did not hear directly from Ibn Abbas; long tafsirs attributed to Ibn Abbas with unknown transmitters are not acceptable, such as Juyaybir from al-Dahhak.
ITQAN:v4p496/r5.anchor: وأجمع الحفاظ على أن ابن أبي طلحة لم يسمعه من ابن عباس

ITQAN:v4p496/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r6.claim: The longest Ibn Jurayj tafsir route, through Bakr ibn Sahl, Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id, and Musa ibn Muhammad, is questionable.
ITQAN:v4p496/r6.anchor: وأطولها ما يرويه بكر بن سهل الدمياطي عن عبد الغني بن سعيد عن موسى بن محمد عن ابن جريج وفيه نظر

ITQAN:v4p496/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r7.claim: Muhammad ibn Thawr’s transmission from Ibn Jurayj comprises about three large parts and was judged sound.
ITQAN:v4p496/r7.anchor: وروى محمد بن ثور عن ابن جريج نحو ثلاثة أجزاء كبار وذلك صححوه

ITQAN:v4p496/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r8.claim: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad’s one-part transmission from Ibn Jurayj is sound and agreed upon.
ITQAN:v4p496/r8.anchor: وروى الحجاج بن محمد عن ابن جريج نحو جزء وذلك صحيح متفق عليه

ITQAN:v4p496/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r9.claim: Shibl ibn Abbad’s tafsir, through Ibn Abi Najih from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas, is close to sound.
ITQAN:v4p496/r9.anchor: وتفسير شبل بن عباد المكي عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد عن ابن عباس قريب إلى الصحة

ITQAN:v4p496/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r10.claim: The tafsir of Ata ibn Dinar may be recorded and used as evidence.
ITQAN:v4p496/r10.anchor: وتفسير عطاء بن دينار يكتب ويحتج به

ITQAN:v4p496/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r11.claim: The tafsir of Abu Ruwq, about one part, was judged sound.
ITQAN:v4p496/r11.anchor: وتفسير أبي روق نحو جزء صححوه

ITQAN:v4p496/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r12.claim: Al-Suddi’s tafsir has chains to Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas; although leading imams narrated from al-Suddi, Asbat ibn Nasr’s compilation is disputed, yet al-Suyuti calls it the best tafsir.
ITQAN:v4p496/r12.anchor: لكن التفسير الذي جمعه رواه أسباط بن نصر وأسباط لم يتفقوا عليه غير أن أمثل التفاسير تفسير السدي

ITQAN:v4p496/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r13.speaker: الخليلي
ITQAN:v4p496/r13.claim: Ibn Jurayj did not aim to authenticate his tafsir and included both sound and weak reports for each verse.
ITQAN:v4p496/r13.anchor: فإنه لم يقصد الصحة وإنما روى ما ذكر في كل آية من الصحيح والسقيم

ITQAN:v4p496/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r14.speaker: الخليلي
ITQAN:v4p496/r14.claim: Maqatil ibn Sulayman was considered weak, though he met senior Successors and al-Shafi'i indicated his tafsir was usable.
ITQAN:v4p496/r14.anchor: فمقاتل في نفسه ضعفوه وقد أدرك الكبار من التابعين والشافعي أشار إلى أن تفسيره صالح

ITQAN:v4p496/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p496/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p496/r15.claim: Al-Tabari often cites al-Suddi through several routes; Ibn Abi Hatim omits this compilation to restrict himself to the soundest reports, while al-Hakim authenticates some reports through Murra from Ibn Masud and others.
ITQAN:v4p496/r15.anchor: لأنه التزم أن يخرج أصح ما ورد والحاكم يخرج منه في مستدركه أشياء ويصححه لكن من طريق مرة عن ابن مسعود

ITQAN:v2p391#5/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r2.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r2.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the claim that the Quran descended in Quraysh speech means it was predominantly so, since non-Quraysh features occur in readings, including hamza pronunciation that Quraysh lacks.
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عبد البر في التمهيد قول من قال نزل بلغة قريش معناه عندي الأغلب

ITQAN:v2p391#5/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r3.speaker: جمال الدين بن مالك
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r3.claim: Ibn Malik says the Quran is in Hijazi speech except a few Tamimi forms, including assimilation of jussive verbs; Hijazi unassimilated forms are common, as in وليملل.
ITQAN:v2p391#5/r3.anchor: وقال الشيخ جمال الدين بن مالك أنزل الله القرآن بلغة الحجازيين إلا قليلا فإنه نزل بلغة التميميين

ITQAN:v2p453#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r1.speaker: الكوفيون
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r1.claim: Kufan grammarians treat أن as conditional like إن and apply that analysis to these clauses; both forms are reported as read in the cited verses.
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r1.anchor: أن تكون شرطية كالمكسورة قاله الكوفيون وخرجوا عليه ﴿ أن تضل إحداهما ﴾

ITQAN:v2p453#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r2.speaker: ابن هشام
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r2.claim: Ibn Hisham prefers the conditional analysis because both particles occur in the same syntactic position and the following فـ in فتذكر supports it.
ITQAN:v2p453#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن هشام ويرجحه عندي تواردهما على محل واحد والأصل التوافق

ITQAN:v3p196/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p196/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p196/r2.claim: The balanced repetition and matching phrases in “if one of the two errs, then one reminds the other” exemplify verbal ornament and rhythmic balance.
ITQAN:v3p196/r2.anchor: ومنها مراعاة الترصيع وتوازن الألفاظ في التركيب ذكره بعضهم في قوله

ITQAN:v3p82/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p82/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p82/r1.claim: An unqualified expression denotes a thing without restriction; restrict it when evidence does so, but otherwise leave both absolute and qualified wording as stated, following ordinary Arabic usage.
ITQAN:v3p82/r1.anchor: المطلق الدال على الماهية بلا قيد وهو مع المقيد كالعام مع الخاص

ITQAN:v3p82/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.claim: When a qualified ruling has no other basis, it constrains an unqualified one; witness fairness is therefore required in sales and handing orphans their property as well as in divorce and wills.
ITQAN:v3p82/r2.anchor: اشتراط العدالة في الشهود على الرجعة والفرق والوصية في قوله

ITQAN:v3p218#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r4.claim: Commands can remind of favor, express wonder or equal treatment, give practical guidance as in witnessing sales, show contempt, warn, or honor the addressee.
ITQAN:v3p218#2/r4.anchor: والامتنان نحو ﴿ كلوا من ثمره إذا أثمر ﴾

ITQAN:v1p165/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p165/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar dates Uthman’s collection to 25 AH and says a later estimate around 30 AH was asserted without supporting evidence.
ITQAN:v1p165/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر وكان ذلك في سنة خمس وعشرين قال وغفل بعض من أدركناه فزعم أنه كان في حدود سنة ثلاثين

ITQAN:v1p165/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r2.speaker: أبو قلابة
ITQAN:v1p165/r2.claim: Abu Qilaba reports that reading disputes in Uthman's time led to fights; Uthman ordered a standard codex, and when the committee disagreed, they consulted Companions on the Prophet’s recitation and recorded it.
ITQAN:v1p165/r2.anchor: قال اختلفوا في القراءة على عهد عثمان حتى اقتتل الغلمان والمعلمون فبلغ ذلك عثمان بن عفان

ITQAN:v1p165/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r3.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
ITQAN:v1p165/r3.claim: Ibn Sirin reports that Uthman assembled twelve Quraysh and Ansar to copy the codices from the sheets kept at Umar’s house; the committee delayed disputed passages, which Ibn Sirin thought allowed consultation of those last present at the final review.
ITQAN:v1p165/r3.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي داود بسند صحيح عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي لا تقولوا في عثمان إلا خيرا

ITQAN:v1p165/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r4.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p165/r4.claim: Ali says Uthman’s codex decision had the Companions’ agreement and united Muslims after competing readings led some to declare another’s recitation nearly unbelief.
ITQAN:v1p165/r4.anchor: بسند صحيح عن سويد بن غفلة قال قال علي لا تقولوا في عثمان إلا خيرا فوالله ما فعل الذي فعل في المصاحف إلا عن ملأ منا

ITQAN:v1p165/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r5.speaker: ابن التين
ITQAN:v1p165/r5.claim: Ibn al-Tin and others distinguish Abu Bakr’s collection, which guarded against loss by placing the Quran’s dispersed material in ordered sheets, from Uthman’s codex, which addressed escalating reading disputes.
ITQAN:v1p165/r5.anchor: الفرق بين جمع أبي بكر وجمع عثمان أن جمع أبي بكر كان لخشية أن يذهب من القرآن شيء

ITQAN:v1p165/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p165/r6.speaker: ابن التين
ITQAN:v1p165/r6.claim: Uthman copied the sheets into a single surah-ordered codex using Quraysh speech, because the initial allowance of other dialects had eased hardship and was no longer needed.
ITQAN:v1p165/r6.anchor: فنسخ تلك الصحف في مصحف واحد مرتبا لسوره واقتصر من سائر اللغات على لغة قريش

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r1.speaker: محققي أهل السنة
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r1.claim: Quranic content, location, and order must all be transmitted mutawatir; the central miracle and ordinary conditions make detailed mass transmission inevitable, so isolated reports cannot establish Quran.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r1.anchor: وأما في محله ووضعه وترتيبه فكذلك عند محققي أهل السنة للقطع بأن العادة تقضي بالتواتر

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r2.speaker: كثير من الأصوليين
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r2.claim: Many legal theorists require tawatur for the Quran’s wording but allow solitary transmission for its placement and ordering; they cite al-Shafi'i’s establishment of the basmala at each surah.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r2.anchor: وذهب كثير من الأصوليين إلى أن التواتر شرط في ثبوت ما هو من القرآن بحسب أصله وليس بشرط في محله

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r4.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr says some jurists and theologians would establish Quranic status as a legal ruling, but not certainty, from an isolated report; the orthodox reject this.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r4.anchor: ذهب قوم من الفقهاء والمتكلمين إلى إثبات قرآن حكما لا علما بخبر الواحد دون الاستفاضة

ITQAN:v1p209#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r5.speaker: قوم من المتكلمين
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r5.claim: Some theologians allow reasoned establishment of readings and letter-forms if linguistically sound even without proof the Prophet recited them; the orthodox reject and condemn this view.
ITQAN:v1p209#2/r5.anchor: وقال قوم من المتكلمين إنه يسوغ إعمال الرأي والاجتهاد في إثبات قراءة وأوجه وأحرف

ITQAN:v3p187/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p187/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p187/r1.claim: One explanation takes the dual phrase as covering two or more by naming the minimum; the better analysis makes the pronoun refer back to the two witnesses already mentioned without qualification.
ITQAN:v3p187/r1.anchor: وقيل أراد ( فإن كانتا اثنتين فصاعدا ) فعبر بالأدنى عنه وعما فوقه إكتفاء ونظيره

ITQAN:v3p187/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p187/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p187/r2.claim: The phrase about a bird flying with its wings reinforces literal bird and flight, since bird can be metaphorical and flying can mean running quickly.
ITQAN:v3p187/r2.anchor: فقوله ( يطير ) لتأكيد أن المراد بالطائر حقيقته فقد يطلق مجازا على غيره وقوله ( بجناحيه )

ITQAN:v3p187/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p187/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p187/r3.claim: “They say with their mouths” reinforces literal speech, since saying can also describe inward thought.
ITQAN:v3p187/r3.anchor: ونظيره ﴿ يقولون بألسنتهم ﴾ لأن القول يطلق مجازا على غير اللسان

ITQAN:v3p187/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p187/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p187/r4.claim: “Hearts that are in the chests” specifies literal hearts because heart can metaphorically mean eye; likewise eyes may metaphorically refer to hearts.
ITQAN:v3p187/r4.anchor: لأن القلب قد يطلق مجازا على العين كما أطلقت العين مجازا على القلب

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r1.claim: The wāw of oath governs genitive, as in “By God, our Lord, we were not polytheists.”
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r1.anchor: فالجارة واو القسم نحو ﴿ والله ربنا ما كنا مشركين ﴾

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r2.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r2.claim: Some grammarians treat wāw as an accusative particle for a comitative object, as in “gather your affair and your partners”; the Quran has no other example.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r2.anchor: والناصبة واو مع فتنصب المفعول معه في رأي قوم نحو

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r3.speaker: الكوفيون
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r3.claim: Kufan grammarians say a present verb after negation or a request may be governed by wāw, including these examples.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r3.anchor: والمضارع في جواب النفي أو الطلب عند الكوفيين نحو

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r4.speaker: الكوفيون
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r4.claim: The Kufans also posit a wāw of redirection, which shifts a verb from its expected case to accusative, as in one reading of the angels’ question.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r4.anchor: واو الصرف عندهم ومعناها أن الفعل كان يقتضي إعرابا فصرفته عنه إلى النصب

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r5.claim: Conjunction wāw merely joins items and can connect accompanying, preceding, or following elements without itself specifying sequence.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r5.anchor: وهي لمطلق الجمع فتعطف الشيء على مصاحبه نحو ﴿ فأنجيناه وأصحاب السفينة ﴾

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r6.claim: Unlike other conjunctions, wāw occurs with إما, with لا after negation, and with لكن; it can also join a general and its specific, the reverse, synonyms, or coordinated genitives by proximity.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r6.anchor: وتفارق سائر حروف العطف في اقترانها بإما نحو ﴿ إما شاكرا وإما كفورا ﴾

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r8.speaker: الخارزنجي
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r8.claim: Al-Khwarizmi reads wāw before subjunctive verbs as causal.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r8.anchor: وللتعليل وحمل عليه الخارزنجي الواو الداخلة على الأفعال المنصوبة

ITQAN:v2p523#4/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r9.claim: The resumptive wāw introduces an independent clause in examples including “fear God, and God teaches you”; if it coordinated verbs, the case of نقر and the following verbs would change.
ITQAN:v2p523#4/r9.anchor: ثانيها واو الاستئناف نحو ﴿ ثم قضى أجلا وأجل مسمى عنده ﴾ ﴿ لنبين لكم ونقر في الأرحام

ITQAN:v3p194/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.claim: Repeating the explicit name can signal exaltation; al-Baqara 2:282 exemplifies this through repeated mention of Allah.
ITQAN:v3p194/r2.anchor: ومنها قصد التعظيم نحو ﴿ واتقوا الله ويعلمكم الله والله بكل شيء عليم ﴾

ITQAN:v4p428/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p428/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p428/r7.claim: The debt verse is hopeful because God guides people in worldly interests down to writing out debts, large or small, showing His great care and grounds for hoping in His forgiveness.
ITQAN:v4p428/r7.anchor: الخامس عشر آية الدين ووجهه أن الله أرشد عباده

ITQAN:v1p69/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p69/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v1p69/r3.claim: A report in al-Mustadrak has the Prophet answer a question about kalālah by citing the summer verse; revelation during the Farewell Pilgrimage is classified as summer, including the start of al-Māʾidah, ‘Today I perfected,’ the debt verse, and al-Naṣr.
ITQAN:v1p69/r3.anchor: وفي المستدرك عن أبي هريرة أن رجلا قال يا رسول الله ما الكلالة قال أما سمعت الآية التي نزلت في الصيف

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r1.claim: In the travel poem, أطراف suggests both varied strands of conversation and the allusive gestures of companions; it conveys their lively ease, friendship, and pleasure on the journey home.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r1.anchor: ثم دل بلفظه الأطراف على الصفة التي يختص بها الرفاق في السفر من التصرف في فنون القول وشجون الحديث

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r2.claim: The poet says the camels' necks because speed and slowness show especially in their necks and heads, whose movement reveals their spirited gait.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r2.anchor: ثم قال بأعناق المطى ولم يقل بالمطي لأن السرعة والبطء يظهران غالبا في أعناقها

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r3.claim: Poetic excellence cannot be assigned to isolated words: unlike a jewel's intrinsic beauty, the relevant analogy is meanings enhancing one another through composition and relation.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p17/r3.anchor: بل حق هذا المثل أن يوضع في نصرة بعض المعاني الحكمية والتشبيهية بعضا وازدياد الحسن منها بأن يجامع شكل منها شكلا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r1.claim: Jurjānī endorses al-Āmidī’s view that rain's fashioning and weaving of plants is literal, not metaphor; al-Āmidī praises al-Buḥturī's phrasing and calls Abū Tammām's explicit weaver comparison ugly.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r1.anchor: اعلم أن هذا الاستدلال كأحسن ما يكون إلا أن الفائدة تتم بأن تبين جهته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r2.claim: Jurjānī explains that explicit simile names both subjects, while implicit simile transfers the comparison's name to its subject; the same distinction lets actions be compared explicitly or called swimming and flight metaphorically.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r2.anchor: والقول فيه أن التشبيه كما لا يخفى يقتضي شيئين مشبها ومشبها به ثم ينقسم إلى الصريح وغير الصريح

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r3.claim: In the Abū Dulāma example, Jurjānī maps each mule leg's unstable or curved movement to a specific hand motion in kneading or baking dough.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p329/r3.anchor: أرى الشهباء تعجن إذ غدونا برجليها وتخبز باليمين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p227/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p227/r1.claim: Although tamthīl, simile, and metaphor are only three labels, explaining their divisions and fine distinctions requires extensive reading and thought; Jurjānī defends that detailed inquiry against dismissive critics.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p227/r1.anchor: ولئن كان الذي يتكلف شرحه لا يزيد على مؤدي ثلاثة أسماء وهي التمثيل والتشبيه والاستعارة فإن ذلك يستدعي جملا من القول

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r1.speaker: معترض
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r1.claim: An interlocutor objects that calling a brave man a lion does not transfer the word outside its meaning, since the intended comparison is courage, already associated with lions.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r1.anchor: فإن قلت لا أسلم أنه جرى على شئ لم يوضع له في اللغة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r2.claim: Jurjānī replies that lion includes bodily shape and visible traits as well as courage; applying its name to a man strips away those literal traits and transfers the name by an imagined likeness.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r2.anchor: فأنا وإن كنا لم ندل به على معنى لم يتضمنه اسم الأسد في أصل وضعه فقد سلبناه بعض ما وضع له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r3.claim: By contrast, attributing an action to spring is literal: the language predicates an act without asserting anything about the subject's nature, so no part of the word's meaning is displaced.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p359/r3.anchor: لإثبات الفعل للشيء من غير أن يتعرض لذلك الشيء ما هو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r1.claim: ‘You are the beloved’ presents love as a whole genus confined to one person, implying the speaker loves no one else; ‘Zayd, the one departing’ identifies a single known departure instead.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r1.anchor: ألا ترى أنك قد أعطيت بقولك : أنت الحبيب ، أنك لا تحب غيره

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r2.claim: Adding a habitual quality, as in ‘Zayd who goes about your need’, makes the description generic and restores the genus-like sense found in ‘you are the beloved’.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r2.anchor: زيد المنطلق في حاجتك ، تريد الذي من شأنه أن يسعى في حاجتك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r3.claim: A class noun becomes a distinct type when qualified; this applies both to ordinary nouns and to verbal nouns such as knowledge, striking, travel, and standing.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r3.anchor: من شأن أسماء الأجناس كلها إذا وصفت أن تتنوع بالصفة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r4.claim: A verbal noun also divides into types through its complement: striking with a sword differs from striking with a stick, despite sharing the name ‘striking’.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p153/r4.anchor: وهو أن من شأن المصدر أن يفرق بالصلات ، كما يفرق بالصفات

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r1.claim: Coordinated clauses need related subjects and reports; pairing Abu al-Husayn’s generosity with the bitterness of separation is jarring because the ideas have no connection.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r1.anchor: وذلك لأنه لا مناسبة بين كرم أبي الحسين ومرارة النوى ، ولا تعلق لأحدهما بالآخر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r2.claim: When clauses concern one person, the conjunction clearly asserts both actions together; without it, the second statement could retract the first.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r2.anchor: كنت قد أفدت بالواو أنك أوجبت له الفعلين جميعا ، وجعلته يفعلهما معا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r3.claim: Coordination inside a relative or similarly linked construction tightens the pairing further, so the actions cannot sensibly be understood apart.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p176/r3.anchor: في الصلة ازداد الاشتباك والاقتران حتى لا يتصور تقدير إفراد في أحدهما عن الآخر

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r1.claim: With ‘not ... except’, placing the predicate after the subject restricts the predicate to that subject, while placing the predicate first restricts the subject to those bearing that predicate.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r1.anchor: فقد قصرت في الأول الصفة على الموصوف ، وفي الثاني الموصوف على الصفة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r2.claim: ‘Zayd is nothing but standing’ excludes incompatible states such as sitting, but does not exclude unrelated qualities such as being tall, white, or learned; ‘no one is standing but Zayd’ is context-bound.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r2.anchor: لم نرد أنك نفيت ما ليس من القيام بسبيل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r3.claim: The restriction denies that another, incompatible state replaces the named one, rather than denying all accompanying attributes; unlike ‘innamā’, ‘mā ... illā’ already excludes every contrary state.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p263/r3.anchor: ليس المعنى على نفي الشركة ، ولكن على نفي أن لا يكون المذكور

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r1.claim: A parable’s purpose is inferred from the combined sense, not from literal words: a ruler’s image of advancing one foot and drawing back the other means wavering over whether to pledge allegiance.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r1.anchor: وأنه لم يعرف ذلك من لفظ التقديم والتأخير ، أو من لفظ الرجل ، ولكن بأن علم أنه لا معنى

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r2.claim: The Prophet’s ‘green plants of dung heaps’ figures a beautiful woman of poor upbringing, just as ‘much ash in the pot’ figures generous hospitality; the inferred meaning, not the phrase, is the parable.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p321/r2.anchor: ضرب عليه السلام خضراء الدمن مثلا للمرأة الحسناء في منبت السوء

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r1.claim: The source of eloquence and inimitability is the arrangement of meanings, not the order of bare words; a word-focused account of the Qur’an’s merit collapses.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r1.anchor: لم يكن المطلوب أبدا إلا ترتيب المعاني

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r2.claim: Fasāḥa is attributed to a word because it names the quality by which that word signals rhetorical merit; the meaning itself is not directly described as eloquent.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r2.anchor: إنما اختصت الفصاحة باللفظ ، وكانت من صفته من حيث كانت عبارة عن كون اللفظ على وصف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r3.claim: Older critics’ ‘noble’ or ‘restless’ word is shorthand for semantic fit with neighboring meanings: wording is called settled or awkward because of what it conveys in the composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p64/r3.anchor: كقولهم : ' لفظ متمكن ' ؛ يريدون أنه بموافقة معناه لمعنى ما يليه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r1.claim: A word is not eloquent in isolation: the same word can be excellent in one context and ordinary elsewhere because its merit appears only after it enters a composition.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r1.anchor: المزية التي من أجلها نصف اللفظ في شأننا هذا بأنه فصيح ، مزية تحدث من بعد أن لا تكون

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r2.claim: Though ordinary usage calls words eloquent rather than meanings, the claim that eloquence lies in meaning means that the merit behind an eloquent word ultimately returns to its meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r2.anchor: إن غرضنا من قولنا : إن الفصاحة تكون في المعنى ، أن المزية التي من أجلها استحق اللفظ الوصف بأنه فصيح ، عائدة في الحقيقة إلى معناه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r3.claim: Since a speaker cannot alter linguistic words or add a new formal quality to them, while eloquence is the speaker’s achievement, the merit must be in meaning.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p297/r3.anchor: الفصاحة فيما نحن فيه عبارة عن مزية هي بالمتكلم البتة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r1.claim: Jurjānī says scholars agree that nazm is indispensable to eloquent speech; without it, unusual meanings alone confer no rank or completeness.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r1.anchor: قد علمت إطباق العلماء على تعظيم شأن النظم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r2.claim: Nazm means arranging speech as grammar requires, following its rules and distinctions rather than merely placing words in sequence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r2.anchor: ليس النظم إلا أن تضع كلامك الوضع الذي يقتضيه علم النحو

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r3.claim: The composer must consider the different forms available within each grammatical category, such as alternative word orders and predicate forms.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p76/r3.anchor: فينظر في الخبر إلى الوجوه التي تراها في قولك

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r1.speaker: القائلون
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r1.claim: Critics argue that one meaning can be expressed in two ways, one eloquent and one not; this would give words an independent share in excellence.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r1.anchor: العقلاء قد اتفقوا على أنه يصح أن يعبر عن المعنى الواحد بلفظين

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r2.claim: If the comparison concerns synonymous individual words, it misses the issue: Jurjānī is discussing eloquence produced by composition, not isolated vocabulary.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r2.anchor: كلامنا نحن في فصاحة تحدث من بعد التأليف دون الفصاحة التي توصف بها اللفظة مفردة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r3.claim: If it concerns whole expressions, the same basic meaning can be plain or artistically fashioned, like a simple piece of jewelry versus an expertly crafted one.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p310/r3.anchor: سبيل المعاني أن ترى الواحد منها غفلا ساذجا عاميا موجودا في كلام الناس كلهم

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r1.claim: The commonplace thought that nature cannot change becomes newly striking in al-Mutanabbī’s line, where nature resists being carried away.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r1.anchor: يراد من القلب نسيانكم وتأبى الطباع على الناقل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r2.claim: An eloquent expression improves and adorns a shared underlying meaning, giving it a distinctive image that a plain paraphrase lacks.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r2.anchor: إنه يصح أن تكون هاهنا عبارتان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r3.claim: If a critic admits the added beauty in the poetic examples, the excellence lies in the newly shaped meaning, not in the letters’ sound; denying it makes discussion futile.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p311/r3.anchor: ليس لله بمستنكر أن يجمع العالم في واحد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r1.claim: Composed speech is built from grammatical relations, chiefly a noun with its predicate or a verb with its subject; further syntax adds qualifications or extensions.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r1.anchor: تفسير ذلك أن الأصل مبتدأ تلقى له خبرا من بعد تثنيه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r2.claim: The poem challenges anyone who reduces nazm to shared grammar to explain how that account can establish the Qur’an’s unmatched inimitability.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p18/r2.anchor: فما الذي زاد في هذا الذي عرفوا حتى غدا العجز يهمي سيل واديه

KHATTABI:v1p67/r1.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p67/r1.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p67/r1.claim: The elephant parody raises grand expectations but then dwells only on trunk and tail, omitting the creature’s intelligence, obedience, tusks, ears, and intricate design.
KHATTABI:v1p67/r1.anchor: وإذ قد دلك فيالة رأيك وسوء اختيارك على معارضة القرآن العظيم بذكر الفيل وأوصافه , فهلا أتيت منها

KHATTABI:v1p67/r2.author: al-Khaṭṭābī
KHATTABI:v1p67/r2.speaker: author
KHATTABI:v1p67/r2.claim: Analogy is judged by shared meanings rather than physical size: elephant and mosquito share animal functions and head and trunk features, while the mosquito’s wings offset its small body.
KHATTABI:v1p67/r2.anchor: مدار الحكم في باب التشبيه والتمثيل على المعاني دون الأعيان والأجسام , والبعوض حيوان من أوجه كالفيل

DAMGHANI:v1p359/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r1.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r1.claim: Fusūq can mean a sin or offense that falls upon those who violate the instruction.
DAMGHANI:v1p359/r1.anchor: ولا يضار كاتب ولا شهيد وان لم تفعلوا فانه فسوق بكم يعني مأثما يحل عليكم

DAMGHANI:v1p139/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p139/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p139/r7.claim: Ḥaqq can mean money or a financial debt owed by one party to another.
DAMGHANI:v1p139/r7.anchor: " وليملل الذي عليه الحق " يعني المال كقوله تعالى ( فيها ) " فإن كان الذي عليه الحق سفيها أو ضعيفا " يعني المال

DAMGHANI:v1p266/r20.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r20.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r20.claim: Shahīd can mean a person who testifies to the truth in people's legal rights.
DAMGHANI:v1p266/r20.anchor: وأشهدوا شهيدين من رجالكم كقوله تعالى في سورة الطلاق

DAMGHANI:v1p431/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r10.claim: The two women witnesses are unidentified women, not a named individual or pair.
DAMGHANI:v1p431/r10.anchor: الثانى عشر : المراة المجهولة . قوله تعالى فى سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p175/r1.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r1.speaker: الأعرابي
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r1.claim: A Bedouin used the phrase دعاك الله to mean that God punished you; this is a detached lexical fragment in the segment.
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r1.anchor: قال الأعرابي : دعاك الله أي عذبك الله

DAMGHANI:v1p175/r2.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r2.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r2.claim: Adnā means more likely or more fitting: documenting a debt makes doubt less likely and testimony more reliable.
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r2.anchor: فوجه منها : أدنى يعني أجدر قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

DAMGHANI:v1p134/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p134/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p134/r12.claim: Ḥāḍirah means a current, immediate transaction conducted between the parties.
DAMGHANI:v1p134/r12.anchor: الرابع : حاضر بمعنى حال قوله تعالى في سورة البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r1.claim: Al-Dīn is what a person undertakes; religious commitment means undertaking what God requires.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الدين : ما التزمه الإنسان :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r2.speaker: غيره
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r2.claim: Another definition makes religion divine speech that disciplines the self and restrains natural impulses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r2.anchor: وحده غيره فقال : الدين قول إلهي رادع للنفس يقومها

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r3.claim: Dīn can mean dominion: to dāna a people is to subdue them, and they then submit.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r3.anchor: والدين يقال ويراد به : الملكة والسلطان . يقال : دنت القوم

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba derives God’s dīn from this sense of domination and submission.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r4.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة : والدين لله إنما هو من هذا .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r5.speaker: القطامي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r5.claim: Al-Quṭāmī’s line uses tadīnuka for making someone submissive.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r5.anchor: قال القطامي : - كانت نوار تدينك الأديانا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r6.claim: A second cited line also uses dīn for an authority or condition of subjugation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r6.anchor: وأنشدوا من ذلك أيضا : - لئن حللت بجو في بني أسد

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r8.claim: Dīn can mean worship, as shown by a poem asking whether this is always his and the speaker’s religion.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r8.anchor: والدين يقال ويراد به العبادة وأنشدوا من ذلك : -

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r9.claim: Dāyana means transacting by extending a loan; adāna means borrowing on debt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p295/r9.anchor: وتقول : داينت الرجل إذا عاملته فأعطيته دينا وأدنت إذا أخذت بدين

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r1.claim: Shahīd means witness, related to shāhid as ʿalīm is related to ʿālim, and derives from witnessing.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r1.anchor: الشهيد : يقال ويراد به : الشاهد . يقال : شاهد وشهيد .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r2.claim: Testimony is reporting what one has witnessed; mashhad is a place where people gather.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r2.anchor: والشهادة : الإخبار بما شوهد والمشهد محضر الناس .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r8.claim: Shahīd can mean a witness testifying truth against the person testified against, including debt witnesses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p377/r8.anchor: والرابع : الشاهد بالحق على المشهود عليه . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r2.claim: Ḥaqq can mean money or property owed as a debt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p267/r2.anchor: والسابع : المال ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r1.claim: Al-marʾa means an adult female descendant of Adam; al-marʾ means a man.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r1.anchor: المرأة : اسم للأنثى البالغة من أولاد آدم والرجل : المرء .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r14.claim: Some add an unidentified woman, as in the debt testimony formula of one man and two women.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p571/r14.anchor: والثالث : امرأة مجهولة . ومنه قوله تعالى [ في البقرة ] :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r1.speaker: علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r1.claim: Adnā is the elative form of d-n-w, meaning nearness or proximity.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : أدنى . أفعل ، من الدنو ، وهو القرب .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r2.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r2.claim: Ibn Fāris distinguishes hamzated danīʾ, meaning low or inferior, from unhamzated danī, meaning near.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r2.anchor: قال ابن فارس : الدنيء من الرجال مهموز : الدون . والدني غير مهموز : القريب

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r3.speaker: ابن فارس
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r3.claim: Ibn Fāris says the world is called al-dunyā because it is near, and gives dunyāwī as its relative form.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r3.anchor: وسميت الدنيا : لدنوها . والنسبة إليها دنياوي .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r4.claim: Dānaytu bayna al-amrayn means bringing two matters close together; the hadith’s danū means eat what is nearest.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r4.anchor: ودانيت بين الأمرين : قاربت بينهما ( وفي الحديث ) : ( إذا أكلتم فدنوا

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r5.claim: In the debt verse, adnā means more likely or more conducive to avoiding doubt.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r5.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن أدنى في القرآن على أربعة أوجه : - أحدها : بمعنى أجدر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r1.claim: Bayʿ is exchanging one item of property for another under specified terms.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r1.anchor: البيع : استبدال مال بمال على صفة مخصوصة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r2.claim: In Arabic, bayʿ may also mean buying; the cited line says to buy a cloak for a shepherd.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r2.anchor: وربما سمي الشراء بيعا عند العرب . وأنشدوا :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r4.claim: One reported Qurʾānic sense of bayʿ is a contract of exchange.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p194/r4.anchor: وذكر أهل التفسير أن البيع في القرآن على ثلاثة أوجه : - أحدها : عقد المعاوضة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r1.claim: Ḥuḍūr is the opposite of absence; ḥaḍar contrasts with the open countryside, and ḥaḍāra means settled urban life.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r1.anchor: الحضور : ضد الغيبة . والحضر : ضد البدو . والحضارة : سكون الحضر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r2.claim: Abū Zayd pronounces ḥaḍāra with a kasra on the ḥāʾ.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r3.speaker: الأصمعي
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r3.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī pronounces ḥaḍāra with a fatḥa; a cited line illustrates the word.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r3.anchor: والأصمعي : بفتحها ، وأنشدوا : فمن تكن الحضارة أعجبته

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r4.claim: With ḍamma, ḥuḍur means an enemy.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r5.claim: With fatḥa, ḥaḍar means a fortress; ʿAdī’s line supplies the usage.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r5.anchor: والحضر : بفتحها حصن في قول عدي : - وأخو الحضر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r9.claim: Ḥuḍūr can mean something immediately available or present, as with a spot transaction.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p263/r9.anchor: والرابع : الحلول ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة :

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r1.speaker: أكثر العلماء
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r1.claim: Most scholars treat the relevant ruling in Surat al-Ma'ida as decisive and unrepealed because that sura was the last revealed.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r1.anchor: وأكثر العلماء يذهب إلى أن هذا باب من الحكم (محكم)

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r2.claim: Some hold that the relevant ruling in al-Ma'ida was abrogated by the testimony rule of two men or one man and two women.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p221/r2.anchor: وبعضهم يذهب إلى أنه منسوخ بقوله سبحانه:

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r2.claim: Ḍalāl can mean forgetting: the forgetful person turns away from a matter and its recollection.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p254/r2.anchor: والضلال: النسيان. والناسي للشيء عادل عنه وعن ذكره

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r1.claim: The passage condemns people who relabel falsehood, degradation, shamelessness, error, and unbelief as utility, instinct, freedom, reason, and science, then call themselves scholars and reformers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r1.anchor: فخذ منه الكذب فى فلسفة المنفعة، والتسفلَ فى شفاعة الغريزة، والوقاحة فى زعم الحرية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r2.claim: A teacher may wear a turban and claim religious standing while carrying a destructive scientific ideology into the young; the reader should not be deceived by appearances.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r2.anchor: أيها القارئ فلا يغرنك منهم من يلبس العمامة ويتسم بسمة الشرع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r3.claim: The passage depicts such a teacher as parasitic and socially destructive, weakening life and strength and leaving illness, harm, or constriction wherever he acts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r3.anchor: كان هذا المعلم أخزاه الله كان دودة فى قبر ثم نفخه الله إنسانا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r4.claim: The author says scholars unfairly burden the Qur'an with every scientific objection and shun it, like aircraft deluded by rising into the sky and mounting a campaign toward the sun.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p32/r4.anchor: على إنك ترى أصحابنا العلماء لا يتحاملون على شىء، ما يتحاملون على القرآن الكريم.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r1.claim: Sadd means a barrier or protection; sadad shifts to uprightness and sound guidance in speech, action, and affairs, while adl usually concerns judgments and opposes injustice.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r1.anchor: والسدُّ: الحاجز المانع أو الواقي. ونُقل إلى السداد بمعنى الاستقامة، والسداد التوفيق إلى الصواب من القول والعمل والأمر، على حين يغلب اختصاص العدل بالأحكام

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r2.claim: Qur'anic contexts use adl for equality, compensation, and justice in judgment, arbitration, and testimony, supporting its broad semantic range and frequent legal use.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r2.anchor: ويبدو الفقر الدقيق بين سديد وعدل، إذا تدبرنا الاستعمال القرآني للعدل. فيهدينا سياق آياته، إلى معنى المساواة في مثل آيات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r3.claim: The author concludes that sadad is narrower, chiefly denoting soundness and reform in speech or opinion, whereas adl is broader and most often appears in legal contexts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p459/r3.anchor: فلعل السداد أخص بالقول والرآي، صوابا وإصلاحاً. ودلالة العدل أعم، مع غلبة مجيئها في الأحكام، والله أعلم.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r1.speaker: القاموس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r1.claim: Al-Qamus glosses sa'ima as becoming bored or weary, providing the basic meaning behind the command not to tire of recording debts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r1.anchor: قال في (القاموس) : سئم الشيء ومنه، كفرح.. ملَّ فهو سئوم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r2.speaker: ابن الأثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r2.claim: Ibn al-Athir explains the prophetic phrase Allah does not become weary until you do as meaning that He does not tire as you tire.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r2.anchor: وكذلك فسره "ابن الأثير" بالملل في حديث: "إن الله لا يسأم حتى تسأموا"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r3.claim: Al-Raghib sharpens the sense to weariness from repetition or prolonged duration, citing Qur'anic usage and Zuhayr's poem about life's burdens.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r3.anchor: الراغب فقال إنها: الملالة مما يتكرر ويكثُر لبثُه، فعلاً أو انفعالاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas's gloss of sa'ama as lassitude describes a result or outward sign of weariness, rather than a separate basic meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p448/r4.anchor: وأما الفتور فيما نُقل عن ابن عباس في تفسير الكلمة، فيأتي نتيجة للسآمة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Nafi ibn al-Azraq that his answers are not conjecture but knowledge God taught him.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r1.anchor: لا والله، ما هذا مني تخرصا لكنه علم علمنيه الله.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the most brazen person either someone who speaks without knowledge or someone who conceals knowledge God gave him.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r2.anchor: رجل تكلم بما لا علم له به، أو رجل كتم الناس علماً علمه الله - عز وجل -.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r3.speaker: نجدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r3.claim: Najda says they want Ibn Abbas to explain Qur'anic questions with Arabic evidence because God revealed the Qur'an in clear Arabic.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r3.anchor: وقال نجدة: فإنا نريد أن نسألك عن أشياء من كتاب الله - عز وجل - فتفسره لنا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas invites them to ask whatever they wish; this transmission preserves 255 questions and closes with the completion of Ibn al-Azraq's questions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p303/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سلاني عما بدا لكما تجدا علمه عندي حاضرا إن شاء الله تعالى.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r1.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r1.claim: Al-Razi recast Jurjani's theory in a better order and style, while acknowledging that Jurjani established its principles and rules but left the topics poorly arranged and wrote at great length.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r1.anchor: كالفخر الرازي الذي ألف كتابه (نهاية الإيجاز في دراية الإعجاز) فاعترف بأن الجرجاني كان الذي استخرج أصول هذا العلم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r2.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع المصري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r2.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isba's Badi al-Qur'an organized rhetoric into 120 chapters seeking Qur'anic examples, but usually named a device and supplied examples without explaining their rhetorical force.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r2.anchor: كصنيع ابن أبي الإصبع المصري (ت 654 هـ) الذي نسق كتابه (بديع القرآن) - والبديع عنده بمعنى البلاغة - في مائة وعشرين باباً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r3.speaker: السكاكي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r3.claim: Al-Sakkaki made rhetoric in Miftah al-Ulum an autonomous, rule-bound craft, separating it from the question of inimitability and from the syntactic meanings Jurjani had included in nazm.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r3.anchor: وإمام هذه المدرسة هو "السكاكي" - ت 626 هـ - الذي جعل البلاغة في (مفتاح العلوم) علماً يُحَّصل

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r4.claim: Later rhetoric concentrated on formal taxonomies of simile, metaphor, figurative language, metonymy, and embellishment, while Qur'anic examples were sparse beside examples from human speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p129/r4.anchor: ثم كان الجهد، كل الجهد، موجهاً إلى العناية بإجراء الصنعة البلاغية التي تتعلق في التشبيه مثلاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r1.claim: The passage rejects calling Qur'anic endings saj' merely because they resemble rhyme: saj' subordinates wording to rhyme, whereas Qur'anic wording follows the meaning.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r1.anchor: لأن السجع يتبع المعنى فيه اللفظَ الذي يؤدى السجع، وليس كذلك ما اتفق مما هو في تقدير السجع من القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r2.claim: Even if occasional Qur'anic endings are conceded as pauses or verbal ornaments, their incidental, unintended occurrence does not make the discourse saj'.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r2.anchor: فإن ذلك إذا اعترض الخطاب لم يُعد سجعاً، على ما قد بَيَّنا في القليل من الشعر كالبيت الواحد

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r3.claim: Calling the Qur'an saj' would make it blameworthy by ordinary standards because saj' requires regular measures and a fixed pattern, unlike uneven Qur'anic endings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p255/r3.anchor: ويقال لهم: لو كان الذي في القرآن، على ما تقدرونه، سجعاً لكان مذموماً مرذولاً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r1.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r1.claim: A theologian's argument says either the Qur'an is inherently beyond human imitation, or people could imitate it but were prevented from doing so, making their failure miraculous.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r1.anchor: وقد قرر بعض المتكلمين الإعجاز بطريق يشمل قول أهل السنة، وقول المعتزلة في الصرفة، فقال: إن كان القرآن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r2.speaker: ابن كثير
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir finds the diversion argument unsatisfactory because the Qur'an is inherently miraculous, though useful as a concessive argument in debate.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r2.anchor: نقله "ابن كثير" ورأى أن هذه الطريقة إنما تصلح على سبيل التنزل والمجادلة، لكنها غير مرضية

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r3.speaker: الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r3.claim: Al-Razi uses this argument in his tafsir to explain the miraculousness of short suras such as al-Asr and al-Kawthar.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r3.anchor: وبهذه الطريقة أجاب الرازي في تفسيره عن سؤاله في السور القصار كالعصر وإنا أعطيناك الكوثر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r4.claim: The theoretical debate did not end rhetorical inquiry: later Mu'tazilites treated diversion as one aspect of inimitability, while non-Mu'tazilite surveyors soon focused on rhetorical inimitability.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p89/r4.anchor: والمسألة كما ترى قد عولجت في مجال الجدل النظري وإن آلت بالمعتزلة أنفسهم، بعد الجيل الأول من شيوخهم، إلى أن اعتبار الصرفة وجهاً من وجوه الإعجاز

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r1.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r1.claim: Classical tajdīd meant reviving neglected religious practice in its original form; Khuli instead defines renewal as development that discovers something new through ijtihād.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r1.anchor: يميز الشيخ أمين الخولي بوضوح بين التجديد في مفهوم القدماء ومفهومه المختلف للتجديد

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r2.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r2.claim: Khuli departed from the revivalist reform program associated with al-Tahtawi, al-Afghani, and Muhammad Abduh, which relied on inherited principles to restore earlier glory.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r2.anchor: تجاوز الشيخ أمين الخولي وجهة الإحياء والإصلاح التي بدأت مع الشيخ رفاعة رافع الطهطاوي في القرن التاسع عشر

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r3.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r3.claim: Khuli fashioned a different path for understanding religion and interpreting its texts, beyond inherited foundations and principles.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r3.anchor: استطاع الشيخ أمين الخولي أن يشتق نهْجًا يتلمس في ضوئه دربًا مغايرًا لما عرفناه من أصولٍ ومبادئ موروثةٍ

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r4.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r4.claim: He used evolution to rebuild religious knowledge and Arabic language studies, disrupting traditional linguistic and rhetorical scholarship and opening new horizons in Azhar ethics.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r4.anchor: ظل الخولي مسكونًا بفكرة التطور، واستبدت به هذه الفكرة إلى الحد الذي استند فيه إليها بوصفها مرجعيةً لإعادة بناء المعارف الدينية

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r5.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r5.claim: Khuli defended Darwinian biological evolution, finding comparable hierarchical classifications of beings in the Ikhwan al-Safa, Miskawayh, Avicenna, and Ibn Tufayl.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r5.anchor: لم يتردد الشيخ الخولي في الدفاع عن نظرية التطور الداروِنية في الأحياء، وأصر على منحها مشروعيةً

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r6.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r6.claim: Khuli regarded renewal at the head of each century as a major revolutionary work the community needs, almost a periodic social revolution.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r6.anchor: شغف الخولي بالتجديد إلى الحد الذي كان برأيِه هو الثورة الكبرى في كل قرن

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r7.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r7.claim: He extended evolution across theology, law, language, and all moral, intellectual, social, and spiritual dimensions of human life, treating it as a universal law rather than biology's specialty.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r7.anchor: توسع الخولي في تطبيق فكرة التطور على علم الكلام والفقه واللغة، بل تعميمها لتشمل أبعاد الوجود البشري المعنوية والفكرية والاجتماعية والأخلاقية كافة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r8.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r8.claim: Khuli analogized the emergence of new ideas to biological evolution: social conditions and proponents' conviction help new ideas outcompete old ones until they take root.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r8.anchor: يكتب الخولي: «صار كل باحث يتصدى لدرس شيء من ذلك إنما يتقدم إليه مسلمًا بعمل ناموس النشوء فيه

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r9.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r9.claim: The author sees Khuli's appeal to modern science as a contemporary reformist strategy, but criticizes some thinkers for forcing scientific theories onto the Qur'an until it seems to lack independent content.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r9.anchor: كما تمادى بعضُهم وأسرف في توظيف فرضيات ونظريات وقوانين العلم الجديدة في تفسير القرآن

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r10.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r10.claim: Khuli rejected irrational claims that Arabic is uniquely perfect or complete: like other languages, it is a living social organism whose words die, arise, and develop through use.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r10.anchor: شدد الخولي على أن العربية ليست استثناءً من اللغات البشرية

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r11.claim: Khuli traced the gap between written Classical Arabic and colloquial speech to early lexicographers privileging Bedouin usage and excluding common urban vocabulary.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r11.anchor: وكيف أن المنهج الذي اعتمده المعجميون الأوائل في جمع اللغة تبنى لغة البدو في الصحراء العربية خاصة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r12.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r12.claim: The author reads this account as showing Arabic's inherited Bedouin worldview and limited urban vocabulary; Abbasid Arabic then borrowed and coined terms to cover city life's new realities.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r12.anchor: فعوضت ذلك بالاستيراد من غيرها، واشتقاق وتوليد ألفاظ جديدة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r13.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r13.claim: Khuli held that developing beliefs is possible and now necessary, both because life requires it and to protect religion's continued relevance and compatibility with thought and action.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r13.anchor: لا يتردد الشيخ أمين الخولي في القول بأن «تطور العقائد ممكن، وهو اليوم واجب لحاجة الحياة إليه

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r14.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r14.claim: He urged a new approach to unseen matters, rejecting excessive attribution of phenomena to the unseen and detailed speculation that scientific-minded younger generations cannot absorb.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r14.anchor: في السياق نفسه يدعو الخولي إلى رؤية جديدة في التعاطي مع الغيبيات

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r15.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r15.claim: Khuli read scriptural stories as representations that convey meanings, not historical records; detailed literal claims can clash with modern sensibilities, as in prohibitions of images despite their use in religious teaching.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r15.anchor: يشير الخولي إلى أن القصص تتحدث لغة التمْثيل وليس لغة التاريخ

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r16.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r16.claim: Khuli opposed ahistorical readings of heritage: each tradition is shaped by the particular temporal and spatial conditions of its period and changes as those conditions change.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r16.anchor: يشدد الخولي على رفض أية قراءة لا تاريخية للتراث

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r17.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r17.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r17.claim: Khuli explained changing theological positions on divine essence and attributes, God's speech, predestination, and free will through changes in time, place, and social environment.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r17.anchor: ويحيل الخولي الخلاف بين المتكلمين، وتغير الأقوال وتنوعَها في مسائل: «الذات والصفات، والكلام الإلهي

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r18.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r18.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r18.claim: He applied gradual progression to material and immaterial life alike: forms begin simply, compete, and develop as what is fit survives and becomes more complex.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r18.anchor: يرى أمين الخولي أن «ناموس التدرج والترقي في الكائنات جميعًا، المادي منها والمعنوي على السواء

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r19.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r19.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r19.claim: Khuli described Islamic beliefs as developing from simple early forms to more complex ones as Muslims moved from Bedouin life into civilization and encountered learning and other peoples' thought; he contrasted the clear creed of the salaf with the interpretive creed of later scholars.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r19.anchor: ففي «الإسلام يبدو جليًّا الأخذُ التدريجي للناس في الاعتقاد

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r20.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r20.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r20.claim: The author regards Khuli's position as an early call for a new kalām: an age-responsive effort to interpret and justify belief, protecting faith from extremism and stagnation as well as defending it.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r20.anchor: ودعوتُه هذه من الدعوات المبكرة في دنيا الإسلام لبناءِ «عِلْم كلام جديد»، على وفق التسمية المتداوَلة اليوم

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r21.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r21.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r21.claim: The author interprets Khuli's historicity as the view that ideas resemble and arise from their environments: intellectually fertile settings generate complex thought, while poorer settings produce simpler ideas.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r21.anchor: كأن الشيخ الخولي هنا يستعير مفهوم «التاريخية» من الفلسفة والعلوم الإنسانية الحديثة، ليطبقه على مجالاتِ التراث المتنوعة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r22.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r22.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r22.claim: Khuli insisted that renewal begins by thoroughly understanding the old and changing our role from guarding and sanctifying heritage to studying it critically.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r22.anchor: وهو في كل ذلك يصر على ضرورة دراسة التراث والتبصر بمسالكه المتنوعة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r23.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r23.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r23.claim: The author reads Khuli's 'killing' of the old as discernment, not destruction: identify inert inherited elements and understand how their concepts and questions restrict present life and future movement.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r23.anchor: معنى القتل هنا ليس التدمير والإبادة، إنما هو اكتشاف العناصر الميتة في التراث

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r24.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r24.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r24.claim: Khuli allowed renewal to find new insight by drawing on existing old material, as well as by independent reasoning that produces something previously unknown.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r24.anchor: إذ يفسره على أنه: «اهتداء إلى جديد كان بعد أن لم يكن، سواء أكان الاهتداء إلى هذا الجديد بطريق الأخذ من قديم كان موجودًا

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r25.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r25.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r25.claim: The author says Khuli sought to breathe new life into old material after accreted misunderstanding had hardened it; he did not advocate discarding the entire past.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r25.anchor: أَولًا: تحيين ما هو قديم ببعث روح جديدةٍ فيه، بعد أن تحجر مما تراكم عليه من الماضي

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r26.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r26.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r26.claim: Khuli differed from reformers who repackaged old content in new forms and treated heritage as an exhaustive storehouse; he called for genuinely novel work.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r26.anchor: وهذا ما يمتاز به هو عن جماعةٍ من المصلحين في عصره

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r27.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r27.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r27.claim: Khuli made evolution comprehensive across fundamentals, beliefs, worship, and transactions, extending reform beyond the commonly accepted scope of legal dealings; the author says including worship may be his distinctive position.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r27.anchor: استيعاب وشمول التطور بوصفه «سنة شاملة في: الأصول والعقائد والعبادات والمعاملات»

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r28.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r28.speaker: author
