RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r28.claim: The author notes that worship is conventionally treated as fixed by revelation, unlike transactions, but Khuli still urged reconsidering legal and theological works in light of changing realities.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r28.anchor: ذلك أن المعروف أن أحكام العبادات توقيفية، لا تتغير أو تتبدل أو تتطور

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r29.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r29.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r29.claim: Khuli argued that new events absent from old fiqh books cannot halt the world's course; rigidity risks alienating ordinary people from a religion unable to address their lives.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r29.anchor: ذلك ما أشار إليه بقوله: «إن الناس تحدث لهم باختلاف الزمان أمور ووقائع لم يرد لها ذكر في كتب الفقه القديمة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r30.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r30.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r30.claim: In a discussion with the Shaykh al-Azhar, Khuli rejected restricting change to a few worship rulings and said Islamic law selects what is easier to practice and best suited to endure.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r30.anchor: رفض الشيخ الخولي انحصارَ التطور ببعض أحكام العبادات

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r31.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r31.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r31.claim: Khuli raised whether worshippers could follow congregational Friday and festival prayers through televised broadcasts, seeing and hearing the imam when local mosques are crowded.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r31.anchor: إذ يقول: «وماذا يكون الرأي في حكم الاقتداء بالأجهزة المتطورة التي تُذاع بها الصلوات الجامعة من جمعة وعيد

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r32.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r32.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r32.claim: For Khuli, transactions turn on public benefit wherever it exists; evolving the presentation of beliefs, worship, and transactions should keep religious life connected to ordinary life.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r32.anchor: وأحكام المعاملات عند الشيخ الخولي تدور مدارَ المصلحة

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r33.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r33.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r33.claim: The author says Khuli did not fully explain the basis or applications of evolving worship rulings and cautiously reads him as seeking easier performance of obligations through a broader use of hardship relief and secondary rulings.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r33.anchor: ولا أظنه يعني أكثر من فتاوى تيسير وتسهيل أداء الفرائض العبادية

RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r34.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r34.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r34.claim: The author judges general calls to adapt fiqh insufficient unless scholars rebuild the underlying principles and inference rules so they can yield alternative rulings responsive to changing times and places.
RIFAI-KHULI:c2/r34.anchor: ما لم تتوغل في البنية التحتية العميقة للاستنباط الفقهي، وتعيد بناء ما ترتكز عليه

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r1.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r1.claim: Al-Rifai treats a book as its own interpretive key: Qur'anic verses illuminate one another, but readers cannot attain complete neutrality because their formation and assumptions shape interpretation.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r1.anchor: مفتاح تفسير كل كتاب هو الكتاب ذاته؛ لأن نصوصَه مُضَاءٌ بعضُها بالبعض الآخر، سواء أكان كتابًا مقدسًا أو غيره، آياتُ القرآن الكريم تفسر إحداها الأخرى.

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r2.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r2.claim: Al-Rifai argues that al-Tabataba'i's Tafsir al-Mizan announces Qur'an-by-Qur'an exegesis yet is heavily shaped by his philosophical, mystical, theological, and legal formation and by Greek and later Shi'i thought.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r2.anchor: مثلًا نقرأ في مقدمة تفسير (الميزان) للعلامة محمد حسين الطباطبائي أن منهجه يقوم على تفسير القرآن بالقرآن، غير أن كل ما جاء في تفسيره

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r3.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r3.claim: Khuli says interpreters color a text, especially a literary one: a reader's personality sets its intellectual level and the horizon within which its meaning is understood.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r3.anchor: تحدث الشيخ أمين الخولي عن فكرة تلوين النص بوضوح في قوله: «إن الشخص الذي يفسر نصًّا يلون هذا النص

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r4.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r4.claim: Khuli describes readers as pulling a phrase in different directions and drawing from it only what their intellectual capacity permits; language's figurative range enables this coloring.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r4.anchor: يشير الشيخُ الخولي إلى ذلك قائلًا: «فهو في حقيقة الأمر يَجُر إليه العبارة جرًّا، ويشدها شدًّا؛ يمطها إلى الشمال، وحينًا إلى الجنوب

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r5.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r5.claim: Al-Rifai suspects Khuli borrowed the image of coloring text from Junayd's saying that water takes its vessel's color, and sees Sufi and gnostic methods as valuable resources beyond inherited tafsir and legal theory.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r5.anchor: وأظن أن أمين الخولي اقتبس مصطلح «يلون النص» من التعبير المشهور للمتصوف الجنيد البغدادي

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r6.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r6.claim: Khuli holds that interpreters' personalities mark every method and era of exegesis, whether transmitted or reasoned, despite claims of detachment and objectivity.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r6.anchor: يكتب الخولي: «على هذا الأصل وجدنا آثارَ شخصية المتصدين لتفسير القرآن، تطبع تفسيرهم له في كل عهد وعصر، وعلى أي طريقة ومنهج

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r7.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r7.claim: Khuli rejects the claim that transmitted exegesis escapes the interpreter's personal imprint simply because it explains verses through reports without overt intervention.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r7.anchor: يرفض الشيخ الخولي رأي من يستثني التفسير الروائي من بصمة ذات المفسر، مُسَوغًا ذلك بأن هذا الضرْب من التفسير

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r8.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r8.claim: For Khuli, a narrator's choice to gather reports that seem relevant to a verse, and to accept or reject them, exposes the interpreter's horizon and prior assumptions.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r8.anchor: يكتب الخولي: «ولعله لا يبدو هذا الأثر الشخصي واضحًا في التفسير المروي لأول وهلة، ولكنك تتبينُه إذا ما قَدرْت أن المتصدي

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r9.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r9.claim: Al-Rifai draws the consequence that transmitted tafsir is a form of opinion-based exegesis, and even Qur'an-by-Qur'an interpretation depends on the interpreter's selection of verses and words.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r9.anchor: في ضوء هذا الفهم يصبح التفسير الروائي أحد أشكال التفسير بالرأي، حسب المصطلح المعروف في أنواع التفسير

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r10.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r10.claim: An exegete's field colors interpretation: a theologian produces kalam-oriented tafsir, a jurist legal tafsir, a Sufi mystical tafsir, and a literary scholar literary tafsir.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r10.anchor: فمثلًا لو كان المفسر متكلمًا، يكتسي تفسيرُه صبغةً كلامية، ولو كان فقيهًا يكتسي تفسيرُه صبغةً فقهية

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r11.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r11.claim: Al-Rifai stresses that even Qur'an-by-Qur'an exegesis is shaped by hidden assumptions when an interpreter chooses one verse or word to explain another.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r11.anchor: كأن الخولي يقرر قاعدةً كُليةً في التفسير، لا تستثني أي شكل من أشكال التفسير من التحرر من بصمة المفسر وفهمِه الخاص

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r12.speaker: أمين الخولي
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r12.claim: Khuli describes reciprocal effects between an exegete's worldview, specialized knowledge, and interpretation; connecting disciplines to tafsir can enrich those disciplines too.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r12.anchor: وكما يتحدث الخولي عن التأثير المتبادَل بين رؤية المفسر للعالَم والعلم الذي يتخصص فيه وبين عملية التفسير، ينبه أيضًا إلى تفاعُل ذلك العلم

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r13.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r13.claim: Al-Rifai argues that applying disciplines in new fields helps them develop by exposing gaps, defects, and errors.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r13.anchor: العلوم تنمو وتتطور من خلال اتساع مجالات تطبيقها في حقولٍ علمية جديدة؛ إذ يفضح التطبيق ثغراتِها ويكشف عيوبَها

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r14.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r14.claim: Al-Rifai says Khuli's position does not entail relativism; it frees Qur'anic meaning from exegetes' errors and treats their readings as historically conditioned rather than eternally authoritative.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r14.anchor: لا أظن الشيخ الخولي يورطنا في نسبية الفَهْم، بل أراه يحاول تحرير فهم النص القرآني من سوء فهم وأخطاء المفسرين

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r15.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r15.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r15.claim: Al-Rifai says Muhammad Ahmad Khalaf Allah embodied Khuli's reformist method, while Aisha Abd al-Rahman remained attached to inherited tafsir and did not adopt modern hermeneutics.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r15.anchor: ففي الوقت الذي تمثل محمد أحمد خلف الله نهجَ أستاذه الخولي في أطروحته للدكتوراه،٨ أخفقت تلميذتُه وزوجتُه عائشة عبد الرحمن

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r16.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r16.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r16.claim: Al-Rifai suggests Bint al-Shati avoided departing from inherited methods out of fear after Khalaf Allah's dissertation drew fierce attacks; he adds that she may not have grasped Khuli's critique of inherited tafsir.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r16.anchor: كأن بنت الشاطئ لم تشأ أن تتورط في الخُروج على المناهج الموروثة للتفسير، لخوفِها من ردود الأفعال

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r17.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r17.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r17.claim: Al-Rifai argues that reform is emotionally and materially costly and requires courage to challenge convention.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r17.anchor: التجديد شديد الوطأة على النفس والمشاعر والمصالح، لا يستسيغُه إلا عقلٌ شجاع، وإنسانٌ يمتلك قدرة المغامرة

RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r18.author: ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Rifāʿī
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r18.speaker: author
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r18.claim: Al-Rifai cites Muhammad Rashid Rida's Salafi turn after Muhammad Abduh's death as another example of students reverting to inherited tradition rather than following a reformist teacher.
RIFAI-KHULI:c6/r18.anchor: وهذا ما نراه ماثلًا في النزوع السلفي للشيخ محمد رشيد رضا، بعد رحيل أستاذه الشيخ محمد عبده، وغيره

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r1.claim: A Qur’anic story has several lessons and evidentiary uses; it is not literally repeated, since each occurrence brings forward the aspect suited to its context and purpose.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r1.anchor: وهذا شأن القصص القرآني، فأنت ترى أن القصة في القرآن كأنها تتكرر في أكثر من موطن

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r2.claim: The story of Moses shows that God’s decree cannot be altered: Pharaoh killed Israelite boys to prevent his downfall, yet raised in his own house the person destined to end his rule.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r2.anchor: بيان أن قدر الله ماضٍ لا محالة وأنه لا يستطيع أحد أن يغيره أو يرجئه مهما حاول واتخذ من أسباب ووسائل

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r3.claim: Moses’ story also displays the terrible end of Pharaoh as the consequence of injustice and unjust rulers.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r3.anchor: ومنها: بيان عاقبة الظُلم والظالمين، ويتجلى ذلك في نهاية فرعون النهاية الوبيلة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r4.claim: The Israelites’ formation in humiliation, cowardice, and worldliness explains their resistance to Moses’ reform; after forty years in the wilderness that generation died and a differently formed generation emerged.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r4.anchor: ذكر نفسية وتكوين بني إسرائيل الذين تربوا على الذلة والجبن والخنوع وذكر عنادهم وصَلَفِهم وجُبنهم وحبهم للدنيا

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r5.claim: Once known and believed, truth has irresistible power against enticement and threat, shown by the sorcerers’ belief in Moses and the faith of Pharaoh’s wife.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r5.anchor: بيان أن الحق له السطان الأعظم على النفوس إذا ما عرفته وآمنت به، وأنه ليس بوسع أيّ أحد أن يحول بينها وبينه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r6.claim: The Qur’an adapts each story to its context by omitting some details, expanding or summarizing others, changing sequence, and varying expression without changing the meaning.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r11/r6.anchor: بل تراه أحياناً يغير في التعبيرات ونظم الكلام تغييراً لا يخل بالمعنى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r1.claim: The doubled form يُضَارّ can be read as active or passive; spelling the consonant without assimilation would distinguish the two forms.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r1.anchor: كلمة (ضارّ) هل هي مبني للفاعل او المفعول؟ نقول هي تحتمل الإثنين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r2.claim: The verse forbids both a writer or witness harming others by withholding or distorting testimony and others pressuring them into changing or withholding it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p111/r2.anchor: أراد الإثنين معاً ومعنى الآية أنه نهى الكاتب والشهيد أن يضُرّا غيرهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r1.claim: The undiacritized form يُضارّ can be active or passive; spelling the assimilated consonant separately would distinguish يُضارِر from يُضارَر.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r1.anchor: كلمة (ضارّ) هل هي مبني للفاعل او المفعول؟ نقول هي تحتمل الإثنين ولو أراد التنصيص لفكّ الإدغام

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r2.claim: The verse forbids writers and witnesses from harming others by suppressing, refusing, or distorting testimony, and forbids others from coercing them into the same harms.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p560/r2.anchor: والله تعالى أراد الإثنين معاً ومعنى الآية أنه نهى الكاتب والشهيد أن يضُرّا غيرهما

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p859/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p859/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p859/r1.claim: The segment catalogs Qur’anic uses of the no-blame formula in legal allowances, including immediate trade, pilgrimage, travel prayer, food, entering uninhabited houses, and other cases.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p859/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى (إِلَّا أَنْ تَكُونَ تِجَارَةً حَاضِرَةً تُدِيرُونَهَا بَيْنَكُمْ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَلَّا تَكْتُبُوهَا (282)) وفي النساء

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r1.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r1.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r1.claim: Al-Khūlī’s approach to Qur’anic interpretation lies at the intersection of preserving intellectual origins and renewing them.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r1.anchor: والحق أنه يرابض في صلب التقاطع بينهما

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r2.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r2.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r2.claim: Interpretation is the starting point for intellectual work that renews the civilization, because the Qur’an anchors its origins and Muslim communal identity.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r2.anchor: القرآن الكريم هو نقطة الإحالة المرجعية الثابتة التي تمثل مبتدأ حضارتنا ومرتكزها

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r3.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r3.speaker: طه حسين
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r3.claim: Ṭāhā Ḥusayn calls the Qur’an neither poetry nor prose but Qur’an, marking it as a singular literary event.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r3.anchor: قال طه حسين — الأستاذ العميد — ليس شعرًا ولا نثرًا بل قرآنًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r4.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r4.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r4.claim: The author compares the Qur’an’s appearance in Arab civilization to philosophy’s appearance in the West: each was a decisive turn in outlook and method.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r4.anchor: يماثل ظهور الفلسفة في سيرورة الحضارة الغربية، منعطف جذري وتغيير حاسم

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r5.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r5.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r5.claim: Pre-revelation cultural inheritances persisted in Egypt through Pharaonic customs and the Coptic calendar, and other Muslim countries also retained pre-Qur’anic inheritances.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r5.anchor: من الفرعونية: شم النسيم، السبوع، ذكرى الأربعين، الحانوتي أو الحنوطي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r6.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r6.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r6.claim: Despite those inheritances, the Qur’an quickly gathered them into a new civilizational phase that shaped the later historical course.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r6.anchor: استوعبت كل هذا لتمثل مرحلة جديدة، نقطة بدء جديدة، مُشكلة كل المسار التاريخي اللاحق

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r7.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r7.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r7.claim: The Qur’an’s linguistic character makes authenticity a distinctive concern: language is the fabric of thought and consciousness, not a container for thought.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r7.anchor: ليست اللغة قالبًا أو وعاءً يُملأ بالفكر مثلما تُملأ السلة بالفاكهة، بل إن اللغة هي ذاتها نسيج التفكير

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r8.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r8.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r8.claim: The Qur’an’s linguistic force accompanied a kind of historical amnesia, as conquered peoples abandoned their national languages, which had embodied earlier social life and values.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r8.anchor: هجران البلدان المفتوحة للغاتها القومية التي هي إطار تفاعلاتها السابقة الطويلة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r9.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r9.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r9.claim: Islam presented itself as a continuation, development, and refinement of earlier revealed religions, especially Judaism and Christianity.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r9.anchor: يُعد نفسه امتدادًا وتطويرًا وتنقيحًا للديانات السماوية السابقة، وبالتحديد اليهودية والمسيحية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r11.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r11.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r11.claim: Although modern historical, archaeological, and anthropological research recovered ancient national origins, consciousness had already settled within the Qur’anic frame.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r11.anchor: قد استقر تمامًا في إطار النص القرآني

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r12.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r12.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r12.claim: The Qur’an became the center around which the heritage sciences arose, beginning with the linguistic disciplines because the Qur’an is a linguistic phenomenon.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r12.anchor: الانبثاقة الجبارة الفريدة لعلوم اللغة، التي أسفرت عن جهاز اشتقاقي ونحوي وصرفي لا مثيل له

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r13.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r13.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r13.claim: Rhetoric studied the Qur’an’s inimitability, jurisprudence derived rulings by analogy with it, and kalām rationalized it and developed toward philosophy.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r13.anchor: ثم البلاغة لتكشف عن إعجازه، يتبعهما الفقه ليستنبط الأحكام قياسًا عليه، وعلم الكلام من أجل عقلنة القرآن

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r14.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r14.speaker: حسن حنفي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r14.claim: Ḥasan Ḥanafī contrasts an Islamic civilization formed around the Qur’an with Western Christian civilization, where the book emerged from tradition; the Gospels followed the Christian call rather than serving as its source.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r14.anchor: وقد أشار المفكر الإسلامي المجدد حسن حنفي إلى أن هذا هو الفارق المحوري والجدلي بين الحضارة العربية الإسلامية، والحضارة الغربية المسيحية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r15.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r15.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r15.claim: The author notes that seventeenth-century historical criticism, associated with Spinoza, Richard Simon, and Jean Astruc, examined alteration and change in sacred books.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r15.anchor: ظهور علم النقد التاريخي للكتب المقدسة في القرن السابع عشر مع سبينوزا وريتشارد سيمون وجان أوستريك

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r16.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r16.speaker: حسن حنفي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r16.claim: Ḥasan Ḥanafī identifies three distinguishing Qur’anic features: it is the final, complete revelation; preserved in writing; and revealed gradually over twenty-three years in response to human needs.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r16.anchor: على كل هذا يقول حسن حنفي: أهم ما يميزنا كأمة، سواء إذا كنا مجتمعًا حاليًّا أو حضارة سابقة هو أننا قد تلقينا «وحيًّا» يمتاز على الأقل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r17.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r17.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r17.claim: The author links gradual, situation-responsive revelation to Al-Khūlī’s principle that the Qur’an is closely connected to human life, which grounds his literary school of interpretation.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r17.anchor: هو تواتر من حلول لمشكلات واجهت الفرد والجماعة، وذلك قريب مما أسماه شيخنا أمين الخولي: «وثيق اتصال القرآن بالحياة الإنسانية»

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r18.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r18.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r18.claim: Al-Khūlī’s literary approach challenges rigid, literal, static exegesis because that mode permits neither development nor renewal.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r18.anchor: نقض للتفسير الحرفي الثبوتي الجامد، الذي لا يؤذن بتطوير أو تجديد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r19.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r19.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r19.claim: Al-Khūlī treats the Qur’an’s psychological inimitability as its profound effect on the human psyche through sweetness of wording and meaning, sound, and rhythm.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r19.anchor: الخولي بدوره كان في طليعة روادنا الذين تعرضوا لصلة علم النفس بالبلاغة والأدب

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r20.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r20.speaker: السكاكي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r20.claim: Al-Sakkākī’s view, as reported through Al-Khūlī, is that the Qur’an’s psychological inimitability is apprehended through artistic taste rather than described or explained.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r20.anchor: يرى الخولي الإعجاز النفسي للقرآن متروكًا للإحساس الفني والذوق الأدبي؛ لأنه — كما انتهى السكاكي — يُدرك ولا يوصف أو يُعلل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r21.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r21.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r21.claim: Psychological interpretation can draw on psychology’s hypotheses and theories because verbal art is closely connected to the human psyche.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r21.anchor: التفسير النفسي للقرآن الكريم يقوم على أساس وطيد من صلة الفن القولي بالنفس الإنسانية

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r22.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r22.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r22.claim: The Qur’an is miraculous literary art serving religious guidance: art voices the conscience, while religion addresses belief and the heart and disciplines human feeling.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r22.anchor: فن أدبي معجز، من حيث هو هدى وبيان ديني، يقوم على سياسة النفوس البشرية وترويض الوجدان

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r23.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r23.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r23.claim: Al-Khūlī uses the psychological dimension to connect religion and literature and argues for reading the Qur’an topic by topic.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r23.anchor: هكذا عن طريق البعد النفسي يبلور الخولي نقطة التلاقي بين الدين وبين الأدب، ليخرج بدعواه للتفسير الأدبي للقرآن الكريم، موضوعًا موضوعًا

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r24.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r24.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r24.claim: The muṣḥaf’s arrangement does not preserve topical unity or chronology, Meccan and Medinan verses intermingle, and one subject appears in varied contexts; topical reading best enables deeper engagement.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r24.anchor: ترك وحدة الموضوع، ولم يلزمها مطلقًا. وترك أيضًا الترتيب الزمني لظهور الآيات

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r25.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r25.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r25.claim: Topical interpretation is always colored by the historical period in which it is undertaken.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r25.anchor: هذا التناول مصبوغ بصبغة العصر الذي يتم فيه

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r26.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r26.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r26.claim: The Qur’an uses taʾwīl, while legal theorists developed a specialized sense that later became common among theologians; Al-Khūlī considers tafsīr broader than taʾwīl.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r26.anchor: على أساس أن الأول أعم من الثاني. وقد استعمل القرآن الكريم كلمة «التأويل»

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r27.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r27.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r27.claim: Interpretive forms multiply because interpreters bring different cultural backgrounds to the text.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r27.anchor: وقد تنوعت ألوانه وتعددت بتعدد ثقافات المتصدين له

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r28.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r28.speaker: الأقدمون
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r28.claim: Early scholars classified tafsīr as a discipline that has neither matured nor burned out, unlike grammar and theology, which had both matured and burned out, and jurisprudence and hadith, which had matured but not burned out.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r28.anchor: التفسير علم — كما أشار الأقدمون — ما نضج وما احترق، مقابل النحو وعلم أصول الدين

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r29.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r29.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r29.claim: Hermeneutics has an older sense, the interpretation of sacred books, and a modern sense that developed into a major late-twentieth-century philosophical current.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r29.anchor: الهيرُمنيوطيقا في أصوله القديمة هو علم تأويل الكتب أو النصوص المقدسة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r30.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r30.speaker: فيلهلم دلتاي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r30.claim: Dilthey’s hermeneutic position treats interpretation or understanding as a method for the social and historical sciences.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r30.anchor: أحدهما يتبع فيلهلم دلتاي W. Dilthey (١٨٣٣–١٩١١) ويرى التأويل أو الفهم Verstehen

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r31.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r31.speaker: مارتن هيدجر
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r31.claim: Heidegger’s position treats interpretation as an ontological, existential event in which text and interpreter interact within the history of understanding.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r31.anchor: أما الموقف الثاني فيتبع مارتن هيدجر M. Heidegger (١٨٨٩–١٩٧٦) ويرى التأويل

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r32.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r32.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r32.claim: The author follows the Heideggerian line, treating hermeneutics as lived experience of texts and as dialogue that fuses text and reader across past and present.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r32.anchor: وسوف نسير الآن عبر الخط الهيدجري لنجد الهيرمنيوطيقا نظرية عن الخبرة الواقعية الحية بالنص

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r33.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r33.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r33.claim: Hermeneutics applies to religious, inherited, philosophical, and legal texts; in reading, text and reader, past and present, enter a reciprocal relation that keeps new understanding possible.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r33.anchor: إنها حوار مستمر مع النص يجعله مفتوحًا دائمًا لفهم جديد وتأويل جديد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r34.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r34.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r34.claim: A text opens a relationship with truth rather than stating a final truth; readers in each era give it contemporary language and fill it with meaning according to general purposes.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r34.anchor: النص لا يقول الحقيقة، بل يفتح علاقة مع الحقيقة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r35.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r35.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r35.claim: A text gains particular content when a present-day reader speaks on its behalf; without the present’s participation, it becomes frozen and detached from reality.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r35.anchor: يكتسب مضمونًا محددًا حين يتحدث المفسر القارئ نيابة عنه، يتحدث بلغته، لغة الحاضر

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r36.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r36.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r36.claim: A writer’s work of classification ends when the text is produced, but reading, interpretation, and understanding remain open-ended tasks.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r36.anchor: أما القراءة، التأويل والتفسير فمهمة مستمرة، إمكانية مفتوحة دومًا لفهم جديد

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r37.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r37.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r37.claim: Hermeneutics became an independent discipline that both draws on and informs the human sciences; it engages theories of knowledge, being, and value, especially epistemology.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r37.anchor: يستفيد من علوم إنسانية عديدة، وبنفس القدر يفيدها. وتصب فيه نظريات المعرفة والوجود والقيمة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r38.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r38.speaker: هانز جيورج جادامر
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r38.claim: Gadamer’s Truth and Method (1960) established hermeneutics as a powerful method, said to rival experimental science in importance for understanding the human reality of texts.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r38.anchor: وهو هانز جيورج جادامر H. G. Gadamer بكتابه الرائد «الحقيقة والمنهج» Wahrheit Und Methode (١٩٦٠)

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r39.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r39.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r39.claim: Hermeneutics developed schools and became a broad intellectual current with strong influence on cultural life and literary criticism.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r39.anchor: أصبحت الهيرمنيوطيقا علمًا له مدارسه، واتجاهًا واسعًا مارس سيطرة كبيرة على الأجواء الثقافية ومدارس النقد الأدبي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r40.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r40.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r40.claim: Hermeneutics rejects the gap between reader and text: meaning depends on the context of production and the recipient’s horizon, so it varies across times and places.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r40.anchor: فهم النص ليس كموضوع مفارق، بل في سياق إنتاجه وفي أفق المتلقي له، فتتعدد مدلولاته بتعدد آفاق المتلقين باختلاف الأزمنة والأمكنة

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r41.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r41.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r41.claim: Interpretation makes the text living and renewable by placing responsibility on reading: the reader reshapes its raw material according to the cultural horizon of the present.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r41.anchor: النص مادة خام، القارئ يشكلها ويعيد تشكيلها في عصره تبعًا للأفق الثقافي المعطى

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r42.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r42.speaker: أمين الخولي
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r42.claim: Al-Khūlī argues that a reader’s personality, intellectual level, and mental horizon limit what the reader can understand from a text; Arabic’s rich resources permit many interpretive extensions.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r42.anchor: يقول الخولي: إن الشخص الذي يفسر نصًّا، يلون هذا النص — لا سيما النص الأدبي — بتفسيره له وفهمه إياه

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r43.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r43.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r43.claim: The author attributes the crisis of Islamic culture and Arab civilization to the failure of interpretation and renewal, followed by a long era of commentaries, glosses, and marginalia.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r43.anchor: حدثت حين عجزت عن التأويل، وتوقفت عن التفسير المتجدد، ودخلت في ليل الشروح والتعليقات والمتون والهوامش والحواشي

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r44.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r44.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r44.claim: Renewing Qur’anic interpretation is necessary for the renewal and flourishing of Arab-Islamic thought, a goal pursued by Islamic thinkers since the Nahḍa began.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r44.anchor: فكان تجديد التفسير شرطًا لتجديد الفكر العربي الإسلامي وازدهاره

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r45.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r45.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r45.claim: The author concludes that Al-Khūlī substantially achieved this renewalist aim.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r45.anchor: ونحسب أن أمين الخولي قد أصاب الكثير من سويداء هذا الهدف

GHARNATI:v1p179/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r2.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r2.claim: The author invokes the Qurʾan’s exalted standing in the heavenly register as part of his praise of the divine gift of scripture.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r2.anchor: وقد قال سبحانه فيه: (وإنه في أم الكتاب لدينا لعلي حكيم

GHARNATI:v1p179/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r3.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r3.claim: Muhammad is praised as the chosen prophet endowed with the Book and clear proofs that open the path for people of insight.

GHARNATI:v1p179/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r4.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r4.claim: The cited warning says that only one who follows the Reminder and fears the Merciful unseen benefits from the Messenger’s warning.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r4.anchor: إنما تنذر من اتبع الذكر وخشي الرحمن بالغيب

GHARNATI:v1p179/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r5.speaker: النبي
GHARNATI:v1p179/r5.claim: The Prophet says every prophet received signs sufficient for people to believe, while his own special gift was revelation, through which he hopes to have the most followers on Judgment Day.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r5.anchor: اعتبرت قوله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: " ما من نبي إلا وقد أعطي

GHARNATI:v1p179/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r6.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r6.claim: The author says the Prophet had countless miracles besides the Qurʾan, but the Qurʾan is the clearest, wisest, most guiding, and most enduring miracle.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r6.anchor: بدروب لا يحصيها العد، ولا كاد تنحصر بالحد

GHARNATI:v1p179/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r7.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r7.claim: The Qurʾan joins proof and testimony with clarification of the path and the condition of each group, and remains directly observable to those who reflect.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r7.anchor: فإنما ضمنت إلى - الدلالة والشهادة إيضاح الطربق وأعلمت بحال كل فريق

GHARNATI:v1p179/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar Ibn al-Zubayr al-Gharnāṭī
GHARNATI:v1p179/r8.speaker: author
GHARNATI:v1p179/r8.claim: Unlike other miracles known through later reports rather than direct observation, the Qurʾan remains pure and present for reflection across the ages.
GHARNATI:v1p179/r8.anchor: وليس كالعيان، فلله ما أعظمها معجزة باقية مدى الدهور

NASHR:v2p236/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r1.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p236/r1.claim: Ḥamza reads the hamza in أن تضل with kasra.
NASHR:v2p236/r1.anchor: في: أن تضل فقرأ حمزة بكسر الهمزة

NASHR:v2p236/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r2.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p236/r2.claim: The other readers read the hamza in أن تضل with fatḥa.

NASHR:v2p236/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r3.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v2p236/r3.claim: Ḥamza reads the r in فتذكر in the nominative.
NASHR:v2p236/r3.anchor: في: فتذكر فقرأ حمزة أيضا برفع الراء، والباقون بفتحها

NASHR:v2p236/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r4.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p236/r4.claim: The other readers read the r in فتذكر with fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p236/r4.anchor: الباقون بفتحها، وقرأه ابن كثير، والبصريان بالتخفيف

NASHR:v2p236/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r5.speaker: ابن كثير والبصريان
NASHR:v2p236/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr and the two Basran readers pronounce فتذكر without gemination.
NASHR:v2p236/r5.anchor: قرأه ابن كثير، والبصريان بالتخفيف، وقرأ الباقون بالتشديد

NASHR:v2p236/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r6.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p236/r6.claim: The other readers pronounce فتذكر with gemination.

NASHR:v2p236/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r7.speaker: عاصم
NASHR:v2p236/r7.claim: ʿĀṣim reads both words in تجارة حاضرة in the accusative.
NASHR:v2p236/r7.anchor: في: تجارة حاضرة فقرأه عاصم بالنصب فيهما

NASHR:v2p236/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r8.speaker: الباقون
NASHR:v2p236/r8.claim: The other readers read both words in تجارة حاضرة in the nominative.

NASHR:v2p236/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p236/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p236/r9.claim: The preceding discussion gives a lightened r in يضار and reports Abū Jaʿfar's sukūn there, with disagreement transmitted from him.
NASHR:v2p236/r9.anchor: وتقدم تخفيف راء يضار، وإسكانها لأبي جعفر والخلاف عنه في ذلك

NASHR:v1p6/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r1.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
NASHR:v1p6/r1.claim: Abū ʿUbayd lists Companion transmitters of reading forms: numerous Muhājirūn including Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, and Ibn Masʿūd, and Anṣār including Ubayy, Muʿādh, Zayd, and Anas.
NASHR:v1p6/r1.anchor: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام في أول كتابه في القراءات: من نقل عنهم شيء من وجوه القراءة

NASHR:v1p6/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
NASHR:v1p6/r2.claim: After the Prophet’s death and the wars against apostates and Musaylima, in which about five hundred Companions were killed, Abū Bakr was urged to compile the Qurʾan lest it be lost with them; he first hesitated because the Prophet had not ordered it.
NASHR:v1p6/r2.anchor: وقتل من الصحابة نحو الخمسمائة، أشير على أبي بكر بجمع القرآن في مصحف واحد خشية أن يذهب بذهاب الصحابة

NASHR:v1p6/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
NASHR:v1p6/r3.claim: Abū Bakr and the Companions agreed to collection, and Zayd ibn Thābit gathered the Qurʾan into sheets kept successively by Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and Ḥafṣa.
NASHR:v1p6/r3.anchor: فجمعه في صحف كانت عند أبي بكر - رضي الله عنه - حتى توفي، ثم عند عمر - رضي الله عنه - حتى توفي، ثم عند حفصة

NASHR:v1p6/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r4.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
NASHR:v1p6/r4.claim: Around 30 AH, Ḥudhayfa saw Muslims in Armenia and Azerbaijan disputing whose recitation was more correct and urged ʿUthmān to intervene before they divided like Jews and Christians.
NASHR:v1p6/r4.anchor: فرأى الناس يختلقون في القرآن ويقول أحدهم للآخر قراءتي أصح من قراءتك، فأفزعه ذلك وقدم على عثمان

NASHR:v1p6/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r5.speaker: عثمان
NASHR:v1p6/r5.claim: ʿUthmān borrowed Ḥafṣa’s sheets and appointed Zayd, Ibn al-Zubayr, Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Ḥārith to copy them; in disagreement with Zayd, they were to write in Quraysh’s tongue because revelation came in it.
NASHR:v1p6/r5.anchor: أن ينسخوها في المصاحف، وقال: إذا اختلفتم أنتم وزيد في شيء فاكتبوه بلسان قريش

NASHR:v1p6/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r6.speaker: عثمان
NASHR:v1p6/r6.claim: ʿUthmān sent codices to Basra, Kufa, Syria, Mecca, Yemen, and Bahrain, left one in Medina, and kept the central copy for himself.
NASHR:v1p6/r6.anchor: فوجه بمصحف إلى البصرة، ومصحف إلى الكوفة، ومصحف إلى الشام، وترك مصحفا بالمدينة، وأمسك لنفسه مصحفا

NASHR:v1p6/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p6/r7.claim: The community agreed on the contents of these codices and set aside divergent additions, omissions, and word substitutions that had been permitted but were not established by widespread transmission as Qurʾan.
NASHR:v1p6/r7.anchor: وأجمعت الأمة المعصومة من الخطأ على ما تضمنته هذه المصاحف وترك ما خالفها من زيادة ونقص وإبدال كلمة بأخرى

NASHR:v1p6/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p6/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p6/r8.claim: The codices were left without dots or vowel marks so their script could accommodate sound transmitted readings; reliance was on memorization as well as the written outline.
NASHR:v1p6/r8.anchor: وجردت هذه المصاحف جميعها من النقط والشكل ليحتملها ما صح نقله وثبت تلاوته عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -، إذ كان الاعتماد على الحفظ لا على مجرد الخط

NASHR:v1p237/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p237/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p237/r3.claim: Some authorities treat alternative stops as mutually exclusive: choosing one stop bars the other, including the paired stops inside this verse.
NASHR:v1p237/r3.anchor: بين الوقفين مراقبة على التضاد، فإذا وقف على أحدهما امتنع الوقف الآخر

NASHR:v1p237/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p237/r4.speaker: أبو الفضل الرازي
NASHR:v1p237/r4.claim: Abu al-Fadl al-Razi was the first to point out this mutual monitoring between pause locations, borrowing the idea from prosody.
NASHR:v1p237/r4.anchor: وأول من نبه على المراقبة في الوقف الإمام الأستاذ أبو الفضل الرازي

NASHR:v2p227/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p227/r1.speaker: ابن كثير والبصريان
NASHR:v2p227/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir and the two Basrans read the rāʾ with ḍamma; the other readers use fatḥa. The author gives no semantic distinction here.
NASHR:v2p227/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير، والبصريان برفع الراء، وقرأ الباقون بفتحها

NASHR:v2p227/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p227/r2.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p227/r2.claim: Abu Jaʿfar has two transmitted forms: some routes lighten and silence the rāʾ, while other routes double it with fatḥa; all retain the alif’s lengthening at the meeting of two sukūns.
NASHR:v2p227/r2.anchor: واختلف عن أبي جعفر في سكونها مخففة، فروى عيسى من طريق ابن مهران

NASHR:v1p382#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p382#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p382#2/r2.claim: Within the two-kasra class, three loci are disputed: للنبي إن أراد and بيوت النبي except in Nafi’s reading, and من الشهداء أن تضل in Hamza’s reading.
NASHR:v1p382#2/r2.anchor: والمختلف فيه ثلاثة مواضع (للنبي إن أراد، و

NASHR:v1p382#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p382#2/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو
NASHR:v1p382#2/r5.claim: Abu Amr drops the first of the two hamzas in all three same-vowel classes; Ibn al-Jazari corrects one attributed Abu Rabiʿa route as mistaken and identifies the sound route.
NASHR:v1p382#2/r5.anchor: فقرأ أبو عمرو بإسقاط الهمزة الأولى منهما في الأقسام الثلاثة

NASHR:v1p387/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r1.claim: The differing-hamza class has one locus, من الشهداء أن, except for Hamza’s reading, as already noted in the two-kasra discussion.
NASHR:v1p387/r1.anchor: والمختلف فيه موضع واحد، وهو (من الشهداء أن)

NASHR:v1p387/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r2.claim: The fifth class has a ḍamma then kasra and 22 agreed occurrences, including ولا يأب الشهداء إذا and الفقراء إلى الله; six occurrences differ, including Maryam’s يا ذكرياء إنا and five addresses to the Prophet attributed to Nafi.

NASHR:v1p387/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p387/r5.claim: For the fifth class, early authorities mostly replace the softened second hamza with a pure kasra waw; later authorities mostly use a between-between sound. Al-Dani says the latter is better by analogy, the former stronger in transmission.
NASHR:v1p387/r5.anchor: فذهب بعضهم إلى أنها تبدل واوا خالصة مكسورة

NASHR:v2p208/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p208/r4.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر وقالون
NASHR:v2p208/r4.claim: These readers silence the medial hāʾ of هو when it follows waw, fāʾ, or lām, as in وهو, فهو, لهو, وهي, فهي, and لهي; al-Kisai also does so in ثم هو.
NASHR:v2p208/r4.anchor: فقرأه أبو عمرو والكسائي وأبو جعفر وقالون بإسكان الهاء إذا كان قبلها واو، أو فاء، أو لام

NASHR:v2p208/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p208/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p208/r5.claim: Abu Jaʿfar has both sukūn and ḍamma routes for the hāʾ in ثم هو and يمل هو; Ibn al-Jazari accepts both as sound.
NASHR:v2p208/r5.anchor: وكلا الوجهين فيهما صحيح عن أبي جعفر

NASHR:v2p208/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p208/r6.speaker: قالون
NASHR:v2p208/r6.claim: Qalun likewise has both hāʾ forms in these two phrases, though the sukūn route is rare through Abu Nashit; Ibn al-Jazari read both through the cited routes.
NASHR:v2p208/r6.anchor: والوجهان فيهما صحيحان عن قالون، وبهما قرأت له من الطرق المذكورة

NASHR:v2p235/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p235/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p235/r1.claim: Two Bazzī-related readings, known through Ibn Badahan alone from al-Zaynabi, were absent from the other authorities’ routes; al-Dani included them by textual analogy, and al-Shatibi followed, while this author includes them because they appear in the Taysir and Shatibiyya and fit the Bazzī rule.
NASHR:v2p235/r1.anchor: كل من ذكر طريق الزينبي هذا عن أبي ربيعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r1.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r1.claim: The excerpt recalls a report that the Quran was being written on parchments in the Prophet's presence; the speaker is not identified in this continuation.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r1.anchor: قال كنا عند النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم نؤلف القرآن في الرقاع

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r2.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r2.claim: In al-Bukhari's report, after the Yamama deaths Umar feared further losses among Quran reciters would cause the Quran to be lost and urged Abu Bakr to collect it.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r2.anchor: فقد أخرج البخاري في صحيحه عن زيد بن ثابت أيضا قال أرسل إلى أبو بكر مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر بن الخطاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r3.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r3.claim: Abu Bakr initially questioned doing what the Prophet had not done, but Umar persisted, saying collection was good, until God opened Abu Bakr's heart to the proposal.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r3.anchor: قال عمر : هذا والله خير فلم يزل يراجعني حتى شرح الله صدري

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r4.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r4.claim: Abu Bakr chose Zayd as young, intelligent, trusted, and a former revelation scribe; Zayd found collection as burdensome as moving a mountain, then accepted after Abu Bakr pressed him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r4.anchor: إنك شاب عاقل لا نتهمك وقد كنت تكتب الوحي لرسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم فنتبع القرآن فأجمعه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r5.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r5.claim: Zayd collected from palm stalks, flat stones, and men's memories; he found the end of al-Tawba only with Khuzayma al-Ansari, and the sheets later passed from Abu Bakr to Umar to Hafsa.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r5.anchor: فتتبعت القرآن أجمعه من العسب واللخاف وصدور الرجال ووجدت آخر سورة التوبة مع خزيمة الأنصاري لم أجدها مع غيره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r6.claim: A disconnected Ibn Abi Dawud report with trustworthy transmitters says Abu Bakr instructed Umar and Zayd to write any Quran text presented by two witnesses; Alusi supposes they attested its writing before the Prophet or its final-year review.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r6.anchor: بسند رجاله ثقات مع إنقطاع أن أبا بكر قال لعمر وزيد مع أنه كان حافظا أقعدا على باب المسجد فمن جاءكما بشاهدين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r7.claim: Alusi explains that only Khuzayma's single testimony sufficed for the al-Tawba verses because the Prophet had equated his testimony with that of two men.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r7.anchor: وإنما أكتفوا في آية التوبة بشهادة خزيمة لأن رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم جعل شهادته بشهادة رجلين

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r8.claim: The claim that the two witnesses meant one person who memorized the text and another who had it written has no basis.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r8.anchor: والقول بأن المراد بالشاهدين الحفظ والكتابة مما لا حجار له

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r9.claim: Reports that Ali stayed behind after the Prophet's death to compile the Quran include weak and fabricated routes; sound material may mean collecting it in memory or compiling it differently for another purpose.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r9.anchor: وما شاع أن عليا كرم الله وجهه لما توفي رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم تخلف لجمعه فبعض طرقه ضعيف وبعضها موضوع وما صح فمحمول

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r10.claim: A good-chain Ibn Abi Dawud report from Abd Khayr says Ali called Abu Bakr the person with the greatest merit in the codices and the first to collect God's Book in the stated official sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r10.anchor: سمعت عليا يقول أعظم الناس في المصاحف أجرا أبو بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r11.claim: Calling Abu Bakr the first collector does not conflict with al-Qarmani's statement that Umar first collected it, since the intended collection differs.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r11.anchor: فلا ينافي ما في مختصر القرماني أن أول من جمعه عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r12.speaker: أبو بريدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r12.claim: Abu Burda's strange, disconnected report says Salim, freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, first collected the Quran in a codex, swearing not to wear his cloak until finishing.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r12.anchor: وما روى عن أبي بريدة أنه قال أول من جمع القرآن في مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة أقسم لا يرتدي برداء حتى يجمعه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r13.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r13.claim: Al-Suyuti treats Salim as one of Abu Bakr's commissioned collectors, but Alusi calls this an error because Salim died at Yamama, before Abu Bakr ordered the collection.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r13.anchor: وهي عثرة منه لا يقال لصاحبها لعا لأن سالما هذا قتل في وقعة اليمامة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r14.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r14.claim: Alusi rejects saying Uthman first collected the Quran: al-Bukhari's report from Anas says Uthman standardized one reading in year 25 when Hudhayfa feared Syrian and Iraqi differences could divide the community.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r14.anchor: فقد روى البخاري عن أنس أن حذيفة بن اليماني قدم على عثمان وكان يغازي أهل الشام في فتح أرمينية وآرذبيجان مع أهل العراق

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r15.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r15.claim: At Hudhayfa's urging, Uthman borrowed Hafsa's sheets, appointed Zayd and three Qurashis to copy them, directed Qurashi wording in disputes, returned the sheets, sent copies to regions, and burned other codices.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r15.anchor: فأرسل إلى حفصة أنأرسلي إلينا بالصحف ننسخها ثم نردها إليك فأرسلت بها حفصة إلى عثمان

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r16.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r16.claim: While copying, Zayd noticed a missing verse of al-Ahzab that he had heard the Prophet recite; they found it with Khuzayma and inserted it in its surah.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r16.anchor: ففقدت آية من الأحزاب حين نسخنا المصحف قد كنت أسمع رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقرأ بها فألتمسناها فوجدناها مع خزيمة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r17.speaker: سويد بن غفلة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r17.claim: A sahih Ibn Abi Dawud chain from Suwayd ibn Ghafala quotes Ali asking people to speak only well of Uthman, since he acted on the codices with the group's agreement; another report says Ali would have done the same.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r17.anchor: بسند صحيح عن سويد بن غفلة عنه : لا تقولوا في عثمان إلا خيرا فوالله ما فعل في المصاحف إلا عن ملأ منا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r18.claim: Alusi calls the report that Ibn Masud threatened to treat Uthman's codex as they treated his a lie, along with claims that Uthman mistreated him.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r18.anchor: وما نقل عن إبن مسعود أنه قال لما أحرق مصحفه : لو ملكت كما ملكوا لصنعت بمصحفهم كما صنعوا بمصحفي كذب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r19.claim: Alusi's conclusion, shared by several critical scholars, is that Uthman added, removed, or rearranged nothing in Abu Bakr's collection; he only unified readings in Quraysh's dialect.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p21#2/r19.anchor: صرحوا بأن عثمان لم يصنع شيئا فيما جمعه أبو بكر من زيادة أو نقص أو تغيير ترتيب سوى أنه جمع الناس على القراءة بلغة قريش

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r1.claim: God sent Muḥammad with guidance and the true religion as mercy to all, glad tidings for believers, and warning for opponents; through him prophethood was completed, the message sealed, and noble character perfected.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r1.anchor: أرسل رسوله بالهدى ودين الحق رحمة للعالمين، وبشيرا للمؤمنين، ونذيرا للمخالفين

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r2.claim: God's Qur'an is a light that guides people away from error and saves them from ignorance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r2.anchor: وأنزل عليه بفضله نورا هدى به من الضلالة، وأنقذ به من الجهالة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r3.claim: Those who follow the Qur'an attain success, while those who turn away after hearing it incur loss.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r3.anchor: وحكم بالفلاح لمن تبعه، وبالخسارة لمن أعرض عنه بعد ما سمعه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r4.claim: The Qur'an is inimitable: creation cannot answer it or produce a sura like it, although God makes its recitation easy for people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r4.anchor: أعجز الخليقة عن معارضته وعن الإتيان بسورة من مثله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r5.claim: The Qur'an commands and forbids, gives glad tidings and warnings, offers admonitions, recounts past peoples for reflection, presents parables, and points to signs of divine oneness for contemplation.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r5.anchor: أمر فيه وزجر، وبشر وأنذر وذكر المواعظ ليتذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r6.claim: Realizing these purposes requires knowledge of tafsīr and its features, occasions of revelation, rulings, abrogating and abrogated verses, and specific and general language.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r6.anchor: ولا حصول لهذه المقاصد فيه إلا بدراية تفسيره وأعلامه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r7.claim: The Qur'an is an inimitable, deep sea whose scholarly secrets and true meanings have no end.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r7.anchor: ثم هو كلام معجز وبحر عميق، لا نهاية لأسرار علومه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r8.claim: Early scholars wrote books on Qur'anic sciences according to their understanding and knowledge; Baghawī thanks God for their efforts and asks mercy for them all.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p33/r8.anchor: وقد ألف أئمة السلف في أنواع علومه كتبا، كل على قدر فهمه، ومبلغ علمه،

BIQAI-FULL:v5p564/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p564/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p564/r1.claim: The promise that God teaches those who fear Him supports the preceding point about expanded understanding of Qur'anic knowledge.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r1.speaker: جماعة منهم أبو بكر الباقلائي وابن عبد البر وأبو بكر بن العربي والطبري والطحاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r1.claim: Al-Baqillani, Ibn Abd al-Barr, Ibn al-Arabi, al-Tabari, and al-Tahawi, with this view attributed to Ibn Uyayna and Ibn Wahb, hold that the seven-letter license was later abrogated after allowing tribal dialects.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r1.anchor: الباقلائي وابن عبد البر وأبو بكر بن العربي والطبري والطحاوي ، وينسب إلى ابن عيينة وابن وهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r2.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r2.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the license lasted through the Prophet’s life, implying abrogation after his death either by the Companions’ consensus or prophetic instruction.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r2.anchor: وقال ابن العربي دامت الرخصة مدة حياة النبي عليه السلام ، وظاهر كلامه أن ذلك نسخ بعد وفاة رسول الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r3.speaker: عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r3.claim: Abrogation proponents cite Umar’s statement that the Quran was revealed in Quraysh speech and his ban on Ibn Masud’s Hudhayl form of حتى.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r3.anchor: واستدلوا على ذلك بقول عمر : إن القرآن نزل بلسان قريش ، وبنهيه عبد الله بن مسعود أن يقرأ ( فتول عنهم حتى حين )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r4.speaker: عثمان
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r4.claim: Uthman instructed codex scribes to use Quraysh speech whenever they differed over a letter, as evidence for the abrogation view.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r4.anchor: وبقول عثمان لكتاب المصاحف فإذا اختلفتم في حرف فاكتبوه بلغة قريش فإنما نزل بلسانهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r5.claim: Ibn Ashur says Uthman’s phrase may mean Quraysh speech predominated in the Quran, or that its dialect absorbed tribal forms through Mecca’s centrality and the Ukaz market.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r5.anchor: يريد أن لسان قريش هو الغالب على القرآن ، أو أراد أنه نزل بما نطقوا به من لغتهم وما غلب على لغتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r6.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r6.claim: One explanation makes the seven letters synonymous expressions conveying one meaning, a concession letting reciters use whichever synonym comes readily to ease recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r6.anchor: الأول أن المراد بالأحرف الكلمات المترادفة للمعنى الواحد ، أي أنزل بتخيير قارئه أن يقرأه باللفظ الذي يحضره من المرادفات تسهيلا عليهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r7.claim: On this explanation the majority take seven literally, limiting the concession to seven synonyms or dialects; Ibn Ashur notes such abundance is impossible for most words and rare even for dialect forms.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r7.anchor: وعلى هذا الجواب فقيل المراد بالسبعة حقيقة العدد وهو قول الجمهور فيكون تحديدا للرخصة بأن لا يتجاوز سبعة مرادفات أو سبع لهجات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن عطية وأبو حاتم والباقلاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r8.claim: Abu Ubayda, Ibn Atiyya, Abu Hatim, and al-Baqillani identify the seven dialects as Quraysh, Hudhayl, Taym al-Ribab, Azd, Rabi'a, Hawazin, and Sa'd ibn Bakr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r8.anchor: فقال أبو عبيدة وابن عطية وأبو حاتم والباقلاني هي من عموم لغات العرب وهم : قريش ، وهذيل ، وتيم الرباب ، والأزد ، وربيعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r9.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r9.claim: Another enumeration includes Quraysh, Banu Darim, and the upper Hawazin clans Sa'd, Jusham, and Nasr ibn Muawiya, plus Thaqif; some substitute Khuza'a for Tamim.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r9.anchor: وبعضهم يعد قريشا ، وبني دارم ، والعليا من هوازن وهم سعد بن بكر ، وجشم بن بكر ، ونصر بن معاوية ، وثقيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r10.speaker: أبو علي الاهوازي وابن عبد البر وابن قتيبة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r10.claim: Abu Ali al-Ahwazi, Ibn Abd al-Barr, and Ibn Qutayba restrict the seven dialects to Mudar tribes: Quraysh, Hudhayl, Kinana, Qays, Dabba, Taym al-Ribab, and Asad ibn Khuzayma.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r10.anchor: وقال أبو علي الاهوازي ، وابن عبد البر ، وابن قتيبة هي لغات قبائل من مضر وهم قريش ، وهذيل ، وكنانة ، وقيس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r11.speaker: جماعة منهم عياض
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r11.claim: A group including Iyad treats seven as figurative for plurality, allowing synonymous alternatives even within one dialect; Ibn Ashur illustrates this with variant readings and Umar’s disagreement with Hisham despite their shared dialect.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r11.anchor: الثاني : لجماعة منهم عياض : أن العدد غير مراد به حقيقته ، بل هو كناية عن التعدد والتوسع ، وكذلك المرادفات ولو من لغة واحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r12.claim: Ibn Masud permitted replacing أثيم with فاجر when a man could not pronounce أثيم, illustrating latitude for synonymous recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r12.anchor: فقال له ابن مسعود : أتستطيع أن تقول طعام الفاجر ? قال نعم ، قال فاقرأ كذلك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r13.speaker: ابن عبد البر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r13.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr explains the seven as contextual latitude to substitute a fitting divine attribute, such as حكيم for عليم, while preserving contextual propriety after punishment or mercy passages.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r13.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب ابن عبد البر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r14.speaker: البيهقي وأبو الفضل الرازي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r14.claim: For those who hold the report un-abrogated, al-Bayhaqi and Abu al-Fadl al-Razi say seven denotes Quranic categories: commands and prohibitions, lawful and forbidden matters, report and performance, literal and figurative, or general and specific meanings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r14.anchor: فقد ذهبوا في تأويله مذاهب : فقال جماعة منهم البيهقي وأبو الفضل الرازي أن المراد من الأحرف أنواع أغراض القرآن كالأمر والنهي ، والحلال والحرام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r15.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r15.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r15.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects that categorical account as mismatched with the hadith’s transmitted context of concession and ease, and says its forced sevenfold classifications do not withstand objection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p56/r15.anchor: ولا يخفى أن كل ذلك لا يناسب سياق الحديث على اختلاف رواياته من قصد التوسعة والرخصة . وقد تكلف هؤلاء حصر ما زعموه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r1.claim: Kitab is originally an unrestricted generic noun or a definite, familiar one; in the latter sense it frequently names the Quran.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r1.anchor: القرآن كثيرا قال تعالى ) ذلك الكتاب لا ريب فيه (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r2.claim: The Quran is called a book because it gathers the revealed law, resembling the Torah and the Gospel, though the Gospel was written by followers rather than during Jesus’s lifetime.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r2.anchor: وإنما سمي كتابا لأن الله جعله جامعا للشريعة فأشبه التوراة لأنها كانت مكتوبة في زمن الرسول المرسل بها ، وأشبه الإنجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r3.claim: God ordered the Prophet to write all revelation as proof for converts who had not received it by memorizing it in their hearts.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r3.anchor: ولأن الله أمر رسوله أن يكتب كل ما أنزل عليه منه ليكون حجة على الذين يدخلون في الإسلام ولم يتلقوه بحفظ قلوبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r4.claim: Calling the revelation a book foretold miraculously that it would be written in codices, as shown by Quranic passages describing it as a revealed book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r4.anchor: وفي هذه التسمية معجزة للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بأن ما أوحي إليه سيكتب في المصاحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r5.claim: The Prophet appointed companions to record revelation from its beginning; Ibn Ashur names Abdullah ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Sarh, Abdullah ibn Amr, Zayd ibn Thabit, and Muawiya ibn Abi Sufyan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r5.anchor: ولذلك اتخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أصحابه كتابا يكتبون ما أنزل إليه ؛ من أول ما ابتدئ نزوله ، ومن أولهم عبد الله ابن سعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r6.claim: When Abu Bakr ordered a written codex, the collected text matched what Muslims had retained by heart with what had been written down.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r6.anchor: وقد وجد جميع ما حفظه المسلمون في قلوبهم على قدر ما وجدوه مكتوبا يوم أمر أبو بكر بكتابة المصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r7.claim: Dhikr means a reminder of what people must believe and do; in the cited verse, the Prophet is to explain that reminder to people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r7.anchor: وأما الذكر فقال تعالى ) وأنزلنا إليك الذكر لتبين للناس ما نزل إليهم ( أي لتبينه للناس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r8.claim: Wahy is named for the angel’s delivery to the Prophet, which conveys God’s intent like translated human speech; its compositions were not made by humans.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r8.anchor: ووجه هذه التسمية أنه ألقي إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بواسطة الملك وذلك الإلقاء يسمى وحيا لأنه يترجم عن مراد الله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r9.claim: The Quran is also called God’s speech, as in the command to shelter a polytheist until he hears the speech of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r9.anchor: وأما كلام الله فقال تعالى ) وإن أحد من المشركين استجارك فأجره حتى يسمع كلام الله (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r10.speaker: عبد الله ابن مسعود
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r10.claim: When Abu Bakr sought a name for the written Quran, suggestions Injil and Sifr were rejected for their Christian and Jewish associations; Ibn Masud proposed Mushaf, a name he had seen used in Abyssinia.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p73/r10.anchor: فقال عبد الله ابن مسعود : رأيت بالحبشة كتابا يدعونه المصحف فسموه مصحفا يعني أنه رأى كتابا غير الإنجيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r1.claim: Discussion of the Quran’s name, verses, suras, ordering, and titles directly serves tafsir, especially interpretation of sura openings and connections, and avoids repeated exposition.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r1.anchor: في اسم القرآن وآياته وسوره وترتيبها وأسمائها هذا غرض له مزيد اتصال بالقرآن . وله اتصال متين بالتفسير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r2.claim: Tafsir studies the Quran to clarify its meanings and guidance, instruction, manners, and reform of the community and its dealings with other peoples through linguistic and rhetorical evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r2.anchor: موضوع علم التفسير هو القرآن لتبيان معانيه وما يشتمل عليه من إرشاد وهدى وآداب وإصلاح حال الأمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r3.claim: The Quran is God’s Arabic speech revealed to Muhammad through Gabriel, whose task is to convey to the community the wording revealed to him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r3.anchor: فالقرآن هو الكلام الذي أوحاه الله تعالى كلاما عربيا إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بواسطة جبريل على أن يبلغه الرسول إلى الأمة باللفظ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r4.claim: The community acts on the revealed wording and recites what it can in prayer; reciting the Quran is itself worship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r4.anchor: للعمل به ولقراءة ما يتيسر لهم أن يقرأوه منه في صلواتهم وجعل قراءته عبادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r5.claim: The Quran proves the Messenger’s claim for all people by challenging its first Arab hearers to produce something comparable, which they failed to do.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r5.anchor: وجعله كذلك آية على صدق الرسول في دعواه الرسالة عن الله إلى الخلق كافة بأن تحدى منكريه والمترددين فيه من العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r6.claim: The challenge descends from ten suras, to one sura, to an explicit warning that they could never produce one; Ibn Ashur also cites the Quran’s answer to demands for a sign.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r6.anchor: دعاهم أول الأمر إلى الإتيان بعشر سور مثله فقال ) أم يقولون افتراه قل فأتوا بعشر سور مثله مفتريات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r7.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r7.claim: The Prophet says each prophet received signs through which people believed, while his own gift was revelation; Ibn Ashur notes further meanings are discussed in his Bukhari commentary.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p70/r7.anchor: وقد بين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ذلك بقوله ما من الأنبياء نبي إلا أوتي من الآيات ما مثله آمن عليه البشر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r1.claim: The Quran associates knowledge with light and life, illustrating the point with verses describing the living, emergence from darkness to light, learned understanding, and the learned versus ignorant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r1.anchor: ) لتنذر من كان حيا ( وقوله ) يخرجهم من الظلمات إلى النور (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r2.claim: This Quranic inimitability clearly sets its style and purposes apart from poetry.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r2.anchor: وهذا النوع من الإعجاز هو الذي خالف به القرآن أساليب الشعر وأغراضه مخالفة واضحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r3.speaker: الشاطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r3.claim: Al-Shatibi says Quranic meanings and interpretation must stay within what is customary among Arabs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r3.anchor: والشاطبي قال في الموافقات : إن القرآن لا تحمل معانيه ولا يتأول إلا على ما هو متعارف عند العرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r4.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests al-Shatibi may have been avoiding difficult objections economically, but asks how this view can deny the Quran’s continuing miracle to later peoples.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r4.anchor: ولعل هذا الكلام صدر منه في التفصي من مشكلات في مطاعن الملحدين اقتصادا في البحث وإبقاء على نفيس الوقت ، وإلا فكيف ينفي إعجاز القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r5.speaker: محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r5.claim: The authentic report says every prophet received signs that people believed because of, while Muhammad’s gift was revelation and he hoped for the greatest following.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r5.anchor: وقد بدت لي حجة لتعلق هذه الجهة الثالثة بالإعجاز ودوامه وعمومه وهي قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم في الحديث الصحيح ما من الأنبياء نبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur reads آمن عليه as believing because of the sign and according to its terms: each prophet’s miracle addressed a field especially admired and beyond his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r6.anchor: الأولى أن قوله ما مثله آمن عليه البشر اقتضى أن كل نبي جاء بمعجزة هي إعجاز في أمر خاص كان قومه أعجب به وأعجز عنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r7.claim: Unlike earlier action miracles such as the staff, water from stone, and healing, Muhammad’s miracle is the Quran’s wording and meanings, beyond human imitation and available for study in every age.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r7.anchor: الثانية أن قوله وإنما كان الذي أوتيت وحيا اقتضى أن ليست معجزته من قبيل الأفعال كما كانت معجزات الرسل الأولين أفعالا لا أقوالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r8.claim: The fa of فأرجو marks a consequence: only a miracle lasting across ages explains the Prophet’s hope for the largest following, since generations with different capacities can recognize it; followers means adherents to true religion, not mere affiliation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r8.anchor: إذ قد عطف بالفاء المؤذنة بالترتب ، فالمناسبة بين كونه أوتي وحيا وبين كونه يرجو أن يكون أكثرهم تابعا لا تنجلي إلا إذا كانت المعجزة صالحة لجميع الأزمان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r9.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests the Prophet’s hope may mean more followers than all the other prophets combined, and says this has in fact occurred in true religious adherence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r9.anchor: ولعل الرجاء متوجه إلى كونه أكثر من جميعهم تابعا أي أكثر أتباعا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r10.claim: This scholarly dimension of inimitability belongs to the Quran as a whole, not every verse or sura separately; the challenge is only alluded to in the challenge to inconsistency.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r10.anchor: وهذه الجهة من الإعجاز إنما تثبت للقرآن بمجموعه أي مجموع هذا الكتاب إذ ليست كل آية من آياته ولا كل سورة من سوره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r11.claim: For Arabs, the Quran’s sciences were inaccessible before its revelation; Ibn Ashur cites the statement that neither Muhammad nor his people knew them beforehand.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r11.anchor: وإعجازه من هذه الجهة للعرب ظاهر : إذ لا قبل لهم بتلك العلوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r12.claim: For the general public, the miracle is that such knowledge came through a man raised unlettered among an unlettered people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r12.anchor: وإعجازه لعامة الناس أن تجيء تلك العلوم من رجل نشأ أميا في قوم أميين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r13.claim: For People of the Book, the Quran reports their religious knowledge through an unlettered Prophet distant from their communities, abrogates their religions, and denounces their distortions; had he learned from them, they would have exposed it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p128/r13.anchor: وإعجازه لأهل الكتاب خاصة إذ كان ينبئهم بعلوم دينهم مع كونه أميا ، ولا قبل لهم بأن يدعوا أنهم علموه لأنه كان بمرأى من قومه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r1.claim: A human trying to compose a medium-length sura would need prolonged revision and still leave awkward sentences; the Quran’s fluent composition entails no such labor.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r1.anchor: لقضى زمنا مديدا في تأليف ما يقدر بسورة من متوسط سور القرآن ، ولما سلم مع ذلك من جمل يتعثر فيها اللسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r2.claim: Quranic prose uses balanced, near-rhyming endings without rhetorical necessity or the constraints of meter, giving it smooth and harmonious delivery.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r2.anchor: فبنى نظمه على فواصل وقرائن متقاربة فلم تفته سلاسة الشعر ولم ترزح تحت قيود الميزان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r3.claim: The Quran’s prose form itself contributes to its inimitability; it gathers known Arabic styles and innovates new ones.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r3.anchor: فكان كونه من النثر داخلا في إعجازه ، وقد اشتمل القرآن على أنواع أساليب الكلام العربي وابتكر أساليب لم يكونوا يعرفونها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r4.claim: Stylistic variety shows divine origin because literary geniuses usually excel in only one or two styles, and intensifies the challenge by denying opponents the excuse that they had not tried a given style.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r4.anchor: وإن لذلك التنويع حكمتين داخلتين في الإعجاز : أولاهما ظهور أنه من عند الله ؛ إذ قد تعارف الأدباء في كل عصر أن يظهر نبوغ نوابغهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r5.claim: A distinctive Quranic style combines exhortation and legislation: its apparent wording teaches listeners what they need, while its depths yield many legal and ethical rulings to learned readers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r5.anchor: أنه جاء في نظمه بأسلوب جامع بين مقصديه وهما : مقصد الموعظة ومقصد التشريع ، فكان نظمه يمنح بظاهره السامعين ما يحتاجون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur cites the statement that only God and those firmly grounded in knowledge know its interpretation as an example of the Quran’s layered meanings and allusions to causes and purposes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r6.anchor: وقد قال في الكلام على بعضه ) وما يعلم تأويله إلا الله والراسخون في العلم ( هذا من حيث ما لمعانيه من العموم والإيماء إلى العلل والمقاصد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur calls tafannun the artful movement between topics through parenthesis, analogy, conclusion, varied synonyms, and frequent grammatical shifts, before returning to the main subject and renewing attention.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r7.anchor: ومن أساليبه ما أسميه بالتفنن وهو بداعة تنقلاته من فن إلى فن بطرائق الاعتراض والتنظير والتذييل والإتيان بالمترادفات عند التكرير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r8.claim: The two parables of hypocrites, the fire and the rainstorm, exemplify this movement between styles and topics.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r8.anchor: ومن أبدع أمثلة ذلك قوله ) مثلهم كمثل الذي استوقد نارا فلما أضاءت ما حوله ذهب الله بنورهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r9.claim: Transitions are finely connected and barely noticed, holding listeners’ attention and relieving the weariness of extended recitation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r9.anchor: وفي هذا التفنن والتنقل مناسبات بين المنتقل منه والمنتقل إليه هي في منتهى الرقة والبداعة بحيث لا يشعر سامعه وقارئه بانتقاله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r10.claim: The Quran encourages extended recitation; Ibn Ashur reads ما تيسر as reciting as much as one can manage, with coherence and stylistic variety helping sustain it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r10.anchor: من أغراض القرآن استكثار أزمان قراءته كما قال تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r11.speaker: أبو بكر بن العربي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r11.claim: In Siraj al-Muridin, Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi calls the links among Quranic verses a great science, making them cohere like a single phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r11.anchor: نقل عن أبي بكر بن العربي أنه قال في كتابه سراج المريدين ارتباط آي القرآن بعضها مع بعض حتى تكون كالكلمة الواحدة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r12.speaker: عز الدين بن عبد السلام
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r12.claim: Izz al-Din ibn Abd al-Salam, as quoted by al-Zarkashi, calls coherence a good science but says connection requires a unified subject; distinct causes and rulings across more than twenty years resist linking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r12.anchor: ونقل الزركشي عن عز الدين بن عبد السلام المناسبة علم حسن ويشترط في حسن ارتباط الكلام أن يقع في أمر متحد مرتبط أوله بآخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r13.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r13.claim: Al-Razi says the Quran is inimitable through arrangement and verse order as well as eloquent wording and noble meanings; al-Isfahani suggests this is what style-based claims mean.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r13.anchor: وقال شمس الدين محمود الأصفهاني في تفسيره نقلا عن الفخر الرازي أنه قال إن القرآن كما أنه معجز بسبب فصاحة ألفاظه وشرف معانيه هو أيضا معجز بسبب ترتيبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r14.claim: Rhetoric extends beyond the states of verbal syntax to the ways in which those structures deliver meaning.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p115/r14.anchor: إن بلاغة الكلام لا تنحصر في أحوال تراكيبه اللفظية ، بل تتجاوز إلى الكيفيات التي تؤدي بها تلك التراكيب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p47/r1.speaker: حذيفة بن اليمان
